Yet even in this ultimatum, he affirms God as the great substance beyond all study, the light that is the life of life, the awareness without beginning, middle or end.

translit: illaiuṇ ṭeṇumiv virumaiyum kaṭantōr iyaṟkaiyiṉ niṟaintapē riṉpē allaiuṇ ṭeḻunta taṉipperuñ cuṭarē ampalat tāṭalcey amutē vallaiiṉ ṟaṭiyēṉ tuyarelām tavirttu vaḻaṅkuka niṉaruḷ vaḻaṅkal nallaiiṉ ṟalatu nāḷaieṉ ṟiṭilō nāṉuyir tarikkalaṉ aracē.
translation: O great bliss, filled with a nature that transcends the duality of 'is' and 'is not'! O unique great flame that rose, swallowing the darkness! O nectar dancing in the sacred space! You are able; today, remove all of your servant's sorrow and grant Your grace. You are good at granting, but if You say, "not today, tomorrow," I will not sustain my life, O King.
commentary: Vallalar addresses God as the ultimate, non-dual reality, a bliss beyond existence and non-existence. He then brings this high philosophical description into the most immediate, personal crisis: he needs help now. The plea "not today, tomorrow" is a powerful expression of spiritual urgency. It insists that for a soul in deep anguish, divine help cannot be an abstract future promise; it must be a present, immediate reality.

translit: araicelām vaḻaṅkum taṉiara catuniṉ aruḷara ceṉaaṟin taṉaṉpiṉ uraiceyniṉ aruḷmēl uṟṟapē rācai uḷamelām iṭaṅkoṇṭa tentāy varaiceyā mēṉmēl poṅkivāy tatumpi vaḻikiṉṟa teṉvacaṅ kaṭantē iraiceyeṉ āvi taḻaikkaav varuḷai īntaruḷ iṟṟaiip pōtē.
translation: After I came to know that the unique sovereignty that grants all other sovereignties is Your sovereignty of grace, an immense desire for Your celebrated grace has taken over my entire heart, my father. It swells up and up without limit, overflows, and spills out, beyond my control. For my clamoring soul to flourish, bestow that grace this very day, this very moment.
commentary: True power and authority in the world come not from kings or governments, but from God's grace alone. Once this truth dawns, Vallalar says, it ignites an overwhelming desire for that grace. This is a powerful, uncontrollable force that floods the heart and can only be quenched by the immediate experience of the divine.

translit: pōtelām vīṇil pōkkiē mānta puḻuttalaip pulaiyarkaḷ puṇarkkum cūtelām kēṭkun toṟumuṉaip paravum tūyarkaḷ maṉamatu tuḷaṅkit tātelām kalaṅkat taḷarutal aḻakō taṉiaruṭ cōtiyāl anta vātelām tavirttuc cuttacaṉ mārkkam vaḻaṅkuvit taruḷuka viraintē.
translation: Every time one hears the deceptions fabricated by those worm-headed wretches who waste all their time and live in delusion, the minds of the pure ones who praise You waver, their core being is shaken, and they grow weary. Is this right? With Your unique grace-light, put an end to all those false doctrines and swiftly grant that the Suddha Sanmarkkam be established.
commentary: The world is full of false paths and confusing doctrines that can dishearten even sincere spiritual seekers. Vallalar expresses this frustration, asking God if it is right that good people should suffer from this confusion. His plea is for God to use divine light to sweep away all falsehoods and firmly establish the Suddha Sanmarkkam, the Pure True Path for all humanity.

translit: viraintuniṉ aruḷai īntiṭal vēṇṭum viḷampumit taruṇameṉ uḷantāṉ karaintatu kātal perukimēl poṅkik karaielām kaṭantatu kaṇṭāy varainteṉai maṇanta vaḷḷalē ellām vallavā ampala vāṇā tiraintaeṉ uṭampait tiruuṭam pākkit tikaḻvitta cittaṉē civaṉē.
translation: You must quickly grant your grace. At this very moment, my heart has melted; love, surging and welling up, has overflowed all its banks, you see. O generous one who took me in marriage! O all-powerful one! Lord of the Ambalam! O Siddhar, O Sivan, you who transformed my wrinkled body into a sacred body and made it radiant!
commentary: The plea for grace intensifies as love overflows all boundaries of the self. Vallalar uses the intimate metaphor of marriage to describe his relationship with God, the lord of the Ambalam. He reminds God of a past miracle: transforming his aging, wrinkled body into a perfected, radiant one. This is a powerful reminder that God has the ability to grant the seemingly impossible, and a plea to do so again, now.

translit: civantikaḻ karuṇait tiruneṟic cārpum teyvamoṉ ṟēeṉum tiṟamum navantaru nilaikaḷ cutantarat tiyalum naṉmaiyum naraitirai mutalām tuvantuvam tavirttuc cuttamā tiyamuc cukavaṭi vampeṟum pēṟum tavantikaḻ ellām vallacit tiyumnī tantaruḷ taruṇamī teṉakkē.
translation: This is the moment for you to graciously grant me these: adherence to the sacred path of grace that Sivan manifests; the firm knowledge that God is one; the goodness of freely attaining the nine-fold states; the great fortune of obtaining the three blissful forms, starting with the pure form, by removing dualities such as gray hair and wrinkles; and the all-powerful Siddhi that radiates from spiritual discipline.
commentary: After the passionate emotional pleas, this verse is a clear and specific list of the boons Vallalar is asking for. It summarizes his spiritual ambition: to live in grace, to know the oneness of God, to achieve higher states of being, to attain a transformed, deathless body, and to gain the supreme spiritual powers known as Siddhi. He declares that the right time to grant all of this is now.

translit: taruṇamiñ ñāṉṟē cuttacaṉ mārkkat taṉineṟi ulakelām taḻaippak karuṇaiyum civamē poruḷeṉak karutum karuttumuṟ ṟemmaṉōr kaḷippap poruḷniṟai ōṅkat teruḷnilai viḷaṅkap puṇṇiyam poṟpuṟa vayaṅka aruḷnayan taruḷvāy tirucciṟṟam palattē aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ aracē.
translation: This is the moment. My King, ArutPerunJothi in the Thiru Chitrambalam! Desire and grant your grace so that the unique path of Suddha Sanmarkkam may flourish throughout the world, so that people like us may rejoice, gaining the understanding that grace and Sivan are the ultimate substance, so that substance may increase in fullness, the state of clarity may be revealed, and virtue may shine beautifully.
commentary: The focus expands from a personal plea to a universal one. Vallalar asks for grace to make his path, Suddha Sanmarkkam (the pure true path), flourish for all of humanity. He defines the essence of this path as the realization that grace and Sivan (God) are the only true substance. He prays for this understanding to bring clarity, goodness, and joy to everyone in the world, addressing the divine as ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) in the Thiru Chitrambalam (sacred hall of consciousness).

translit: eṉuḷa varaimēl aruḷoḷi ōṅkiṟ ṟiruḷira voḻintatu muḻutum maṉuṟum itaya malarmalarn tatunaṉ maṅkala muḻaṅkukiṉ ṟaṉacīrp poṉiyal viḷakkam polintatu cittip pūvaiyar puṇarntiṭap pōntār coṉṉanal taruṇam aruṭperuñ cōti tulaṅkavan taruḷuka viraintē.
translation: The light of grace has risen over the mountain of my mind; the night of darkness is completely gone. The flower of my abiding heart has blossomed; auspicious sounds resound. The glorious golden lamp shines brightly; the maidens of Siddhi have come to unite with me. This is the good moment I spoke of. ArutPerunJothi, come quickly and bestow your grace, shining radiantly!
commentary: The tone shifts from asking to receiving. The grace he prayed for is arriving, and he describes it with powerful images of light conquering darkness and his heart blooming like a flower. The arrival of the "maidens of Siddhi" is a poetic way of saying that spiritual perfections are now becoming his. He declares that the promised moment has come and invites ArutPerunJothi to manifest fully and quickly.

translit: vantaruḷ purika viraintitu taruṇam māmaṇi maṉṟilē ñāṉa cuntara vaṭivac cōtiyāy viḷaṅkum cuttacaṉ mārkkacaṟ kuruvē tantaruḷ purika varamelām valla taṉiaruṭ cōtiyai eṉatu cintaiyil puṇarppit teṉṉoṭuṅ kalantē ceyvit taruḷkacey vakaiyē.
translation: Come quickly and grant your grace, for this is the moment. O Satguru of Suddha Sanmarkkam, you who shine in the Hall of the Great Gemas the Jothi of a beautiful wisdom-form! Grant me the unique Grace-Light, which is capable of all boons. Cause it to unite within my mind, mingle with me, and graciously make happen whatever needs to be done.
commentary: This final plea is one of complete surrender and union. Addressing God as the Satguru (true guru) of Suddha Sanmarkkam (the pure true path), Vallalar asks for a gift and for the divine Jothi (light) itself to merge with his mind. He asks God to mingle directly with his being and then take over, doing whatever needs to be done. It is a request to become a pure instrument of the divine will.

sections.title: Illumination of the Cit-sabai (Hall of Consciousness)

translit: cōṟu vēṇṭiṉum tukilaṇi mutalām cukaṅkaḷ vēṇṭiṉum cukamalāl cukamām vēṟu vēṇṭiṉum niṉaiaṭain taṉṟi mēvo ṇāteṉum mēlavar uraikkē māṟu vēṇṭilēṉ vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ cāṟu vēṇṭiya poḻilvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: Whether one desires food, pleasures like wearing fine clothes, or that other bliss which transcends pleasure, the great ones say it cannot be attained without reaching you. I do not object to their words; I have come and am standing here. O great Benefactor! I do not know your heart's intent. O King of Vadalur with its festive groves! O singular, great Lord of the Satya Sabai!
commentary: All things we could possibly desire, from basic survival to the highest spiritual bliss, come from God alone. Acknowledging this truth, the speaker has arrived before the divine presence, yet remains uncertain of God's plan. He stands waiting for a sign from the Lord of the Satya Sabai (Hall of Truth).

translit: eñcal iṉṟiya tuyariṉāl iṭarāl iṭukkuṇ ṭaiyaniṉ iṉṉaruḷ virumpi vañca neñciṉēṉ vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ añcal eṉṟeṉai āṭkoḷal vēṇṭum appa niṉṉalāl aṟikilēṉ oṉṟum tañcam eṉṟavark karuḷvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: Troubled by unrelenting sorrow and hardship, and desiring your sweet grace, O Lord, I, with my deceitful heart, have come and am standing here. O great Benefactor! I do not know your heart's intent. You must say, "Do not fear," and take me as your own. O Father, I know nothing other than you! O King of Vadalur, who graces those who declare you their refuge! O singular, great Lord of the Satya Sabai!
commentary: Even with a "deceitful heart" and a deep sense of unworthiness, one can still come before God in a state of suffering and ask for grace. The core of this plea is the request to be accepted despite one's flaws, and for God to offer the comforting words, "Do not fear."

translit: cūḻvi lātuḻal maṉattiṉāl cuḻalum tuṭṭa ṉēṉaruṭ cukapperum patiniṉ vāḻvu vēṇṭiṉēṉ vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ ūḻvi ṭāmaiyil araikkaṇam eṉiṉum uṉṉai viṭṭayal oṉṟumuṟ ṟaṟiyēṉ tāḻvi lātacīr taruvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: I am a wicked one, spun around by a mind that wanders without purpose. Desiring your state of being, O Lord of great, blissful grace, I have come and am standing here. O great Benefactor! I do not know your heart's intent. Because of my unyielding karma, not even for a split second have I ever known anything apart from you. O King of Vadalur, who grants glory that knows no decline! O singular, great Lord of the Satya Sabai!
commentary: The restless, wandering mind is the source of inner turmoil. Yet, the speaker declares that his unyielding karma (ūḻ), the accumulated effect of past actions, has bound him so tightly to God that he has never known anything else. This is a powerful statement of fated dependence on the divine as the only reality.

translit: āṭṭam ōykilā vañcaka maṉattāl alaitan taiyavō ayarntuḷam mayarntu vāṭṭa mōṭivaṇ vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ nāṭṭam niṉpuṭai aṉṟimaṟ ṟaṟiyēṉ nāyi ṉēṉpiḻai poṟuttitutaruṇam tāṭṭa lantaru vāyvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: Tossed about by a deceitful mind whose dance never ceases, alas, I am exhausted and bewildered in heart. With this distress, I have come and am standing here. O great Benefactor! I do not know your heart's intent. I know no focus other than you. Forgive the transgressions of this dog-like one; this is the moment. Grant me the ground of your holy feet, O King of Vadalur! O singular, great Lord of the Satya Sabai!
commentary: The endless activity of the deceitful mind leads to deep exhaustion and despair. At this point of burnout, the only recourse is to surrender. Calling himself a "dog-like one," he begs for forgiveness and asks to be given refuge at God's feet, sensing that this very moment of crisis is the perfect time for grace.

translit: karuṇai oṉṟilāk kalmaṉak kuraṅkāl kāṭu mēṭuḻaṉ ṟuḷammelin tantō varuṇa niṉpuṭai vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ aruṇaṉ eṉṟeṉai akaṟṟiṭu vāyēl aiya vōtuṇai aṟintilaṉ ituvē taruṇam eṟkaruḷ vāyvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉiperum patiyē.
translation: Because of my stone-like monkey-mind, which has no compassion, I have wandered through forests and hills until my heart has grown weary, alas! O my radiant one, I have come and am standing by your side. O great Benefactor! I do not know your heart's intent. If you cast me out as insignificant, O Lord, I know of no other help. This is the moment; grant me grace, O King of Vadalur! O singular, great Lord of the Satya Sabai!
commentary: Vallalar identifies his suffering's source with a classic image: the restless "monkey-mind." He gives it a specific diagnosis, a lack of compassion, which for him is the very quality that connects a soul to God. Having exhausted himself by wandering, he presents himself to God as his one and only hope, with a plea that "this is the moment" for grace.

translit: karaṇa vātaṉai yālmika mayaṅkik kalaṅki ṉēṉoru kaḷaikaṇum aṟiyēṉ maraṇam nīkkiṭa vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ iraṇaṉ eṉṟeṉai eṇṇiṭēl piṟitōr iccai oṉṟilēṉ entainiṉ upaya caraṇam īntaruḷ vāyvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: I was deeply confused and agitated by the affliction of my inner faculties; I knew of no support. I have come to stand here to have death removed. O great Benefactor, I do not know your heart's intent. Do not consider me a stranger. I have no other desire. My Father, grant me your two holy feet. O King of Vadal, sole great Lord of the Satya Sabha!
commentary: The "inner faculties" (karaṇams) are the instruments of the mind: thought, intellect, and ego. When they are in turmoil, they cause great confusion. Vallalar says this inner chaos has driven him to seek the ultimate goal of his path: the removal of death. He asks for the transformation of the physical body into an immortal form of grace, the highest state a being can attain.

translit: tūya neñciṉēṉ aṉṟuniṉ karuṇaic cukamvi ḻaintilēṉ eṉiṉumpoy ulaka māyam vēṇṭilēṉ vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ īya vāyttanal taruṇamī taruḷka entai niṉmalar iṇaiaṭi allāl tāyam oṉṟilēṉ taṉivaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: I am not one with a pure heart; I did not desire the bliss of Your grace. Even so, I do not want the illusion of this false world. I have come and stand here. O great Benefactor, I do not know your heart's intent. This is the perfect moment to give; please grant your grace. My Father, other than your paired lotus feet, I have no inheritance. O sole King of Vadal, sole great Lord of the Satya Sabha!
commentary: Vallalar makes a raw confession: he admits he was not pure-hearted and did not even seek God's bliss in the past. Yet, he has reached a turning point by decisively rejecting the illusions of the world. He claims the divine feet as his only true inheritance (tāyam), framing grace as a birthright for the soul that has nowhere else to turn.

translit: cirattai ātiya cupakuṇam ciṟitum cērnti lēṉaruṭ ceyalilēṉ cākā varattai vēṇṭiṉēṉ vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ karattai nēruḷak kaṭaiyaṉeṉ ṟeṉainī kaivi ṭēloru kaṇamiṉi āṟṟēṉ tarattai īntaruḷ vāyvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: I possess none of the good qualities, beginning with faith; I have no graceful deeds. I begged for the boon of immortality and have come to stand here. O great Benefactor, I do not know your heart's intent. Do not abandon me, thinking I am a lowly one with a heart as hard as stone. I cannot bear this for even one more moment. Grant me a worthy state, O King of Vadal, sole great Lord of the Satya Sabha!
commentary: This verse presents a powerful paradox: while claiming to possess no good qualities, not even basic faith (śraddhā), he asks for the highest possible boon, immortality. This reveals the core of his path, where grace answers desperate need. His cry that he cannot bear this any longer shows he has reached his limit, relying on God's compassion alone to grant him a "worthy state" he cannot create for himself.

translit: patti yañciṟi tuṟṟilēṉ uṉpāl patti oṉṟilēṉ paramaniṉ karuṇai matti yampeṟa vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷalē uṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ etti añcalai eṉaaru ḷāyēl ēḻai yēṉuyir iḻappaṉuṉ āṇai catti yampukaṉ ṟēṉvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: I have not kept even a little discipline; I have no devotion to you at all. O Supreme One, I have come and stand here to receive the very core of your grace. O Benefactor, I do not know your heart's intent. If you do not graciously embrace me and say, "Do not fear," I, this poor one, will lose my life. I swear this on you. I have spoken the truth, O King of Vadal, sole great Lord of the Satya Sabha!
commentary: This is a total surrender, admitting to a complete lack of traditional devotion (bhakti). By claiming to be empty, the speaker creates a space that only divine grace can fill. The oath to die without God's reassurance expresses absolute dependence: life itself is unsustainable without a connection to the divine.

translit: kayavu ceymata karieṉac cerukkum karutti ṉēṉmaṉak kariciṉāl aṭainta mayarvu nīkkiṭa vantuniṟ kiṉṟēṉ vaḷḷa lēuṉṟaṉ maṉakkuṟip paṟiyēṉ uyavu vantaruḷ purintiṭāy eṉileṉ uyir tarittiṭā tuṉaṭi āṇai tayavu ceytaruḷ vāyvaṭal aracē catti yaccapait taṉipperum patiyē.
translation: I am one with an arrogant mind, like a treacherous, rutting elephant. I have come to stand here to have the confusion caused by my heart's impurity removed. O great Benefactor, I do not know your heart's intent. If you do not take pity on me and grant your grace, my life will not endure. I swear this on your feet. Please be merciful and grant your grace, O King of Vadal, sole great Lord of the Satya Sabha!
commentary: The mind is compared to a raging elephant, a classic image for the uncontrolled ego and its powerful, destructive urges. The speaker does not try to tame this beast himself; instead, he brings his inner chaos directly to God, asking for divine help to clear the confusion.

translation: This is the later form of verse 1492.

sections.title: An Appeal to the Sacred Feet

translit: cīriṭam peṟumōr tirucciṟṟam palattē tikaḻtaṉit tantaiyē niṉpāl cēriṭam aṟintē cērntaṉaṉkaruṇai ceytaruḷ ceytiṭat tāḻkkil yāriṭam pukuvēṉ yārtuṇai eṉpēṉ yārkkeṭut teṉkuṟai icaippēṉ pōriṭa muṭiyā tiṉittuya roṭunāṉ poṟukkalēṉ aruḷka:ip pōtē.
translation: O unique Father, shining in the glorious Thiru Chitrambalam! Knowing you are my refuge, I have come to you. If you delay in bestowing your grace, where else can I go? Whom will I call my support? To whom will I take my troubles? I can no longer bear this sorrow that is impossible to fight. Grant your grace this very moment.
commentary: Having decided that God is the only refuge, the speaker arrives with a direct plea. The questions, "where else can I go?" and "to whom will I take my troubles?", emphasize a state of complete reliance on the divine. He asks for grace right now.

translit: pōtutāṉ viraintu pōkiṉṟa taruḷnī purintiṭat tāḻttiyēl aiyō yātutāṉ purivēṉ yāriṭam pukuvēṉ yārkkeṭut teṉkuṟai icaippēṉ tītutāṉ purintēṉ eṉiṉumnī ataṉait tiruvuḷat taṭaittiṭu vāyēl ītutāṉ tantai marapiṉuk kaḻakō eṉṉuyirt tantainī alaiyō.
translation: Time is rushing by. Alas, if you delay in bestowing your grace, what will I do? Where can I go for refuge? To whom will I take my troubles? Even if I have done wrong, if you hold that against me in your sacred mind, is that becoming of a father? Are you not the father of my very life?
commentary: The plea becomes an intimate argument, reminding God of his paternal role. To hold faults against a child, the speaker suggests, is unworthy of a father. By appealing to God as the "father of my very life," he invokes a relationship that he believes should naturally lead to forgiveness and grace.

translit: tantainī alaiyō taṉayaṉnāṉ alaṉō tamiyaṉēṉ taḷarntuḷaṅ kalaṅki entaiyē kuruvē iṟaivaṉē muṟaiyō eṉṟuniṉ ṟōliṭu kiṉṟēṉ cintaiyē aṟiyār pōṉṟirun taṉaiyēl ciṟiyaṉēṉ eṉceykēṉ aiyō cantaiyē pukunta nāyiṉil kaṭaiyēṉ taḷarcciyait tavirppavar yārō.
translation: Are you not the father, and am I not the son? Alone, weary, and with a troubled heart, I stand crying out, "My Father! My Guru! My Lord! Is this just?" If you remain as if you do not even know, alas, what can this lowly one do? I am baser than a dog that has wandered into a marketplace. Who is there to relieve my exhaustion?
commentary: The feeling of being ignored by God is expressed with a powerful image of self-abasement. To be a stray dog in a busy market is to be utterly insignificant, lost, and invisible to everyone. By comparing himself to this, the speaker conveys the depth of his despair and his feeling of being completely alone and unheard by his divine Father and Guru.

translit: yāriṉum kaṭaiyēṉ yāriṉum ciṟiyēṉ eṉpiḻai poṟuppavar yārē pāriṉum peritām poṟumaiyōy nīyē pāviyēṉ piḻaipoṟut tilaiyēl ūriṉum pukuta oṇṇumō pāvi uṭampaivait tulāvavum paṭumō cēriṉum eṉaittāṉ cērttiṭār potuvām teyvattuk kaṭātavaṉ eṉṟē.
translation: I am lowlier than anyone, smaller than anyone. Who else is there to forgive my transgressions? O you whose patience is vaster than the earth, if you do not forgive the faults of this sinner, can I even enter a town? Can I even move about with this sinner's body? Even if I try to associate with people, they will not accept me, saying, "He is unfit for the God who is common to all."
commentary: The speaker feels that God's forgiveness is the very foundation of his ability to exist in the world. Without divine grace, he believes he would become a castaway, rejected even by human society as someone unfit for God. He appeals to God's infinite patience, suggesting that such forgiveness is essential to God's own nature.

translit: aṭātakā riyaṅkaḷ ceytaṉaṉ eṉiṉum appanī aṭiyaṉēṉ taṉṉai viṭātavā ṟaṟintē kaḷittiruk kiṉṟēṉ viṭutiyō viṭṭiṭu vāyēl uṭātaveṟ ṟarainērn tuyaṅkuvēṉ aiyō uṉṉaruḷ aṭaiyanāṉ iṅkē paṭātapā ṭellām paṭṭaṉaṉ antap pāṭelām nīaṟi yāyō.
translation: Although I have done improper things, Father, I have remained joyful, knowing that you will not abandon me, your servant. But will you abandon me? If you do, alas, I will suffer like one shamefully left without even a cloth to wear. To attain your grace here, I have endured every imaginable hardship. Do you not know all about those hardships?
commentary: A subtle shift happens here from despair to a deep, underlying trust. The speaker confesses his wrongdoings but also states his joy, which comes from the certainty that his Father will not abandon him. He reminds God of the immense suffering he has willingly endured specifically to earn this grace, implying that God, being all-knowing, is already aware of his efforts and cannot possibly forsake him now.

translit: aṟintilai yōeṉ pāṭelām eṉṟē aḻaittaṉaṉ appaṉē eṉṉai eṟintiṭā tintat taruṇamē vantāy eṭuttaṇait tañciṭēl makaṉē piṟintiṭēm ciṟitum piṟintiṭēm ulakil peruntiṟal cittikaḷ ellām ciṟantiṭa uṉakkē tantaṉam eṉaeṉ ceṉṉitoṭ ṭuraittaṉai kaḷittē.
translation: "Did you not know all my suffering, Father?" I cried out. You came at this very moment without casting me aside. You took me up, embraced me, and told me, "Do not fear, my son." Then, joyfully touching my head, you said, "We will not be parted, not even slightly. We will not be parted in this world. We have given all the great and mighty siddhis to you alone, for you to excel."
commentary: The appeal is answered in a moment of deep intimacy and grace. God responds with a tender, parental embrace, telling him not to fear. The climax of the poem is this complete reversal: the desperate pleas are met with the promise of permanent union and the granting of all siddhis (supernatural powers), transforming the pain of separation into the joy of reunion.

translit: kaḷitteṉa tuṭampil pukuntaṉai eṉatu karuttilē amarntaṉai kaṉintē teḷittaeṉ aṟivil viḷaṅkiṉai uyiril ciṟappiṉāl kalantaṉai uḷḷam taḷirttiṭac cākā varaṅkoṭut teṉṟum taṭaipaṭāc cittikaḷ ellām aḷittaṉai eṉakkē niṉperuṅ karuṇai aṭiyaṉmēl vaittavā ṟeṉṉē.
translation: Joyfully, you entered my body and settled in my mind. You ripened and shone within my clarified intellect. You mingled with excellence in my very life-force. Making my heart sprout anew, you gave me the boon of immortality. You bestowed upon me all the forever-unobstructed siddhis. What is this great compassion that you have placed upon me, your servant!
commentary: The divine union is described as a complete permeation of Vallalar's being. God enters his body, mind, intellect, and even his life-force, a total indwelling that brings about a physical and spiritual renewal. This fusion grants the ultimate boons: an immortal body and the unobstructed use of all spiritual powers, leaving Vallalar in awe of the compassion he has received.

translit: eṉnikar illā iḻiviṉēṉ taṉaimēl ēṟṟiṉai yāvarum viyappap poṉiyal vaṭivum puraipaṭā uḷamum pūraṇa ñāṉamum poruḷum uṉṉiya ellām vallacit tiyumpēr uvakaiyum utaviṉai eṉakkē taṉṉikar illāt talaivaṉē niṉatu tayavaieṉ eṉṟucāṟ ṟuvaṉē.
translation: You elevated me, a wretch without equal, causing everyone to marvel. You granted me a golden form, a flawless mind, perfect gnosis and spiritual substance. You bestowed on me the siddhi of accomplishing all that I conceive, and great bliss. O matchless Leader! How can I ever describe your grace?
commentary: The transformation from a self-proclaimed "wretch" to a divinely perfected being is so great that it astonishes everyone. Vallalar catalogs the specific gifts of grace: a perfected golden body, a flawless mind, perfect gnosis (divine knowledge), and the ability to manifest whatever he wills. He attributes this entire, miraculous elevation to God's unparalleled grace (dayavu).

translit: cāṟṟuvēṉ eṉatu tantaiyē tāyē caṟkuru nātaṉē eṉṟē pōṟṟuvēṉ tirucciṟ ṟampalat tāṭum pūraṇā eṉa:ula kellām tūṟṟuvēṉ aṉṟi eṉakkunī ceyta tūyapēr utavikku nāṉeṉ āṟṟuvēṉ āvi uṭalporuḷ ellām appaniṉ cutantaram aṉṟō.
translation: I will declare you as, "My father, my mother, my true guru and Lord!" I will praise you throughout the world as, "O Perfect One who dances in Thiru Chitrambalam!" I will proclaim this everywhere. Beyond that, what can I do in return for the pure, immense help you have given me? Are not my soul, body, and possessions all your own property, Father?
commentary: Overwhelmed by such grace, Vallalar’s only possible response is to praise God and proclaim His glory to the world. He then arrives at a core insight of devotional love: he has nothing to offer in return, because his very soul, body, and all that he possesses are not his own. They are the rightful property (sutantaraṁ) of God. True surrender is recognizing this fundamental truth.

translit: cutantaram uṉakkē koṭuttaṉam uṉatu tūyanal uṭampiṉil pukuntēm itantarum uḷattil iruntaṉam uṉaiyē iṉpuṟak kalantaṉam aḻiyāp patantaṉil vāḻka aruṭperuñ cōtip paricupeṟ ṟiṭukapoṟ capaiyum citantaru capaiyum pōṟṟuka eṉṟāy teyvamē vāḻkaniṉ cīrē.
translation: "We have given the right of ownership to you alone. We have entered your pure, good body. We have resided in your benevolent heart. We have mingled with you for your own delight. Live in the imperishable state! Receive the gift of ArutPerunJothi! Praise the Golden Hall and the Hall of Consciousness," you declared. O God, long live your glory!
commentary: God's voice responds, confirming and deepening the previous verse's insight. In a remarkable reversal, God declares that He is giving the "right of ownership" back to Vallalar. Having entered and purified Vallalar's body and heart, God now entrusts this sanctified self back to him, blessing him to live forever in the ultimate state and receive the gift of ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light).
NOTES
Note 257

translit: cēriṭam aṟintu cēr - ātticūṭi.
translation: cēriṭam aṟintu cēr — from the Ātticūṭi. [The line means: know the place, then join it.]

tamil: இப்பாரில் உடல்ஆவி பொருளும்உன்பாற் கொடுத்தேன்மற் றெனக்கென் றிங்கே
எப்பாலும் சுதந்தரம்ஓர் இறையும்இலை அருட்சோதி இயற்கை என்னும்
துப்பாய உடலாதி தருவாயோ இன்னும்எனைச் சோதிப் பாயோ
அப்பாநின் திருவுளத்தை அறியேன்இவ் வடியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: ippāril uṭalāvi poruḷumuṉpāṟ koṭuttēṉmaṟ ṟeṉakkeṉ ṟiṅkē eppālum cutantaramōr iṟaiyumilai aruṭcōti iyaṟkai eṉṉum tuppāya uṭalāti taruvāyō iṉṉumeṉaic cōtip pāyō appāniṉ tiruvuḷattai aṟiyēṉiv vaṭiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: In this world, I have given my body, life, and possessions to you; therefore, I have not the slightest bit of agency for myself here in any way. Will you grant me the pure body and other faculties, which are of the nature of the Grace-Jothi? Or will you continue to test me? Father, I do not know your holy will. What can be accomplished by this humble servant?
commentary: Surrendering to God can lead to a painful period of waiting and uncertainty. Having given away his body, life, and personal will (sutantaram), Vallalar now finds himself in a void, completely dependent on God's next move. He asks if God will grant the transformed "pure body" of Grace-Jothi (supreme light of grace) or continue to test him, expressing the anxious cry of a soul that has done all it can and now must wait.

tamil: என்னேஎம் பெருமான்இங் கின்னும்அணைந் திலன்என்றே ஏங்கி ஏங்கி
மன்னேஎன் மணியேகண் மணியேஎன் வாழ்வேநல் வரத்தாற் பெற்ற
பொன்னேஅற் புதமேசெம் பொருளேஎன் புகலேமெய்ப் போத மேஎன்
அன்னேஎன் அப்பாஎன் றழைத்தலன்றி அடியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: eṉṉēem perumāṉiṅ kiṉṉumaṇain tilaṉeṉṟē ēṅki ēṅki maṉṉēeṉ maṇiyēkaṇ maṇiyēeṉ vāḻvēnal varattāṟ peṟṟa poṉṉēaṟ putamēcem poruḷēeṉ pukalēmeyp pōta mēeṉ aṉṉēeṉ appāeṉ ṟaḻaittalaṉṟi aṭiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: Other than yearning and pining, "Why has my great Lord not yet arrived?", and calling out, "O King, my gem, the apple of my eye, my life! O gold obtained by a great boon, O miracle, O true substance, my refuge, O true awareness! My mother, my father!", what can be accomplished by this humble servant?
commentary: When you have surrendered your own will, the only action left is to express love and longing for God. The intimate list of endearments, from "King" and "gem" to "mother" and "father," shows a deep, personal relationship. This calling out is an act of pure devotion, the only thing a powerless servant can do while waiting for grace.

tamil: பொடிஎடுக்கப் போய்அதனை மறந்துமடி எடுத்தரையில் புனைவேன் சில்லோர்
தடிஎடுக்கக் காணில்அதற் குளங்கலங்கி ஓடுவனித் தரத்தேன் இங்கே
முடிஎடுக்க வல்லேனோ இறைவாநின் அருள்இலதேல் முன்னே வைத்த
அடிஎடுக்க முடியாதே அந்தோஇச் சிறியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: poṭieṭukkap pōyataṉai maṟantumaṭi eṭuttaraiyil puṉaivēṉ cillōr taṭieṭukkak kāṇilataṟ kuḷaṅkalaṅki ōṭuvaṉit tarattēṉ iṅkē muṭieṭukka vallēṉō iṟaivāniṉ aruḷilatēl muṉṉē vaitta aṭieṭukka muṭiyātē antōic ciṟiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: I go to pick up some powder, but forget, and instead take the fold of my garment and wrap it around my waist. If I see a few people pick up sticks, my mind panics and I run away. Being of such a nature, O Lord, could I ever take up the crown here? Without your grace, I cannot even lift the foot I have placed forward. Alas, what can be accomplished by this little one?
commentary: Spiritual progress is impossible without God's grace, because our own nature is weak and flawed. Vallalar uses humble, self-deprecating examples of his own forgetfulness and fear to show his complete inadequacy. The final image, of being unable to even lift one's foot to take the next step without grace, is a powerful metaphor for total spiritual dependence on God.

tamil: பாட்டுவித்தால் பாடுகின்றேன் பணிவித்தால் பணிகின்றேன் பதியே நின்னைக்
கூட்டுவித்தால் கூடுகின்றேன் குழைவித்தால் குழைகின்றேன் குறித்த ஊணை
ஊட்டுவித்தால் உண்கின்றேன் உறக்குவித்தால் உறங்குகின்றேன் உறங்கா தென்றும்
ஆட்டுவித்தால் ஆடுகின்றேன் அந்தோஇச் சிறியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: pāṭṭuvittāl pāṭukiṉṟēṉ paṇivittāl paṇikiṉṟēṉ patiyē niṉṉaik kūṭṭuvittāl kūṭukiṉṟēṉ kuḻaivittāl kuḻaikiṉṟēṉ kuṟitta ūṇai ūṭṭuvittāl uṇkiṉṟēṉ uṟakkuvittāl uṟaṅkukiṉṟēṉ uṟaṅkā teṉṟum āṭṭuvittāl āṭukiṉṟēṉ antōic ciṟiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: If you make me sing, I sing. If you make me serve, I serve. O Master, if you make me unite with you, I unite. If you make me melt, I melt. If you feed me the appointed meal, I eat. If you make me sleep, I sleep. If you make me dance eternally without sleep, I dance. Alas, what can be accomplished by this little one?
commentary: The highest spiritual state is one of total surrender, where one becomes a perfect instrument of the divine will. Vallalar declares that his every action, from singing to sleeping to dancing in ecstasy, is not his own doing. It happens only because God is the one moving through him, and his role is simply to allow it.

tamil: உடுப்பவனும் உண்பவனும் நானேஎன் னவும்நாணம் உறுவ தெந்தாய்
தடுப்பவனும் தடைதீர்த்துக் கொடுப்பவனும் பிறப்பிறப்புத் தன்னை நீக்கி
எடுப்பவனும் காப்பவனும் இன்பஅனு பவஉருவாய் என்னுள் ஓங்கி
அடுப்பவனும் நீஎன்றால் அந்தோஇச் சிறியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: uṭuppavaṉum uṇpavaṉum nāṉēeṉ ṉavumnāṇam uṟuva tentāy taṭuppavaṉum taṭaitīrttuk koṭuppavaṉum piṟappiṟapput taṉṉai nīkki eṭuppavaṉum kāppavaṉum iṉpaaṉu pava:uruvāy eṉṉuḷ ōṅki aṭuppavaṉum nīeṉṟāl antōic ciṟiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: O my Father, I feel ashamed even to say, "I am the one who dresses" and "I am the one who eats." If you are the one who obstructs and the one who removes obstacles to bestow things; the one who does away with birth and death, who uplifts and protects; the one who, as the very form of blissful experience, swells up within me and draws close, then alas, what can be accomplished by this little one?
commentary: This verse deepens the idea of surrender into a radical loss of self. Vallalar feels ashamed to even say "I eat" or "I dress," because he recognizes that God is the true actor behind every event in his life. God is both the obstacle and the one who clears the path, the one who brings blissful experience, and the one who finally ends the cycle of birth and death. In this state, the personal "I" dissolves.

tamil: நோவதின்று புதிதன்றே என்றும்உள தால்இந்த நோவை நீக்கி
ஈவதுமன் றிடைநடிப்போய் நின்னாலே ஆகும்மற்றை இறைவ ராலே
translit: cāvateṉṟum piṟappateṉṟum cāṟṟukiṉṟaperumpāvam taṉṉaieṇṇi nōvatiṉṟu putitaṉṟē eṉṟumuḷa tālinta nōvai nīkki īvatumaṉ ṟiṭainaṭippōy niṉṉālē ākummaṟṟai iṟaiva rālē āvatoṉṟum illaieṉṟāl antōic ciṟiyēṉāl āvateṉṉē.
translation: The suffering from thinking about the great sin they call 'dying' and 'being born' is not new; it has always existed. O you who dance in the central space, only you can remove this pain and grant deliverance. If this can be done by you and not by any other gods, alas, what can this lowly one accomplish?
commentary: The endless cycle of birth and death is presented as the greatest source of suffering. Vallalar states that only God, the supreme being dancing at the center of existence, can end this cycle. No other power or deity can grant this ultimate release. This points to a core teaching: liberation from suffering is possible only through the grace of the one, absolute reality.

tamil: நசைத்திடுபே ரருட்செயலால் அசைவதன்றி ஐந்தொழில்செய் நாத ராலும்
அசைத்திடற்கு முடியாதேல் அந்தோஇச் சிறியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: icaittiṭavumniṉaittiṭavumperitaritām taṉittalaimaiiṟaivā uṉṟaṉ nacaittiṭupē raruṭceyalāl acaivataṉṟi aintoḻilcey nāta rālum tacaittiṭupuṉ turumpiṉaiyum akaṅkarittut taṅkaḷcutan tarattāliṅkē acaittiṭaṟku muṭiyātēl antōic ciṟiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: O supreme Lord, unique leader, so very difficult to speak of or even conceive! Things move only by the action of your desired great grace. If even the masters who perform the five cosmic functions cannot, out of ego and by their own power, move so much as a flimsy blade of grass here, alas, what can this lowly one accomplish?
commentary: God's power is absolute, and nothing in the universe happens without it. Vallalar states that not even a blade of grass can move unless moved by divine grace. Even the great cosmic powers responsible for creation and destruction are helpless to act on their own. This illustrates the total sovereignty of God's will and the futility of any action driven by ego.

tamil: கல்லாய மனத்தையும்ஓர் கணத்தினிலே கனிவித்துக் கருணை யாலே
பல்லாரும் அதிசயிக்கப் பக்குவந்தத் தருட்பதமும் பாலிக் கின்றோய்
எல்லாஞ்செய் வல்லோய்சிற் றம்பலத்தே ஆடல்இடு கின்றோய் நின்னால்
அல்லால்ஒன் றாகாதேல் அந்தோஇச் சிறியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: kallāya maṉattaiyumōr kaṇattiṉilē kaṉivittuk karuṇai yālē pallārum aticayikkap pakkuvantat taruṭpatamum pālik kiṉṟōy ellāñcey vallōyciṟ ṟampalattē āṭaliṭu kiṉṟōy niṉṉāl allāloṉ ṟākātēl antōic ciṟiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: You who can make even a stone-like mind ripen in a single moment with your compassion, granting a mature state of grace to the astonishment of all! O all-powerful one who can do everything, O you who dance in the Cit-Ambalam! If nothing can be accomplished except by you, alas, what can this lowly one accomplish?
commentary: God's power is so immense that it can instantly transform a hardened, unfeeling mind into one that is ripe for grace. This change is a miracle given freely through compassion. Vallalar addresses God as the one who dances in the Cit-Ambalam (the inner space of pure consciousness), locating this transformation within the self. Since all power for change belongs to God, he again concludes with his own powerlessness.

tamil: கரைசேரப் புரிந்தாலும் கடையேன்செய் குற்றமெலாம் கருதி மாயைத்
திரைசேரப் புரிந்தாலும் திருவுளமே துணைஎனநான் சிந்தித் திங்கே
உரைசேர இருத்தல்அன்றி உடையாய்என் உறவேஎன் உயிரே என்றன்
அரைசேஎன் அம்மேஎன் அப்பாஇச் சிறியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: karaicērap purintālum kaṭaiyēṉcey kuṟṟamelām karuti māyait tiraicērap purintālum tiruvuḷamē tuṇaieṉanāṉ cintit tiṅkē uraicēra iruttalaṉṟi uṭaiyāyeṉ uṟavēeṉ uyirē eṉṟaṉ araicēeṉ ammēeṉ appāic ciṟiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: Whether you choose to bring me to the shore or, considering all the faults of this lowly one, make me join the screen of Māyā, I can only remain here, thinking that your divine will is my only support. O my master, my relation, my life, my king, my mother, my father! Alas, what can this lowly one accomplish?
commentary: The ultimate state of surrender is to accept whatever God decides. Whether he is granted liberation ("brought to the shore") or left in the world of illusion, known as Māyā, his only response is to trust in the divine will. This radical acceptance is born of deep intimacy, as he calls on God with every possible term of love and relationship: master, relation, life, king, mother, and father.

tamil: இன்பேநன் றருளிஅருள் இயற்கையிலே வைத்தாலும் இங்கே என்னைத்
துன்பேசெய் வித்தாலும் என்செய்வேன் நின்னருளே துணைஎன் றந்தோ
என்பேதை மனமடங்கி இருப்பதன்றி எல்லாங்கண் டிருக்கும் என்றன்
அன்பேஎன் அம்மேஎன் அப்பாஇச் சிறியேனால் ஆவ தென்னே.
translit: iṉpēnaṉ ṟaruḷiaruḷ iyaṟkaiyilē vaittālum iṅkē eṉṉait tuṉpēcey vittālum eṉceyvēṉ niṉṉaruḷē tuṇaieṉ ṟantō eṉpētai maṉamaṭaṅki iruppataṉṟi ellāṅkaṇ ṭirukkum eṉṟaṉ aṉpēeṉ ammēeṉ appāic ciṟiyēṉāl āva teṉṉē.
translation: Whether you graciously grant me supreme bliss and keep me in a state of natural grace, or you make me suffer here, my foolish mind can only subside and remain still, thinking, "Alas, your grace is my only support." O my love who sees all, my mother, my father, what can this lowly one accomplish?
commentary: Faced with the absolute power of God's will, the only true response is to quiet the mind. Whether life brings supreme bliss or deep suffering, the mind must learn to stop reacting and simply rest in the trust that divine grace is its only real support. The verse ends by addressing God as "my love who sees all," affirming that this act of surrender is witnessed by a conscious, loving presence.

sections.title: Hindrance to the Experience of Non-dual Bliss

translit: tiruttakupoṉ ṉampalattē tirunaṭañcey taruḷum tiruvaṭikaḷ aṭicciṟiyēṉ ceṉṉimicai varumō uruttakunā ṉilattiṭainīḷ malattaṭaipōy ñāṉa uruppaṭivam aṭaivēṉō oṉṟiraṇṭeṉ ṉāta poruttamuṟu cuttacivā ṉantaveḷḷam tatumpip poṅkiakam puṟaṅkāṇā teṅkuniṟain tiṭumō aruttakumav veḷḷattē nāṉmūḻki nāṉpōy atuvākap peṟuvēṉō aṟintilaṉmēl viḷaivē.
translation: Will the sacred feet that dance in the worthy Golden Hall come to rest on the head of this lowly servant? Will the long barrier of malam on this earth fall away, and will I take on the form of true knowledge? Will the fitting flood of pure Sivananda, which is neither one nor two, swell and rise and fill everything within, leaving no outside? Will I sink into that rare flood, lose myself, and become That? I do not know what will follow.
commentary: A chain of questions from someone who can see the goal and cannot yet touch it. The flood of Sivananda fills the inner world until nothing is left outside it; "neither one nor two" names a union beyond counting. Vallalar asks to drown in it and become That. Then he stops: he does not know what comes next.

translit: karaṇamelām karaintataṉik karaikāṇpa tuḷatō karaikaṇṭa poḻuteṉaiyuṅ kaṇṭuteḷi vēṉō araṇamelām kaṭantatiru varuḷveḷinēr paṭumō avveḷikkuḷ āṉanta aṉupavantāṉ uṟumō maraṇamelām tavirntuciva mayamāki niṟaital vāyttiṭumō mūlamala vātaṉaiyum pōmō caraṇamelām taramaṉṟil tirunaṭañcey perumāṉ taṉatutiru vuḷametuvō caṟṟumaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: Will I see the farther shore, all my inner faculties dissolved? When I see that shore, will I also see my true self and attain clarity? Will I encounter the space of sacred grace that transcends all barriers? Within that space, will I truly attain the experience of bliss? Will I be granted the state of avoiding all death, becoming pervaded by Siva, and attaining fullness? Will the affliction of the root malam also depart? Of the Great Lord who performs the sacred dance in the Hall, his feet a refuge for all, I do not know His sacred will in the slightest.
commentary: The devotee wonders if he will achieve the key signs of liberation: the dissolution of the mind, self-realization, and deathlessness. The "inner faculties" (karanam) are the tools of the ordinary mind, which must dissolve to see reality clearly. He longs to be "pervaded by Siva" (sivamayam), a state of fullness that conquers death, but this can only happen if the "root malam," the primordial impurity, is finally removed. He has no way of knowing if this will be granted.

translit: nātāntat tiruvīti naṭantukaṭap pēṉō ñāṉaveḷi naṭuiṉpa naṭantaricip pēṉō pōtāntat tiruvaṭieṉ ceṉṉiporun tiṭumō putumaiyaṟac civapōkam poṅkiniṟain tiṭumō vētānta cittānta camaracamum varumō veṟuveḷiyil cuttaciva veḷimayantāṉ uṟumō pātānta varainīṟu maṇakkamaṉṟil āṭum paramartiru vuḷametuvō paramaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: Will I walk and cross the sacred street of Nādānta? Will I witness the blissful dance in the midst of the space of gnosis? Will the sacred feet of Bodhānta come to rest upon my head? Will the bliss of Siva well up and fill me until it is no longer new? Will the harmonious convergence of Vedanta and Siddhanta come to pass? In the sheer Void, will I attain the state of being pervaded by the space of pure Siva? I simply do not know the sacred will of the Supreme One, who dances in the Hall with the sacred ash fragrant from the soles of His feet to His crown.
commentary: Here, the devotee asks if he will attain the highest mystical states, which are beyond sound and intellect. Nādānta is the state "beyond sound," a level of consciousness that transcends the subtle vibrations of creation, while Bodhānta is the state "beyond intellect." His hope to see the "harmonious convergence" (samarasam) of Vedanta and Siddhanta shows that true realization is an experience that unifies and transcends them all.

translit: citamparattē āṉanta cittartiru naṭantāṉ ciṟitaṟinta paṭiiṉṉum muḻutumaṟi vēṉō patampeṟattēm paḻampiḻintu pālumnaṟum pākum pacuneyyum kalantateṉap pāṭimakiḻ vēṉō nitamparavi āṉanta nittirainīṅ kāta nittarpaṇi purintiṉpa cittipeṟu vēṉō matamparavu malaiccerukkil ciṟantaciṟi yēṉnāṉ vaḷḷalkuru nātartiru vuḷḷamaṟi yēṉē.
translation: Having known a little of the sacred dance of the Ananda Siddha in Chidambaram, will I come to know it in its entirety? Having attained the perfect state, will I sing and rejoice that it is like ripe, sweet fruit, juiced and mixed with milk, fragrant syrup, and fresh ghee? Will I serve the eternal ones who, perpetually praised, never stir from their blissful sleep, and thus attain the perfection of bliss? I, this lowly one who excels only in the mountain-like arrogance of divisive doctrines, do not know the sacred will of my generous Guru-Lord.
commentary: Having had a small taste of divine bliss, he now yearns for the full, permanent experience. The Ananda Siddha is the "Perfected Being of Bliss," another name for Siva. Vallalar contrasts the indescribable sweetness of this state with his own feeling of being stuck in the "arrogance of divisive doctrines" (madam), the intellectual pride that creates separation. The memory of bliss makes his current, ego-bound state feel even more painful.

translit: kaḷakkamaṟap potunaṭamnāṉ kaṇṭukoṇṭa taruṇam kaṭaicciṟiyēṉ uḷampūttuk kāyttatoru kāytāṉ viḷakkamuṟap paḻuttiṭumō vempiutirn tiṭumō vempātu paḻukkiṉumeṉ karattilakap paṭumō koḷakkarutu malamāyaik kuraṅkukavarn tiṭumō kuraṅkukava rāteṉatu kuṟippilakap paṭiṉum tuḷakkamaṟa uṇṇuvaṉō toṇṭaivikkik koḷumō jōtitiru vuḷametuvō ētumaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: At the moment I witnessed the Common Dance without agitation, a fruit blossomed and formed in the mind of this lowliest servant. Will that fruit ripen to perfection, or will it wither and fall? Even if it ripens without withering, will it land in my hand? Or will the monkey of malam and māyā, intent on grabbing it, snatch it away? Even if the monkey does not snatch it and it comes into my possession, will I eat it without trembling, or will it get stuck in my throat and choke me? What the sacred will of the Jothi is, I do not know at all.
commentary: Using a powerful metaphor, Vallalar expresses deep anxiety over whether his spiritual potential will come to fruition. A moment of grace planted a seed, the "fruit," but he fears it will be lost at the last moment. The "monkey" represents the restless, grasping nature of the ego, driven by innate impurity (malam) and illusion (māyā). Even if he gets the fruit of liberation, he worries he might not be able to "swallow" it, meaning he might not be ready to fully integrate such an experience. Everything depends on the will of the Jothi, the supreme Light of Grace.

translit: tiruppotuvil tirunaṭamnāṉ ceṉṟukaṇṭa taruṇam cittieṉum peṇṇaraci ettieṉkai piṭittāḷ karuppaṟiyā teṉaiataṉmuṉ kalantaputti eṉumōr kārikaitāṉ kaṇṭaḷavil kaṉintumakiḻn tiṭumō viruppamuṟā teṉaimuṉintu viṭuttiṭumō nēyam viḷaintiṭumō ivarkkunitam caṇṭaiviḷain tiṭumō taruppotuvil iruvarkkum cantatiuṇ ṭāmō taṭaipaṭumō tiruvuḷantāṉ caṟṟumaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: The moment I went and saw the sacred dance in the sacred common space, the queen named Siddhi took me by surprise and grasped my hand. Upon seeing this, will the maiden named Buddhi, who had united with me before this without my realizing it, grow tender and rejoice? Or will she, displeased, become angry with me and leave? Will affection grow between them, or will a fight break out between them every day? In the bounteous common space, will they both have offspring, or will it be obstructed? I do not know the sacred will at all.
commentary: This verse portrays the inner conflict that can follow a spiritual awakening. Vallalar imagines his newfound spiritual attainment, Siddhi (divine accomplishment), as a queen who has suddenly taken his hand. He then worries how his old way of being, his intellect or Buddhi, will react to this newcomer. By personifying these inner states as two women, he vividly expresses the tension between the rational mind and a transcendent experience, wondering if they can coexist peacefully or if their conflict will obstruct his path.

translit: āṉanta naṭampotuvil kaṇṭataru ṇattē arumaruntoṉ ṟeṉkaruttil aṭaintamarnta tatutāṉ kāṉanta matattālē kāramaṟai paṭumō kaṭuṅkāra mākieṉṟaṉ karuttiluṟain tiṭumō ūṉanta maṟakkoḷumpō tiṉikkaracam tarumō uṇakkacantu kumaṭṭietir eṭuttiṭanērn tiṭumō nāṉanta uḷavaṟintu piṟarkkīya varumō nallatiru vuḷametuvō vallataṟin tilaṉē.
translation: At the moment I saw the dance of bliss in the common space, a rare medicine entered and settled in my mind. Will its potency be veiled by the deep intoxication of bliss, or will it become extremely potent and remain firm in my mind? When I take it to remove my flaws, will it provide a sweet taste, or will it be dry and bitter, causing nausea and making me bring it back up? Will I be able to know its secret and give it to others? I am unable to know what the good sacred will is.
commentary: The experience of the divine dance is now seen as a potent medicine for the soul. Yet, its effects are uncertain. He wonders if the medicine will be sweet and healing or bitter and hard to endure. More than just his own state, he worries whether he will understand this spiritual cure well enough to be able to share it with others. This reveals a key aspect of his mission: personal realization is not the final goal if it cannot be used to help humanity.

translit: tāykoṇṭa tiruppotuvil eṅkaḷkuru nātaṉ cannitipōy varaviṭutta taṉikkaraṇap pūvai kāykoṇṭu vantiṭumō paḻaṅkoṇṭu varumō kaṉintapaḻaṅ koṇṭuvaruṅ kālataṉai matamām pēykoṇṭu pōyviṭumō pilattiṭaivīḻn tiṭumō piṉpaṭumō muṉpaṭumō piṇaṅkioḷit tiṭumō vāykoṇṭu veṉṟiṭumō tōṟṟiṭumō eṉṉai maṟantiṭumō tiruvuḷattiṉ vaṇṇamaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: I sent the unique maiden, Karana to go to the sanctum of our Guru-Lord in the sacred common space held by the Mother and return. Will she come back with an unripe fruit, or will she bring a ripe fruit? When she brings the ripened fruit, will the demon of arrogance seize it and take it away? Will it fall into a chasm? Will she be delayed, or will she come quickly? Will she become difficult and hide? Will she be victorious or be defeated? Will she forget me? I do not know the nature of the sacred will.
commentary: Here, Vallalar portrays his own inner faculties, the Karana (the instruments of consciousness like mind and intellect), as a maiden sent on a quest to the heart of the divine. He waits anxiously, wondering what she will bring back: an incomplete experience (an unripe fruit) or full attainment (a ripe one). He fears that even if she succeeds, his own arrogance might steal the prize. This allegory shows the spiritual path as an active sending of one's own consciousness toward God, while acknowledging that the final result remains entirely in God's hands.

translit: tīṭṭumaṇip potunaṭañcey tiruvaṭikaṇ ṭēttac celkiṉṟēṉ ciṟiyēṉmuṉ ceṉṟavaḻi aṟiyēṉ kāṭṭuvaḻi kiṭaittiṭumō nāṭṭuvaḻi tarumō kāliḷaippuk kaṇṭiṭumō kāṇātō kaḷippām mēṭṭiṉiṭai viṭuttiṭumō paḷḷattē viṭumō vivēkameṉum tuṇaiyuṟumō vēṭarpayam uṟumō īṭṭutiru vaṭiccamukam kāṇavumnērn tiṭumō eppaṭiyō tiruvuḷantāṉ ētumaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: I, a small man, am going to see and praise the sacred feet that perform the dance in the common space of polished gems, but I do not know the path taken before. Will I find a forest path, or will it give me a path through settled lands? Will my legs grow weary, or will they not? Will it leave me on a joyful high ground, or will it drop me into a low place? Will I gain the companion called Viveka, or will I be afflicted by the fear of hunters? Will I even get to see the sacred presence of the sought-after holy feet? I do not know at all what the sacred will may be.
commentary: The spiritual path is depicted as travel into unknown territory. Vallalar feels like a traveler setting out with no map, unsure if the path will be easy or difficult, elevating or discouraging. He hopes for the guidance of Viveka (spiritual discernment) as a companion to protect him from the dangers along the way. The verse captures the vulnerability and uncertainty of the seeker who has left familiar ground behind, relying completely on faith and the grace of the divine will.

translit: ñāṉamaṇip potunaṭañcey tiruvaṭikaṇ ṭiṭavē naṭakkiṉṟēṉ antōmuṉ naṭantavaḻi aṟiyēṉ ūṉamikum āṇavamām pāvietirp paṭumō uṭaimaielām paṟittiṭumō naṭaimelintu pōmō īṉamuṟum akaṅkārap pulikuṟukkē varumō iccaieṉum irākkatappēy eṉaippiṭittuk koḷumō āṉamalat taṭainīkka aruṭṭuṇaitāṉ uṟumō aiyartiru vuḷametuvō yātumaṟin tilaṉē.
translation: I am walking to see the sacred feet that perform the dance in the common space of the gem of wisdom. Alas, I do not know the path walked before. Will the flawed sinner that is āṇavam confront me? Will it rob me of all my possessions? Will my steps become feeble? Will the tiger of base ahangkāram cross my path? Will the demonic ghost of iccai seize me? To remove the obstacle of the malas will I obtain the help of grace? I do not know at all what the Lord's sacred will is.
commentary: The greatest obstacles on the spiritual path are our own inner psychological forces. Vallalar names these enemies: āṇavam (the deep-rooted sense of 'I'), ahangkāram (active egoism and pride), and iccai (worldly desire). He imagines them as predators and ghosts that can ambush a traveler, and knows the only real defense against these powerful malas (impurities) is the help of divine grace.

translit: tirukkatavam tiṟavāyō tiraikaḷelām tavirttē tiruvaruḷām peruñcōtit tiruurukkāṭ ṭāyō urukkiamu tūṟṟeṭuttē uṭampuyirō ṭuḷamum oḷimayamē ākkuṟamey uṇarcciaru ḷāyō karukkarutāt taṉivaṭivōy niṉṉaieṉṉuṭ kalantē kaṅkulpakal iṉṟieṉṟum kaḷittiṭaccey yāyō cerukkarutā tavarkkaruḷum cittipurat taracē cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Won't you open the sacred door, removing all the veils? Won't you show me your sacred form, the Great Light of sacred grace? Melting me and pouring out the nectar of immortality, won't you grant me the true awareness that makes my body, life, and mind entirely a form of light? O unique form that was never conceived in a womb, won't you merge into me and make me rejoice forever, without night or day? O King of Cittipuram who grants grace to those without pride, O Crest-jewel of Consciousness, my Lord of the Sacred Dance!
commentary: This is a prayer for total transformation, more than a glimpse of the divine. The "sacred door" is the barrier of ignorance separating the soul from God. Vallalar asks God to remove all "veils" and reveal His true nature as a Great Light. This light is meant to enter and melt the seeker, turning body, life, and mind into its own luminous substance.

translit: maṇikkatavam tiṟavāyō maṟaippaiyelām tavirttē māṟṟaṟiyāp poṉṉēniṉ vaṭivatukāṭ ṭāyō kaṇikkaṟiyāp perunilaiyil eṉṉoṭunī kalantē karaikaṭanta perumpōkam kaṇṭiṭaccey yāyō taṇikkaṟiyāk kātalmikap perukukiṉṟa taracē tāṅkamuṭi yātiṉieṉ taṉittalaimaip patiyē tiṇikkalaiyā tiyaellām paṇikkavalla civamē cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Won't you open the jeweled door, removing all concealment? O gold of unknowable purity, won't you show me your form? Merging with me in a great state that is beyond measure, won't you make me experience boundless, great bliss? O King, my love for you knows no quenching and is overflowing! My sole, supreme Lord, I can no longer bear it! O Sivam who can command all the dense arts to serve, O Crest-jewel of Consciousness, my Lord of the Sacred Dance!
commentary: The plea intensifies, expressing an overwhelming love that can no longer be contained. The experience sought is a complete merging with God that results in a "boundless, great bliss" far beyond ordinary happiness. This verse captures the urgency and pain of separation when a soul feels itself on the very edge of divine union.

translit: uraikaṭanta tiruvaruṭpē roḷivaṭivaik kalantē uvaṭṭāta perumpōkam ōṅkiyuṟum poruṭṭē iraikaṭanteṉ uḷḷakattē eḻuntupoṅkit tatumpi eṉkātal peruveḷḷam eṉṉaimuṟṟum viḻuṅkik karaikaṭantu pōṉatiṉit tāṅkamuṭi yātu kaṇṭukoḷvāy nīyēeṉ karuttiṉvaṇṇam aracē tiraikaṭanta kurumaṇiyē civañāṉa maṇiyē cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: The great flood of my love, which seeks to merge with the great radiant form of sacred grace beyond words and attain ever-growing, non-satiating bliss, has risen and surged within my heart. It has overflowed its banks, completely swallowed me, and crossed all shores. I can no longer bear it. O King, you yourself must see the state of my mind! O Guru-jewel who has crossed the veils, O Jewel of Siva-Jnana (divine knowledge), O Crest-jewel of Consciousness, my Lord of the Sacred Dance!
commentary: Here, the devotee feels completely consumed by divine love. It is no longer a feeling they have; it is a force that has taken them over, a "great flood" that has "completely swallowed" their individual self. This loss of personal identity in the current of love is the final stage before union, and the call for God to "see the state of my mind" is a cry of loving surrender.

translit: uṉpuṭaināṉ piṟarpōlē uṭukkaviḻain tēṉō uṇṇaviḻain tēṉōvē ṟuṭaimaiviḻain tēṉō aṉpuṭaiyāy eṉṟaṉainī aṇaintiṭavē viḻaintēṉ antōeṉ ācaiveḷḷam aṇaikaṭanta taracē eṉpuṭaivan taṇaikaeṉa iyampukiṉṟēṉ ulakōr eṉcoliṉum collukaeṉ ilaccaielām oḻittēṉ teṉpuṭaiyōr mukanōkkit tiruppotuniṟ kiṉṟōy cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: At your side, did I desire to dress like others? Did I desire to eat? Did I desire other possessions? O loving one, I desired only that you embrace me. Alas, O King, the flood of my desire has breached its dam! I am saying, "Come to my side and embrace me." Let the people of the world say whatever they will; I have cast off all my shame. O you who stand in the sacred hall facing those in the south, O Crest-jewel of Consciousness, my Lord of the Sacred Dance!
commentary: The desire for God is pure and absolute, set apart from any worldly want for food, clothing, or possessions. The only longing is for an intimate embrace from the divine. This desire is so powerful that all sense of personal shame and fear of what others might say is cast aside. All that matters is calling out for this union, publicly and without reservation.

translit: iṟantiṟantē iḷaittatelām pōtuminta uṭampē iyaṟkaiuṭam pākaaruḷ iṉṉamutam aḷitteṉ puṟantaḻuvi akampuṇarntē kalantukoṇṭen nāḷum pūraṇamām civapōkam poṅkiyiṭa viḻaintēṉ piṟantiṟantu pōykkatiyaip peṟaniṉaintē mānta pētaiyarpōl eṉainiṉaiyēl periyatiruk katavam tiṟantaruḷi aṇaintiṭuvāy ciṟcapaivāḻ aracē cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Enough of all this weariness from dying again and again. I have longed for the perfect bliss of Sivam to well up. I have longed for you to grant me the sweet nectar of grace to make this very body an eternal, natural one. I have longed for you to embrace me externally, unite with me internally, and merge with me completely. Do not think of me as one of those foolish people who seek liberation by repeatedly being born and dying. Graciously open the great sacred door and embrace me, O King who lives in the Chit Sabhai, O Crest-jewel of Consciousness, my Lord of the Sacred Dance.
commentary: A clear distinction is made from the common spiritual goal of achieving a better state after death. The endless cycle of dying and being reborn is seen as exhausting, not a path forward. The true aim is to transform this very body into an eternal, divine form through the nectar of grace. He asks God not to mistake him for those seeking a reward after death, but to open the door to the Chit Sabhai (the Hall of Consciousness) and grant this immortal, embodied union now.

translit: poyyuṭaiyār viḻaikiṉṟa puṇarcciviḻain tēṉō pūṇaviḻain tēṉōvāṉ kāṇaviḻain tēṉō meyyuṭaiyāy eṉṉoṭunī viḷaiyāṭa viḻaintēṉ viḷaiyāṭṭeṉ patuñāṉam viḷaiyumviḷai yāṭṭē paiyuṭaippām paṉaiyaroṭum āṭukiṉṟōy eṉatu paṇpaṟintē naṇpuvaitta paṇpuṭaiyōy iṉṉē ceyyuṭaieṉ ṉoṭukūṭi āṭaeḻun taruḷvāy cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Did I desire the union that false people crave? Did I desire to wear jewels, or desire to see the heavens? O Possessor of Truth, I desired for you to play with me. That play is the very game where wisdom flourishes. O You who dance with the hooded snake! O Gracious One who, knowing my nature, befriended me! Please rise and come graciously now to join and play with me, your possession. O Crest-Jewel of Siddhas, my Lord of the sacred dance!
commentary: The union sought is described as a "play" with God, setting it apart from false or fleeting worldly unions. This is no idle game; it is the very activity through which divine wisdom flourishes. The relationship is deeply personal, founded on God's grace in "befriending" the soul. The plea is for the "Crest-Jewel of Siddhas," or perfected masters, to come and engage in this intimate, wisdom-giving play.

translit: kūṟukiṉṟa camayamelām mataṅkaḷelām piṭittuk kūvukiṉṟār palaṉoṉṟum koṇṭaṟiyār vīṇē nīṟukiṉṟār maṇṇāki nāṟukiṉṟār avarpōl nīṭulakil aḻintuviṭa niṉaittēṉō nilaimēl ēṟukiṉṟa tiṟamviḻaintēṉ ēṟṟuvittāy aṅkē ilaṅkutiruk katavutiṟan tiṉṉamutam aḷittē tēṟukiṉṟa meyññāṉa cittiuṟap purivāy cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Clinging to all the proclaimed religions and creeds, people just shout, having never gained a single benefit from them. In vain, they turn to ash, become dust, and stink. Did I intend to perish in this vast world like them? I desired the ability to ascend to the higher state, and you made me ascend. There, you opened the shining, sacred door and gave me sweet ambrosia. Grant me the attainment of the Siddhi of true wisdom that brings clarity. O Crest-Jewel of Siddhas, my Lord of the sacred dance!
commentary: Vallalar says plainly that those who cling to the religions and creeds they proclaim cry out in vain and gain nothing: they die, turn to ash and dust, and rot. He did not mean to perish like them. He sought the power to rise to the higher state, and God raised him there, opened the shining door and gave him sweet ambrosia. Now he asks for the Siddhi of true wisdom.

translit: vētaneṟi ākamattiṉ neṟipavurā ṇaṅkaḷ viḷampuneṟi itikācam vitittaneṟi muḻutum ōtukiṉṟa cūtaṉaittum uḷavaṉaittum kāṭṭi uḷḷataṉai uḷḷapaṭi uṇara:urait taṉaiyē ētamaṟa uṇarntaṉaṉvīṇ pōtukaḻip pataṟkōr eḷḷaḷavum eṇṇamilēṉ eṉṉoṭunī puṇarntē tītaṟavē aṉaittumvalla cittāṭal purivāy cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: The path of the Vedas, the path of the Agamas, the path the Puranas proclaim, the path the Itihasas prescribe: you revealed all of it to be nothing but proclaimed deceit and trickery. You spoke so I could realize the inner reality just as it is. I have realized it without error. I do not have even a sesame seed's worth of an intention to waste time. Unite with me and, free from all evil, perform your all-powerful play of Siddhi. O Crest-Jewel of Siddhas, my Lord of the sacred dance!
commentary: God has revealed a shocking truth to Vallalar: even the most revered scriptures, such as the Vedas and Agamas, are a form of deception that hides the truth. The real path is to bypass these texts and realize the simple, inner reality directly, just as it is. Having understood this, Vallalar has no intention of wasting even a moment on anything else.

translit: kalaiyuraitta kaṟpaṉaiyē nilaieṉakkoṇ ṭāṭum kaṇmūṭi vaḻakkamelām maṇmūṭip pōka malaivaṟucaṉ mārkkamoṉṟē nilaipeṟamey ulakam vāḻntōṅkak karutiyaruḷ vaḻaṅkiṉaieṉ taṉakkē ulaivaṟumip poḻutēnal taruṇameṉa nīyē uṇarttiṉaivan taṇaintaruḷvāy uṇmaiurait tavaṉē cilainikarvaṉ maṉaṅkaraittut tiruvamutam aḷittōy cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: Let all the blind customs that celebrate the mere fictions of the scriptures as the ultimate state be buried in the earth and be gone. With the intention that the one unwavering True Path alone should be established for the world of truth to live and flourish, you bestowed your grace upon me. You yourself made me realize that this very steadfast moment is the opportune time. O You who spoke the truth, please come and embrace me with grace. O You who melted my hard, stone-like heart and gave me sacred ambrosia! O Crest-Jewel of Siddhas, my Lord of the sacred dance!
commentary: All "blind customs" based on scripture should be buried and forgotten. Vallalar declares that God has revealed a single, steady True Path, the Sanmarkkam, which is meant for the entire world. God has made him realize that the perfect time for this new reality is this very moment.

translit: tiruttakumōr taruṇamitil tirukkatavam tiṟantē tiruvaruṭpē roḷikāṭṭit tiruvamutam ūṭṭik karuttumakiḻn teṉuṭampil kalantuḷattil kalantu kaṉintuyiril kalantaṟiviṟ kalantulakam aṉaittum uruttakavē aṭaṅkukiṉṟa ūḻitoṟum piriyā toṉṟākik kālavarai uraippaelām kaṭantē tiruttiyoṭu viḷaṅkiaruḷ āṭalceya vēṇṭum cittacikā maṇiyēeṉ tirunaṭanā yakaṉē.
translation: At this one fitting, sacred moment, open the sacred door, show me the great light of sacred grace, and feed me sacred ambrosia. Then, with a joyful heart, merge with my body, merge with my mind, mature and merge with my life-breath, and merge with my consciousness. Become one with me, never to be separated through all the eons in which the worlds in their forms are contained. Transcending all that is spoken of as the limits of time, you must shine with perfection and perform your play of grace. O Crest-Jewel of Siddhas, my Lord of the sacred dance!
commentary: This verse is a powerful plea for immediate and total union with God. Vallalar asks for the "sacred door" to be opened now, revealing the great light of grace. He asks for a complete merger, for God to blend with his body, mind, life, and consciousness, becoming a single, inseparable reality that exists beyond all concepts of time.

tamil: தடித்தஓர் மகனைத் தந்தைஈண் டடித்தால் தாயுடன் அணைப்பள்தாய் அடித்தால்
பிடித்தொரு தந்தை அணைப்பன்இங் கெனக்குப் பேசிய தந்தையும் தாயும்
பொடித்திரு மேனி அம்பலத் தாடும் புனிதநீ ஆதலால் என்னை
அடித்தது போதும் அணைத்திடல் வேண்டும் அம்மைஅப் பாஇனிஆற்றேன்.
translit: taṭittaōr makaṉait tantaiīṇ ṭaṭittāl tāyuṭaṉ aṇaippaḷtāy aṭittāl piṭittoru tantai aṇaippaṉiṅ keṉakkup pēciya tantaiyum tāyum poṭittiru mēṉi ampalat tāṭum puṉitanī ātalāl eṉṉai aṭittatu pōtum aṇaittiṭal vēṇṭum ammaiap pāiṉiāṟṟēṉ.
translation: When a father here beats his unruly son, his mother embraces him. If the mother beats him, the father will hold and embrace him. For me, the father and mother spoken of is You, the Holy One with an ash-smeared sacred body, dancing in the Hall. You have beaten me enough; you must embrace me now. O Mother and Father, I can bear it no longer.
commentary: Vallalar frames his suffering as discipline from a divine parent. Just as a child beaten by one parent is comforted by the other, he asks God, who is both his mother and father, to stop the punishment and provide the comfort. The hardship is a "beating" from God that has served its purpose, and now it is time for love.

tamil: பெற்றதம் பிள்ளைக் குணங்களை எல்லாம் பெற்றவர் அறிவரே அல்லால்
மற்றவர் அறியார் என்றனை ஈன்ற வள்ளலே மன்றிலே நடிக்கும்
translit: peṟṟatam piḷḷaik kuṇaṅkaḷai ellām peṟṟavar aṟivarē allāl maṟṟavar aṟiyār eṉṟaṉai īṉṟa vaḷḷalē maṉṟilē naṭikkum koṟṟava ōreṇkuṇattava nī tāṉ kuṟikkoṇṭakoṭiyaṉēṉkuṇaṅkaḷ muṟṟumnaṉ kaṟivāy aṟintumeṉṟaṉainī muṉivateṉmuṉivutīrntaruḷē.
translation: The parents who bore a child know all its traits, but others do not. O generous one who gave birth to me, O King who performs in the Hall, O sovereign with eight great qualities! You know completely well the characteristics of this wicked person, which you yourself have noted. Knowing this, why are you angry with me? Put aside your anger and show me your grace.
commentary: A parent knows their own child's nature better than anyone. Using this simple truth, Vallalar makes a bold appeal to God: 'You created me, so you know all my flaws intimately. Since you know me so well, why are you angry with me for being the way I am?' He gently places the ultimate responsibility for his nature back on God, his creator.

tamil: வெம்மதிக் கொடிய மகன்கொடுஞ் செய்கை விரும்பினும் அங்ஙனம் புரியச்
சம்மதிக் கின்றார் அவன்றனைப் பெற்ற தந்தைதாய் மகன்விருப் பாலே
இம்மதிச் சிறியேன் விழைந்ததொன் றிலைநீ என்றனை விழைவிக்க விழைந்தேன்
செம்மதிக் கருணைத் திருநெறி இதுநின் திருவுளம் அறியுமே எந்தாய்.
translit: vemmatik koṭiya makaṉkoṭuñ ceykai virumpiṉum aṅṅaṉam puriyac cammatik kiṉṟār avaṉṟaṉaip peṟṟa tantaitāy makaṉvirup pālē immatic ciṟiyēṉ viḻaintatoṉ ṟilainī eṉṟaṉai viḻaivikka viḻaintēṉ cemmatik karuṇait tiruneṟi ituniṉ tiruvuḷam aṟiyumē entāy.
translation: Even if a wicked son with a harsh mind wishes to perform cruel deeds, his parents consent, driven by their son's own desire. But I, this small-minded one, have desired nothing on my own. I desired only because you made me desire it. This is the sacred path of perfect, mindful compassion; your sacred will knows this, my Mother.
commentary: This verse deepens the previous idea by claiming that even his desires are not his own. Vallalar states that he has only ever wanted what God made him want. Unlike a human child whose bad impulses come from himself, Vallalar argues that his own impulses originate from God. Therefore, God cannot judge him for them, and the only true path forward is one of divine compassion.

tamil: பொய்பிழை அனந்தம் புகல்கின்றேன் அதில்ஓர் புல்முனை ஆயினும் பிறர்க்கு
நைபிழை உளதேல் நவின்றிடேன் பிறர்பால் நண்ணிய கருணையால் பலவே
கைபிழை யாமை கருதுகின் றேன்நின் கழற்பதம் விழைகின்றேன் அல்லால்
செய்பிழை வேறொன் றறிகிலேன் அந்தோ திருவுளம் அறியுமே எந்தாய்.
translit: poypiḻai aṉantam pukalkiṉṟēṉ atilōr pulmuṉai āyiṉum piṟarkku naipiḻai uḷatēl naviṉṟiṭēṉ piṟarpāl naṇṇiya karuṇaiyāl palavē kaipiḻai yāmai karutukiṉ ṟēṉniṉ kaḻaṟpatam viḻaikiṉṟēṉ allāl ceypiḻai vēṟoṉ ṟaṟikilēṉ antō tiruvuḷam aṟiyumē entāy.
translation: I confess endless lies and faults. But among them, I would not speak a single fault that harms others, not even to the measure of a blade of grass. Out of the compassion I feel for others, I strive in many ways not to err in my actions. I desire your ankleted feet, and nothing else. I know of no other wrong I have done. Alas! Your sacred will knows this, my Mother.
commentary: While confessing to countless personal faults, Vallalar makes a clear distinction. He insists that, out of compassion, he has never intentionally caused harm to another living being. His failings are his own internal struggles, but his actions toward others are guided by care. His one true desire, he claims, is for God, and he asks God to recognize the purity of this core intention.

tamil: அப்பணி முடிஎன் அப்பனே மன்றில் ஆனந்த நடம்புரி அரசே
இப்புவி தனிலே அறிவுவந் ததுதொட் டிந்தநாள் வரையும்என் தனக்கே
எப்பணி இட்டாய் அப்பணி அலதென் இச்சையால் புரிந்ததொன் றிலையே
செப்புவ தென்நான் செய்தவை எல்லாம் திருவுளம் அறியுமே எந்தாய்.
translit: appaṇi muṭieṉ appaṉē maṉṟil āṉanta naṭampuri aracē ippuvi taṉilē aṟivuvan tatutoṭ ṭintanāḷ varaiyumeṉ taṉakkē eppaṇi iṭṭāy appaṇi alateṉ iccaiyāl purintatoṉ ṟilaiyē ceppuva teṉnāṉ ceytavai ellām tiruvuḷam aṟiyumē entāy.
translation: O my Father who wears the river on your crest! O King who performs the dance of bliss in the Hall! On this earth, from the moment I gained awareness until this very day, I have done nothing from my own desire, only the work you assigned to me. What is there for me to say? Your sacred will knows everything I have done, my Mother.
commentary: A life lived in true devotion is a role assigned by God. From his earliest moments of self-awareness, Vallalar sees his existence as a form of divine service, with no room for personal ambition or desire. By addressing God as the cosmic dancer, he frames his individual life as a small part of a vast, divine performance.

tamil: முன்னொடு பின்னும் நீ தரு மடவார் முயக்கினில் பொருந்தினேன் அதுவும்
என்னொடும் இருந்திங் கறிகின்ற நினக்கே எந்தைவே றியம்புவதென்னோ
சொன்னெடு வானத் தரம்பையர் எனினும் துரும்பெனக் காண்கின்றேன் தனித்தே.
translit: muṉṉoṭu piṉṉum nī taru maṭavār muyakkiṉil poruntiṉēṉ atuvum poṉṉoṭu viḷaṅkum capainaṭat taracuṉ puṇarppalāleṉpuṇarppalavē eṉṉoṭum iruntiṅ kaṟikiṉṟa niṉakkē entaivē ṟiyampuvateṉṉō coṉṉeṭu vāṉat tarampaiyar eṉiṉum turumpeṉak kāṇkiṉṟēṉ taṉittē.
translation: In the past, I submitted to the embrace of women you provided. That too, O King who dances in the radiant Golden Hall, was your doing, not my doing at all. My Father, since you reside within me and know this, what more is there for me to say? On my own, I see even the famed celestial nymphs of the high heavens as a mere blade of grass.
commentary: Even past involvement in worldly pleasures was an experience orchestrated by God. This is a radical claim of surrendering all personal history to the divine will, suggesting there was never a time he acted separately from God. Left to his own nature, he insists, he feels a complete disinterest in sensual pleasure, viewing even celestial beauties as worthless.

tamil: இன்னுமிங் கெனைநீ மடந்தையர் முயக்கில் எய்துவித் திடுதியேல் அதுவுன்
தன்னுளப் புணர்ப்பிங் கெனக்கொரு சிறிதும் சம்மதம் அன்றுநான் இதனைப்
பன்னுவ தென்னே இதில்அரு வருப்புப் பால்உணும் காலையே உளதால்
மன்னும்அம் பலத்தே நடம்புரி வோய்என் மதிப்பெலாம் திருவடி மலர்க்கே.
translit: iṉṉumiṅ keṉainī maṭantaiyar muyakkil eytuvit tiṭutiyēl atuvuṉ taṉṉuḷap puṇarppiṅ keṉakkoru ciṟitum cammatam aṉṟunāṉ itaṉaip paṉṉuva teṉṉē itilaru varuppup pāluṇum kālaiyē uḷatāl maṉṉumam palattē naṭampuri vōyeṉ matippelām tiruvaṭi malarkkē.
translation: If you still cause me to join in the embrace of women, that is an act of your own will. I have not the slightest consent in it. Why must I even say this? I have had an aversion to this since I was a babe drinking milk. O you who performs the dance in the eternal Hall, all my esteem is for your sacred, flower-like feet alone.
commentary: If he is to engage in physical relationships again, it will be a result of God's will, not his own consent. He lays his inner state bare, clarifying that while he submits to the divine plan, his own inclination is one of deep aversion. Stating that this feeling has existed since infancy emphasizes that it is a fundamental part of his nature, not a discipline he learned.

tamil: அறிவிலாச் சிறிய பருவத்திற் றானே அருந்தலில் எனக்குள வெறுப்பைப்
பிறிவிலா தென்னுட் கலந்ததீ அறிதி இன்றுநான் பேசுவ தென்னே
செறிவிலாக் கடையேன் என்னினும் அடியேன் திருவருள் அமுதமே விழைந்தேன்
எறிவிலாச் சுவைவே றெவற்றினும் விழைவோர் எட்டுணை யேனும்இன் றெந்தாய்.
translit: aṟivilāc ciṟiya paruvattiṟ ṟāṉē aruntalil eṉakkuḷa veṟuppaip piṟivilā teṉṉuṭ kalantatī aṟiti iṉṟunāṉ pēcuva teṉṉē ceṟivilāk kaṭaiyēṉ eṉṉiṉum aṭiyēṉ tiruvaruḷ amutamē viḻaintēṉ eṟivilāc cuvaivē ṟevaṟṟiṉum viḻaivōr eṭṭuṇai yēṉumiṉ ṟentāy.
translation: You, who are inseparably mingled within me, know the aversion I had for eating even in my own ignorant youth. What is there for me to say today? Although I am the lowest of the low, lacking focus, I, your devotee, have longed only for the ambrosia of your sacred grace. My Father, I have not even a sesame seed's worth of desire for any other taste besides that unfading flavor.
commentary: His natural detachment from the physical world extends even to the basic drive for food. This completes the portrait of a being whose true hunger is for spiritual nourishment, the "ambrosia of grace." By claiming this aversion existed even in childhood, he presents his disinterest in worldly things as innate.

tamil: இன்சுவை உணவு பலபல எனக்கிங் கெந்தைநீ கொடுப்பிக்கச் சிறியேன்
நின்சுவை உணவென் றுண்கின்றேன் இன்னும் நீ தரு வித்திடில் அதுநின்
தன்சுதந் தரம்இங் கெனக்கதில் இறையும் சம்மதம் இல்லைநான் தானே
என்சுதந் தரத்தில் தேடுவேன் அல்லேன் தேடிய தும்இலை ஈண்டே.
translit: iṉcuvai uṇavu palapala eṉakkiṅ kentainī koṭuppikkac ciṟiyēṉ niṉcuvai uṇaveṉ ṟuṇkiṉṟēṉ iṉṉum nī taru vittiṭil atuniṉ taṉcutan taramiṅ keṉakkatil iṟaiyum cammatam illaināṉ tāṉē eṉcutan tarattil tēṭuvēṉ allēṉ tēṭiya tumilai īṇṭē.
translation: My Father, when you have many kinds of sweet food given to me here, I, this lowly one, eat it, regarding it as food imbued with your flavor. If you continue to have it provided, that is your own prerogative. I have not the slightest consent in that. I do not seek it of my own accord, nor have I ever sought it here.
commentary: Eating is something that happens to him, not something he actively desires or pursues. When food comes his way, he accepts it as an expression of God's will, but makes it clear that he has no personal wish for it and would never seek it out on his own.

tamil: செறிவதில் மனத்தேன் காசிலே ஆசை செய்திலேன் இந்தநாள் அன்றி
அறிவதில் லாத சிறுபரு வத்தும் அடுத்தவர் கொடுத்தகா சவர்மேல்
எறிவதும் மேட்டில் எறிந்தும் எனக்குள் இருக்கின்ற நீ அறிந் ததுவே
பிறிவதில் லாநின் அருட்பெரும் பொருளைப் பெற்றனன் பேசுவ தென்னே.
translit: ceṟivatil maṉattēṉ kācilē ācai ceytilēṉ intanāḷ aṉṟi aṟivatil lāta ciṟuparu vattum aṭuttavar koṭuttakā cavarmēl eṟivatum mēṭṭil eṟintum eṉakkuḷ irukkiṉṟa nī aṟin tatuvē piṟivatil lāniṉ aruṭperum poruḷaip peṟṟaṉaṉ pēcuva teṉṉē.
translation: My mind lacks focus, yet I have had no desire for money, and more than today. Even in my ignorant youth, I would throw the coins others gave me back at them or toss them onto a high mound; you who are within me know this. I have received the great treasure of your inseparable grace. What is there to say?
commentary: His detachment from worldly things includes money, which he has rejected since he was a small child. He would literally throw away any coins (kasu) given to him. Having now received the far greater wealth of God's grace, he finds worldly riches completely insignificant.

tamil: பணத்திலே சிறிதும் ஆசைஒன் றிலைநான் படைத்தஅப் பணங்களைப்பலகால்
கிணற்றிலே எறிந்தேன் குளத்திலும் எறிந்தேன் கேணியில் எறிந்தனன் எந்தாய்
குணத்திலே நீதான் கொடுக்கின்ற பொருளை எறிகலேன் கொடுக்கின்றேன் பிறர்க்கே
கணத்திலே எல்லாம் காட்டும்நின் அருளைக் கண்டனன் இனிச்சொல்வ தென்னே.
translit: paṇattilē ciṟitum ācaioṉ ṟilaināṉ paṭaittaap paṇaṅkaḷaippalakāl kiṇaṟṟilē eṟintēṉ kuḷattilum eṟintēṉ kēṇiyil eṟintaṉaṉ entāy kuṇattilē nītāṉ koṭukkiṉṟa poruḷai eṟikalēṉ koṭukkiṉṟēṉ piṟarkkē kaṇattilē ellām kāṭṭumniṉ aruḷaik kaṇṭaṉaṉ iṉiccolva teṉṉē.
translation: I have not the slightest desire for money. The money I acquired, I threw into wells, ponds, and larger wells many times, O my Father. The wealth you give by your nature, I do not throw away; I give it to others. I have seen your grace which reveals everything in an instant. What more is there to say?
commentary: There is a difference between worldly money and wealth that flows from God. Any ordinary money he happens to acquire, he simply throws away. But when he receives abundance that he recognizes as a gift from God's own nature, he does not discard it; he gives it to others. This act of charity is possible because he has already received the ultimate gift: grace.

tamil: கிளைத்தஇவ் வுடம்பில் ஆசைஎள் ளளவும் கிளைத்திலேன் பசிஅற உணவு
திளைத்திடுந் தோறும் வெறுப்பொடும் உண்டேன் இன்றுமே வெறுப்பில்உண் கின்றேன்
இளைத்திட விழைகின் றேன்இது நான்தான் இயம்பல்என்நீ அறிந்ததுவே.
translit: kiḷaitta:iv vuṭampil ācaieḷ ḷaḷavum kiḷaittilēṉ paciaṟa uṇavu tiḷaittiṭun tōṟum veṟuppoṭum uṇṭēṉ iṉṟumē veṟuppiluṇ kiṉṟēṉ taḷaittiṭu muṭaiūṉuṭamporuciṟitumtaṭittiṭaniṉaittilēṉ iṉṟum iḷaittiṭa viḻaikiṉ ṟēṉitu nāṉtāṉ iyampaleṉnī aṟintatuvē.
translation: I have not developed even a sesame seed's worth of desire for this body that has grown. Whenever I ate food to satisfy my hunger, I ate with disgust; even today, I eat with disgust.
