translit: kaṟṟavar kallār piṟarpiṟar kuraleṉ kātilē kiṭaittapō tellām maṟṟavar tamakkeṉ uṟṟatō avartam marapiṉar uṟaviṉar tamakkuḷ uṟṟatiṅ ketuvō eṉṟuḷam naṭuṅki ōṭippārt tōṭippārt tiravum eṟṟaru pakalum ēṅkināṉ aṭainta ēkkamun tiruvuḷam aṟiyum.
translation: Whenever the voices of the learned, the unlearned, or any others reached my ears, my heart would tremble, wondering what might have happened to them, or to their family and relatives. Your divine mind knows the anxiety with which I ran to check, night and day.
commentary: This reveals the extraordinary, almost painful, intensity of Vallalar's compassion. For him, simply hearing another person's voice was enough to trigger immediate, active concern for their well-being. His compassion was not a calm, abstract principle; it was a constant, visceral anxiety for others that left him unable to rest.

tamil: கருணையம் பதிநங் கண்ணுள்மா மணிநம் கருத்திலே கலந்ததெள் ளமுதம்
மருள்நெறி தவிர்க்கும் மருந்தெலாம் வல்ல வள்ளல்சிற் றம்பலம் மன்னும்
பொருள்நிறை இன்பம் நம்மைஆண் டளித்த புண்ணியம் வருகின்ற தருணம்
தருணம்இப் போதென் றெண்ணிநான் இருக்கும் தன்மையும் திருவுளம் அறியும்.
translit: karuṇaiyam patinaṅ kaṇṇuḷmā maṇinam karuttilē kalantateḷ ḷamutam maruḷneṟi tavirkkum maruntelām valla vaḷḷalciṟ ṟampalam maṉṉum poruḷniṟai iṉpam nammaiāṇ ṭaḷitta puṇṇiyam varukiṉṟa taruṇam taruṇamip pōteṉ ṟeṇṇināṉ irukkum taṉmaiyum tiruvuḷam aṟiyum.
translation: The Lord of Compassion, the great gem in our eye, the clear nectar mingled in our consciousness, the generous benefactor reigning in the small sacred space who is the all-powerful medicine averting the path of delusion, the sacred merit that ruled and graced us as substantive bliss, Your divine mind knows my state, as I wait thinking, "The moment for his arrival is now!"
commentary: Despite the suffering described in previous verses, this poem ends with intense and hopeful expectation. Vallalar lists intimate names for God: the gem inside our eye, the nectar mixed into our consciousness, the medicine that cures delusion. He is waiting with the firm belief that the "Lord of Compassion" is near and about to arrive at this very moment.

tamil: இமையவர் பிரமர் நாரணர் முதலோர் எய்துதற் கரியபே ரின்பம்
தமைஅறிந் தவருட் சார்ந்தபே ரொளிநம் தயாநிதி தனிப்பெருந் தந்தை
அமையும்நம் உயிர்க்குத் துணைதிருப் பொதுவில் ஐயர் தாம் வருகின்ற சமயம்
சமயம்இப் போதென் றெண்ணிநான் இருக்கும் தன்மையும் திருவுளம் அறியும்.
translit: imaiyavar piramar nāraṇar mutalōr eytutaṟ kariyapē riṉpam tamaiaṟin tavaruṭ cārntapē roḷinam tayāniti taṉipperun tantai amaiyumnam uyirkkut tuṇaitirup potuvil aiyar tām varukiṉṟa camayam camayamip pōteṉ ṟeṇṇināṉ irukkum taṉmaiyum tiruvuḷam aṟiyum.
translation: The great bliss unattainable by the celestials, Brahma, Narayana, and the others; the great light that is attained by those who have realized the self; our treasure of compassion; our unique, great Father; the fitting companion for our soul; the Master in the sacred common space, Your divine mind knows my state, as I wait thinking, "The time for his arrival is now!"
commentary: The state of union Vallalar awaits surpasses the heavens of even the highest traditional gods, like Brahma and Vishnu (Narayana). He claims this supreme bliss is for human beings who realize the true self. By calling this ultimate reality a "Father" and "companion," he frames the spiritual goal as a deeply personal and loving relationship.

tamil: அடியனேன் உள்ளம் திருச்சிற்றம் பலத்தென் அமுதநின் மேல்வைத்த காதல்
நெடியஏழ் கடலில் பெரிதெனக் கிந்நாள் நிகழ்கின்ற ஆவலும் விரைவும்
படியஎன் தன்னால் சொலமுடி யாது பார்ப்பறப் பார்த்திருக் கின்றேன்
செடியனேன் இருக்கும் வண்ணங்கள் எல்லாம் திருவுளங் கண்டதே எந்தாய்.
translit: aṭiyaṉēṉ uḷḷam tirucciṟṟam palatteṉ amutaniṉ mēlvaitta kātal neṭiyaēḻ kaṭalil periteṉak kinnāḷ nikaḻkiṉṟa āvalum viraivum paṭiyaeṉ taṉṉāl colamuṭi yātu pārppaṟap pārttiruk kiṉṟēṉ ceṭiyaṉēṉ irukkum vaṇṇaṅkaḷ ellām tiruvuḷaṅ kaṇṭatē entāy.
translation: O my nectar of the sacred small space! The love this devotee's heart holds for You is greater than the seven vast seas. I cannot describe in words the eagerness and urgency I feel today. I am watching without blinking. O my Father, Your divine mind has witnessed all the states of this flawed one.
commentary: His love for God has become so vast that it feels greater than the oceans and can no longer be expressed in words. This overwhelming love translates into a state of total, steady attention, where he is "watching without blinking" for God's appearance. Even in this moment of supreme devotion, he calls himself "flawed," showing his complete humility and reliance on divine grace.

tamil: பன்னிரண் டாண்டு தொடங்கிநான் இற்றைப் பகல்வரை அடைந்தவை எல்லாம்
உன்னிநின் றுரைத்தால் உலப்புறா ததனால் ஒருசில உரைத்தனன் எனினும்
என்னுளத் தகத்தும் புறத்தும்உட் புறத்தும் இயல்புறப் புறத்தினும் விளங்கி
மன்னிய சோதி யாவும்நீ அறிந்த வண்ணமே வகுப்பதென் நினக்கே.
translit: paṉṉiraṇ ṭāṇṭu toṭaṅkināṉ iṟṟaip pakalvarai aṭaintavai ellām uṉṉiniṉ ṟuraittāl ulappuṟā tataṉāl orucila uraittaṉaṉ eṉiṉum eṉṉuḷat takattum puṟattumuṭ puṟattum iyalpuṟap puṟattiṉum viḷaṅki maṉṉiya cōti yāvumnī aṟinta vaṇṇamē vakuppateṉ niṉakkē.
translation: If I were to recount all I have been through from the age of twelve until this day, it would be endless, so I have mentioned only a few things. Even so, O enduring Jothi that shines within my heart and without, in its inner dimensions and its outer nature, since You know everything, what is there for me to explain to You?
commentary: After briefly touching on his life's story, Vallalar realizes that explaining himself to God is unnecessary. The divine light, or Jothi, is an all-knowing presence that has witnessed every moment, both internally and externally. This turns his prayer from a report into an act of deep intimacy, acknowledging that God already knows him completely.

tamil: இதுவரை அடியேன் அடைந்தவெம் பயமும் இடர்களும் துன்பமும் எல்லாம்
பொதுவளர் பொருளே பிறர்பொருட் டல்லால் புலையனேன் பொருட்டல இதுநின்
மதுவளர் மலர்ப்பொற் பதத்துணை அறிய வகுத்தனன் அடியனேன் தனக்கே
எதிலும்ஓர் ஆசை இலைஇலை பயமும் இடரும்மற் றிலைஇலை எந்தாய்.
translit: ituvarai aṭiyēṉ aṭaintavem payamum iṭarkaḷum tuṉpamum ellām potuvaḷar poruḷē piṟarporuṭ ṭallāl pulaiyaṉēṉ poruṭṭala ituniṉ matuvaḷar malarppoṟ patattuṇai aṟiya vakuttaṉaṉ aṭiyaṉēṉ taṉakkē etilumōr ācai ilaiilai payamum iṭarummaṟ ṟilaiilai entāy.
translation: O universal Being! All the terrible fear, hardships, and suffering that I, your slave, have endured until now were for the sake of others, not for my own sake, I, the lowly one. I declare this, knowing your honey-filled, golden pair of flower-like feet. For me, your slave, there is absolutely no desire for anything. There is no fear and no hardship, my Father.
commentary: Vallalar makes the ultimate declaration of his path: all the suffering he has ever endured was for the sake of other beings, not for himself. His spiritual life was an act of radical compassion, taking on the world's pain. Because his struggles were never for personal gain, he can now affirm that he is entirely free from his own desires, fears, and hardships, having been emptied for the benefit of all.

tamil: என்னள விலையே என்னினும் பிறர்பால் எய்திய கருணையால் எந்தாய்
உன்னுறு பயமும் இடருமென் தன்னை உயிரொடும் தின்கின்ற தந்தோ
இன்னும்என் றனக்கிவ் விடரொடு பயமும் இருந்திடில்என்உயிர் தரியா
தன்னையும் குருவும் அப்பனும் ஆன அமுதனே அளித்தருள் எனையே.
translit: eṉṉaḷa vilaiyē eṉṉiṉum piṟarpāl eytiya karuṇaiyāl entāy uṉṉuṟu payamum iṭarumeṉ taṉṉai uyiroṭum tiṉkiṉṟa tantō iṉṉumeṉ ṟaṉakkiv viṭaroṭu payamum iruntiṭileṉuyir tariyā taṉṉaiyum kuruvum appaṉum āṉa amutaṉē aḷittaruḷ eṉaiyē.
translation: My Father, though I have no suffering for myself, due to the compassion I have for others, the resulting fear and hardship are eating me alive, alas! If this hardship and fear persist for me, my life cannot endure. O Nectar who is my Mother, Guru, and Father, grant your grace and save me.
commentary: His compassion is so deep that the suffering of others has become his own. This vicarious pain is not a metaphor; he feels it so intensely that it is "eating him alive," and he pleads for grace to endure it.

tamil: பயத்தொடு துயரும் மறைப்புமா மாயைப் பற்றொடு வினையும்ஆ ணவமும்
கயத்தவன் மயக்கும் மருட்சியும் எனது கருத்திலே இனிஒரு கணமும்
வியத்திடத் தரியேன் இவையெலாந் தவிர்த்துன் மெய்யருள் அளித்திடல் வேண்டும்
உயத்தரு வாயேல் இருக்கின்றேன் இலையேல் உயிர்விடு கின்றனன் இன்றே.
translit: payattoṭu tuyarum maṟaippumā māyaip paṟṟoṭu viṉaiyumā ṇavamum kayattavaṉ mayakkum maruṭciyum eṉatu karuttilē iṉioru kaṇamum viyattiṭat tariyēṉ ivaiyelān tavirttuṉ meyyaruḷ aḷittiṭal vēṇṭum uyattaru vāyēl irukkiṉṟēṉ ilaiyēl uyirviṭu kiṉṟaṉaṉ iṉṟē.
translation: I can no longer bear for fear, sorrow, obscuration, attachment to great māyā, karma, āṇavam, and the bewildering confusion caused by the vile one to arise in my mind for even another moment. You must remove all these and grant me your true grace. If you save me, I will remain. If not, I will give up my life this very day.
commentary: He lists the fundamental obstacles to spiritual clarity: fear, sorrow, māyā (cosmic illusion), karma (the binding law of action and consequence), and āṇavam (the principle of ego and spiritual darkness). He has reached his breaking point and presents an ultimatum: God must grant him grace immediately, or he will not survive.

tamil: ஐயநான் பயத்தால் துயரினால் அடைந்த அடைவைஉள் நினைத்திடுந் தோறும்
வெய்யதீ மூட்டிவிடுதல்ஒப் பதுநான் மிகஇவற் றால்இளைத் திட்டேன்
வையமேல் இனிநான் இவைகளால் இளைக்க வசமிலேன் இவைஎலாம் தவிர்த்தே
உய்யவைப் பாயேல் இருக்கின்றேன் இலையேல் உயிர்விடு கின்றனன் இன்றே.
translit: aiyanāṉ payattāl tuyariṉāl aṭainta aṭaivaiuḷ niṉaittiṭun tōṟum veyyatī mūṭṭiviṭutalop patunāṉ mika:ivaṟ ṟāliḷait tiṭṭēṉ vaiyamēl iṉināṉ ivaikaḷāl iḷaikka vacamilēṉ ivaielām tavirttē uyyavaip pāyēl irukkiṉṟēṉ ilaiyēl uyirviṭu kiṉṟaṉaṉ iṉṟē.
translation: O Lord! Whenever I recall the state I reached through fear and sorrow, it is like lighting a cruel fire. I have become completely exhausted by these things. On this earth, I no longer have the strength to be worn down by them. If you remove all these and cause me to be saved, I will remain. If not, I will give up my life this very day.
commentary: The repetition of the ultimatum from the previous verse conveys a state of complete exhaustion. The memory of past suffering is a constant, active torment. His continued existence is now entirely dependent on divine intervention.

tamil: பயந்துயர் இடர்உள் மருட்சியா தியஇப் பகைஎலாம் பற்றறத் தவிர்த்தே
நயந்தநின் அருளார்அமுதளித் தடியேன் நாடிஈண் டெண்ணிய எல்லாம்
வியந்திடத் தருதல் வேண்டும்ஈ தெனது விண்ணப்பம் நின்திரு உளத்தே
வயந்தரக் கருதித் தயவுசெய் தருள்க வள்ளலே சிற்சபை வாழ்வே.
translit: payantuyar iṭaruḷ maruṭciyā tiya:ip pakaielām paṟṟaṟat tavirttē nayantaniṉ aruḷāramutaḷit taṭiyēṉ nāṭiīṇ ṭeṇṇiya ellām viyantiṭat tarutal vēṇṭumī teṉatu viṇṇappam niṉtiru uḷattē vayantarak karutit tayavucey taruḷka vaḷḷalē ciṟcapai vāḻvē.
translation: O generous One! O Life of the Chit Sabhai! You must completely uproot all these enemies, such as fear, sorrow, hardship, and inner confusion. You must give me the nectar of your grace that I desire and wondrously grant all that I, your slave, have sought and conceived of here. This is my appeal. Please consider it favorably in your sacred will and bestow your kindness and grace.
commentary: He concludes his appeal with a clear summary of his request: remove the inner enemies of fear and confusion, and grant the grace to fulfill his mission. He addresses God as the living reality of the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness), the ultimate space of divine presence.

tamil: என்னுயிர் காத்தல் கடன்உனக் கடியேன் இசைத்தவிண் ணப்பம்ஏற் றருளி
உன்னுமென் உள்ளத் துறும்பயம் இடர்கள் உறுகண்மற் றிவைஎலாம் ஒழித்தே
நின்னருள் அமுதம் அளித்தென தெண்ணம் நிரப்பியாட் கொள்ளுதல் வேண்டும்
மன்னுபொற் சபையில் வயங்கிய மணியே வள்ளலே சிற்சபை வாழ்வே.
translit: eṉṉuyir kāttal kaṭaṉuṉak kaṭiyēṉ icaittaviṇ ṇappamēṟ ṟaruḷi uṉṉumeṉ uḷḷat tuṟumpayam iṭarkaḷ uṟukaṇmaṟ ṟivaielām oḻittē niṉṉaruḷ amutam aḷitteṉa teṇṇam nirappiyāṭ koḷḷutal vēṇṭum maṉṉupoṟ capaiyil vayaṅkiya maṇiyē vaḷḷalē ciṟcapai vāḻvē.
translation: It is your duty to protect my soul. Graciously accept the request I, your slave, have made. You must remove all the fear, afflictions, and suffering that arise in my mind, give me the nectar of your grace, fulfill my desire, and take me as your own, O radiant Gem in the eternal golden hall! O great Benefactor! O Life of the hall of consciousness!
commentary: Vallalar makes the bold claim that it is God's "duty" to protect a soul devoted to him. This shows an incredible intimacy and confidence in his relationship with the divine. He asks for the removal of suffering and for God to "take me as your own," expressing a deep longing for complete union.

tamil: பரிக்கிலேன் பயமும் இடரும்வெந் துயரும் பற்றறத் தவிர்த்தருள் இனிநான்
புரிக்கிலே சத்தை அகற்றிஆட் கொள்ளும் பொற்சபை அண்ணலே கருணை
வரிக்கணேர் மடந்தை பாகனே சிவனேவள்ளலே சிற்சபை வாழ்வே.
translit: parikkilēṉ payamum iṭarumven tuyarum paṟṟaṟat tavirttaruḷ iṉināṉ tarikkilēṉ ciṟitumtarikkilēṉ uḷḷamtarikkilēṉ tarikkilēṉ antō purikkilē cattai akaṟṟiāṭ koḷḷum poṟcapai aṇṇalē karuṇai varikkaṇēr maṭantai pākaṉē civaṉēvaḷḷalē ciṟcapai vāḻvē.
translation: I cannot bear it. Graciously remove this fear, affliction, and burning sorrow completely. From now on, I cannot endure it, not even a little. My heart cannot endure it. I cannot endure it, I cannot endure it, alas! O Lord of the golden hall who takes me as your own, removing even the slightest trace of my impurity! O Embodiment of grace! O one who shares your body with the young woman with line-drawn eyes! O Sivan! O great Benefactor! O Life of the hall of consciousness!
commentary: The repeated cries of "I cannot endure it" reveal a state of pure emotional agony beyond structured prayer. In this moment of utter surrender, he calls on God by many names, invoking the divine as the compassionate Lord of the golden hall, as the form united with the Goddess, and as Sivan (The Auspicious One), reaching for every aspect of grace he can imagine.

tamil: வரிக்கணேர் இன்ப வல்லியை மணந்த - முதற்பதிப்பு, பொ. சு., ச.மு.க. பதிப்பு.
translit: varikkaṇēr iṉpa valliyai maṇanta - mutaṟpatippu, po. cu., ca.mu.ka. patippu.
translation: varikkaṇēr iṉpa valliyai maṇanta — reading of the first edition and of the Po. Su. and S. Mu. Ka. editions.

translit: appānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum āruyirkaṭ kellāmnāṉ aṉpuceyal vēṇṭum eppārum eppatamum eṅkaṇumnāṉ ceṉṟē entainiṉa taruṭpukaḻai iyampiyiṭal vēṇṭum ceppāta mēṉilaimēl cuttaciva mārkkam tikaḻntōṅka aruṭcōti celuttiyiṭal vēṇṭum tappētu nāṉceyiṉum nīpoṟuttal vēṇṭum talaivaniṉaip piriyāta nilaimaiyumvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: Father, you must listen to my requests and grant your grace. I must love all precious lives. I must go to every world, every realm, everywhere, and proclaim the glory of your grace, my Father. You must direct the Grace-Jothi so the Pure Siva Path, which is beyond the highest state that can be spoken, flourishes brightly. Whatever mistakes I make, you must forgive them. O Leader, I also need a state in which I am never separated from you.
commentary: This prayer reframes spiritual aspiration away from personal gain and toward universal service. Vallalar asks for the capacity to love all beings, the mission to spread God's glory, and the establishment of his Pure Siva Path. He requests forgiveness so he can remain a worthy instrument, constantly connected to the divine Grace-Jothi (aruṭcōti, or Grace-Light) that fuels his work.

translit: aiyānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum aṭimuṭikaṇ ṭennāḷum aṉupavittal vēṇṭum poyyāta vāymaikaḷē pukaṉṟiṭutal vēṇṭum pukaṉṟapaṭi pukaṉṟapaṭi purintiṭutal vēṇṭum eyyātaaruṭcōti eṉkaiyuṟal vēṇṭum iṟanta:uyir tamaimīṭṭum eḻuppiyiṭal vēṇṭum naiyāta vaṇṇamuyir kāttiṭutal vēṇṭum nāyakaniṉ taṉaippiriyā tuṟutalumvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: Lord, you must listen to my requests and grant your grace. I must see and experience your feet and crown forever. I must speak only unfailing truths. I must act exactly according to what I have spoken. The inexhaustible Grace-Jothi must come into my hands. I must bring the dead back to life. I must protect lives so they do not perish. O Master, I also need to be firmly united with you, never to be separated.
commentary: Here, the requests become even deeper. Vallalar asks for perfect integrity, where speech and action are one. He then makes two astonishing claims: he asks for the divine Grace-Jothi (aruṭcōti) to be placed in his hands, and for the power to resurrect the dead. For Vallalar, compassion is a force so powerful that, when perfected, it can defy death itself, offering protection and new life to all beings.

translit: aṇṇānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum aḻiyāta taṉivaṭivam yāṉaṭaital vēṇṭum kaṇṇāra niṉaieṅkum kaṇvattal vēṇṭum kāṇāta kāṭcielām kaṇṭukoḷal vēṇṭum paṇṇāra niṉṟaṉaiyē pāṭiyuṟal vēṇṭum paramāṉan tapperuṅkūt tāṭiyiṭal vēṇṭum uṇṇāṭi uyirkaḷuṟum tuyartavirttal vēṇṭum uṉaippiriyā tuṟukiṉṟa uṟavatuvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: Lord, you must listen to my requests and grant your grace. I must attain a unique, indestructible form. I must see you everywhere to my eyes' fill. I must see all the sights that have never been seen. I must sing of you alone in melodious tunes. I must dance the great dance of supreme bliss. I must discern the suffering beings feel within and remove it. I need that relationship of being united with you, never to be separated.
commentary: The transformation of the self is presented as the key to helping others. Attaining an immortal body and seeing God everywhere are not the final goals; they are the means to an even greater end. The purpose of this divine perception and bliss is to be able to feel the suffering of all beings as one's own and have the power to remove it.

translit: attānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum aruṭperuñcō tiyaippeṟṟē akaṅkaḷittal vēṇṭum cettārai mīṭṭumiṅkē eḻuppiyiṭal vēṇṭum tiruccapaikkē aṭimaikaḷāc ceyvittal vēṇṭum ottārum uyarntārum tāḻntārum evarum orumaiuḷar ākiula kiyalnaṭattal vēṇṭum ettālum aḻiyāta vaṭivatilē nāṉum entāyum oṉṟāka iṉituṟalvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: Father, you must listen to my requests and grant your grace. I must receive the Vast Grace-Light and rejoice in my heart. I must raise the dead and bring them back here. I must cause them to become servants of the sacred assembly. The equal, the high, and the low, all people must live their worldly lives with a single mind of unity. In a form that is by any means indestructible, I and you, my Parent, must sweetly dwell as one.
commentary: Receiving the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) is directly linked to a spiritual and social revolution. The power it confers is for raising the dead and establishing a community of service. This verse gives a clear vision for a new society without class or hierarchy, where all people live in a state of unity. The ultimate union with God is the foundation for this transformed world.

translit: araicēnāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum aruṭperuñcō tiyaippeṟṟē akamakiḻtalvēṇṭum varaicērev vulakamumōr oḻukkamuṟal vēṇṭum maṭintārai mīḷavumnāṉ varuvittal vēṇṭum puraicērum kolaineṟiyum pulaineṟiyum ciṟitum poruntāmal evvuyirum purintuvattal vēṇṭum uraicērmeyt tiruvaṭivil entāyum nāṉum oṉṟāki eññāṉṟum ōṅkutalvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: King, you must listen to my requests and grant your grace. I must receive the Vast Grace-Light and rejoice in my heart. All worlds without exception must attain a single moral order. I must again cause the dead to return. All beings must understand and rejoice, completely rejecting the flawed path of killing and the path of eating flesh. In the glorious true form celebrated in speech, my Parent and I must become one and be forever exalted.
commentary: Here, the "single moral order" for a redeemed world is explicitly defined. The foundation of this universal law is the complete rejection of killing and meat-eating. Vallalar presents this core ethical commitment, known as jīvakāruṇyam (compassion for all living beings), as the necessary condition for universal joy and for becoming one with God.

translit: aṭikēḷnāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum aṇṭamelām piṇṭamelām kaṇṭukoḷal vēṇṭum tuṭicērev vulakamumet tēvarumev vuyirum cuttaciva caṉmārkkam peṟṟiṭutal vēṇṭum paṭivāṉum paṭaittalmutal aintoḻilum ñāṉam paṭaittalmutal aintoḻilum nāṉpurital vēṇṭum oṭiyāta tiruvaṭivil entāyum nāṉum oṉṟāki eññāṉṟum ōṅkutalvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: O Master, you must listen to my request and bestow grace. I must behold all the macrocosms and all the microcosms. All worlds, all devas, and all living beings must attain the Sutha Siva Sanmarkkam. I must perform the five cosmic functions beginning with creation, and the five functions of wisdom beginning with its creation. In your imperishable, sacred form, my Father and I must become one and flourish forever.
commentary: The prayer reaches its peak with an astonishing request for ultimate responsibility. Vallalar asks to serve God and to take on the very functions of God: creating, preserving, and transforming the cosmos. This expresses the final stage of union, where the devotee's will merges with the divine will to guide all beings to the Sutha Siva Sanmarkkam, the true path of universal goodness.

translit: ammānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum āṇavamā tiyamuḻutum aṟuttuniṟṟal vēṇṭum immālait tattuvaṅkaḷ ellāmeṉ vacattē iyaṅkioru tīmaiyumil lātiruttal vēṇṭum emmāṉnāṉ vēṇṭutalvēṇ ṭāmaiyaṟal vēṇṭum ēkaciva pōkaaṉu pōkamuṟal vēṇṭum tammāṉat tiruvaṭivil entāyum nāṉum cārntukalan tōṅkukiṉṟa taṉmaiyumvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: O Mother, you must listen to my request and bestow grace. I must completely sever and stand free from āṇavam and all that follows it. All these garlands of tattvas must operate under my control, free from any harm. My Lord, my own states of wanting and not wanting must cease. I must attain the experience of the singular bliss of Siva. I also desire the state where, in your self-existent sacred form, my Father and I approach, merge, and flourish.
commentary: This prayer focuses on the inner transformation required for union with the divine. Vallalar asks to be completely freed from āṇavam, the primal sense of a separate "I" or ego that keeps the soul bound. He also asks for mastery over the tattvas, the fundamental principles that make up reality, so they operate under his benevolent control. By ceasing to be driven by personal wants and desires, he hopes to experience the singular bliss of God and merge into that divine reality.

translit: accānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum āṟanta nilaikaḷelām aṟintaṭaital vēṇṭum eccārpum ākiuyirk kitampurital vēṇṭum eṉaiaṭuttār tamakkellām iṉputaral vēṇṭum iccāti camayavikaṟ paṅkaḷelām tavirttē evvulakum caṉmārkkap potuvaṭaital vēṇṭum uccāti antamilāt tiruvaṭivil yāṉum uṭaiyāyum kalantōṅkum orumaiyumvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: O Father, you must listen to my request and bestow grace. I must know and attain all the states of the six philosophical conclusions. I must become every kind of support and do good for all living beings. I must give bliss to all who approach me. Casting aside all these distinctions of caste and religion, all worlds must attain the universal Sanmarkkam. I also desire the oneness where, in your sacred form which has no beginning or end, I and you, my Lord, merge and flourish.
commentary: Vallalar makes a powerful call for a universal spirituality that transcends all social and religious boundaries. He explicitly asks that "all these distinctions of caste and religion" be cast aside, so the whole world can embrace a single, common path, the Sanmarkkam. This isn't just a philosophical idea; he prays for the ability to become a source of comfort and bliss for every living being, embodying this universal principle on his way to oneness with God.

translit: aṟivānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum aintoḻilnāṉ purintulakil aruḷviḷakkal vēṇṭum ceṟiyāta karaṇamelām ceṟittaṭakkal vēṇṭum cittānta vētāntap potuciṟattal vēṇṭum eṟiyāteṉ eṇṇamelām iṉitaruḷal vēṇṭum ellāñcey vallacittē eṉakkaḷittal vēṇṭum piṟiyāteṉ ṉoṭukalantu nīiruttal vēṇṭum perumāṉniṉ taṉaippāṭi āṭutalvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: O Wisdom, you must listen to my request and bestow grace. I must perform the five cosmic functions and make grace shine in the world. I must gather and subdue all the scattered inner faculties . The common ground of Siddhānta and Vedānta must be exalted. You must sweetly grant all my thoughts without casting any aside. You must bestow on me the siddhi that can do all things. You must remain merged with me, never separating. O great Lord, I must sing of you and dance.
commentary: This final prayer describes the state of a fully realized being, whose will is one with God's. He asks to control his inner faculties (karaṇam) and reconcile the great philosophical paths of Siddhānta and Vedānta. The request for God to grant all his thoughts implies a state where his mind is so pure that every thought is already an expression of divine will. He seeks the siddhi (supernatural power) to do anything as an instrument of grace, living in an inseparable union with God.

translit: aruḷānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum aṇuttuṇaiyum ciṉaṅkāmam aṭaiyāmai vēṇṭum maruḷāya ulakamelām maruḷnīṅki ñāṉa maṉṟiṭattē vaḷḷaluṉai vāḻttiyiṭal vēṇṭum iruḷāmai uṟalvēṇṭum eṉaiaṭuttār cukamvāyn tiṭalvēṇṭum evvuyirum iṉpaṭaital vēṇṭum poruḷāmōr tiruvaṭivil uṭaiyāyum nāṉum puṇarntukalan toṉṟākip poruntutalvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: O Grace, you must listen to my request and bestow grace. I must not possess even an atom's worth of anger or desire. The entire deluded world must be freed from its delusion and praise you, the generous Patron, in the Hall of Wisdom. I must attain the state of being without darkness. Those who have approached me must attain happiness. All living beings must attain bliss. I desire that in your sacred form, the one true Substance, you, my Lord, and I unite, merge, become one, and perfectly abide.
commentary: This prayer links personal purity to the liberation of the entire world. Freedom from even a trace of anger or desire is sought as a condition for helping all of humanity awaken from its "delusion." The prayer that "all living beings must attain bliss" expresses the heart of his compassionate mission, seeing no separation between his own salvation and the well-being of others.

translit: amalānāṉ vēṇṭutalkēṭ ṭaruḷpurital vēṇṭum āṭiniṟkuñ cēvaṭiyaip pāṭiniṟka vēṇṭum emaṉātit taṭaieṉṟum eytāmai vēṇṭum ellāmcey vallatiṟaṉ eṉakkaḷittal vēṇṭum kamaiyātiaṭaintuyirkaḷ ellāmcaṉ mārkkam kātalittē tiruppotuvaik kaḷittēttal vēṇṭum vimalāti uṭaiyaoru tiruvaṭivil yāṉum vimalānī yuṅkalantē viḷaṅkutalvēṇ ṭuvaṉē.
translation: O Immaculate One, you must hear my requests and bestow your grace. I must stand and sing of the sacred red feet that dance. I must never encounter the obstacle of death or any other. You must grant me the all-accomplishing power. All living beings, having attained forbearance and other virtues, must come to love the Sanmarkkam and joyfully praise the sacred common space. And I desire that in a single sacred form, endowed with immaculateness and other virtues, you, O Immaculate One, and I should merge and shine forth as one.
commentary: The goal of spiritual life, in this verse, is to transcend the final limit of mortality itself. By asking to overcome the obstacle of Eman (the god of death), Vallalar seeks a state of being beyond physical decay. He desires this "all-accomplishing power" so he can help all beings discover the Sanmarkkam, the universal True Path. The ultimate end, repeated throughout these verses, is the complete and luminous merging of the soul with God.

Note 279

translit: tiruelām tarumōr teyvamām oruvaṉ tirucciṟṟam palantikaḻ kiṉṟāṉ uruelām uṇarcci uṭalporuḷ āvi uḷaelām āṅkavaṉ taṉakkē teruelām aṟiyak koṭuttaṉaṉ vēṟu ceyalilēṉ eṉaniṉait tiruntēṉ aruelām uṭaiyāy nīaṟin tatuvē aṭikkaṭi uraippateṉ niṉakkē.
translation: The One, a divine being who grants all prosperity, shines in the Thiru Chitrambalam All forms, feelings, body, possessions, life-breath, and all that exists belong to Him alone. For all the world to know, I have given everything to Him, thinking to myself, "I have no other action." O You who possess all grace! You already know this. Why should I keep repeating it to you?
commentary: True spiritual life begins with the radical act of giving everything back to God. Vallalar affirms that the One who shines in the Thiru Chitrambalam (the sacred hall of consciousness) is the true owner of his body, feelings, life, and possessions. Having consciously surrendered all, he finds he has no independent action left to perform. The verse ends with a tender, devotional complaint: since you are all-knowing, you already see the state of my heart.

translit: niṉaittapō tellām niṉṉaiyē niṉaittēṉ niṉaippaṟa niṉṟapō tellām eṉaittaṉi ākki niṉkaṇē niṉṟēṉ eṉceyal eṉṉaōr ceyalum tiṉaittaṉai eṉiṉum purintilēṉ ellām civaṉceya lāmeṉap purintēṉ aṉaittumeṉ aracē nīaṟin tatuvē aṭikkaṭi uraippateṉ niṉakkē.
translation: Whenever I thought, I thought only of you. Whenever I stood beyond thought, you made me solitary and I stood within you. As for my own action, I have not performed even a millet-seed's worth. I understood that everything is Siva's action. My King, you know all of this. Why should I keep repeating it to you?
commentary: In a state of total surrender, one's own thoughts and actions are no longer felt as personal. Vallalar explains that whenever he thinks, he thinks of God; when he moves beyond thought, he stands absorbed in God. He concludes that he has not performed even the smallest action from his own will, realizing that "everything is Siva's action." This is a re-identification where the self becomes an instrument of the divine.

translit: kaḷittapō tellām niṉiyal uṇarntē kaḷittaṉaṉ kaṇkaḷnīr tatumpit tuḷittapō tellām niṉaruḷ niṉaittē tuḷittaṉaṉ cūḻntavar uḷattait teḷittapō tellām niṉtiṟam pukaṉṟē teḷittaṉaṉ ceykaivē ṟaṟiyēṉ oḷittiru vuḷamē aṟintativ vaṉaittum uraippateṉ aṭikkaṭi uṉakkē.
translation: Whenever I rejoiced, I rejoiced only from realizing your nature. Whenever my eyes welled up and shed tears, they did so thinking of your grace. Whenever I clarified the minds of those around me, I did so by speaking of your greatness. I know no other action. Your radiant sacred will knows all this. Why should I keep repeating it to you?
commentary: Here, even the most personal feelings are revealed to have a divine source. Joy becomes a deep rejoicing in God's nature. Tears come from being moved by divine grace. In this state of complete surrender, every human experience becomes a channel for the divine.

translit: uṇṭatum porunti uvantatum uṟaṅki uṇarntatum ulakiyal uṇarvāl kaṇṭatum karutik kaḷittatum kalaikaḷ kaṟṟatum karaintatum kātal koṇṭatum niṉṉō ṭaṉṟināṉ taṉitteṉ kuṟippiṉil kuṟittatoṉ ṟilaiyē oṇtakum uṉatu tiruvuḷam aṟinta turaippateṉ aṭikkaṭi uṉakkē.
translation: What I ate, what I took pleasure in, my sleeping and waking, what I saw with worldly awareness, what I contemplated and rejoiced in, the arts I learned and spoke of, the love I felt: I have not intended a single one of these things on my own, apart from you. Your luminous and worthy sacred will knows this. Why should I keep repeating it to you?
commentary: This verse dissolves the boundary between spiritual and worldly life. For the surrendered soul, even the most mundane acts like eating, sleeping, or learning are not performed by a separate self. Every action and intention is intertwined with the divine, leaving no room for an independent personal life.

translit: kaḷavilē kaḷitta kālattum nīyē kaḷittaṉai nāṉkaḷit taṟiyēṉ uḷavilē uvanta pōtumnī tāṉē uvantaṉai nāṉuvan taṟiyēṉ koḷa:ilē camumōr kuṟippilēṉ aṉaittum kuṟittaṉai koṇṭaṉai nīyē aḷavilē ellām aṟintaṉai aracē aṭikkaṭi uraippateṉ niṉakkē.
translation: Even in times when I rejoiced in secret, it was you who rejoiced; I do not know how to rejoice. Even when I delighted openly, it was you yourself who delighted; I do not know how to delight. I have not the slightest intent to take anything. You intended all things and you took them. O King, you know everything immeasurably. Why should I keep repeating it to you?
commentary: This verse makes a bold claim about who is actually living our lives. The joy we feel, whether secret or open, is God rejoicing through us. The self, which believes it is the one feeling and choosing, is revealed to be a vessel for an experience that belongs entirely to the divine.

translit: tilakavāḷ nutalār tamaikkaṉa viṭattum ciṟitumnāṉ viḻaintilēṉ inta ulakavāḻ vatilōr aṇuttuṇai eṉiṉum uvappilēṉ ulakuṟu māyaik kalakavā taṉaitīr kālameṉ ṟuṟumō kaṭavuḷē eṉattuyarn tiruntēṉ alakilāt tiṟalōy nīaṟin tatunāṉ aṭikkaṭi uraippateṉ niṉakkē.
translation: Even in my dreams, I have not in the slightest desired women with bright, tilaka-adorned foreheads. I find not even an atom's worth of pleasure in this worldly life. I was in distress, wondering, "O God, when will the time come when the turbulent tendencies of worldly delusion are gone?" O one of limitless power, what you already know, why should I tell you again and again?
commentary: After declaring his complete surrender, Vallalar reveals the inner state that makes it possible: a deep detachment from worldly pleasures. He longs for the time when his vāsanai (ingrained mental impressions) will be dissolved. These are the turbulent, deep-seated habits of mind that keep the soul bound to worldly delusion, and his only sorrow is that they still remain.

translit: cātiyum matamum camayamum tavirntēṉ cāttirak kuppaiyum taṇantēṉ nītiyum nilaiyum cattiyap poruḷum nittiya vāḻkkaiyum cukamum ātiyum naṭuvum antamum illā aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ ṟaṟintēṉ ōtiya aṉaittum nīaṟin tatunāṉ uraippateṉ aṭikkaṭi uṉakkē.
translation: I have given up caste, religion, and creed. I have abandoned the rubbish heap of scriptures. I came to know that justice, the true state, the substance of Truth, eternal life, and bliss are the Vast Grace-Light, which has no beginning, middle, or end. All that I have said, you already know. Why should I tell you again and again?
commentary: The direct experience of God makes all conventional religion and scripture obsolete. Vallalar makes the radical statement that he has abandoned caste and creed and the entire "rubbish heap" of sacred texts. For him, the ultimate reality is the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), the living source of justice, truth, and eternal life itself.

translit: pittelām uṭaiya ulakartaṅ kalakap pitaṟṟelām eṉṟoḻin tiṭumō cattelām oṉṟeṉ ṟuṇarntacaṉ mārkka caṅkameṉ ṟōṅkumō talaimaic cittelām valla cittaṉeṉ ṟuṟumō terintilēṉ eṉattuyarn tiruntēṉ ottelām uṉatu tiruvuḷam aṟinta turaippateṉ aṭikkaṭi uṉakkē.
translation: I was in distress, lamenting: "When will all the chaotic babbling of these mad worldlings cease? When will the Sangam of Sanmarkkam, which has realized that all of existence is One, flourish? When will I become the Siddhan who is master of all supreme powers of consciousness? I do not know." Your sacred will knows all of this completely. Why should I tell you again and again?
commentary: Vallalar’s spiritual path is more than for personal salvation; it includes a powerful vision for the entire world. He aches for the day when humanity will stop its "chaotic babbling" and unite in a Sangam (community) of Sanmarkkam (the True Path), realizing the oneness of all existence. His personal desire to become a Siddhan (a master of perfected powers) is tied to this hope for a collective awakening.

translit: oṉṟeṉak kāṇum uṇarccieṉ ṟuṟumō ūḻitō ṟuḻiceṉ ṟiṭiṉum eṉṟumiṅ kiṟavā iyaṟkaieṉ ṟuṟumō iyalaruṭ cittikaḷ eṉaivan toṉṟaleṉ ṟuṟumō aṉaittumeṉ vacattē uṟutaleṉ ṟōeṉat tuyarntēṉ uṉtiru vuḷamē aṟintativ vaṉaittum uraippateṉ aṭikkaṭi uṉakkē.
translation: I was in distress, lamenting: "When will I attain the consciousness that sees all as One? When will I attain the nature of never dying here, even if eons upon eons pass? When will the natural grace-given powers come and unite with me? When will everything come under my control?" Your sacred will alone knows all of this. Why should I tell you again and again?
commentary: Here, Vallalar lists the highest goals of his path: seeing all as One, achieving physical immortality, and mastering all divine powers. The wish to never die means transforming the body into a deathless vessel of grace. Attaining the siddhis (supernatural powers) and having everything come under his control means perfectly aligning his will with the divine will, becoming a flawless instrument for its work in the world.

translit: kaḷḷāvā taṉaiyaik kaḷaintaruḷ neṟiyaik kātalit torumaiyil kalantē uḷḷavā ṟinta ulakelām kaḷippuṟ ṟōṅkutal eṉṟuvan tuṟumō vaḷḷalē atukaṇ ṭaṭiyaṉēṉ uḷḷam makiḻtaleṉ ṟōeṉat tuyarntēṉ oḷḷiyōy niṉatu tiruvuḷam aṟinta turaippateṉ aṭikkaṭi uṉakkē.
translation: I was in distress, lamenting: "When will the time come for the entire world to weed out its deceptive tendencies, to love the path of grace and merge into Oneness, to know things as they truly are, and to flourish in bliss? O generous benefactor, when will this servant's heart rejoice upon seeing that?" O Radiant One, what your sacred will knows, why should I tell you again and again?
commentary: The greatest joy is seeing all of humanity find happiness. Vallalar’s personal fulfillment depends on the awakening of the entire world. He longs for the day when everyone will cast off their inner deceptions, embrace the path of grace, and live together in a state of blissful Oneness. His own happiness is postponed until that collective joy is achieved.

translit: tiruuṭaiyāy ciṟcapaivāḻ civapatiyē ellām ceyyavalla taṉittalaimaic cittacikā maṇiyē uruuṭaieṉ uyirkkuyirāy oḷirkiṉṟa oḷiyē uṉṉutoṟum eṉṉuḷattē ūṟukiṉṟa amutē aruuṭaiya peruveḷiyāy atuviḷaṅku veḷiyāy appālu māyniṟainta aruṭperuñcō tiyaṉē maruuṭaiyāḷ civakāma vallimaṇa vāḷā vantaruḷka aruṭcōti tantaruḷka viraintē.
translation: O Lord of sacred grace! O Siva Pathi dwelling in the Chit Sabhai! O Citta Sikāmaṇi the sole sovereign who can accomplish all things! O Light that shines as the life of my embodied soul! O Amutham that wells up in my heart whenever I think of you! O ArutPerunJothi, who became the great formless space, the space where it shines, and who fills what is even beyond that! O Bridegroom of the fragrant Sivakama Valli! Come, bestow your grace! Grant the Grace-Light, and grant it quickly!
commentary: The poem begins by invoking God with a cascade of names, each revealing a different aspect of the divine. He is the Lord of the Hall of Consciousness (Chit Sabhai), the crest-jewel of perfected beings (Citta Sikāmaṇi), the light within the soul, and finally the formless Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi). The verse builds from abstract qualities to an intensely personal and urgent demand: "Come, and grant the Light, quickly."

translit: collavaṉē poruḷavaṉē turiyapatat tavaṉē tūyavaṉē nēyavaṉē cōtiuru vavaṉē nallavaṉē naṉṉitiyē ñāṉacapā patiyē nāyakaṉē tāyakaṉē naṇpavaṉē aṉaittum allavaṉē āṉavaṉē ammaiappā eṉṉai āṇṭavaṉē tāṇṭavaṉē aruṭkuruvē ellām vallavaṉē civakāma vallimaṇa vāḷā maṉṉavaṉē eṉṉavaṉē vantaruḷka viraintē.
translation: O You who are the Word and its Meaning! O You of the state of Turiya, O Pure One, Loving One, O You whose form is Jothi! O Good One! O goodly Treasure! O Lord of the Gñānasabai! O Leader, Motherly Refuge, and Friend! You who are none of these things, yet have become all of them! O Mother, Father, You who have taken me as your own! O Tāṇḍavaṉ! O Guru of Grace! O All-powerful One! O Bridegroom of Sivakama Valli! O King! O my very own! Come and bestow your grace, quickly!
commentary: The list of divine names continues, highlighting a central paradox of spiritual life. God is both the ultimate transcendent reality, like the fourth state of consciousness (Turiya), and an intimate, personal companion: a mother, father, and friend. Vallalar captures this mystery in the line, "You who are none of these things, yet have become all of them," before concluding with the tenderest claim, "O my very own!"

translit: turiyanilai tuṇintavarum collarummeyp poruḷē cuttacivā ṉantacapaic cittacikā maṇiyē periyaciva patiyēniṉ perumaiaṟin tiṭavē pērācaip paṭukiṉṟēṉ pittarkaḷil periyēṉ kariyamaṇit tiṟattiṉaiyum kāṇavallēṉ allēṉ kaṇmaṇiyē niṉtiṟattaik kāṇutalval lēṉō ariyaperum poruḷāmuṉ aruṭcōti eṉakkē aḷittaṉaiyēl aṟintukoḷvēṉ aḷittiṭuka viraintē.
translation: O true Substance, which even those who have decisively realized the Turiya state find difficult to describe! O Citta Sikāmaṇi of the Suddha Sivāṉanda Sabai! O great Siva Pathi, I have a immense craving to know your greatness. I am the greatest among madmen. I am unable to even perceive the nature of the dark jewel of your throat; O apple of my eye, will I ever be able to perceive your true nature? If you grant your Grace-Light to me, that rare and great substance, then I will know. Grant it, and grant it quickly!
commentary: The speaker expresses an almost unbearable "immense craving" (pērācai) to know God, calling himself the "greatest among madmen" for this desire. He feels utterly inadequate, unable to grasp even a small part of God's reality. From this place of humility, he concludes that human effort is futile. The only way to know God is for God to reveal Himself directly by granting His Grace-Light.

translit: maṟappaṟiyāp pēraṟivil vāyttaperuñ cukamē malaivaṟiyā nilainirampa vayaṅkiyacem poruḷē iṟappaṟiyāt tiruneṟiyileṉṉaivaḷart taruḷum eṉṉuṭaiya naṟṟāyē entāyē niṉatu ciṟappaṟiyā ulakamelām ciṟappaṟintu koḷavē cittacikā maṇiyēnī cittielām viḷaṅkap piṟappaṟiyāp peruntavarum viyappavantu taruvāy peruṅkaruṇai aracēnī taruntaruṇam ituvē.
translation: O great bliss attained in the supreme knowledge that knows no forgetting! O perfect Substance that brightly fills the state that knows no confusion! O my good mother and my father, who graciously nurtures me in the sacred path that knows no death! O Citta Sikāmaṇi, so that the entire world, which does not know your glory, may recognize it, you must come and give, making all Siddhis manifest, to the amazement of even the great ascetics who are beyond birth. O King of immense compassion, this is the very moment for you to give.
commentary: The focus of the prayer shifts from personal need to a universal one. Vallalar asks God to manifest His glory and powers (siddhis) so that the entire world, which is ignorant of Him, might see and believe. He wants a revelation so undeniable it would astonish even the most advanced sages. The personal plea becomes a call for a global awakening, and the time for it, he declares, is now.

translit: muṉṉuḻaippāl uṟumeṉavē moḻikiṉṟār moḻiyiṉ muṭivaṟiyēṉ ellāmcey muṉṉavaṉē nīeṉ taṉṉuḻaippārt taruḷvāyēl uṇṭaṉaittum oruniṉ taṉatucutan taramēiṅ keṉatucutan taramō eṉṉuḻaippāl eṉpayaṉō iraṅkiaru ḷāyēl yāṉāreṉ aṟivetumēl eṉṉaimatip pavarār poṉṉuḻaippāl peṟalumari taruḷilaiyēl ellām potunaṭañcey puṇṇiyanī eṇṇiyavā ṟāmē.
translation: Some say that attainment comes from one's own prior effort. I do not know the final truth of that statement. O You who were before all, You who accomplish everything, if you were to see my own effort and then bestow grace, is it not true that all that exists is your singular freedom alone? What freedom do I have here? What is the use of my own effort? If you do not take pity and grant your grace, who am I? What is my knowledge? And who would value me? Without grace, attainment is difficult even with the labor one expends for gold. O Sacred One who performs the universal dance, everything will happen only as you will it.
commentary: Vallalar confronts the idea that spiritual attainment comes from one's own effort. He questions this, arguing that our efforts are meaningless without God's compassionate grace. If all existence is an expression of God's singular freedom, he asks, what real freedom or power do we have? He concludes that personal effort is worth nothing on its own; everything that happens is simply God's will.

translit: viḻittuviḻit timaittālum cuṭarutayam ilaiyēl viḻikaḷviḻit tiḷaippatalāl viḷaivoṉṟum ilaiyē moḻittiṟañcey taṭikkaṭināṉ muṭukimuyaṉ ṟālum muṉṉavaniṉ peruṅkaruṇai muṉṉiṭaliṉ ṟeṉilō ceḻittuṟunaṟ payaṉetuvō tiruvuḷantāṉ iraṅkil ciṟuturumpōr aintoḻilum ceytiṭalcat tiyamē paḻitturaippār uraikkaelām pacupatiniṉ ceyalē parinteṉaiyum pāṭuvittup paricumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: Even if I keep my eyes open and blink repeatedly, if the flame does not dawn, there is no result other than my eyes growing weary. Even if I use my skill with words and strive again and again, O Foremost One, if Your great grace does not come forward, what prosperous, good result can there be? If Your sacred will shows compassion, it is a truth that even a tiny blade of grass can perform the five cosmic functions. Let the critics say what they will; everything is Your doing, Pasupathi. Lovingly make me sing, and be pleased to grant me the prize.
commentary: Spiritual striving without grace is like trying to see in a room with no light. You can strain your eyes all you want, but you will only grow tired. In the same way, all poetic and spiritual efforts are useless unless God's grace comes forward. With that grace, however, anything is possible: even a tiny blade of grass could perform the five great cosmic acts. He ends by accepting that everything, including the criticism of others, is the doing of Pasupathi, the Lord of all beings.

translit: mānirupā tiparcūḻa maṇimuṭitāṉ poṟuttē maṇṇāḷa vāṉāḷa maṉattilniṉait tēṉō tēṉoruvā moḻicciyarait tiḷaikkaviḻain tēṉō tīñcuvaikaḷ virumpiṉaṉō tīmaikaḷcey tēṉō nāṉorupā vamumaṟiyēṉ naṉṉitiyē eṉatu nāyakaṉē potuviḷaṅkum naṭarāja patiyē ēṉorumai ilarpōlnī irukkiṉṟāy aḻakō eṉorumai aṟiyāyō yāvumaṟin tāyē.
translation: Surrounded by great kings and wearing a jeweled crown, did I ever think of ruling the earth and the heavens? Did I long to delight in women whose words are like unending honey? Did I desire sweet tastes? Did I do evil things? I am not aware of any sin. O my good treasure! My Lord! O Nataraja Pathi, who shines forth in the sacred Hall! Why do you act like someone who lacks unity? Is this right? Do you not know my own state of unity, you who know all things?
commentary: Vallalar makes a heartfelt declaration of his motives, insisting he has never craved worldly power, sensual pleasures, or committed any sins he is aware of. His focus has been singularly on God. He then asks a poignant question to the Divine Dancer, Nataraja Pathi (Lord Nataraja): "You know all things, and you know my heart is unified in its devotion to you. Why, then, do you act so distant?" It is a lover's complaint, an intimate challenge from a devotee for God to be true to His all-knowing nature.

translit: pāvimaṉak kuraṅkāṭṭam pārkkamuṭi yātē pativeṟuttēṉ nitiveṟuttēṉ paṟṟaṉaittum tavirntēṉ āviuṭal poruḷaiuṉpāṟ koṭuttēṉuṉ aruṭpē rācaimaya mākiuṉai aṭuttumuyal kiṉṟēṉ kūvieṉai āṭkoḷḷa niṉaiyāyō niṉatu kuṟippaṟiyēṉ paṟpalakāl kūṟiiḷaik kiṉṟēṉ tēviciva kāmavalli makiḻummaṇa vāḷā teruḷniṟaivāṉ amutaḷikkum taruṇamitu tāṉē.
translation: I cannot bear to watch the dance of my sinful monkey-mind. I have renounced my home, renounced wealth, and given up all attachments. I have given my life, body, and possessions to You. Having become entirely a being of great desire for Your grace, I strive, drawing near to You. Will You not consider calling out and enslaving me? I do not understand Your intention; I say this many times and grow weary. O Bridegroom who delights the Goddess Sivakamavalli, this is the very moment to grant me the ambrosia filled with clarity.
commentary: The restless, uncontrollable nature of the mind is so unbearable that it drove Vallalar to abandon every worldly attachment. He describes his mind as a "sinful monkey" whose antics he cannot stand to watch. This inner torment led him to renounce his home, wealth, and his very self, giving everything over to God. Now, possessed by a "great desire" for grace alone, he pleads with the bridegroom of the goddess Sivakamavalli (the consort of Siva at Chidambaram) to accept him, insisting the moment is now.

translit: kaṭṭaviḻnta kamalameṉak karuttaviḻntu niṉaiyē karutukiṉṟēṉ vēṟoṉṟum karutukilēṉ itutāṉ ciṭṭaruḷam tikaḻkiṉṟa civapatiyē niṉatu tiruvuḷamē aṟintatunāṉ cepputaleṉ puvimēl viṭṭakuṟai toṭṭakuṟai iraṇṭumniṟain taṉaṉnī viraintuvantē aruṭcōti purintaruḷum taruṇam toṭṭatunāṉ tuṇainturaittēṉ nīuṇartta uṇarntē colvatalāl eṉaṟivāl collavallēṉ aṉṟē.
translation: Like a lotus that has unbound its petals, my mind has unfolded and I think only of You; I think of nothing else. O Sivapati who shines in the hearts of the virtuous, Your sacred will alone knows this. What is there for me to say on this earth? The karma left over and the karma newly made are both resolved. This is the moment for You to come swiftly and graciously bestow the grace-light, I have touched on this and spoken boldly, but I only say what I have understood as You revealed it. I am not able to speak from my own knowledge.
commentary: Vallalar describes his mind as having unfolded completely toward God, like a lotus opening its petals. He insists this state is a reality that Sivapati (Lord Siva) alone knows and has revealed to him. He declares that the consequences of his past actions (karma) are now resolved. This makes it the perfect moment for God to come and bestow the grace-light (Arut Jothi). He is simply reporting what grace has already shown him.

translit: kāṭṭaielām kaṭantuviṭṭēṉ nāṭṭaiaṭain tuṉatu kaṭinakarppoṉ matiṟkāṭci kaṇkuḷirak kaṇṭēṉ kōṭṭaielām koṭināṭṭik kōlamiṭap pārttēṉ kōyiliṉmēl vāyililē kuṟaikaḷelām tavirntēṉ cēṭṭaiaṟṟuk karuvielām eṉvacamniṉ ṟiṭavē cittielām peṟṟēṉnāṉ tirucciṟṟam palamēl pāṭṭaielām pāṭukiṉṟēṉ itutaruṇam patiyē palantarumeṉ uḷantaṉilē kalantuniṟain taruḷē.
translation: I have passed through all the forests and reached the country; I have seen the sight of Your guarded city's golden walls, a vision that cooled my eyes. I saw the fortress adorned with planted flags and beautiful patterns. At the temple's upper gate, all my failings were removed. With all restlessness gone and my inner faculties under my control, I have obtained all the siddhis. I am singing all the songs about the sacred Chitrambalam. This is the moment, O Master! Graciously merge with and fill my heart, which will then bear fruit.
commentary: Using the image of travel, Vallalar declares he has passed through the wilderness of spiritual struggle and arrived at God's sacred city. At the gates of this inner temple, his flaws fell away, his restless mind and senses came under his control, and he obtained all spiritual powers (siddhis). Having arrived and fully prepared himself, he announces that the time for union is now, asking the Master to merge completely with his being so it may finally bear fruit.

translit: cittielām vallaciva cittaṉuḷam kalantāṉ cettārai eḻuppukiṉṟa tirunāḷkaḷ aṭutta ittiṉamē toṭaṅkiaḻi yātanilai aṭaitaṟ kēṟṟakuṟi ēṟṟaviṭat ticaintiyalkiṉ ṟaṉanām cattiyamē peruvāḻvil peruṅkaḷippuṟ ṟiṭutal cantēkit talaiyātē cāṟṟiyaeṉ moḻiyai nittiyavāṉ moḻieṉṉa niṉaintumakiḻ tamaivāy neñcēnī añcēluḷ añcēlañ cēlē.
translation: The Siva Siddha, master of all siddhis, has mingled with my heart. The sacred days for raising the dead are drawing near. Beginning this very day, the right signs for attaining the imperishable state are manifesting harmoniously in the right place. It is a certainty that we will rejoice greatly in the great life; do not doubt and wander. Consider the words I have spoken to be the eternal, celestial word, and be joyful and at peace. O Heart, you must not fear; do not fear within; do not fear at all.
commentary: In a triumphant shift of tone, Vallalar announces that union with God is real and the time for miracles, even raising the dead, is here. The "Siva Siddha," a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis), has merged with his heart. He speaks directly to his own heart, commanding it to stop all fear and doubt. What he says is an eternal truth, he declares, promising a great life of absolute joy. The devotee is no longer pleading for grace but has become a confident vehicle for it.
NOTES
Note 254

tamil: திருநிலையில் - முதற் பதிப்பு, பொ. சு., பி. இரா.
translit: tirunilaiyil - mutaṟ patippu, po. cu., pi. irā.
translation: tirunilaiyil — reading of the first edition, the Po. Su. edition, and the P. Irā. edition.

tamil: பொழுது விடிந்த தினிச்சிறிதும் பொறுத்து முடியேன் எனநின்றே
அழுது விழிகள் நீர்துளும்பக் கூவிக் கூவி அயர்கின்றேன்
பழுது தவிர்க்கும் திருச்செவிக்குள் பட்ட திலையோ பலகாலும்
உழுது களைத்த மாடனையேன் துணைவே றறியேன் உடையானே.
translit: poḻutu viṭinta tiṉicciṟitum poṟuttu muṭiyēṉ eṉaniṉṟē aḻutu viḻikaḷ nīrtuḷumpak kūvik kūvi ayarkiṉṟēṉ paḻutu tavirkkum tiruccevikkuḷ paṭṭa tilaiyō palakālum uḻutu kaḷaitta māṭaṉaiyēṉ tuṇaivē ṟaṟiyēṉ uṭaiyāṉē.
translation: The day has dawned. I cannot bear it even a moment longer. I stand weeping, my eyes overflowing with tears, calling out to you again and again until I grow weary. Has my cry, repeated so many times, not reached your sacred ear that removes all faults? Like an ox exhausted from plowing, I know no other support, O my Master.
commentary: The speaker's spiritual suffering has become unbearable. He feels like a farm animal worked to the point of collapse, with no one else to turn to. The dawn of a new day brings no relief, only a renewed and desperate sense that he cannot endure the separation from God a moment longer.

tamil: உடையாய் திருஅம் பலத்தாடல் ஒருவா ஒருவா உலவாத
கொடையாய் எனநான் நின்றனையே கூவிக் கூவி அயர்கின்றேன்
தடையா யினதீர்த் தருளாதே தாழ்க்கில் அழகோ புலைநாயிற்
கடையாய்த் திரிந்தேன் கலங்குதல்சம் மதமோ கருணைக் கருத்தினுக்கே.
translit: uṭaiyāy tiruam palattāṭal oruvā oruvā ulavāta koṭaiyāy eṉanāṉ niṉṟaṉaiyē kūvik kūvi ayarkiṉṟēṉ taṭaiyā yiṉatīrt taruḷātē tāḻkkil aḻakō pulaināyiṟ kaṭaiyāyt tirintēṉ kalaṅkutalcam matamō karuṇaik karuttiṉukkē.
translation: O my Master! O peerless One who never ceases your dance in the sacred hall! O inexhaustible Munificence! I stand calling out to you again and again until I am weary. If you delay, not removing my obstacles and bestowing your grace, is that fitting? I have wandered about, lower than a vile dog. Is my distress acceptable to your mind of compassion?
commentary: The plea intensifies, addressing God as the one who performs the eternal dance in the sacred hall, the ambalam. Comparing himself to something lower than a stray dog, the speaker questions whether his prolonged suffering is fitting for a God whose very nature is compassion. It is a cry of anguish, asking why God would delay in removing the obstacles to their union.

tamil: கருணைக் கருத்து மலர்ந்தெனது கலக்க மனைத்துந் தவிர்த்தேஇத்
தருணத் தருளா விடில்அடியேன் தரியேன் தளர்வேன் தளர்வதுதான்
அருணச் சுடரே நின்னருளுக் கழகோ அழகென் றிருப்பாயேல்
translit: karuṇaik karuttu malarnteṉatu kalakka maṉaittun tavirttēit taruṇat taruḷā viṭilaṭiyēṉ tariyēṉ taḷarvēṉ taḷarvatutāṉ aruṇac cuṭarē niṉṉaruḷuk kaḻakō aḻakeṉ ṟiruppāyēl teruṇaṟ patañcār aṉparelāmcirippār nāṉum tikaippēṉē.
translation: O Flame of dawn-red light! Unless your compassionate mind blossoms right now to remove all my turmoil, unless you grant your grace at this very moment, I, your slave, will not survive. I will falter. And would my faltering be a good thing for your grace? If you were to think it as right, all the devotees who have reached the clear, good state would laugh, and I too would be bewildered.
commentary: The plea reaches a critical point: without grace at this very moment, the speaker feels he will spiritually collapse. He then makes a powerful emotional appeal, asking if his failure would bring honor to God's grace. Other perfected devotees would surely find such an outcome strange, leaving him shamed and bewildered. This is an argument born of desperation, suggesting that God's own reputation for compassion is on the line.

tamil: திகைப்பார் திகைக்க நான்சிறிதும் திகையேன் எனநின் திருவடிக்கே
வகைப்பா மாலை சூட்டுகின்றேன் மற்றொன் றறியேன் சிறியேற்குத்
தகைப்பா ரிடைஇத் தருணத்தே தாராய் எனிலோ பிறரெல்லாம்
நகைப்பார் நகைக்க உடம்பினைவைத் திருத்தல் அழகோ நாயகனே.
translit: tikaippār tikaikka nāṉciṟitum tikaiyēṉ eṉaniṉ tiruvaṭikkē vakaippā mālai cūṭṭukiṉṟēṉ maṟṟoṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ ciṟiyēṟkut takaippā riṭaiit taruṇattē tārāy eṉilō piṟarellām nakaippār nakaikka uṭampiṉaivait tiruttal aḻakō nāyakaṉē.
translation: Let those who are bewildered remain bewildered; I will not be dismayed in the slightest. With that resolve, I place a garland of varied verses at your sacred feet. I know nothing else. If you do not give to me, this lowly one, at this very moment in this world of hindrances, everyone else will laugh. And while they laugh, is it fitting to keep this body, O my Lord?
commentary: Amidst the turmoil, a defiant faith emerges. The speaker resolves to continue his worship through poetry, which he calls a "garland of varied verses," presenting this act of creation as his only recourse. He then makes a final, desperate appeal, questioning the value of his own life if God allows him to become an object of public shame.

tamil: நாயிற் கடையேன் கலக்கமெலாம் தவிர்த்து நினது நல்லருளை
ஈயிற் கருணைப் பெருங்கடலே என்னே கெடுவ தியற்கையிலே
சேயிற் கருதி அணைத்தான்என் றுரைப்பா ருனைத்தான் தெரிந்தோரே.
translit: nāyiṟ kaṭaiyēṉ kalakkamelām tavirttu niṉatu nallaruḷai īyiṟ karuṇaip peruṅkaṭalē eṉṉē keṭuva tiyaṟkaiyilē tāyiṟ peritumtayavuṭaiyāṉ kuṟṟam purintōṉ taṉṉaiyumōr cēyiṟ karuti aṇaittāṉeṉ ṟuraippā ruṉaittāṉ terintōrē.
translation: O great ocean of compassion! If you were to remove all the turmoil of this one who is lower than a dog, and bestow your good grace, what would be lost from your very nature? Indeed, those who truly know you declare: "He whose compassion is greater than a mother's considers even one who has done wrong to be a child and embraces him."
commentary: The argument shifts to God's own nature, asking what could possibly be lost by showing mercy. Vallalar uses a deeply moving analogy: God's compassion is even greater than a mother's, who embraces her child regardless of its faults. This redefines the relationship, appealing to a loving parent whose very identity is unconditional grace.

tamil: தெரிந்த பெரியர்க் கருள்புரிதல் சிறப்பென் றுரைத்த தெய்வமறை
திரிந்த சிறியர்க் கருள்புரிதல் சிறப்பிற் சிறப்பென் றுரைத்தனவே
புரிந்தம் மறையைப் புகன்றவனும் நீயே என்றால் புண்ணியனே
விரிந்த மனத்துச் சிறியேனுக் கிரங்கி அருளல் வேண்டாவோ.
translit: terinta periyark karuḷpurital ciṟappeṉ ṟuraitta teyvamaṟai tirinta ciṟiyark karuḷpurital ciṟappiṟ ciṟappeṉ ṟuraittaṉavē purintam maṟaiyaip pukaṉṟavaṉum nīyē eṉṟāl puṇṇiyaṉē virinta maṉattuc ciṟiyēṉuk kiraṅki aruḷal vēṇṭāvō.
translation: The sacred scriptures declare it is excellent to bestow grace on the great and wise, and they declare it is the excellence of excellences to bestow grace on the small and wayward. If you are the very one who uttered those scriptures, O Virtuous One, should you not then take pity on me, a small person with a scattered mind, and bestow your grace?
commentary: Here, the speaker uses scripture to build his case, turning his own unworthiness into his greatest strength. He argues that while showing grace to the worthy is good, the ultimate expression of divinity is saving the "small and wayward." By identifying with the flawed, he presents himself as the perfect opportunity for God to demonstrate this supreme form of compassion.

tamil: வேண்டார் உளரோ நின்னருளை மேலோ ரன்றிக் கீழோரும்
ஈண்டார் வதற்கு வேண்டினரால் இன்று புதிதோ யான்வேண்டல்
தூண்டா விளக்கே திருப்பொதுவிற் சோதி மணியே ஆறொடுமூன்
றாண்டா வதிலே முன்னென்னை ஆண்டாய் கருணை அளித்தருளே.
translit: vēṇṭār uḷarō niṉṉaruḷai mēlō raṉṟik kīḻōrum īṇṭār vataṟku vēṇṭiṉarāl iṉṟu putitō yāṉvēṇṭal tūṇṭā viḷakkē tiruppotuviṟ cōti maṇiyē āṟoṭumūṉ ṟāṇṭā vatilē muṉṉeṉṉai āṇṭāy karuṇai aḷittaruḷē.
translation: Is there anyone who does not want Your grace? The high and the low alike eagerly desire it here. Is my asking for it something new today? O Lamp that needs no trimming, O Gem of Light in the sacred common space! You took me in when I was nine years old. Grant me compassion, grace me!
commentary: The argument culminates in a powerful personal appeal, reminding God of their shared history. Vallalar refers to a specific mystical experience in his childhood when he first felt divine grace, asking why that same compassion would be withheld now. This transforms the plea from a general argument into an intimate reminder: "You chose me once before; do not abandon me now."

tamil: அருளே வடிவாம் அரசேநீ அருளா விடில்இவ் வடியேனுக்
கிருளே தொலைய அருளளிப்பார் எவரே எல்லாம் வல்லோய்நின்
பொருளேய் வடிவிற் கலைஒன்றே புறத்தும் அகத்தும் புணர்ந்தெங்குந்
தெருளே யுறஎத் தலைவருக்குஞ் சிறந்த அருளாய்த் திகழ்வதுவே.
translit: aruḷē vaṭivām aracēnī aruḷā viṭiliv vaṭiyēṉuk kiruḷē tolaiya aruḷaḷippār evarē ellām vallōyniṉ poruḷēy vaṭiviṟ kalaioṉṟē puṟattum akattum puṇarnteṅkun teruḷē yuṟaet talaivarukkuñ ciṟanta aruḷāyt tikaḻvatuvē.
translation: O King whose very form is grace, if you do not show grace, who else is there to grant it to this servant and dispel my darkness? O Omnipotent One! A single portion of your substantive form unites with the outer and inner worlds, bringing clarity everywhere and shining as the supreme grace for all masters.
commentary: The argument here rests on a simple, powerful idea: there is no other source of grace but God. If God, whose very nature is grace, withholds it, then the soul is left in total darkness. Vallalar adds that even a tiny fragment of God's reality is powerful enough to bring light and clarity to the entire universe, both inside and out.

tamil: திகழ்ந்தார் கின்ற திருப்பொதுவில் சிவமே நின்னைத் தெரிந்துகொண்டு
புகழ்ந்தார் தம்மைப் பொறுத்திடவும் புன்மை அறிவால் பொய்உரைத்தே
இகழ்ந்தேன் தனைக்கீழ் வீழ்த்திடவும் என்னே புவிக்கிங் கிசைத்திலைநீ
அகழ்ந்தார் தமையும் பொறுக்கஎன அமைத்தாய் எல்லாம் அமைத்தாயே.
translit: tikaḻntār kiṉṟa tiruppotuvil civamē niṉṉait terintukoṇṭu pukaḻntār tammaip poṟuttiṭavum puṉmai aṟivāl poyuraittē ikaḻntēṉ taṉaikkīḻ vīḻttiṭavum eṉṉē puvikkiṅ kicaittilainī akaḻntār tamaiyum poṟukkaeṉa amaittāy ellām amaittāyē.
translation: O Sivam in the shining, full, sacred common space! Why have you not decreed to the world that you would support those who understand and praise you, and cast down me, who, with base knowledge, spoke lies and scorned you? Instead, you established the principle: "Forgive even those who dig you up." You have ordained everything.
commentary: Vallalar marvels at the unexpected nature of divine law. He asks why God has not established a simple rule of rewarding the faithful and punishing people like him who have been scornful. Instead, he finds that God's principle is one of radical forgiveness, like the earth that sustains even those who dig into it. This reveals a God of infinite patience rather than one of strict justice.

tamil: எல்லாம் வகுத்தாய் எனக்கருளில் யாரே தடுப்பார் எல்லாஞ்செய்
வல்லான் வகுத்த வண்ணம்என மகிழ்வார் என்கண் மணியேஎன்
சொல்லா னவையும் அணிந்துகொண்ட துரையே சோதித் திருப்பொதுவில்
நல்லாய் கருணை நடத்தரசே தருணம் இதுநீ நயந்தருளே.
translit: ellām vakuttāy eṉakkaruḷil yārē taṭuppār ellāñcey vallāṉ vakutta vaṇṇameṉa makiḻvār eṉkaṇ maṇiyēeṉ collā ṉavaiyum aṇintukoṇṭa turaiyē cōtit tiruppotuvil nallāy karuṇai naṭattaracē taruṇam itunī nayantaruḷē.
translation: You have ordained everything. If you grant me grace, who can stop it? All will rejoice, saying, "It is as the all-powerful one has decreed." O apple of my eye! O Master who has worn even my garlands of words! O Good One in the luminous sacred common space! O King of the compassionate dance! This is the moment. Please desire it and grant your grace.
commentary: The tone shifts from pleading to confident assertion. Because God's power is absolute, no one can object if grace is given; everyone will simply accept it as the divine will. The language becomes deeply intimate, with Vallalar calling God "apple of my eye" and urging that "this is the moment" for grace to be granted. It is a call for God to enact a decision that only God can make.

tamil: நயந்த கருணை நடத்தரசே ஞான அமுதே நல்லோர்கள்
வியந்த மணியே மெய்யறிவாம் விளக்கே என்னை விதித்தோனே
கயந்த மனத்தேன் எனினும்மிகக் கலங்கி நரகக் கடுங்கடையில்
பயந்த பொழுதும் தாழ்த்திருத்தல் அழகோ கடைக்கண் பார்த்தருளே.
translit: nayanta karuṇai naṭattaracē ñāṉa amutē nallōrkaḷ viyanta maṇiyē meyyaṟivām viḷakkē eṉṉai vitittōṉē kayanta maṉattēṉ eṉiṉummikak kalaṅki narakak kaṭuṅkaṭaiyil payanta poḻutum tāḻttiruttal aḻakō kaṭaikkaṇ pārttaruḷē.
translation: O King of the dance of desired compassion! O nectar of wisdom! O gem that good people marvel at! O lamp of true knowledge, the one who created me! Although I have a base mind, when I am deeply agitated and fearful in the harsh ocean of hell, is it fitting for you to delay? Look upon me from the corner of your eye and grant your grace.
commentary: This is a cry of desperation from the depths of suffering. Vallalar lists God's glorious qualities, then contrasts them with his own base mind and terror. He asks a poignant question: is it fitting for such a compassionate creator to delay helping when his creation is in such agony? The final request for a mere glance "from the corner of your eye" emphasizes how a small act of divine attention is all that is needed for salvation.

tamil: பார்த்தார் இரங்கச் சிறியேன்நான் பாவி மனத்தால் பட்டதுயர்
தீர்த்தாய் அந்நாள் அதுதொடங்கித் தெய்வந் துணைஎன் றிருக்கின்றேன்
ஈர்த்தால் அதுகண் டிருப்பதுவோ கருணைக் கழகிங் கெந்தாயே.
translit: pārttār iraṅkac ciṟiyēṉnāṉ pāvi maṉattāl paṭṭatuyar tīrttāy annāḷ atutoṭaṅkit teyvan tuṇaieṉ ṟirukkiṉṟēṉ cērttārulakil innāḷil ciṟiyēṉ taṉaiven tuyarppāvi īrttāl atukaṇ ṭiruppatuvō karuṇaik kaḻakiṅ kentāyē.
translation: On that day, you put an end to the suffering this lowly one endured because of my sinful mind, which made onlookers pity me. From then on, I have lived believing that God is my support. In this world of attachments, if the sin of fierce suffering drags this lowly one down today, will you just stand by and watch? Is that beautiful for compassion, my mother?
commentary: This is a powerful appeal based on a past relationship. Vallalar reminds God of a previous rescue, which became the foundation of his faith. Now that suffering has returned, he questions whether God will simply watch, framing it as a matter of divine character. The address "my mother" makes the plea deeply personal and urgent.

tamil: தாயே எனைத்தான் தந்தவனே தலைவா ஞான சபாபதியே
பேயேன் செய்த பெருங்குற்றம் பொறுத்தாட் கொண்ட பெரியோனே
நீயே இந்நாள் முகமறியார் நிலையில் இருந்தால் நீடுலகில்
நாயே அனையேன் எவர்துணைஎன் றெங்கே புகுவேன் நவிலாயே.
translit: tāyē eṉaittāṉ tantavaṉē talaivā ñāṉa capāpatiyē pēyēṉ ceyta peruṅkuṟṟam poṟuttāṭ koṇṭa periyōṉē nīyē innāḷ mukamaṟiyār nilaiyil iruntāl nīṭulakil nāyē aṉaiyēṉ evartuṇaieṉ ṟeṅkē pukuvēṉ navilāyē.
translation: O Mother! O Father who gave me myself! O Leader! O Lord of the hall of wisdom! O Great one who forgave the great faults committed by this ghoul-like one and enslaved me! If you, today, act as if you do not know me, where in this vast world will I, who am like a dog, go for refuge, crying "Who is my support?" Please tell me.
commentary: The feeling here is one of utter dependence and the fear of being abandoned. Vallalar lists God's roles as parent, master, and redeemer, reminding God of their shared history of forgiveness. His greatest fear is that God might now act like a stranger, leaving him with nowhere to turn for refuge. The Jnana Sabai is the hall of pure wisdom-consciousness.

tamil: ஆயேன் வேதா கமங்களைநன் கறியேன் சிறியேன் அவலமிகும்
பேயேன் எனினும் வலிந்தென்னைப் பெற்ற கருணைப் பெருமானே
நீயே அருள நினைத்தாயேல் எல்லா நலமும் நிரம்புவன்நான்
காயே எனினும் கனிஆகும் அன்றே நினது கருணைக்கே.
translit: āyēṉ vētā kamaṅkaḷainaṉ kaṟiyēṉ ciṟiyēṉ avalamikum pēyēṉ eṉiṉum valinteṉṉaip peṟṟa karuṇaip perumāṉē nīyē aruḷa niṉaittāyēl ellā nalamum nirampuvaṉnāṉ kāyē eṉiṉum kaṉiākum aṉṟē niṉatu karuṇaikkē.
translation: I have not studied the Vedas and Agamas well. Though I am a lowly, miserable ghoul, O great Lord of compassion who forcefully took me as your own! If you decide to grant your grace, I will become full of every good thing. Is it not so that for your compassion, even an unripe fruit becomes ripe?
commentary: Human effort and scriptural knowledge are not the basis for grace. Vallalar admits he lacks religious learning and feels worthless, but this does not matter because God's compassion chose him regardless of his merit. The final line beautifully illustrates the power of grace: just as a glance can ripen a fruit, a moment of divine compassion can perfect an imperfect soul.

tamil: கருணா நிதியே என்இரண்டு கண்ணே கண்ணிற் கலந்தொளிரும்
தெருணா டொளியே வெளியேமெய்ச் சிவமே சித்த சிகாமணியே
இருணா டுலகில் அறிவின்றி இருக்கத் தரியேன் இதுதருணம்
தருணா அடியேற் கருட்சோதி தருவாய் என்முன் வருவாயே.
translit: karuṇā nitiyē eṉiraṇṭu kaṇṇē kaṇṇiṟ kalantoḷirum teruṇā ṭoḷiyē veḷiyēmeyc civamē citta cikāmaṇiyē iruṇā ṭulakil aṟiviṉṟi irukkat tariyēṉ itutaruṇam taruṇā aṭiyēṟ karuṭcōti taruvāy eṉmuṉ varuvāyē.
translation: O treasure of compassion! O my two eyes! O light of clear wisdom that mingles and shines within my eyes! O expanse! O true Sivam! O crest-jewel of the Siddhas! I cannot bear to live without knowledge in this dark world. This is the moment. O youthful one, grant your grace-Jothi to this slave. Come before me.
commentary: The experience of God's absence is felt as a kind of spiritual blindness in a dark world. God is the very light of perception within one's own eyes. The plea is a desperate cry for illumination, for the arrival of the grace-Jothi (light of grace) that will end the darkness of ignorance. This light is the goal of all perfected beings, the Siddhas.

tamil: வருவாய் என்கண் மணிநீஎன் மனத்திற் குறித்த வண்ணமெலாம்
தருவாய் தருணம் இதுவேமெய்த் தலைவா ஞான சபாபதியே
இருவாய் அலநின் திருவடிப்பாட் டிசைக்கும் ஒருவாய் இசைத்தேனே.
translit: varuvāy eṉkaṇ maṇinīeṉ maṉattiṟ kuṟitta vaṇṇamelām taruvāy taruṇam ituvēmeyt talaivā ñāṉa capāpatiyē uruvāyciṟitu tāḻkkiluyir oruvum uraittēṉ eṉṉuṭaivāy iruvāy alaniṉ tiruvaṭippāṭ ṭicaikkum oruvāy icaittēṉē.
translation: Come, you who are the apple of my eye. Grant everything I have conceived in my mind. This is the very moment, O true Leader, Lord of the Hall of Wisdom. If you delay in manifesting your form even a little, my life will leave me. I have spoken. My mouth is not a duplicitous one; it is the single mouth that sings in praise of your sacred feet.
commentary: The plea for God's presence now intensifies into a matter of life and death. Vallalar declares that if God, the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom, delays in appearing, his life will end. This expresses total dependence, where life itself is sustained only by the divine connection. He assures God of his sincerity, stating that his prayer is the single, honest cry of his entire being.

tamil: தேனே திருச்சிற் றம்பலத்தில் தெள்ளா ரமுதே சிவஞான
வானே ஞான சித்தசிகா மணியே என்கண் மணியேஎன்
ஊனே புகுந்தென் உளங்கலந்த உடையாய் அடியேன் உவந்திடநீ
தானே மகிழ்ந்து தந்தாய்இத் தருணம் கைம்மா றறியேனே.
translit: tēṉē tirucciṟ ṟampalattil teḷḷā ramutē civañāṉa vāṉē ñāṉa cittacikā maṇiyē eṉkaṇ maṇiyēeṉ ūṉē pukunteṉ uḷaṅkalanta uṭaiyāy aṭiyēṉ uvantiṭanī tāṉē makiḻntu tantāyit taruṇam kaimmā ṟaṟiyēṉē.
translation: O Honey! O clear, rare nectar in the sacred little hall! O sky of Siva-wisdom, crest-jewel of perfected wisdom, apple of my eye! O Master who entered my flesh and mingled with my being! For me, your devotee, to rejoice, you yourself happily gave this. At this moment, I know no way to repay you.
commentary: The desperate plea has been answered, and the tone shifts to one of blissful gratitude. God's presence is experienced as an overwhelming sweetness, a nectar discovered within the Thiru Chitrambalam (the sacred inner space). This union is not abstract but physical and total, as God enters his very flesh and mingles with his being. Faced with a gift given so freely, Vallalar is left speechless, knowing there is no possible way to repay such infinite grace.

tamil: அறியேன் சிறியேன் செய்தபிழை அனைத்தும் பொறுத்தாய் அருட்சோதிக்
குறியே குணமே பெறஎன்னைக் குறிக்கொண் டளித்தாய் சன்மார்க்க
நெறியே விளங்க எனைக்கலந்து நிறைந்தாய் நின்னை ஒருகணமும்
பிறியேன் பிறியேன் இறவாமை பெற்றேன் உற்றேன் பெருஞ்சுகமே.
translit: aṟiyēṉ ciṟiyēṉ ceytapiḻai aṉaittum poṟuttāy aruṭcōtik kuṟiyē kuṇamē peṟaeṉṉaik kuṟikkoṇ ṭaḷittāy caṉmārkka neṟiyē viḷaṅka eṉaikkalantu niṟaintāy niṉṉai orukaṇamum piṟiyēṉ piṟiyēṉ iṟavāmai peṟṟēṉ uṟṟēṉ peruñcukamē.
translation: You forgave all the wrongs committed by me, this ignorant, lowly one. You singled me out and granted grace so I would receive the mark and quality of the Grace-Jothi. You mingled with me and filled me, making the path of Sanmarkkam shine. I will not be separate from you for even a moment; I will not be separate. I have attained deathlessness; I have reached a state of great bliss.
commentary: Here, Vallalar describes the results of the divine union: complete forgiveness, transformation, and the attainment of immortality. His past failings are erased as God fills him with the qualities of the Grace-Jothi (light of grace). This inner merging illuminates the true path, or Sanmarkkam. The final state is one of triumphant bliss and deathlessness, where he vows he will never again be separate from the divine.

tamil: சுகமே நிரம்பப் பெருங்கருணைத் தொட்டில் இடத்தே எனைஅமர்த்தி
அகமே விளங்கத் திருஅருளா ரமுதம் அளித்தே அணைத்தருளி
முகமே மலர்த்திச் சித்திநிலை முழுதும் கொடுத்து மூவாமல்
translit: cukamē nirampap peruṅkaruṇait toṭṭil iṭattē eṉaiamartti akamē viḷaṅkat tiruaruḷā ramutam aḷittē aṇaittaruḷi mukamē malarttic cittinilai muḻutum koṭuttu mūvāmal cakamēlirukkap purintāyē tāyē eṉṉait tantāyē.
translation: Placing me in the cradle of great compassion, you filled me with bliss. You gave me the rare nectar of your sacred grace to make my inner self shine, and you embraced me. You made my face blossom, gave me the complete state of Siddhi, and made it so I could live upon the earth without aging. O Mother, you gave yourself to me.
commentary: Here, God's grace is experienced as the nurturing care of a mother. This divine mother places the soul in a "cradle of compassion," feeding it with grace until the inner self shines. This loving care leads to the attainment of Siddhi (spiritual perfection) and, remarkably, the ability to live on Earth without the body aging or decaying. The ultimate gift is God giving God's own self.

tamil: தந்தாய் இன்றும் தருகின்றாய் தருவாய் மேலுந் தனித்தலைமை
எந்தாய் நினது பெருங்கருணை என்என் றுரைப்பேன் இவ்வுலகில்
சிந்தா குலந்தீர்த் தருள்எனநான் சிறிதே கூவு முன்என்பால்
வந்தாய் கலந்து மகிழ்கின்றாய் எனது பொழுது வான்பொழுதே.
translit: tantāy iṉṟum tarukiṉṟāy taruvāy mēlun taṉittalaimai entāy niṉatu peruṅkaruṇai eṉeṉ ṟuraippēṉ ivvulakil cintā kulantīrt taruḷeṉanāṉ ciṟitē kūvu muṉeṉpāl vantāy kalantu makiḻkiṉṟāy eṉatu poḻutu vāṉpoḻutē.
translation: You gave in the past, you give today, and you will give in the future, O my Father, my singular Lord. How can I even begin to describe your great compassion? Before I could even cry out, "Relieve the anguish of my mind in this world and grant your grace," you came to me. You mingle with me and rejoice. My time is now divine time.
commentary: The flow of grace is constant and unending, stretching across all time. Vallalar marvels at the immediacy of God's response, which arrives even before a prayer is fully formed. This divine presence is a continuous state of joyous mingling, which transforms the devotee's ordinary experience of time into a sacred, divine unfolding.
