The verse is filled with the language of intimate love, addressing God as the "apple of my two eyes" and "Lord of my life," showing the personal, relational core of his devotion.

translit: uṉṉaimaṟan tiṭuvēṉō maṟappaṟiyēṉ maṟantāl uyirviṭuvēṉ kaṇantariyēṉ uṉāṇai itunī eṉṉaimaṟan tiṭuvāyō maṟantiṭuvāy eṉilyāṉ eṉṉaceyvēṉ eṅkuṟuvēṉ evarkkuraippēṉ entāy aṉṉaiyiṉum tayavuṭaiyāy nīmaṟantāy eṉiṉum akilamelām aḷittiṭumniṉ aruḷmaṟavā teṉṟē iṉṉumikak kaḷittiṅkē irukkiṉṟēṉ maṟavēl itutaruṇam aruṭcōti eṉakkuvirain taruḷē.
translation: Would I forget you? I do not know how to forget. If I were to forget, I would give up my life, unable to endure for even a moment, this is my vow on you. But will you forget me? If you do forget me, what will I do, where will I go, to whom will I speak, my Father? You who are more compassionate than a mother, even if you forget me, I remain here still, very joyful, knowing that your grace, which sustains the entire universe, will not forget. Do not forget! This is the moment. O Grace-Jothi, hasten and grant your grace to me.
commentary: Vallalar makes a powerful vow: his memory of God is so total that to forget would mean death. He then asks a heart-wrenching question: what if God forgets him? He finds his answer in a deep trust that even if the Lord forgets, the universal Grace that sustains the cosmos cannot. Based on this trust, he declares, "This is the moment," and asks the "Grace-Jothi" to act.

translit: nāṉmaṟantēṉ eṉiṉumeṉait tāṉmaṟavāṉ eṉatu nāyakaṉeṉ ṟāṭukiṉṟēṉ eṉiṉumitu varaiyum vāṉmaṟantēṉ vāṉavarai maṟantēṉmāl ayaṉai maṟantēṉnam uruttirarai maṟantēṉeṉ ṉuṭaiya ūṉmaṟantēṉ uyirmaṟantēṉ uṇarccielām maṟantēṉ ulakamelām maṟantēṉiṅ kuṉṉaimaṟan taṟiyēṉ pāṉmaṟanta kuḻaviyaippōl pārēliṅ keṉaiyē parintuniṉa taruṭcōti purintumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: I dance with the thought, "Even if I forget, my Lord will not forget me." And yet, up to this point, I have forgotten the heavens, forgotten the celestials, forgotten Mal and Ayan, forgotten our Rudras. I have forgotten my own flesh, forgotten my life, forgotten all sensation, forgotten the entire world, but here, I have never known what it is to forget you. Do not look upon me here as a baby who has forgotten its milk. With compassion, joyfully bestow your Grace-Jothi and grant me your grace.
commentary: Vallalar describes a state of total absorption in God, where everything else has fallen away from his awareness. He has forgotten the world, his own body, and even the great gods of the Hindu pantheon like Vishnu (Mal) and Brahma (Ayan). He compares himself to a baby who might seem to have forgotten its hunger but whose fundamental need remains; his need for divine grace is just as essential.

translit: teruviṭattē viḷaiyāṭit tirintaeṉai valintē civamālai aṇintaṉaiac ciṟuvayatil inta uruviṭattē niṉakkirunta ācaielām innāḷ ōṭiyatō putiyaoru uruvuviḻain tatuvō karuviṭattē eṉaikkātta kāvalaṉē uṉatu kālpiṭittēṉ viṭuvēṉō kaippiṭiaṉ ṟatutāṉ veruviṭatteṉ uyirppiṭikāṇ uyirakaṉṟāl aṉṟi viṭamāṭṭēṉ viṭamāṭṭēṉ viṭamāṭṭēṉ nāṉē.
translation: While I was just wandering and playing in the street, you forcibly placed the garland of Sivam on me. Has all the desire you had for this form in that tender age fled today? Or do you now long for a new form? O Protector who guarded me even in the womb! I have caught hold of your feet, do you think I will let go? This is more than a grasp of the hand; know that it is my very life desperately holding on. I will not let go unless my life departs. I will not let go, I will not let go, I myself will not let go.
commentary: Vallalar argues that God started this relationship, claiming him for the divine path ("placing the garland of Sivam on me") when he was just a child. Now, he challenges God directly: "Did you change your mind?" This is the raw, intimate plea of a beloved. He declares his hold on God is the desperate grasp of his very life force, which he vows never to release.

translit: periyaṉaruṭ peruñcōtip peruṅkaruṇaip perumāṉ perumpukaḻaip pēcutalē perumpēṟeṉ ṟuṇarntē turiyanilat tavarellām tutikkiṉṟār ēḻai tutittalperi tala:iṅkē tutittiṭaeṉ ṟeḻunta ariyaperum pērācaik kaṭalperitē atueṉ aḷavukaṭan tiḻukkiṉṟa tātaliṉāl viraintē uriyaaruḷ amutaḷittē niṉaittutippit taruḷvāy ulakamelām kaḷittōṅka ōṅkunaṭat taracē.
translation: Realizing that speaking the great fame of the Great One, the vast Grace-Jothi, the Lord of vast compassion, is the greatest blessing, all those in the state of turīya praise you. The praise of this poor one is not significant. However, the rare and immense ocean of desire that has risen within me to praise you is vast indeed; it pulls me beyond my limits. Therefore, O King of the sublime dance who performs so that all worlds may rejoice and flourish, hasten! Give me the fitting nectar of grace and graciously make me praise you.
commentary: Even those in the highest states of consciousness, called turīya (a fourth state beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep), find their greatest blessing in praising God. Vallalar feels his own praise is small in comparison, yet the desire to praise has become an overwhelming force within him. He ends by asking for the one thing he wants most: the gift of grace that will allow him to praise God worthily.

translit: kavalaielām tavirntumikak kaḷippiṉoṭu niṉaiyē kaikuvittuk kaṇkaḷilnīr kaṉintucuran tiṭavē cavalaimaṉac calaṉamelām tīrntucuka mayamāyt tāṉētāṉ ākiiṉpat taṉinaṭañcey iṇaittāḷ tavalaruñcīrc coṉmālai vaṉaintuvaṉain taṇintu tāṉāki nāṉāṭat taruṇamitu tāṉē kuvalaiyattār aticayikka eḻuntaruḷi varuvāy kuruvēeṉ kuṟṟamelām kuṇamākakkoṇ ṭavaṉē.
translation: With all my worries gone and with great delight, I bring my hands together to You alone as tears of love flow from my eyes. With all the agitations of my feeble mind resolved, I become filled with bliss. I repeatedly weave garlands of words of imperishable glory and adorn the pair of sacred feet that perform the unique dance of bliss, being Itself by Itself. This truly is the moment for me to dance, having become You. Arise and come, to the astonishment of the people of the world! O Guru, you who have accepted all my faults as virtues.
commentary: This is a vision of perfect, blissful union with the divine. With all worldly worries and mental chatter gone, the soul becomes one with God's own consciousness, which Vallalar experiences as a cosmic dance. He asks God, his Guru, to make this state of unity happen now, to the astonishment of the world, trusting in a divine love that sees all his human faults as virtues.

translit: paṭikaḷelām ēṟṟuvittīr paramanaṭam puriyum patiyaiaṭai vittīrap patinaṭuvē viḷaṅkum koṭikaḷniṟai maṇimāṭak kōyilaiyum kāṭṭik koṭuttīrak kōyililē kōpuravā yililē ceṭikaḷilāt tirukkatavam tiṟappittuk kāṭṭit tirumpavumnīr mūṭuvittīr tiṟantiṭutal vēṇṭum aṭikaḷitu taruṇamiṉi araikkaṇamum tariyēṉ ampalattē naṭampurivīr aḷittaruḷvīr viraintē.
translation: You made me climb all the steps. You brought me to the city where the supreme dance is performed. In the middle of that city, You showed me the temple of jeweled towers filled with flags. At that temple's tower gate, You had the flawless, sacred door opened for me to see, and then You closed it again. It must be opened. Master, this is the moment. I cannot bear it for even half an instant longer. You who dance in the Hall, grant this, grant it swiftly!
commentary: God has led him all the way to the final door of enlightenment but has now closed it, and Vallalar pleads with unbearable urgency for it to be opened immediately. The spiritual path is pictured as a climb up to a celestial temple; he was shown the inner truth but then shut out. This captures the intense frustration and longing of a soul on the very brink of the ultimate experience, where the wait of even a single moment feels like an eternity.

translit: peṭṭiitil ulavāta perumporuḷuṇ ṭitunī peṟukaeṉa atutiṟakkum peruntiṟavuk kōlum eṭṭiraṇṭum teriyātēṉ eṉkaiyilē koṭuttīr itutaruṇam tiṟantataṉai eṭukkamuyal kiṉṟēṉ aṭṭiceya niṉaiyātīr araikkaṇamum tariyēṉ araikkaṇattuk kāyiramā yiraṅkōṭi āka vaṭṭiiṭṭu nummiṭattē vāṅkuvaṉnum āṇai maṇimaṉṟil naṭampurivīr vantaruḷvīr viraintē.
translation: You told me, "In this box is a great, imperishable treasure. Take it." You placed the master key to open it in my hands, I who know nothing. This is the moment. I am trying to open it and take the treasure now. Do not think of hindering me. I cannot bear it for even half an instant. For that half-instant's delay, I will charge you interest of a thousand thousand crores and collect it from you, I swear this on you! You who dance in the jeweled hall, come and grant this, grant it swiftly!
commentary: Using the bold metaphor of a locked treasure box, Vallalar tells God, "You gave me the key; do not stop me from opening it now." God has already provided the means for realization, and Vallalar warns him not to create any last-minute obstacles. He even threatens to charge "interest" for any delay, a startlingly intimate and demanding expression of how precious this final moment is. He is more than asking; he is claiming a promise.

translit: kaikkicainta poruḷeṉakku vāykkicaintuṇ pataṟkē kālameṉṉa kaṇakkeṉṉa karutumiṭam eṉṉa meykkicaintaṉ ṟuraittatunīr cattiyam cattiyamē viṭuvēṉō iṉṟaṭiyēṉ viḻaṟkiṟaittēṉ alavē ceykkicainta civapōkam viḷaittuṇavē iṟaittēṉ tiṉantōṟum kāttiruntēṉ tiruvuḷamē aṟiyum maikkicainta viḻiammai civakāma valli makiḻanaṭam purikiṉṟīr vantaruḷvīr viraintē.
translation: "For you to eat and enjoy the substance that has come into your hand, what does time matter? What does calculation matter? What does place matter?" What you spoke that day, agreeing in truth, is the absolute truth, the absolute truth. Will I, your devotee, let you go today? I have not wasted my water on a barren field. I watered this field to cultivate and consume the crop of Sivam's bliss. I have waited every day, as your divine will knows. You who dance to delight the Lady Sivakami Valli, whose eyes are lined with kohl, come and grant this, grant it swiftly!
commentary: Vallalar holds God to a past promise: that once the final prize was within reach, no rules of time or place would matter. He shifts to a farming metaphor, insisting his spiritual efforts were sincere, like watering a fertile field to grow the crop of Sivam's bliss, not wasting water on barren ground. Having done his part, he declares that he has waited long enough for the promised harvest.

translit: parikalattē tiruamutam paṭaittuṇavē paṇittīr paṇittapiṉṉō eṉṉuṭaiya pakkuvampārk kiṉṟīr irunilattē pacittavarkkup pacinīkka vallār ivarperiyar ivarciṟiyar eṉṉalvaḻak kalavē urimaiyuṟṟēṉ umakkēeṉ uḷḷamaṉṟē aṟintīr uṭalporuḷā vikaḷaielām ummateṉak koṇṭīr tirivakattē nāṉvaruntap pārttiruttal aḻakō civakāma vallimakiḻ tirunaṭanā yakarē.
translation: You placed the sacred food on the plate and commanded me to eat. After commanding me, are you now testing my spiritual maturity? On this great earth, it is not the custom for those who can appease hunger to distinguish between who is great and who is small. You knew in my heart from the very beginning that I belong to you by right. You took my body, wealth, and soul, accepting them all as yours. Is it right for you to just watch me suffer in this turmoil? O Lord of the sacred dance that delights Sivakami Valli!
commentary: God's delay is compared to serving a feast but then making the hungry person wait. Vallalar argues that just as a generous person feeds the hungry without judging their status, God should not test the spiritual maturity (pakkuvam) of a soul that is starving for grace. Since Vallalar has already surrendered his body, wealth, and soul, he claims a right to be cared for, questioning if it is right for God to simply watch him suffer.

translit: poykoṭutta maṉamāyaic cēṟṟilviḻā teṉakkē poṉmaṇimē ṭaiyilēṟip puntimakiḻn tirukkak kaikoṭuttīr ulakamelām kaḷikka:ula vāta kāliraṇṭum koṭuttīrek kālumaḻi yāta meykoṭukka vēṇṭumumai viṭamāṭṭēṉ kaṇṭīr mēlēṟi ṉēṉiṉikkīḻ viḻaintiṟaṅkēṉ eṉṟum maikoṭutta viḻiammai civakāma valli makiḻanaṭam purikiṉṟīr vantaruḷvīr viraintē.
translation: So I would not fall into the mire of the mind's illusion, which deals in lies, you gave me a hand to climb onto a golden, jeweled dais and be glad in spirit. So that all the world may rejoice, You gave me two feet that never fail. You must give me the undying Body of Truth. See here, I will not let you go! I have climbed up; I will never again wish to descend. You who dance to delight the Lady Sivakami Valli, whose eyes are lined with kohl, come and grant this, grant it swiftly!
commentary: Acknowledging the grace he has already received, which lifted him from illusion onto a firm spiritual footing, Vallalar now asks for the ultimate gift: the immortal Body of Truth (mey). His resolve is absolute. He has reached a high point in his spiritual ascent and declares he will never go back down, holding fast to God until this final state is granted.

translit: miṉpōlē vayaṅkukiṉṟa viricaṭaiyīr aṭiyēṉ viḷaṅkumuma tiṇaiaṭikaḷ meyaḻuntap piṭittēṉ muṉpōlē ēmāntu viṭamāṭṭēṉ kaṇṭīr muṉivaṟiyīr iṉioḷikka muṭiyātu numakkē eṉpōlē irakkamviṭṭup piṭittavarkaḷ ilaiyē eṉpiṭikkuḷ icaintatupōl icaintatilai piṟarkkē poṉpōlē muyalkiṉṟa meyttavarkkum aritē poytavaṉēṉ ceytavamvāṉ vaiyakattiṟ peritē.
translation: O you with spreading locks gleaming like lightning! I, your devotee, have clutched your two radiant feet so they press against my body. I will not be fooled and let go as I was before, you see. You who know no anger, you can no longer hide. There are none who have seized you as unrelentingly as I have. You have never consented to another's grasp as you have to mine. This is rare even for true ascetics whose striving is precious as gold. The penance I, this false ascetic, have performed is the greatest in heaven and on earth.
commentary: This verse expresses a fierce, loving determination. Vallalar declares that he has seized God's feet and will not be tricked into letting go as he might have been before. He claims that no one has ever held on with such unrelenting love and that God has yielded to his grasp in a unique way. This celebrates the power of a devotee's loving and desperate attachment to the divine.

translit: etutaruṇam atuteriyēṉ eṉṉiṉumem māṉē ellāñcey vallavaṉē eṉtaṉinā yakaṉē itutaruṇam tavaṟumeṉil eṉuyirpōy viṭumiv veḷiyēṉmēl karuṇaipurin teḻuntaruḷal vēṇṭum matutaruṇa vāricamum malarntataruḷ utayam vāyttatuciṟ capaiviḷakkam vayaṅkukiṉṟa tulakil vitutaruṇa amutaḷitteṉ eṇṇamelām muṭikkum vēlaiitu kālaieṉa viḷampavumvēṇ ṭuvatō.
translation: My Master, although I do not know the opportune moment, you are the all-powerful one who can do everything, my singular Lord. If this moment passes, my very life will depart. You must take pity on this simple one and graciously appear. The fresh, honey-filled lotus has bloomed; the dawn of grace has arrived. The light of the Hall of Consciousnessshines in the world. This is the time to give me the fresh nectar of the moon and fulfill all my intentions. Must I even declare that now is the time?
commentary: An intense urgency fills this verse: the perfect moment for union with God has arrived. He feels that if this opportunity is missed, his very life will end. All the signs are present, as his heart is open like a blooming lotus, and the light of the cit-sabhai, the inner space of pure consciousness, is visible. This is a declaration that the conditions for grace are fully met and the consummation must happen now.

translit: kōḷaṟinta peruntavartam kuṟippaṟintē utavum koṭaiyāḷā civakāmak koṭikkicainta koḻunā āḷaṟintiṅ keṉaiāṇṭa aracēeṉ amutē ampalattē naṭampuriyum arumperuñcō tiyaṉē tāḷaṟintēṉ niṉvaravu cattiyamcat tiyamē cantēkam illaiantat taṉittatiru varaviṉ nāḷaṟintu koḷalvēṇṭum navilukanī eṉatu naṉaviṭaiyā yiṉumaṉṟik kaṉaviṭaiyā yiṉumē.
translation: O benefactor, who perceives the goals of great ascetics and helps them accordingly! O husband perfectly suited for the vine that is Sivakami! O King who recognized and took me as your own, my nectar! O rare, great Jothi that dances in the sacred hall! I have recognized your feet; your coming is truth, absolute truth. There is no doubt about that unique, sacred arrival. I need to know the day, so you must declare it, either in my waking state or in my dreams.
commentary: Here, faith is absolute, but human anxiety still seeks a specific answer. Vallalar is completely certain of God's arrival, yet he pleads to be told the exact day, whether in a dream or in his waking life. He addresses God as the great Jothi, or divine light, dancing in the sacred hall (ampalam), acknowledging the divine nature even while asking for this very human need for certainty to be met.

translit: aṉṟeṉakku nīuraitta taruṇamitu eṉavē aṟintirukkiṉ ṟēṉaṭiyēṉ āyiṉumeṉ maṉantāṉ kaṉṟeṉacceṉ ṟaṭikkaṭiuṭ kalaṅkukiṉṟataracē kaṇṇuṭaiya karumpēeṉ kavalaimaṉak kalakkam poṉṟiṭappē riṉpaveḷḷam poṅkiṭa:iv vulakil puṇṇiyarkaḷ uḷaṅkaḷippup poruntiviḷaṅ kiṭanī iṉṟeṉakku veḷippaṭaeṉ itayamalar micainiṉ ṟeḻuntaruḷi aruḷvatelām iṉitaruḷka viraintē.
translation: I, your devotee, know that this is the very moment you once spoke of to me. Nevertheless, my mind, like a calf, frequently runs about and becomes agitated. O King! O sugarcane with eyes! So that the turmoil of my anxious mind may perish, so that the flood of great bliss may surge, and so that the virtuous of this world may attain joy and shine, you must reveal yourself to me today. Arise from the flower of my heart and swiftly, sweetly grant all that is to be given by grace.
commentary: Even with the spiritual certainty that the promised moment has come, the mind remains restless and anxious. Vallalar compares his mind to a straying calf, acknowledging that intellectual conviction alone cannot calm it. The only true cure is the direct, felt experience of God's presence. He also notes that this event will bring joy to him and to all virtuous people, linking his personal realization to a wider good.

translit: itutaruṇam namaiyāḷaṟ keḻuntaruḷun taruṇam iṉittaṭaioṉ ṟilaikaṇṭāy eṉmaṉaṉē nītāṉ matuviḻumōr īppōlē mayaṅkātē kayaṅki vāṭātē malaṅkātē malarntumakiḻn tiruppāy kutukalamē itutoṭaṅkik kuṟaivilaikāṇ namatu kuruvāṇai namatuperuṅ kulateyvat tāṇai potuvilnaṭam purikiṉṟa puṇṇiyaṉār eṉakkuḷ puṇarnturaitta tiruvārttai poṉvārttai ituvē.
translation: O my mind, this is the moment! This is the moment He will graciously come to rule us. See, there are no more obstacles. Do not be dazed like a fly trapped in honey. Do not be distressed, do not wither, do not be bewildered. Instead, blossom and remain joyful. From now on, it is all celebration, with nothing lacking, you see. I swear this on our Guru, I swear this on our great clan deity. These are the golden words the Virtuous One, who dances in the universal Hall, spoke to me in union.
commentary: After all the pleading, Vallalar now speaks directly to his own mind, commanding it to stop worrying and be joyful. The struggle has ended because he has received a "golden word," an unbreakable inner promise of union from God. This verse marks a shift from anxious seeking to triumphant celebration, based on an unshakeable inner assurance.
NOTES
Note 252

translit: kalakkukiṉṟa - ca. mu. ka. patippu.
translation: kalakkukiṉṟa — reading of the S. Mu. Ka. edition.
Note 253

translit: micaiyiṉ - ca. mu. ka. patippu.
translation: micaiyiṉ — reading of the S. Mu. Ka. edition.

translit: kāraṇa kāriyak kalvikaḷ ellām kaṟpitteṉ ṉuḷḷē kalantukoṇ ṭeṉṉai nāraṇar nāṉmukar pōṟṟamēl ēṟṟi nātānta nāṭṭukkōr nāyakaṉ ākkip pūraṇa māmiṉpam poṅkit tatumpap puttamu tāmaruṭ pōṉakam tantē āraṇa vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: You taught me all knowledge of cause and effect, mingled within me, and took me as your own. You elevated me to be praised by Narayana and the Four-faced One, made me a leader for the land of Nadanta, and gave me the grace-food of fresh ambrosia so that perfect bliss wells up and overflows. You made me dance in the street of the Vedas. You are ArutPerunJothi, my Lord.
commentary: God's grace gives a knowledge of reality that elevates the soul beyond the highest heavens known to traditional worship. Vallalar describes being lifted above even the great gods Narayana (Vishnu) and the Four-faced One (Brahma) to rule in Nadanta, the sublime state beyond sound. This state is one of perfect, overflowing bliss, nourished by the "grace-food" of ambrosia.

translit: tēkamep pōtum citaiyāta vaṇṇam ceyvit telāmvalla cittiyum tantē pōkamel lāmeṉṟaṉ pōkama tākkip pōtānta nāṭṭaip purakkamēl ēṟṟi ēkaci vāṉanta vāḻkkaiyil eṉṟum iṉpuṟṟu vāḻum iyalpaḷit teṉṉai ākama vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: You made my body so it would never decay, gave me the siddhi that can do all things, and made all pleasures my own. You elevated me to protect the land of Bodhanta and granted me the nature to live forever, delighting in the life of singular Siva-bliss. You made me dance in the street of the Agamas. You are ArutPerunJothi, my Lord.
commentary: Grace perfects the physical body, making it immortal and granting the siddhi, or yogic power, to accomplish anything. This is a central and distinct part of Vallalar's teaching: spiritual realization transforms the body. He is elevated to protect Bodhanta (the state of pure consciousness) and enjoys a life of singular bliss united with the divine, which he calls Siva-bliss.

translit: tāṉantam illāta taṉmaiyaik kāṭṭum cākāta kalviyait tanteṉak kuḷḷē tēṉantat teḷḷamu tūṟṟip perukkit tittittuc cittam civamaya mākki vāṉantam ātiyum kaṇṭukoṇ ṭaḻiyā vāḻkkaiyil iṉpuṟṟuc cuttavē tānta āṉanta vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: You gave me the deathless learning that reveals the nature of the endless self. Pouring that clear, honey-like ambrosia into me and making it swell, you sweetened my consciousness and made it one with Siva. You made me delight in an imperishable life, having realized the bliss of the heavens and its origin, and you made me dance in the street of the bliss of pure Vedanta. You are ArutPerunJothi, my Lord.
commentary: The ultimate teaching is the "deathless learning," an inner knowledge that reveals the soul's true, endless nature and confers immortality. This is a direct experience, a sweet ambrosia poured within that makes one's entire consciousness divine. This realization allows him to "dance" in the street of pure Vedanta, a school of philosophy focused on ultimate reality, now understood as a lived, blissful truth.

translit: ciṟcapai iṉpat tirunaṭaṅ kāṭṭit teḷḷamu tūṭṭieṉ cintaiyait tēṟṟip poṟcapai taṉṉil poruttiel lāmcey pūraṇa cittimeyp pōkamum tantē taṟpara māmōr catāṉanta nāṭṭil cattiyaṉ ākkiōr cuttacit tānta aṟputa vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: You showed me the blissful sacred dance in the Chit Sabhai and fed me clear ambrosia, clarifying my mind. Placing me suitably in the Porsabai, you gave me the perfect siddhi that can do all things, along with true enjoyment. You made me a being of truth in the singular land of eternal bliss that is the Supreme Self, and you made me dance in the wondrous street of pure Siddhanta. You are ArutPerunJothi, my Lord.
commentary: The final stage of union involves directly witnessing God's cosmic activity, here described as a blissful dance in the Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness). This vision clarifies the mind and leads to placement in the Porsabai (Golden Hall), granting perfect powers and true enjoyment. He becomes a "being of truth" in the supreme land of eternal bliss, dancing in the street of pure Siddhanta, a path of philosophy and practice now fully realized.

translit: tattuvam ellāmeṉ taṉvacam ākkic cākāva rattaiyum tanteṉait tēṟṟi ottuvan tuḷḷē kalantukoṇ ṭellā ulakamum pōṟṟa uyarnilai ēṟṟic cittie lāmceyac ceyvittuc cattum cittum veḷippaṭac cuttanā tānta attiru vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: You placed all the tattvas under my control, gave me the boon of deathlessness, and brought me clarity. Coming into harmony, you mingled within me and elevated me to a high state praised by all the worlds. You enabled me to perform all siddhis, made Sat and Chit manifest, and made me dance in that sacred street of pure Nadanta. You are ArutPerunJothi, my Lord.
commentary: Here, grace grants understanding and mastery over the fundamental components of existence, the tattvas. This control, along with the boon of deathlessness, comes from God mingling directly with the soul. The experience makes the absolute principles of Sat (Being) and Chit (Consciousness) fully manifest, a state Vallalar calls dancing in the street of pure Nadanta (the reality beyond subtle sound).

translit: ittaṉai eṉṟuniṉ ṟeṇṇiṭal oṇṇā eṉpiḻai yāvaiyum aṉpiṉil koṇṭē cattiya māmciva cittiyai eṉpāl tanteṉai yāvarum vantaṉai ceyavē nittiyaṉ ākkimeyc cuttacaṉ mārkka nītiyai ōtiōr cuttapō tānta attaṉi vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: Taking all my faults, so numerous they cannot be counted, with love, you gave me the true Siva Siddhi. Making me eternal so that all would revere me, you taught me the principles of the true Suddha Sanmarkkam and made me dance in the unique street at the pinnacle of pure knowledge. O ArutPerunJothi, you are my Lord.
commentary: Divine grace creates perfection out of imperfection. Vallalar says God lovingly takes all his countless faults and grants him Siva Siddhi (the perfected state of God-consciousness). This transformation makes him eternal and a living example of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path). He describes this as dancing in the street at the peak of pure knowledge, or bodhānta.

translit: maruntitu maṇiitu mantiram itucey vakaiitu tuṟaiitu vaḻiitu eṉavē irunteṉuḷ aṟivittut teḷḷamu taḷittē eṉṉaiyum taṉṉaiyum ēkama tākkip poruntie lāñceya vallaōr cittip puṇṇiya vāḻkkaiyil naṇṇiyō kānta aruntava vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: Residing within me, you taught me, "This is the medicine, this is the gem, this is the mantra; this is the method, this is the field, this is the way." You gave me clear ambrosia, and uniting me with yourself as one, granted me a blessed life of siddhi that can accomplish anything. You made me dance in the street of rare austerity at the pinnacle of yoga. O ArutPerunJothi, you are my Lord.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual guidance comes directly from God within, who reveals every aspect of the path: the cure, the goal, the mantra (sacred formula), and the method. This inner teaching is a unifying experience, culminating in a blessed life where one has the siddhi (power) to do anything. This is the peak of spiritual practice, which Vallalar calls dancing in the street at the pinnacle of yoga (yogānta).

translit: paticāra vaittumuṟ pacunilai kāṭṭip pācavi mōcaṉap pakkuvaṉ ākki niticāra nāṉ inta nīḷula kattē niṉaittaṉa niṉaittaṉa nēruṟap purintu titicēra maṉṉuyirk kiṉpañcey kiṉṟa cittie lāntantu cuttaka lānta atikāra vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: Placing me in the presence of the Lord, you first showed me the state of the soul and made me mature enough for liberation from bonds. You caused whatever I wished for in this vast world to manifest, bringing me wealth. You gave me all the siddhis that bring joy and stability to enduring lives and made me dance in the street of authority at the pinnacle of pure art. O ArutPerunJothi, you are my Lord.
commentary: The path to liberation begins with a clear understanding of one's own condition. God (Pati) shows the soul (pasu) its state of being caught in limitation (pāsa), making it ready for freedom. Once liberated, the soul is given divine powers to bring joy and stability to others. Vallalar calls this the pinnacle of divine artistry, or kalānta.

translit: iruḷāṉa malamaṟut tikaparaṅ kaṇṭē ellā uyirkaḷum iṉpuṟṟu vāḻa maruḷāṉa paṟpala mārkkaṅkaḷ ellām vaḻituṟai teriyāmal maṇmūṭip pōkat teruḷāṉa cuttacaṉ mārkkama toṉṟē ciṟantu viḷaṅkaōr ciṟcapai kāṭṭum aruḷāṉa vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: You cut away the darkness of impurity so that I might see this world and the next, and so that all beings might live in joy. You caused all the various deluded paths to be buried under earth, their ways and means lost, so that the one clear Suddha Sanmarkkam alone might shine forth in splendor. You made me dance in the street of grace that reveals the one Chit Sabhai. O ArutPerunJothi, you are my Lord.
commentary: God's work is told in two movements. First God cut away the darkness of impurity (malam) so that all beings might live in joy. Then God buried the many deluded paths, their ways lost under the earth, so that the clear Suddha Sanmarkkam alone would shine. Vallalar dances in the street of grace that leads to the Chit Sabhai. ArutPerunJothi is his Lord.

translit: iruṭcātit tattuvac cāttirak kuppai iruvāyppup puṉceyil eruvākkip pōṭṭu maruṭcāti camayaṅkaḷ mataṅkaḷāc cirama vaḻakkelām kuḻikkoṭṭi maṇmūṭip pōṭṭut teruṭcāruñ cuttacaṉ mārkkanaṉ ṉīti ciṟantu viḷaṅkaōr ciṟcapai kāṭṭum aruṭcōti vītiyil āṭaccey tīrē aruṭperuñ jōtieṉ āṇṭavar nīrē.
translation: You took the trash heap of scriptures on principles and the darkness of caste, turned it into manure for a barren field, and discarded it. You took all the customs of deluding castes, religions, doctrines and life-stages, threw them into a pit, and covered them with earth. You did this so that the excellent principles of the clear Suddha Sanmarkkam might shine brightly, making me dance in the street of the light of grace that reveals the one Chit Sabhai. O ArutPerunJothi, you are my Lord.
commentary: God has made manure of the rubbish heap of scriptures built on caste and doctrine, and spread it on a barren field. The customs of deluding castes, religions, sects and life-stages were thrown into a pit and covered with earth. What remains is the clear justice of Suddha Sanmarkkam, shining for all. Vallalar dances in its street of grace. ArutPerunJothi is his Lord.

sections.title: A Petition Before the Divine Presence

tamil: மாழை மாமணிப் பொதுநடம் புரிகின்ற வள்ளலே அளிகின்ற
வாழை வான்பழச் சுவைஎனப் பத்தர்தம் மனத்துளே தித்திப்போய்
ஏழை நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவிக் கேற்றருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
கோழை மானிடப் பிறப்பிதில் உன்னருட் குருஉருக் கொளுமாறே.
translit: māḻai māmaṇip potunaṭam purikiṉṟa vaḷḷalē aḷikiṉṟa vāḻai vāṉpaḻac cuvaieṉap pattartam maṉattuḷē tittippōy ēḻai nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevik kēṟṟaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum kōḻai māṉiṭap piṟappitil uṉṉaruṭ kuruuruk koḷumāṟē.
translation: O generous Lord who performs the dance in the great jeweled golden universal hall! You who bestow grace, sweetening the minds of devotees like the taste of a fine plantain fruit! You must graciously accept this petition of mine, a humble dog, into your sacred ear, so that in this miserable human birth, I may attain your grace-filled form as a Guru.
commentary: This prayer asks for a specific kind of spiritual attainment. Addressing God as the cosmic dancer, the petitioner asks for the grace to become a Guru (spiritual teacher) in this very life. The self-description as a "humble dog" is a traditional expression of deep humility before the divine, while the comparison of grace to a sweet fruit makes the divine presence feel intimate and delightful.

tamil: பொன்னின் மாமணிப் பொதுநடம் புரிகின்ற புண்ணியா கனித்தோங்கி
மன்னு வாழையின் பழச்சுவை எனப்பத்தர் மனத்துளே தித்திப்போய்
சின்ன நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி சேர்த்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
இன்ன என்னுடைத் தேகம்நல் லொளிபெறும் இயலருக் கொளுமாறே.
translit: poṉṉiṉ māmaṇip potunaṭam purikiṉṟa puṇṇiyā kaṉittōṅki maṉṉu vāḻaiyiṉ paḻaccuvai eṉappattar maṉattuḷē tittippōy ciṉṉa nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi cērttaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum iṉṉa eṉṉuṭait tēkamnal loḷipeṟum iyalaruk koḷumāṟē.
translation: O holy one who performs the dance in the great jeweled universal hall of gold! You who are full-grown and ripe, sweetening the minds of devotees like the taste of the fruit of an enduring plantain tree! You must graciously ensure this petition of mine, an insignificant dog, reaches your sacred ear, so that this body of mine may, by grace, attain the nature of receiving a great light.
commentary: The plea here is for the physical body itself to be transformed by grace. The goal is for the body to become a vessel capable of receiving a "great light," which for Vallalar signifies the radiant presence of God's consciousness. The aim is to make the body luminous and divine.

tamil: விஞ்சு பொன்னணி அம்பலத் தருள்நடம் விளைத்துயிர்க் குயிராகி
எஞ்சு றாதபே ரின்பருள் கின்றஎன் இறைவநின் அருள்இன்றி
அஞ்சும் நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி அமைத்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
துஞ்சும் இவ்வுடல் இம்மையே துஞ்சிடாச் சுகஉடல் கொளுமாறே.
translit: viñcu poṉṉaṇi ampalat taruḷnaṭam viḷaittuyirk kuyirāki eñcu ṟātapē riṉparuḷ kiṉṟaeṉ iṟaivaniṉ aruḷiṉṟi añcum nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi amaittaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum tuñcum ivvuṭal immaiyē tuñciṭāc cuka:uṭal koḷumāṟē.
translation: My Lord who enacts the dance of grace in the eminent, gold-adorned hall, becoming the life of all life and bestowing undiminishing great bliss! Without your grace, I am a fearful dog. You must graciously cause your sacred ear to heed my petition, so that this perishing body may, in this very birth, attain an imperishable body of bliss.
commentary: The ultimate aim of the path is revealed here: the transformation of this mortal body into an immortal one. Vallalar prays for an "imperishable body of bliss," right here and now. He identifies the divine dance hall as the ampalam (sacred space), emphasizing that God is the very "life of all life," the source of all existence.

tamil: ஓங்கு பொன்னணி அம்பலத் தருள்நடம் உயிர்க்கெலாம் ஒளிவண்ணப்
பாங்கு மேவநின் றாடல்செய் இறைவநின் பதமலர் பணிந்தேத்தாத்
தீங்கு நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி சேர்த்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
ஈங்கு வீழுடல் இம்மையே வீழ்ந்திடா இயலுடல் உறுமாறே.
translit: ōṅku poṉṉaṇi ampalat taruḷnaṭam uyirkkelām oḷivaṇṇap pāṅku mēvaniṉ ṟāṭalcey iṟaivaniṉ patamalar paṇintēttāt tīṅku nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi cērttaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum īṅku vīḻuṭal immaiyē vīḻntiṭā iyaluṭal uṟumāṟē.
translation: O Lord who performs the dance of grace in the lofty, gold-adorned hall, manifesting as a nature of light for all beings! You must graciously ensure the petition of me, a wicked dog who fails to bow to and praise your lotus feet, reaches your sacred ear, so that this falling body may, in this very birth, attain a natural body that does not fall.
commentary: This verse highlights a core teaching: the physical body, which is naturally subject to decay (a "falling body"), can be transformed into a body that does not "fall." This transformation is a gift of grace from God, who is described as a pure "nature of light." The speaker's self-criticism as a "wicked dog" who fails to worship properly shows that this grace is bestowed out of compassion.

tamil: இலங்கு பொன்னணிப் பொதுநடம் புரிகின்ற இறைவஇவ் வுலகெல்லாம்
துலங்கும் வண்ணநின் றருளுநின் திருவடித் துணைதுணை என்னாமல்
கலங்கு நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி கலந்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
அலங்கும் இவ்வுடல் இம்மையே அழிவுறா அருள்உடல் உறுமாறே.
translit: ilaṅku poṉṉaṇip potunaṭam purikiṉṟa iṟaiva:iv vulakellām tulaṅkum vaṇṇaniṉ ṟaruḷuniṉ tiruvaṭit tuṇaituṇai eṉṉāmal kalaṅku nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi kalantaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum alaṅkum ivvuṭal immaiyē aḻivuṟā aruḷuṭal uṟumāṟē.
translation: O Lord who performs the dance in the radiant, gold-adorned universal hall, standing and bestowing grace so that all this world may shine! You must graciously cause the petition of me, a distressed dog who fails to declare your sacred feet as my only refuge, to merge with your sacred ear, so that this suffering body may, in this very birth, attain an indestructible body of grace.
commentary: The divine dance is more than for the individual seeker; it is an act of grace that makes "all this world shine." Yet the personal plea remains focused and intense: for this body, a source of suffering, to become an "indestructible body of grace." The prayer is for the body itself to become a permanent vessel for grace, ending the cycle of physical suffering and decay in this life.

tamil: சிறந்த பொன்னணித் திருச்சிற்றம் பலத்திலே திருநடம் புரிகின்ற
அறந்த வாதசே வடிமலர் முடிமிசை அணிந்தக மகிழ்ந்தேத்த
மறந்த நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி மடுத்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
பிறந்த இவ்வுடல் இம்மையே அழிவுறாப் பெருநலம் பெறுமாறே.
translit: ciṟanta poṉṉaṇit tirucciṟṟam palattilē tirunaṭam purikiṉṟa aṟanta vātacē vaṭimalar muṭimicai aṇintaka makiḻntētta maṟanta nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi maṭuttaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum piṟanta ivvuṭal immaiyē aḻivuṟāp perunalam peṟumāṟē.
translation: O Lord who performs the sacred dance in the excellent, gold-adorned Thiru Chitrambalam! I am a dog-like one who forgot to wear Your red lotus-feet, which never swerve from righteousness, upon my head and to praise them with a joyful heart. You must lend Your sacred ear to my plea and graciously act, so that this body I was born with may, in this very life, attain the great good of never perishing.
commentary: This prayer joins inner and outer transformation. He confesses that he forgot to wear God's red lotus feet on his head and praise them with a joyful heart, feet that dance in the Thiru Chitrambalam and never swerve from righteousness. Yet he asks that this very body he was born with gain the great good of never perishing, in this life.

tamil: விளங்கு பொன்னணிப் பொதுநடம் புரிகின்ற விரைமலர்த் திருத்தாளை
உளங்கொள் அன்பர்தம் உளங்கொளும் இறைவநின் ஒப்பிலாப் பெருந்தன்மை
களங்கொள் நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி கலந்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
துளங்கும் இவ்வுடல் இம்மையே அழிவுறாத் தொல்லுடல் உறுமாறே.
translit: viḷaṅku poṉṉaṇip potunaṭam purikiṉṟa viraimalart tiruttāḷai uḷaṅkoḷ aṉpartam uḷaṅkoḷum iṟaivaniṉ oppilāp peruntaṉmai kaḷaṅkoḷ nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi kalantaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum tuḷaṅkum ivvuṭal immaiyē aḻivuṟāt tolluṭal uṟumāṟē.
translation: O Lord who dwells in the hearts of devotees who take You into their hearts, Your greatness is peerless! You perform the public dance in the radiant, gold-adorned space. You must allow the plea of this flawed, dog-like one to enter Your sacred ear and graciously act, so that this trembling body may, in this very life, become an ancient, indestructible body.
commentary: The request to transform this "trembling body" into an "ancient, indestructible body" suggests a return to a primordial, perfect state. It means restoring the body to its original, divinely intended form, free from suffering and decay. This is a gift received through grace from a God who dwells within the hearts of devotees.

tamil: வாய்ந்த பொன்னணிப் பொதுநடம் புரிகின்ற வள்ளலே மறைஎல்லாம்
ஆய்ந்தும் இன்னஎன் றறிந்திலா நின்திரு அடிமலர் பணியாமல்
சாய்ந்த நாயினேன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி தரித்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
ஏய்ந்த இவ்வுடல் இம்மையே திருவருள் இயல்உடல் உறுமாறே.
translit: vāynta poṉṉaṇip potunaṭam purikiṉṟa vaḷḷalē maṟaiellām āyntum iṉṉaeṉ ṟaṟintilā niṉtiru aṭimalar paṇiyāmal cāynta nāyiṉēṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi tarittaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum ēynta ivvuṭal immaiyē tiruvaruḷ iyaluṭal uṟumāṟē.
translation: O Benefactor, performing the public dance in the fitting, gold-adorned space! I am a straying, dog-like one who has failed to bow to Your sacred lotus-feet, which even the Vedas, after all their study, could not define. You must accept my plea in Your sacred ear and graciously act, so that this body I have may, in this very life, become a body whose nature is divine grace.
commentary: True understanding of God comes from devotion, more than from studying scriptures. Vallalar notes that even the ancient Vedas could not fully define the divine, yet he, a self-described "straying dog," asks for the grace to transform his body into one whose very substance is grace itself. This places direct, personal experience of grace above even the most sacred texts.

tamil: மாற்றி லாதபொன் னம்பலத் தருள்நடம் வயங்கநின் றொளிர்கின்ற
பேற்றில் ஆருயிர்க் கின்பருள் இறைவநின் பெயற்கழல் கணிமாலை
சாற்றி டாதஎன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி தரித்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
காற்றில் ஆகிய இவ்வுடல் இம்மையே கதியுடல் உறுமாறே.
translit: māṟṟi lātapoṉ ṉampalat taruḷnaṭam vayaṅkaniṉ ṟoḷirkiṉṟa pēṟṟil āruyirk kiṉparuḷ iṟaivaniṉ peyaṟkaḻal kaṇimālai cāṟṟi ṭātaeṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi tarittaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum kāṟṟil ākiya ivvuṭal immaiyē katiyuṭal uṟumāṟē.
translation: O Lord who, as a great fortune, grants bliss to precious lives, shining resplendently while performing the dance of grace in the unequaled golden hall! I am one who has not offered a garland of praise to Your ankleted feet. You must accept my plea in Your sacred ear and graciously act, so that this body, which is made of air, may in this very life become a body of ultimate refuge.
commentary: The body is described as being as fragile as "air," emphasizing its impermanence and vulnerability. The prayer is for this frail vessel to become a "body of ultimate refuge," a final, stable, and eternal form. This transformation is a gift of bliss bestowed by the Lord who dances in the golden hall of reality.

tamil: தீட்டு பொன்னணி அம்பலத் தருள்நடம் செய்துயிர்த் திரட்கின்பம்
காட்டு கின்றதோர் கருணையங் கடவுள்நின் கழலிணை கருதாதே
நீட்டு கின்றஎன் விண்ணப்பம் திருச்செவி நேர்ந்தருள் செயல்வேண்டும்
translit: tīṭṭu poṉṉaṇi ampalat taruḷnaṭam ceytuyirt tiraṭkiṉpam kāṭṭu kiṉṟatōr karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭavuḷniṉ kaḻaliṇai karutātē nīṭṭu kiṉṟaeṉ viṇṇappam tiruccevi nērntaruḷ ceyalvēṇṭum vāṭṭumivvuṭal immaiyē aḻivuṟā vaḷamaṭain tiṭumāṟē.
translation: O God of grace, who performs the dance of grace in the exquisitely crafted, gold-adorned hall, showing bliss to the multitudes of souls! Having failed to contemplate Your paired ankleted feet, I now extend my plea. You must consent to it with Your sacred ear and graciously act, so that this tormenting body may, in this very life, attain indestructible abundance.
commentary: The body is described here as a source of torment, emphasizing the pain and limitation of ordinary physical existence. The prayer is for this very body to be transformed into one that is indestructible and full of abundance. This consistent theme, that a perfected physical form is possible in this life through God's grace, is central to Vallalar's path.
NOTES
Note 248

tamil: விளங்கு பொன்னணித் திருச்சிற் றம்பலத்திலே விரைமலர்த் திருத்தாளை - முதற்பதிப்பு. பொ. சு., ச. மு. க.
translit: viḷaṅku poṉṉaṇit tirucciṟ ṟampalattilē viraimalart tiruttāḷai - mutaṟpatippu. po. cu., ca. mu. ka.
translation: viḷaṅku poṉṉaṇit tirucciṟ ṟampalattilē viraimalart tiruttāḷai — reading of the first edition, and of the Po. Su. and S. Mu. Ka. editions.
Note 249

translit: āṭṭum - paṭivēṟupāṭu. ā. pā.
translation: āṭṭum — variant reading. Ā. Pā. edition.

translit: paṭamāṭṭēṉ tuyarciṟitum paṭamāṭṭēṉ iṉināṉ payappaṭavum māṭṭēṉnum patattuṇaiyē piṭittēṉ viṭamāṭṭēṉ ēmāntu viṭamāṭṭēṉ kaṇṭīr meymmaiitu nummāṇai viḷampiṉaṉnum aṭiyēṉ keṭamāṭṭēṉ piṟarmoḻikaḷ kēṭṭiṭavum māṭṭēṉ kiḷaroḷiam palattāṭal vaḷaroḷinum allāl naṭamāṭṭēṉ eṉuḷattē nāṉcāka māṭṭēṉ nallatiru varuḷālē nāṉtāṉā ṉēṉē.
translation: I will not suffer, not even a little; I will not suffer anymore. I will not be afraid, for I have grasped the support of your feet. I will not let go. I will not be deceived and give up, you see. This is the truth; I, your devotee, declare it in your name. I will not be ruined. I will not listen to the words of others. Other than you, the growing light whose dance fills the radiant hall, nothing else will stir within my heart. I will not die; by your good, sacred grace, I have become who I am.
commentary: This verse is a powerful declaration of fearlessness and absolute trust in God. Having taken refuge in the divine, the speaker announces an end to all suffering and fear, stating a plain truth: by God's grace, "I have become who I am." It marks a shift from seeking to having found, a state of unshakeable inner certainty.

translit: cākāta kalviyilē talaikāṭṭik koṭuttīr taṭaiyaṟiyāk kālkāṭṭit tarampeṟavum aḷittīr mākātal uṭaiyavaṉā maṉaṅkaṉivit taḻiyā vāṉamutum meyññāṉa maruntumuṇap purintīr pōkāta puṉalālē cutta:uṭam piṉarām puṇṇiyarum naṇṇariya potunilaiyun tantīr nākāti patikaḷumniṉ ṟēttavaḷark kiṉṟīr naṭarāja rēnumakku nāṉetucey vēṉē.
translation: You initiated me into the deathless education. You showed me the feet that know no obstacle and granted me high standing. Making me a being of great love, you melted my heart and caused me to consume the undying heavenly ambrosia and the medicine of true wisdom. You gave me the universal state, a state unattainable even by the virtuous who have pure bodies from the ever-present waters. You make me grow, praised even by the serpent kings and other lords. O Nataraja, what can I do for you?
commentary: Overwhelmed with gratitude, the speaker lists the extraordinary gifts received from God. These are spiritual attainments: the "deathless education" leading to immortality, a heart melted with love, and a purified body. This grace has elevated him to a state praised even by celestial beings, leaving him to wonder what offering could possibly repay such generosity from Nataraja (the King of Dance).

translit: vētānta nilaiyumataṉ antattē viḷaṅkum meynnilaiyum kāṭṭuvittīr viḷaṅkiyacit tāntap pōtānta nilaiyumappāl pukalaritām periya poruḷnilaiyum terivittīr puṇṇiyarē numatu pātāntam aṟivittīr cuttavaṭi vuṭaṉē pakarpiraṇa vākārap paricumeṉak kaḷittīr nātāntat taṉicceṅkōl nāṉceluttak koṭuttīr naṭarāja rēnumakku nāṉetucey vēṉē.
translation: You showed me the state of Vedanta and the state of truth that shines at its very end. You revealed the state at the culmination of wisdom in radiant Siddhanta, and beyond that, the state of the great substance which is difficult to describe. O virtuous one, you made me know the ultimate goal signified by your feet. Along with a pure form, you granted me the experience of the articulated form of Pranava. You gave me the unique scepter of Nadanta to wield. O Nataraja, what can I do for you?
commentary: God has revealed the ultimate truths of major philosophical paths, such as Vedanta (a philosophy based on the Upanishads) and Siddhanta (a school of Saivite philosophy), and then shown the speaker what lies beyond them. These gifts include a "pure form" (a perfected, immortal body), the experience of Pranava (the cosmic sound Om), and even authority in the state of Nadanta (the silence beyond all sound). Faced with such supreme gifts, the speaker can only ask in pure wonder: "what can I do for you?"

translit: ārnīeṉ ṟetirviṉavil viṭaikoṭukkat teriyā aṟiviliyēṉ poruṭṭāka aṉṟuvanteṉ taṉakkē ērnīṭum perumporuḷoṉ ṟīntumakiḻn tāṇṭīr iṉṟumvalin teḷiyēṉpāl eytioḷi ōṅkap pārnīṭat tiruvaruḷām peruñcōti aḷittīr pakarumelām vallacittip paṇpuṟavum ceytīr nārnīṭa nāṉtāṉāy naṭampurikiṉ ṟīrē naṭarāja rēnumakku nāṉetucey vēṉē.
translation: For the sake of this ignorant one, me, who did not know how to answer when asked, "Who are you?", you came that day, gave me a glorious, great substance, and joyfully made me yours. Today as well, you purposefully came to this lowly one and, so that light may flourish and the world prosper, granted me the great Jothi of sacred grace. You also gave me the nature of the renowned, all-powerful siddhi. With enduring love, you now dance as I myself. O Nataraja, what can I do for you?
commentary: The spiritual path often begins with the fundamental question, "Who am I?" For the one who has no answer, God personally intervenes to bestow a true identity. This divine gift, the great Jothi (light) of grace, is meant to illuminate the entire world. The culmination of this grace is a state where the distinction between the self and God dissolves, where God "dances as I myself," animating the person's very being.

translit: pāyiramā maṟaikaḷelām pāṭukiṉṟa pāṭṭuṉ pāṭṭēeṉ ṟaṟintukoṇṭēṉ paramporuḷuṉ perumai āyiramā yiraṅkōṭi nāuṭaiyōr eṉiṉum aṇuttuṇaiyum pukalaritēl antōic ciṟiyēṉ vāyiraṅkā vakaipukalat tuṇintēṉeṉ ṉuṭaiya maṉattācai orukaṭalō eḻukaṭalil peritē cēyiraṅkā muṉameṭuttē aṇaittiṭuntāy aṉaiyāy tirucciṟṟam palamviḷaṅkum civañāṉa kuruvē.
translation: I have come to understand that all the songs sung by the Vedas, which serve as prefaces, are your songs. O transcendent substance, if even those with thousands upon thousands of crores of tongues cannot speak an atom's worth of your greatness, alas, this small one has dared to speak without faltering. Is the desire in my mind just one ocean? No, it is greater than the seven oceans! You are like a mother who lifts up and embraces her child before it can even cry out. O master of Siva-Jnana who shines in the sacred hall of consciousness!
commentary: Even the most sacred scriptures, the Vedas, are merely introductions to God's true greatness. Realizing this, the speaker feels both the impossibility of describing the divine and an overwhelming, ocean-sized desire to try. Divine compassion resolves the conflict. God is like a mother who senses her child’s need before it even cries, accepting the heart’s silent, loving intention to praise the master of Siva-Jnana (the wisdom of Siva).

translit: ūṉuraikkum uyiraḷavum ulakaḷavum aṟiyēṉ uṉṉaḷavai aṟivēṉō eṉṉaḷavai aṟintōy vāṉuraikka māṭṭātē varuntiṉavē maṟaiyum vakutturaikka aṟiyātē mayaṅkiṉavē antō kōṉuraikkum kuṟikuṇaṅkaḷ kaṭantaperu veḷimēl kūṭātē kūṭiniṉṟa kōvēniṉ iyalai nāṉuraikka nāṉārō nāṉārō navilvēṉ nāṉeṉavē nāṇukiṉṟēṉ naṭarāja kuruvē.
translation: I do not know the measure of the body, of life, or of the world. You who know my measure, how could I possibly know Yours? The sky cannot speak of it; the Vedas grieved, unable to. Alas, they became confused, not knowing how to define and describe it. O King who stands impossibly united in the great space beyond all signs and qualities proclaimed by masters! Who am I to speak of Your nature? Who am I? Who am I to declare it? O Nataraja Guru, I am ashamed even to say the word 'I'.
commentary: In the face of God's infinite nature, all human knowledge falls short. The speaker confesses that he does not even understand his own small self, let alone the divine, which even the Vedas (sacred texts) could not describe. God exists in a state beyond all form, qualities, or definitions. This realization leads to a deep humility, where the very act of saying "I" feels like an expression of ego, a falsehood before the boundless reality of the divine teacher, the Nataraja Guru.

translit: kaṇṇuṭaiyīr peruṅkaruṇaik kaṭaluṭaiyīr eṉatu kaṇakkaṟintīr vaḻakkaṟintīr kaḷittuvantaṉ ṟuraittīr eṇṇuṭaiyār eḻuttuṭaiyār ellārum pōṟṟa eṉṉitaya malarmicainiṉ ṟeḻuntaruḷi vāmap peṇṇuṭaiya maṉaṅkaḷikkap pērulakam kaḷikkap pettarumut tarumakiḻap pattarelām parava viṇṇuṭaiya aruṭjōti viḷaiyāṭal puriya vēṇṭumeṉṟēṉ eṉpataṉmuṉ virainticaintīr ataṟkē.
translation: You who have eyes! You who are a great ocean of compassion! You know my account and you know my ways. You came joyfully that day and spoke. I said, “You must stand upon the flower of my heart and graciously arise, so that all who possess learning and letters may praise you, so that the heart of the beautiful woman on your left rejoices, the great world rejoices, the bound and the liberated rejoice, all devotees offer praise, and you must perform the play of the heavenly ArutJothi.” Before I could even finish saying this, you swiftly consented to it.
commentary: The devotee’s prayer here is for the entire world. He asks God to manifest the divine play of ArutJothi (grace-light) from within his heart, so that all beings may rejoice and be liberated. This includes the divine feminine principle (the "beautiful woman on your left"), scholars, and souls who are both bound and free. The verse illustrates the immediacy of divine compassion: God, knowing the sincere heart of the devotee, grants this universal prayer before it is even fully articulated.

translit: potunaṭañcey malaraṭieṉ talaimēlē amaittīr puttamutam aḷittīreṉ puṉmaielām poṟuttīr catumaṟaiā kamaṅkaḷelām cāṟṟariya periya taṉittalaimait tantaiyarē cākāta varamum etuniṉaittēṉ niṉaittāṅkē atupuriyum tiṟamum iṉpaaṉu pavanilaiyum eṉakkaruḷu vataṟkē itutaruṇam eṉṟēṉnāṉ eṉpataṉmuṉ koṭuttīr eṉpukalvēṉ eṉpuṭainum aṉpirunta vāṟē.
translation: You placed the flower-feet that perform the cosmic dance upon my head. You gave me fresh ambrosia. You forgave all my wretchedness. O great, supreme, unique Father, whom the four Vedas and the Agamas find impossible to describe! I said, “This is the moment to grant me the boon of immortality, the power to accomplish whatever I think, just as I think it, and the state of blissful experience.” Before I could even finish saying it, you gave them to me. What can I say about the nature of your love for me?
commentary: Vallalar lists the supreme gifts he has requested: immortality, the power to accomplish anything by thought alone, and a permanent state of bliss. The "placing of the feet" on his head is a traditional sign of a guru's highest initiation. That God grants these boons before the request is even finished reveals a divine love so immense that it defies explanation.

translit: karumpiṉmika iṉikkiṉṟa karuṇaiamu taḷittīr kaṇṇaṉaiyir kaṉakacapai karutiyaciṟ capaimuṉ turumpiṉmikac ciṟiyēṉnāṉ aṉṟuniṉṟu tuyarntēṉ tuyarēleṉ ṟellaiyiṭṭīr turaiyēav vellai virumpuṟaā yiṟṟitutāṉ taruṇamintat taruṇam viraintaruḷa vēṇṭumeṉa viḷampiniṉṟēṉ aṭiyēṉ perumpiḻaikaḷ aṉaittiṉaiyum poṟuttaruḷi innāḷ peritaḷittīr aruṭperumai peṟṟavaḷil peritē.
translation: You gave me the ambrosia of compassion, sweeter than sugarcane. You who are like my own eyes! That day, I, smaller than a speck of dust, stood suffering before the Kanaka Sabai and the Chit Sabhai that I cherish. “Suffer no more,” you said, setting a limit. O Lord, the time you set has now arrived. “This is the moment. You must bestow your grace swiftly,” I, your devotee, stood and proclaimed. Forgiving all my great wrongs, today you have given abundantly; the greatness of your grace is greater than that of the mother who bore me.
commentary: The poem recalls a moment of past suffering before the Kanaka Sabai and the Chit Sabhai, where God promised an end to that pain. Vallalar now declares that the time for that promise has come, holding God to his word. Forgiving all his faults, God has given abundantly, and the greatness of this grace exceeds even the love of the mother who bore him.

translit: annāḷil aṭicciṟiyēṉ ampalavā yililē aruḷainiṉain torupuṟattē ayarntaḻutu niṉṟēṉ munnāḷil yāṉpurinta peruntavattāl eṉakku mukamalarntu moḻintaaruṇ moḻiyainiṉain tantac cennāḷai etirpārttē paṉṉāḷum kaḷittēṉ cintaimalarn tiruntēṉac celvamiku tirunāḷ innāḷē ātaliṉāl eṉakkaruḷvīr eṉṟēṉ eṉpataṉmuṉ aḷittīrnum aṉpulakil peritē.
translation: On that day, I, your humble servant, stood weary and weeping to one side at the entrance to the Ambalam, thinking of your grace. Because of the great penance I performed in former times, you spoke words of grace to me with a smiling face. Remembering those words, I spent many days rejoicing, eagerly awaiting that auspicious day, my mind in full bloom. I said, “That prosperous and sacred day is today, so grant me your grace.” Before I could even finish saying it, you gave it. Your love is the greatest in the world.
commentary: This verse returns to the theme of a divine promise made in the past and fulfilled in the present. It highlights that the joy of a spiritual seeker comes from receiving grace and from living in the certain anticipation of it. The repeated detail of God granting the wish "before I could even finish" emphasizes that divine love is immediate, overflowing, and always ready to give.

translit: uruvāy aruvāy oḷiyāy veḷiyāy ulavā orupē raruḷā ramutam taruvāy ituvē taruṇam taruṇam tariyēṉ ciṟitun tariyēṉ iṉinī varuvāy alaiyēl uyirvāḻ kalaṉnāṉ maticēr muṭiem patiyē aṭiyēṉ kuruvāy muṉamē maṉamē iṭamāk kuṭikoṇ ṭavaṉē apayam apayam.
translation: You are form and formless, light and space. Grant me the undiminishing nectar of great grace. This is the moment, the moment! I cannot bear it, not even for a little. I cannot bear it any longer. If you do not come, I cannot live on. O my Lord with the moon-adorned crown, you who long ago came as my guru and made my mind your home! Refuge, refuge!
commentary: This is a cry from the soul at its absolute limit. The feeling of separation from God has become so unbearable that life itself feels impossible. The opening description of God as both form and formless, light and space, gives way to a raw, desperate plea for refuge (abayam). It is a powerful expression of spiritual longing that has reached a point of crisis, where union must happen now.

translit: eṉṉē ceyvēṉ ceyvakai oṉṟiṅ kitueṉ ṟaruḷvāy ituvē taruṇam maṉṉē ayaṉum tirumā lavaṉum matittaṟ kariya periya poruḷē aṉṉē appā aiyā aracē aṉpē aṟivē amutē aḻiyāp poṉṉē maṇiyē poruḷē aruḷē potuvāḻ puṉitā apayam apayam.
translation: What shall I do? Please graciously tell me, "This is the way." This is the moment. O King! O great Reality, beyond the comprehension of even Brahma and the revered Vishnu! O Mother, Father, Master, King! O Love, Wisdom, Nectar! O imperishable Gold, Gem, Substance, Grace! O Holy One who lives in the common space, refuge, refuge!
commentary: Vallalar asks a direct question: what shall I do? He wants God to say plainly, "This is the way," and he insists the moment is now. He calls God by every name of closeness, Mother, Father, Master, King, Love, Wisdom, Nectar, Gold, and cries again and again for refuge (apayam). God is beyond Brahma and Vishnu, yet near enough to be asked.

translit: karuṇā nitiyē apayam apayam kaṉakā karaṉē apayam apayam aruṇā ṭakaṉē apayam apayam aḻakā amalā apayam apayam taruṇā tavaṉē apayam apayam taṉinā yakaṉē apayam apayam teruṇā ṭuṟuvāy apayam apayam tiruvam palavā apayam apayam.
translation: O Treasure of compassion, refuge, refuge! O Source of gold, refuge, refuge! O Dancer of grace, refuge, refuge! O Beautiful One, O Pure One, refuge, refuge! O youthful Ascetic, refuge, refuge! O peerless Lord, refuge, refuge! O you who are attained through clear wisdom, refuge, refuge! O Lord of the sacred Ambalam, refuge, refuge!
commentary: The verse is a litany: each name of God is followed by the same cry, "refuge, refuge" (apayam). Treasure of compassion, Dancer of grace, Pure One, peerless Lord, Lord of the sacred Ambalam. Nothing is argued. The soul simply calls, again and again, to the only One who can hold it.

translit: maruḷum tuyarum tavirum paṭieṉ maṉamaṉ ṟiṭainī varuvāy apayam iruḷum pavamum peṟuvañ cakaneñ ciṉaṉeṉ ṟikaḻēl apayam apayam veruḷum koṭuvem pulaiyum kolaiyum viṭumā ṟaruḷvāy apayam apayam aruḷum poruḷum teruḷum taruvāy apayam apayam apayam apayam.
translation: Come into the arena of my mind so that delusion and sorrow may cease. Refuge! Do not scorn me as one with a deceitful heart who deserves only darkness and rebirth. Refuge, refuge! Graciously grant that I may give up the terrifying, cruel eating of flesh and all murder. Refuge, refuge! Grant me grace, substance, and clarity. Refuge, refuge, refuge, refuge!
commentary: Vallalar asks God to enter the arena of his mind so that delusion and sorrow end, and not to scorn him as a deceitful heart fit only for darkness and rebirth. Above all he asks to be freed from the cruel eating of flesh (pulai) and from murder (kolai). Freedom from flesh-eating and murder stands beside freedom from delusion: both must come before grace and clarity can be given.

translit: iṉiōr iṟaiyum tariyēṉ apayam ituniṉ aruḷē aṟiyum apayam kaṉiyēṉ eṉanī niṉaiyēl apayam kaṉiyēkaruṇaik kaṭalē apayam taṉiyēṉ tuṇaivē ṟaṟiyēṉ apayam takumō takumō talaivā apayam tuṉiyē aṟavan taruḷvāy apayam cukanā ṭakaṉē apayam apayam.
translation: I cannot bear this even for a moment longer, refuge! Only your grace can know my state, refuge! Do not think me unripened, refuge! O perfectly Ripe Fruit, O Ocean of compassion, refuge! I am alone and know no other support, refuge! Is this right? Is this fitting, O Master? Refuge! Come and graciously bless me, ending all my suffering completely, refuge! O Actor in the drama of bliss, refuge, refuge!
commentary: Vallalar cannot wait a moment longer. He asks God not to think him unripe, alone as he is with no other support. "Is this right? Is this fitting?" he asks, as a child asks a parent. He calls God the Ripe Fruit and Ocean of compassion, and asks God to come and end his suffering completely. The cry for refuge runs through every line.

translit: aṭiyār itayām puyaṉē apayam aracē amutē apayam apayam muṭiyā tiṉināṉ tariyēṉ apayam muṟaiyō muṟaiyō mutalvā apayam kaṭiyēṉ alaṉnāṉ apayam apayam karuṇā karaṉē apayam apayam taṭiyēl aruḷvāy apayam apayam taruṇā tavaṉē apayam apayam.
translation: O You who are the lotus in your devotees' hearts, refuge! O King, O Nectar, refuge, refuge! I can bear this no longer, refuge! Is this fair? Is this just? O Primal Lord, refuge! I am not a cruel man, refuge, refuge! O source of compassion, refuge, refuge! Do not delay, grant your grace, refuge, refuge! O youthful ascetic, refuge, refuge!
commentary: Vallalar pleads with the boldness of one who has a claim: "Is this fair? Is this just?" He insists he is not a cruel man, and asks God, the lotus in the hearts of devotees, not to delay. This is the trust of a child who knows the Parent is compassion itself.

translit: malavā taṉainīr kalavā apayam valavā tiruam palavā apayam ulavā neṟinī colavā apayam uṟaivāy uyirvāy iṟaivā apayam palaā kulamnāṉ tariyēṉ apayam palavā pakavā paṉavā apayam nalavā aṭiyēṉ alavā apayam naṭanā yakaṉē apayam apayam.
translation: O You who are untouched by the waters of impurity and latent tendencies, refuge! O Master of virtue, O Lord of the sacred Hall of Consciousness, refuge! Will you not speak of the undying path? Refuge! O Lord, you who dwell as the very breath of life, refuge! I cannot bear these many agonies, refuge! O Manifold One, O Bhagavan, O You who are praised, refuge! Am I not your good devotee? Refuge! O Lord of the Dance, refuge, refuge!
commentary: God is untouched by impurity (malam) and by the tendencies (vācaṉai) that bind souls. Vallalar asks God to speak the undying path to him, the way that does not end in death. He cannot bear his many agonies and asks, "Am I not Your good devotee?" Purity, deathlessness and refuge are woven into one cry.

translit: koṭiyēṉ piḻainī kuṟiyēl apayam kolaitīr neṟieṉ kuruvē apayam muṭiyēṉ piṟavēṉ eṉaniṉ aṭiyē muyalvēṉ ceyalvē ṟaṟiyēṉ apayam paṭiyē aṟiyum paṭiyē varuvāy patiyē katiyē paramē apayam aṭiyēṉ iṉiōr iṟaiyum tariyēṉ aracē aruḷvāy apayam apayam.
translation: Do not take note of the faults of this cruel one, refuge! O my Guru of the path that renounces killing, refuge! Striving at your sacred feet, vowing, "I shall not die, I shall not be born again," I know no other action, refuge! Come in a way that the world can comprehend! O Master, O Goal, O Supreme One, refuge! Your devotee can no longer bear this, not even for an instant. O King, grant your grace, refuge, refuge!
commentary: Vallalar begs God to overlook his flaws and names God as the Guru of the path that ends killing: the true path is compassion that renounces killing. His vow is plain: “I shall not die, I shall not be born again.” Not dying is what he strives for at God's feet. His longing for God to come in a way the world can see is so intense that he can no longer wait.

translit: iṭartīr neṟiyē aruḷvāy apayam iṉināṉ tariyēṉ tariyēṉ apayam viṭarpōl eṉainī niṉaiyēl apayam viṭuvēṉ alaṉnāṉ apayam apayam uṭalō ṭuṟumā poruḷā viyumiṅ kuṉavē eṉavē alavē apayam cuṭarmā maṇiyē apayam apayam cukanā ṭakaṉē apayam apayam.
translation: Grant me the path that ends all suffering, refuge! I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it any longer, refuge! Do not think of me as a deceitful rogue, refuge! I will not let you go, refuge, refuge! My body, my precious possessions, and my very soul here, are they not yours and for you alone? Refuge! O great, radiant Gem, refuge, refuge! O Actor in the drama of bliss, refuge, refuge!
commentary: The plea continues with a new intensity as Vallalar declares he will not let go of God. This is the desperate, loving grip of a child on a parent. He affirms his total surrender by stating that everything he has, even his body and soul, already belongs to God.

translit: kuṟṟam palaā yiṉumnī kuṟiyēl kuṇamē koḷumeṉ kuruvē apayam paṟṟam palamē alatōr neṟiyum patiyē aṟiyēṉ aṭiyēṉ apayam cuṟṟam palavum uṉavē eṉavō tuṇaivē ṟilainiṉ tuṇaiyē apayam ciṟṟam palavā aruḷvāy iṉināṉ ciṟitun tariyēṉ tariyēṉ apayam.
translation: Though my faults are many, do not count them, O my Guru who accepts only virtue, refuge! Other than the great strength of clinging to you, O Master, I, your devotee, know no other path, refuge! I consider all my relations to be yours alone; there is no help other than your help, refuge! O Lord of the Small Hall, grant your grace! I cannot bear this any longer, not even a little, I cannot bear it, refuge!
commentary: Clinging to God is presented as the only possible path. Vallalar extends his devotion beyond personal surrender, offering even his worldly relationships to God and seeing them as part of the divine family. The reference to the 'Lord of the Small Hall' (Chitrambalam) connects this plea to the sacred center of worship, both in the famous temple and within his own heart.
NOTES
Note 241

translit: kaḷiyē - paṭivēṟupāṭu. ā. pā.
translation: kaḷiyē — variant reading. Ā. Pā. edition.

translit: taṉipperun talaivarē tāyava rēeṉ tantaiya rēperun tayavuṭai yavarē paṉippaṟut teṉaiyāṇṭa parampara rēem pārvati purañāṉap paticitam pararē iṉicciṟu poḻutēṉun tāḻttiṭal vēṇṭā iṟaiyava rēumai iṅkukaṇ ṭallāl aṉiccaya ulakiṉaip pārkkavum māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: O singular great Leader! O my Mother, my Father, O One of great compassion! O supreme One who ended my fear and took me as your own! O my Lord of Chidambaram in Parvathipuram, the city of wisdom! Do not delay even for a short moment. O Lord, unless I see you here, I will not even look at this impermanent world. O Vast Grace-Light, I swear this upon you.
commentary: Here Vallalar makes a solemn vow directly to God, whom he addresses with intimate names like Mother and Father. He swears an oath upon the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), his ultimate name for the Divine, that he will refuse to even look at the impermanent world until God grants him a direct vision. This is a powerful act of spiritual commitment, withdrawing all attention from the world to focus it entirely on God.

translit: peṟuvatu numaiaṉṟip piṟitoṉṟum virumpēṉ pēcalnum pēccaṉṟip piṟitoṉṟum pēcēṉ uṟuvatunum aruḷaṉṟip piritoṉṟum uvavēṉ uṉṉalum tiṟaṉaṉṟip piritoṉṟum uṉṉēṉ maṟuneṟi tīrtteṉai vāḻvittuk koṇṭīr vaḷḷalē numtiru varavukaṇ ṭallāl aṟucuvai uṇṭikoṇ ṭaruntavum māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: I desire to attain nothing other than you; I speak of nothing other than you. I rejoice in attaining nothing other than your grace; I think of nothing other than your nature. You rid me of wrongful paths and made me live. O generous benefactor, unless I see your sacred arrival, I will not even partake of a six-flavored meal. O Vast Grace-Light, I swear this upon you.
commentary: This verse deepens the vow, extending it to every faculty of being: desire, speech, emotion, and thought are all to be focused solely on God. Vallalar then brings this total commitment into the physical world by swearing he will not eat a proper meal until God appears. By renouncing even the basic pleasure of food, he demonstrates the urgency and all-consuming nature of his longing for the divine.

translit: karumpiṭai iratamum kaṉiyiliṉ cuvaiyum kāṭṭieṉ uḷḷam kalantiṉik kiṉṟīr virumpinum poṉṉaṭik kāṭpaṭṭu niṉṟēṉ mēlviḷai vaṟikilaṉ viccaioṉ ṟillēṉ turumpiṉum ciṟiyaṉai aṉṟuvan tāṇṭīr tūyanum pēraruṭ cōtikaṇ ṭallāl arumpeṟal uṇṭiyai virumpavum māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: Showing the juice within sugarcane and the sweet taste in fruit, you merge with my heart and sweeten it. Willingly, I stand enslaved to your golden feet. I do not know what will happen next; I possess no special knowledge. You came that day and took as your own this one, who is smaller than a blade of grass. Unless I see your pure, great grace-light, I will not even desire rare food. O Vast Grace-Light, I swear this upon you.
commentary: The experience of God is a felt sweetness that fills the heart. Vallalar contrasts this inner delight with his own deep humility, seeing himself as less than grass and possessing no special spiritual knowledge (viddhai). His path is about being small and open enough to receive a grace that is freely offered.

translit: taṭutteṉai āṭkoṇṭa tantaiya rēeṉ taṉipperun talaivarē capainaṭat tavarē toṭuttoṉṟu colkilēṉ coppaṉat tēṉum tūyanum tiruvaruḷ nēyamviṭ ṭaṟiyēṉ viṭuttiṭil eṉṉainīr viṭuppaṉeṉ uyirai veruvuḷak karuttellām tiruvuḷat taṟivīr aṭuttiṉip pāyalil paṭukkavum māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: O Father who stopped me and took me as your own! My singular great Leader! O Dancer in the Hall! I do not invent and say anything, even in a dream; I have never abandoned my love for your pure, sacred grace. If you abandon me, I will abandon my life. You know in your sacred mind all the fearful thoughts in my heart. From now on, I will not even lie down on my bed. O Vast Grace-Light, I swear this upon you.
commentary: The desperation of waiting deepens into a life-or-death plea. Vallalar's existence has become so intertwined with God that he feels he cannot live without the divine presence. By vowing not even to lie down to sleep, he shows he is in a state of constant, anxious vigil, unable to rest until he achieves union.

translit: kācaiyum paṇattaiyum kaṉṉiyar tamaiyum kāṇiyiṉ āṭciyum karutilēṉ kaṇṭīr nēcanum tiruvaruḷ nēcamoṉ ṟallāl nēcammaṟ ṟilaiitu nīraṟi yīrō ēcaṟal akaṟṟivan teṉṉaimuṉ āṇṭīr iṟaiyava rēumai iṉṟukaṇ ṭallāl ācaiyiṟ piṟaroṭu pēcavum māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: I have considered neither coins, wealth, and maidens, nor rule over land, you see. I have no love other than the love for your sacred grace. Do you not know this? You came before me, removed my disgrace, and took me as your own. O Lord, unless I see you today, I will not even speak affectionately with others. O Vast Grace-Light, I swear this upon you.
commentary: Worldly attachments like wealth, power, and desire for women have lost all their appeal. Vallalar states that his one and only love is for God's grace, and he makes a tender appeal, as if to a lover: "Surely you know this." Refusing to speak affectionately with others shows that his entire capacity for connection is now directed exclusively toward the Divine.

translit: eṉporuḷ eṉuṭal eṉuyir ellām īntaṉaṉ ummiṭat temperu māṉīr iṉpoṭu vāṅkikkoṇ ṭeṉṉaiyāṭ koṇṭīr eṉceyal oṉṟilai yāvumnum ceyalē vaṉpoṭu niṟkilīr eṉpoṭu kalantīr vaḷḷalē numtiru varavukaṇ ṭallāl aṉpoṭu kāṇpārai muṉpiṭa māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: I have given my possessions, my body, and my life, everything, to You, my great Lord. You accepted them with delight and took me as Your own. No action is mine; everything is Your action. You do not stand apart in harshness; You have mingled with my very bones. O generous Giver, until I see Your sacred arrival, I will not even receive those who come to see me with love. O ArutPerunJothi, I swear this upon You.
commentary: This is the culmination of complete surrender. Having given his body, life, and possessions to God, Vallalar no longer sees his actions as his own; they are all expressions of the Divine will. Having merged so completely, the final separation is unbearable. Until he sees the sacred arrival of the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), he will not even perform the basic social act of welcoming loving visitors.

translit: tiruntumeṉ uḷḷat tirukkōyil ñāṉa citti purameṉac cattiyam kaṇṭēṉ iruntaruḷ kiṉṟanīr eṉṉiru kaṇkaḷ iṉpuṟa aṉṟuvan teḻiluruk kāṭṭi varuntalai eṉṟeṉait tēṟṟiya vāṟē vaḷḷalē iṉṟunum varavukaṇ ṭallāl aruntavar nēriṉum poruntavum māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: I have seen the truth that my reforming heart is Your sacred temple, the City of Wisdom's Attainment. You, who graciously abide there, came that day and showed Your beautiful form, delighting my two eyes. Just as You comforted me, saying, “Do not suffer,” O generous Giver, until I see Your arrival today, I will not associate even with great ascetics if they approach me. O ArutPerunJothi, I swear this upon You.
commentary: The true temple of God, he realizes, is his own purified heart. He recalls a past vision where God appeared and comforted him, and holding onto that memory, he escalates his demand. Until God appears again, he will not even associate with great holy men, showing that no spiritual company can substitute for a direct vision of God.

translit: karaikkaṇam iṉṟiyē kaṭalnilai ceytīr karuṇaik kaṭaṟkuk karaikkaṇañ ceyyīr uraikkaṇa vāta uyarvuṭai yīreṉ uraikkaṇa vippala utavicey kiṉṟīr varaikkaṇa eṇkuṇa māniti āṉīr vāymaiyil kuṟittanum varavukaṇ ṭallāl araikkaṇam āyiṉum tarittiṭa māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: You keep the ocean in its place without any wall at its shore, yet You set no shore to Your ocean of compassion. You possess a greatness beyond all words. You give me so many aids I cannot even speak of them. You are the great, immeasurable treasure of eight qualities. Until I see Your truly promised arrival, I cannot endure even for half a moment. O ArutPerunJothi, I swear this upon You.
commentary: Vallalar marvels that God holds the sea within its bounds without any wall, yet sets no shore to the ocean of His own compassion. God's greatness is beyond words, and His help reaches him in more ways than he can tell. Holding God to the promised arrival, he states that he cannot endure even half a moment longer.

translit: maṭukkanum pēraruḷ taṇamu teṉakkē mālaiyum kālaiyum mattiyā ṉattum kaṭukkum iraviṉum yāmattum viṭiyaṟ kālaiyi ṉuntanteṉ kaṭumpaci tīrttu eṭukkunaṟ ṟāyoṭum iṇaintuniṟ kiṉṟīr iṟaiyava rēummai iṅkukaṇ ṭallāl aṭukkavīḻ kalaieṭut tuṭukkavum māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: For me to drink, Your great grace is cool nectar. In the evening, morning, midday, swift night, deep night watch, and dawn, You gave it and quenched my fierce hunger. You stand united with me like a good mother who lifts up her child. O Lord, until I see You here, I will not even pick up and wear the garment that has slipped from my waist. O ArutPerunJothi, I swear this upon You.
commentary: God's grace has nourished him constantly, day and night, like a loving mother feeding her child. Yet, this inner sustenance is no longer enough. He makes a strikingly physical vow: he will not even pick up the garment that has fallen from his waist until God appears in person. This shows a desperate, almost childlike insistence on God's physical presence.

translit: kaṟutturaik kiṉṟavar kaḷitturaik kiṉṟa kālaiī teṉṟē karuttuḷ aṟintēṉ niṟutturaik kiṉṟapal nērmaikaḷ iṉṟi nīṭoḷip poṟpotu nāṭakam purivīr ceṟutturaik kiṉṟavar tērvataṟ kariyīr ciṟcapai yīreṉaic cērntiṭal vēṇṭum aṟutturaik kiṉṟēṉnāṉ poṟuttiṭa māṭṭēṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyīr āṇainum mītē.
translation: I have understood in my heart that this is the time when those who spoke with malice will speak with joy. Disregarding the many conventions people establish, You perform Your play in the vast, radiant Golden Hall. You are difficult to grasp for those who speak in scorn. O One of the Hall of Consciousness, You must come and join me. I state this definitively: I can bear it no longer. O ArutPerunJothi, I swear this upon You.
commentary: He senses that the time for union is near, a time when even his critics will have to rejoice. Addressing God, who performs a divine play in the Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness), he makes a final, absolute demand. He is beyond patience; his need is so total that he simply states a fact: he can no longer bear the separation, and God must come to him now.

sections.title: Garland of the Light of Grace

translit: aruḷviḷakkē aruṭcuṭarē aruṭcōtic civamē aruḷamutē aruḷniṟaivē aruḷvaṭivap poruḷē iruḷkaṭinteṉ uḷamuḻutum iṭaṅkoṇṭa patiyē eṉaṟivē eṉuyirē eṉakkiṉiya uṟavē maruḷkaṭinta māmaṇiyē māṟṟaṟiyāp poṉṉē maṉṟilnaṭam purikiṉṟa maṇavāḷā eṉakkē teruḷaḷitta tiruvāḷā ñāṉa:uru vāḷā teyvanaṭat taracēnāṉ ceymoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O Lamp of Grace, O Flame of Grace, O Sivam of Grace-Jothi! O Nectar of Grace, O Fullness of Grace, O Substance whose very form is Grace! O Lord who dispelled the darkness and took Your place throughout my inner being! O my awareness, O my life-breath, O my sweet kinsman! O great gem that dispelled delusion, O gold of untestable purity! O Bridegroom who performs the dance in the Hall, O blessed One who gave me clarity, O One whose form is wisdom! O King of the divine dance, please graciously accept the words I compose.
commentary: God is defined here entirely by Grace (arul). Every name, from lamp and flame to nectar and substance, is a quality of Grace. ArutPerunJothi isn't a distant deity but an intimate presence that has entered and filled his whole being, dispelling all darkness. He addresses God as Sivam (the auspicious ultimate reality) and Jothi (Light).

translit: kōṭaiyilē iḷaippāṟṟik koḷḷumvakai kiṭaitta kuḷirtaruvē taruniḻalē niḻalkaṉinta kaṉiyē ōṭaiyilē ūṟukiṉṟa tīñcuvaittaṇṇīrē ukantataṇ riṭaimalarnta cukantamaṇa malarē mēṭaiyilē vīcukiṉṟa melliyapūṅ kāṟṟē meṉkāṟṟil viḷaicukamē cukattiluṟum payaṉē āṭaiyilē eṉaimaṇanta maṇavāḷā potuvil āṭukiṉṟa aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O cool tree found for resting from the summer heat! O shade of the tree, O fruit ripened in the shade! O sweet-tasting water welling up in the stream! O fragrant flower that blossomed in the pleasant, cool water! O gentle, flower-scented breeze wafting on the veranda! O pleasure produced by that gentle breeze, O fruit of that pleasure! O Bridegroom who wedded me in the Hall of Dance, O King who dances in the common Hall, please graciously wear my garland.
commentary: God's presence is described through simple experiences of relief and pleasure. Like finding shade on a hot day or cool water when thirsty, God is a tangible comfort and a source of deep, sensory delight. The request for God to wear his garland of words in the Potu (the common Hall of dance) is a plea for this intimate experience to be accepted and made universal.

translit: iṉpuṟanāṉ eyppiṭattē peṟṟaperu vaippē ēṅkiyapō teṉṟaṉṉait tāṅkiyanal tuṇaiyē aṉpuṟaeṉ uṭkalantē aṇṇikkum amutē accamelām tavirtteṉṉai āṭkoṇṭa kuruvē eṉparuvam kuṟiyātē eṉaimaṇanta patiyē iccaiyuṟṟa paṭiellām eṉakkaruḷum turaiyē tuṉpaṟamey aṉparukkē potunaṭañcey aracē tūyatiru vaṭikaḷukkeṉ collumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great treasure I obtained to my delight when I was weary! O good companion who supported me when I was pining! O sweet nectar that lovingly mingled within me! O Guru who removed all my fears and took me as Your own! O Lord who wedded me without regard for my state! O Master who graciously grants me whatever I desire! O King who performs the common dance for true devotees so their suffering ceases! Please graciously adorn Your pure, sacred feet with my words as well.
commentary: God is portrayed here as the ultimate support in moments of human vulnerability. He is a treasure for the weary, a companion for the lonely, and a Guru (spiritual teacher) who erases fear. The most moving idea is that God accepts him unconditionally, wedding him without judging his state of readiness and granting all his heart's desires.

translit: ocittakoṭi aṉaiyēṟkuk kiṭaittaperum paṟṟē uḷmayaṅkum pōtumayak koḻittaruḷum teḷivē pacittapoḻu tetirkiṭaitta pālcōṟṟut tiraḷē payantapoḻu tellāmeṉ payantavirtta turaiyē nacittavarai eḻuppiaruḷ nalkiyamā maruntē nāṉpuṇara nāṉāki naṇṇiyameyc civamē kacittamaṉat taṉpartoḻap potunaṭañcey aracē kaḷitteṉatu coṉmālai kaḻalilaṇin taruḷē.
