translation: O great support found by me, who am like a slender creeper! O clarity that graciously dispels confusion when I am inwardly bewildered! O ball of milk-rice that appeared before me when I was hungry! O Master who removed my fear whenever I was afraid! O great medicine that gave the grace of raising the dead! O true Sivam who approached me, becoming me, so that I could unite with You! O King who performs the common dance for devotees with melted hearts to worship! Please joyfully and graciously wear my garland of words on Your ankleted foot.
commentary: This verse expresses the pinnacle of intimacy, where God becomes the very self of the devotee so that union can happen. God is support for a fragile creeper, clarity in confusion, milk-rice for the hungry. And God is the great medicine that raised the dead and gave them grace: Vallalar states this as God's work, not as an image. This is a complete merging with the true Sivam who meets the soul exactly where it is.

translit: maṉamiḷaittu vāṭiyapō teṉetirē kiṭaittu vāṭṭamelām tavirtteṉakku vāḻvaḷitta nitiyē ciṉamukattār tamaikkaṇṭu tikaittapoḻu tavaraic cirittamukat tavarākki eṉakkaḷitta civamē aṉamukaittāṉ arimutalōr turuviniṟka eṉakkē aṭimuṭikaḷ kāṭṭuvittē aṭimaikoṇṭa patiyē iṉameṉappē raṉpartoḻap potunaṭañcey aracē eṉṉuṭaiya coṉmālai yāvumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O treasure who, when my mind grew weary and withered, appeared before me, removed all my fatigue, and gave me life! O Sivam who, when I was dismayed at seeing people with angry faces, transformed them into people with smiling faces and gave them to me! O Lord who took me as Your slave, revealing Your feet and crown to me, while Brahma who rides the swan, Vishnu, and others searched in vain! O King who performs the common dance for the community of great devotees to worship! Please graciously wear all of my garlands of words.
commentary: God's grace can directly intervene in the world, restoring a tired mind and even changing the hearts of others from anger to peace. While great celestial beings may search for God and fail, He reveals Himself willingly to the humble devotee who has surrendered. This personal revelation is a greater treasure than the knowledge sought by the powerful.

translit: kaṅkulilē varuntiyaeṉ varuttamelām tavirttē kālaiyilē eṉuḷattē kiṭaittaperuṅ kaḷippē ceṅkuvaḷai mālaiyoṭu mallikaippū mālai cērttaṇinteṉ taṉaimaṇanta teyvamaṇa vāḷā eṅkumoḷi mayamāki niṉṟanilai kāṭṭi eṉakattum puṟattumniṟain tilaṅkiyameyp poruḷē tuṅkamuṟat tiruppotuvil tirunaṭañcey aracē coṉmālai cūṭṭukiṉṟēṉ tōḷilaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great delight I found in my heart in the morning, you who removed all the suffering I endured in the night! O divine Bridegroom who wedded me, wearing a combined garland of red water lilies and jasmine flowers! O true substance who showed me the state of being filled with light everywhere, who fills and shines within and without me! O King who performs the sacred dance in purity in the sacred hall, I am placing this garland of words on you; please wear it graciously on your shoulders.
commentary: The experience of God is a transition from the darkness of suffering to the light of inner joy. This divine presence is an all-pervading light that fills the devotee both internally and externally. The dance of God happens in the thiru podu, a sacred common space of consciousness where this universal light is revealed.

translit: karaintuviṭā teṉṉuṭaiya nāvakattē iruntu kaṉattacuvai tarukiṉṟa kaṟkaṇṭē kaṉivāy viraintuvanteṉ tuṉpamelām tavirttaaru ḷamutē meyaruḷē meyyāki viḷaṅkukiṉṟa viḷakkē tirainta:uṭal viraintuṭaṉē poṉuṭampē ākit tikaḻntaḻiyā tōṅkaaruḷ cittēmeyc cattē varainteṉṉai maṇampurintu potunaṭañcey aracē makiḻvoṭunāṉ puṉaintiṭuñcoṉ mālaiaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O rock candy that stays on my tongue without dissolving, giving a dense sweetness! O nectar of grace who came swiftly with a gentle mouth and removed all my suffering! O lamp that shines as truth itself, O true grace! O true being! O supreme intelligence who grants the grace for this wrinkled body to quickly become a golden body, shining imperishably and rising in glory! O King who claimed and married me and performs the dance in the common hall, please joyfully wear this garland of words I have composed.
commentary: The experience of grace is tangible, like a sweet taste on the tongue, and leads to a deep physical transformation. Vallalar states a key teaching: grace turns this wrinkled body, swiftly, into a golden body that shines and never perishes. This means divinizing the physical form here and now, through God as true being (sat) and consciousness (cit).

translit: katikkuvaḻi kāṭṭukiṉṟa kaṇṇēeṉ kaṇṇil kalantamaṇi yēmaṇiyil kalantakatir oḷiyē vitikkumula kuyirkkuyirāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa civamē meyyuṇarntōr kaiyakattē viḷaṅkiyatīṅ kaṉiyē matikkumatik kappuṟampōy vayaṅkutaṉi nilaiyē maṟaimuṭiā kamamuṭimēl vayaṅkumiṉpa niṟaivē tutikkumaṉpar toḻappotuvil naṭampuriyum aracē coṉmālai cūṭṭukiṉṟēṉ tōḷilaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O eye that shows the way to liberation! O jewel mingled in my eye! O radiant light mingled in that jewel! O Sivam, who shines as the life of life for all destined worlds and beings! O sweet fruit that appeared in the hands of those who have realized the truth! O unique state that shines, going beyond intellect and the intellect that perceives intellect! O fulfillment of bliss that shines atop the crown of the Vedas and the crown of the Agamas! O King who performs the dance in the common hall, worshipped by devotees who praise you, I am placing this garland of words on you; please wear it graciously on your shoulders.
commentary: God is both the ultimate destination and the immediate path. He is the eye that shows the way to liberation (gati), the light within that eye, and the life within all life. This supreme reality, which is beyond all intellect and the pinnacle of scripture (Vedas and Agamas), makes itself available as a sweet fruit in the hands of those who have realized the truth.

translit: aṇṭavaḷa vevvaḷavō avvaḷavum avaṟṟil amaintacarā caraaḷavev vaḷavōav vaḷavum kaṇṭatuvāy āṅkavaikaḷ taṉittaṉiyē akattum kāṇpuṟattum akappuṟattum puṟappuṟattum viḷaṅka viṇṭakupē raruṭcōtip peruveḷikku naṭuvē viḷaṅkioru peruṅkaruṇaik koṭināṭṭi aruḷām taṇṭakumōr taṉicceṅkōl naṭattimaṉṟil naṭikkum taṉiaracē eṉmālai tāḷilaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O unique King who dances in the hall! You have perceived the whole extent of the cosmic spheres and all the moving and unmoving things within them, making each one shine individually: within, visibly without, in the inner-outer, and the outer-outer. You shine in the center of the vast expanse of the boundless great Grace-Light, planting a banner of great compassion and wielding a unique, cooling scepter of grace. Please graciously wear my garland on your feet.
commentary: The divine is portrayed as a cosmic king, conscious of every part of creation, from the inner lives of beings to the vastness of space. This king rules from the very center of a universe made of Grace-Light, symbolized by the sacred hall (manram). His rule is one of compassion, a "cooling scepter" that soothes and sustains all that is.

translit: nallācol yōkāntap patikaḷpala kōṭi nāṭṭiyatōr pōtāntap patikaḷpala kōṭi vallārcol kalāntanilaip patikaḷpala kōṭi vaḻuttumoru nātāntap patikaḷpala kōṭi illārnta vētāntap patikaḷpala kōṭi ilaṅkukiṉṟa cittāntap patikaḷpala kōṭi ellāmpē raruṭcōtit taṉicceṅkōl naṭattum eṉaracē eṉmālai iṉitupuṉain taruḷē.
translation: The many tens of millions of domains of the culmination of Yoga, spoken by good teachers; the many tens of millions of domains of the culmination of knowledge, which they established; the many tens of millions of domains of the state of the culmination of experience, spoken by the able; the many tens of millions of praised domains of the culmination of primal sound; the many tens of millions of substantial domains of the culmination of the Vedas; the many tens of millions of shining domains of the culmination of established truths, O my King, whose unique scepter of great Grace-Light rules over them all, please wear my garland sweetly.
commentary: Vallalar lists the highest achievements of various spiritual systems: the culminations of yoga, knowledge, mystical experience, sacred sound, Vedic philosophy (Vedanta), and established doctrine (Siddhanta). He then declares that all these countless paths are subject to a single, higher power: the universal sovereignty of the "great Grace-Light." This light is the source and ruler of all ways.

translit: nāṭṭiyatōr cuttaparā cattiaṇṭam mutalā ñāṉacatti aṇṭamatu kaṭaiyāka ivaṟṟuḷ īṭṭiyapaṟ palacatti cattaraṇṭap pakuti ettaṉaiyō kōṭikaḷum taṉniḻaṟkīḻ viḷaṅkac cūṭṭiyapoṉ muṭiilaṅkac camaracameyñ ñāṉac cuttaciva caṉmārkkap perunilaiyil amarntē nīṭṭiyapē raruṭcōtit taṉicceṅkōl naṭattum nītinaṭat taracēeṉ neṭuñcolaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O King of the just dance, who makes countless crores of cosmic realms shine under Your shadow, from the established cosmos of Pure Para Shakti to the final cosmos of Gnana Shakti, encompassing all the gathered worlds of various Shaktis and Shaktars! Seated in the great state of Samarasa Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam with Your golden crown gleaming, You wield the unique scepter of extended, vast grace-light. Please adorn Yourself with my lengthy words of praise and grant Your grace.
commentary: This verse expands the cosmic vision, describing God as the ruler of countless universes, each governed by different divine powers (Shaktis) and their possessors (Shaktars). The divine presides over them all from a state called Samarasa Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam. This term describes the "True Path of Pure, Universal Harmony," a state where all differences are reconciled in oneness and grace.

translit: taṉperumai tāṉaṟiyāt taṉmaiyaṉē eṉatu taṉittalaivā eṉṉuyirkkuḷ iṉittataṉic cuvaiyē niṉperumai nāṉaṟiyēṉ nāṉmaṭṭō aṟiyēṉ neṭumālnāṉ mukaṉmutalā mūrttikaḷum aṟiyār aṉpuṟumā kamamaṟaikaḷ aṟiyāvē eṉiṉum avarumavai kaḷumcilacol aṇikiṉṟār niṉakkē eṉparuvam kuṟiyātē eṉaiyāṇṭa aracē yāṉumavar pōlaṇikiṉ ṟēṉaṇintiṅ karuḷē.
translation: O One whose nature is not even to know Your own greatness! My singular Leader! The unique sweetness that sweetened within my very life! I do not know Your greatness; and is it only I who do not know it? The great Vishnu, the four-faced Brahma, and the other deities do not know it. The beloved Agamas and Vedas do not know it. Even so, those gods and those scriptures adorn You with a few words. O King who took me as Your own, disregarding my immaturity, I too, like them, am adorning You. Please accept my adornment and grant Your grace here.
commentary: God's greatness is beyond all comprehension. It is a reality so immense that not even the highest gods like Vishnu and Brahma, nor the most sacred scriptures, can grasp it. In a striking paradox, God is so absolute as to be unaware of his own immensity. Yet this same unknowable being showed personal compassion to Vallalar, accepting him despite his unworthiness. The act of writing poetry becomes a humble attempt to adorn the unadornable.

translit: uṇṇa:uṇṇat teviṭṭātē tittitteṉ uṭampō ṭuyiruṇarvum kalantukalan tuḷḷakattum puṟattum taṇṇiyavaṇ ṇamparavap poṅkiniṟain tāṅkē tatumpieṉṟaṉ mayamellām taṉmayamē ākki eṇṇiyaeṉ eṇṇamelām eytaoḷi vaḻaṅki ilaṅkukiṉṟa pēraruḷām iṉṉamutat tiraḷē puṇṇiyamē eṉperiya poruḷēeṉ aracē puṉmoḻieṉ ṟikaḻātē puṉaintumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: As I consume You again and again, You never cloy but only sweeten, mingling with my body, life, and consciousness, inside and out. Spreading with cool beauty, You swell, fill, and overflow, making everything that is "me" into everything that is "You." O sweet ambrosial flood of vast grace, which shines, granting the light for me to attain all I have ever wished for! O embodiment of merit, my great substance, my King! Do not scorn these as humble words; please adorn Yourself with them, rejoice, and grant Your grace.
commentary: The experience of God is described here with the intimate metaphor of eating a food that is endlessly sweet and satisfying. This divine substance does more than nourish, it completely transforms the one who consumes it, dissolving the devotee's sense of a separate self until "me" becomes "You." This union is the ultimate fulfillment, a flood of grace that makes all things possible by merging the individual's will with God's.

translit: nāṭṭārkaḷ cūḻntumatit tiṭamaṇimē ṭaiyilē naṭuirukka eṉṟaṉaiyē nāṭṭiyapē riṟaivā pāṭṭāḷar pāṭutoṟum paricaḷikkum turaiyē paṉṉumaṟaip pāṭṭēmeyp pāṭṭiṉatu payaṉē kūṭṭāḷā civakāmak koṭikkicainta koḻunā kōvēeṉ kaṇavāeṉ kuravāeṉkuṇavā nīṭṭāḷar pukaḻntētta maṇimaṉṟil naṭikkum nītinaṭat taracēeṉ neṭumoḻikoṇ ṭaruḷē.
translation: O great Lord who established me to sit in the center of a jeweled stage, so that the people of the land would gather around and honor me! O Master who gives gifts each time poets sing! O Song of the recited Vedas! O Fruit of true song! O Companion! O Husband fitting for the vine-like Sivakami! O King, my Husband, my Guru, my virtuous One! O King of the just dance, performing in the Jeweled Hall as the great ones extol and praise You! Please accept my lengthy words and grant Your grace.
commentary: Vallalar gives thanks for the spiritual status God has bestowed upon him, picturing it as being placed on a "jeweled stage" for all to see and respect. He then addresses God with a cascade of titles that move from the cosmic to the deeply personal: from the Lord of the universe and the essence of scripture, to Companion, Husband, and Guru (spiritual teacher). This shows a relationship with God that is at once reverent and deeply intimate.

translit: kaikkicainta poruḷēeṉ karutticainta kaṉivē kaṇṇēeṉ kaṇkaḷukkē kalanticainta kaṇavā meykkicainta aṇiyēpoṉ mēṭaiyileṉ ṉuṭaṉē meykalanta taruṇattē viḷaintaperuñ cukamē neykkicainta uṇavēeṉ neṟikkicainta nilaiyē nittiyamē ellāmāñ cattiyamē ulakil poykkicaintār kāṇātē potunaṭañcey aracē puṉmoḻieṉ ṟikaḻātē puṉaintumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: O substance that fits my hand! O ripeness that matches my intent! O my eye! O Husband who has mingled and become one with my very eyes! O jewel adorning my body! O great bliss born at the moment You united Your body with mine on the golden stage! O food perfectly blended with ghee! O state that befits my path! O eternal One! O truth that is everything! O King who performs the universal dance, unseen by those in the world who embrace falsehood! Do not scorn these as humble words; please adorn Yourself with them, rejoice, and grant Your grace.
commentary: God is an immediate, tangible reality. Vallalar describes the divine as a "substance that fits my hand," the "ripeness that matches my intent," and even the "Husband who has mingled with my very eyes." This union is a total, blissful experience, a state of truth that is completely inaccessible to those who live in falsehood. The ultimate reality is something that can be held, tasted, and worn like a jewel.

translit: koṭuttiṭanāṉ eṭuttiṭavum kuṟaiyāta nitiyē kollāta neṟiyēcit tellāñcey patiyē maṭuttiṭavum aṭuttaṭuttē maṭuppataṟkuḷ ḷācai vaippataṉṟi veṟuppaṟiyā vaṇṇaniṟai amutē eṭutteṭuttup pukaṉṟālum ulavāta oḷiyē eṉuyirē eṉuyiruk kicaintaperun tuṇaiyē taṭuttiṭaval lavarillāt taṉimutaṟpē raracē tāḻmoḻieṉ ṟikaḻātē tarittumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: O treasure that does not diminish when I take from what you give! O path of non-killing! O Master who accomplishes all siddhis! O ambrosia, full of goodness, that inspires only the desire to drink you again and again, never knowing aversion! O light that is never exhausted, however much I praise you! O my life, O great companion perfectly suited to my life! O unique, supreme King whom no one has the power to obstruct! Do not scorn these as lowly words; graciously wear them and be pleased.
commentary: The divine is an infinite and inexhaustible resource: a treasure that never runs out, an ambrosia one never tires of, a light that never dims. Central to this divine nature is the "path of non-killing," identifying God directly with the ultimate principle of compassion. God is also the source of all siddhis (divine powers) and the very companion to one's soul.

translit: taṉittaṉimuk kaṉipiḻintu vaṭittoṉṟāk kūṭṭic carkkaraiyuṅ kaṟkaṇṭiṉ poṭiyumikak kalantē taṉittanaṟun tēṉpeytu pacumpālun tēṅkiṉ taṉippāluñ cērttorutīm paruppiṭiyum viravi iṉittanaṟu neyaḷantē iḷañcūṭṭiṉ iṟakki eṭuttacuvaik kaṭṭiyiṉum iṉittiṭunteḷ ḷamutē aṉittamaṟat tiruppotuvil viḷaṅkunaṭat taracē aṭimalarkkeṉ collaṇiyām alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O clear ambrosia, sweeter even than a flavorful confection made by squeezing and filtering the juice of the three great fruits separately and then combining them; by thoroughly mixing in sugar and powdered rock candy; by adding pure fragrant honey, fresh cow's milk, and pure coconut milk; by blending in a sweet lentil cake; and by adding a measure of sweet fragrant ghee before removing it all from gentle heat! O King of the Dance, who shines in the sacred common space so that impermanence vanishes! Graciously adorn your lotus-like feet with this garland, my ornament of words.
commentary: To describe the sweetness of divine experience, Vallalar creates an image of the most exquisite dessert imaginable, combining rare fruits, honey, and milk. Yet, he says, the bliss of God's presence is sweeter still. This presence, revealed in the Thiru Podu (the sacred common space of consciousness), has a specific function: it makes the fleeting nature of ordinary existence disappear. The poem itself is offered as a garland for the feet of this ultimate reality.

translit: malaivaṟiyāp peruñcōti vacciramā malaiyē māṇikka maṇipporuppē marakatappēr varaiyē vilaiaṟiyā uyarāṇip perumuttut tiraḷē viṇṇavarum naṇṇarumōr meypporuḷiṉ viḷaivē kolaiaṟiyāk kuṇattōrtaṅ kūṭṭuṟavē aruṭceṅ kōlnaṭattu kiṉṟataṉik kōvēmey aṟivāl nilaiaṟintōr pōṟṟumaṇi maṉṟilnaṭat taracē niṉṉaṭippoṉ malarkaḷukkeṉ neṭuñcolaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great mountain of diamond, a vast jothi that knows no confusion! O jeweled hill of ruby! O great mountain of emerald! O cluster of priceless, superior, flawless pearls! O fruition of the one true substance, unapproachable even by the celestials! O fellowship of those whose character knows no killing! O unique King who wields the scepter of grace! O King of the Dance in the jeweled hall, praised by those who have realized the ultimate state through true knowledge! Graciously adorn your golden, flower-like feet with my lengthy poem.
commentary: God is portrayed as the most solid, precious, and luminous substance in existence: a mountain of diamond, a hill of ruby, a flawless pearl. This reality, a vast jothi (divine light), is also described as a community, "the fellowship of those whose character knows no killing," grounding supreme truth in the practice of compassion. The highest state is to know this reality and join the dance of praise in its presence.

translit: kaṇkaḷikkap pukaiciṟitum kāṭṭātē puruvak kalainaṭuvē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa kaṟpūra viḷakkē paṇkaḷikkap pāṭukiṉṟa pāṭṭilviḷai cukamē pattaruḷē tittikkap paḻuttataṉip paḻamē maṇkaḷikka vāṉkaḷikka maṇantaciva kāma vallieṉa maṟaikaḷelām vāḻttukiṉṟa vāmap peṇkaḷikkap potunaṭañcey naṭattaracē niṉatu perumpukaḻccē vaṭikaḷukkeṉ arumpumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O camphor flame that shines between the brows, delighting the eyes without a trace of smoke! O bliss that arises from songs sung with joyful melodies! O unique fruit, ripened to be sweet within the grace of your devotees! O King of the Dance, you perform in the common space for the delight of the beautiful woman on your left, whom all the scriptures praise as Sivakama Valli, the one you wedded to the delight of earth and heaven. Graciously adorn your sacred feet of great fame with my budding words.
commentary: The inner experience of God is like a pure camphor flame seen between the eyebrows: a clear, bright light without any smoke or impurity. This divine presence is also felt as the joy that arises from devotional singing. Vallalar connects this inner experience to the cosmic mythology of Siva's dance, performed for the happiness of his consort, Sivakama Valli, a union that brings delight to both heaven and earth.

translit: uruveḷiyē uruveḷikkuḷ uṟṟaveḷi uruvē urunaṭuvum veḷinaṭuvum oṉṟāṉa oṉṟē peruveḷiyē peruveḷiyil peruñcōti mayamē peruñcōti mayanaṭuvē piṟaṅkutaṉip poruḷē maruoḻiyā malarakattē vayaṅkuoḷi maṇiyē mantiramē tantiramē matippariya maruntē tiruoḻiyā tōṅkumaṇi maṉṟilnaṭat taracē ciṟumoḻieṉ ṟikaḻātē cērttumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: O space of form! O form of space that exists within the space of form! O the One who is the single essence at the center of form and the center of space! O great expanse! O embodiment of the vast jothi within the great expanse! O unique substance that shines at the center of that embodiment of vast jothi! O luminous gem shining within the ever-fragrant flower of the heart! O mantra! O tantra! O priceless medicine! O King of the Dance in the jeweled hall where auspiciousness thrives, never fading! Do not scorn these as humble words; graciously accept them and rejoice.
commentary: God is described through a series of paradoxes to point toward a reality beyond ordinary logic. God is both form and the space that contains form, both substance and emptiness, and in the end they are one. This reality is also called a mantra (sacred sound) and a tantra (sacred method), indicating that God is the path, the practice, and the destination all at once.

translit: nāṉeṉṟum tāṉeṉṟum nāṭāta nilaiyil ñāṉavaṭi vāyviḷaṅkum vāṉanaṭu nilaiyē ūṉeṉṟum uyireṉṟum kuṟiyāmē muḻutum oruvaṭivām tiruvaṭivam uvantaḷitta patiyē tēṉeṉṟum karumpeṉṟum cepparitāy maṉamum tēkamumuḷ ḷuyiruṇarvum tittikkum cuvaiyē vāṉeṉṟum oḷieṉṟum vakupparitām potuvil vayaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ mālaiyumēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O central state of the ether, shining as the form of Gnana in a state that does not seek 'I' or 'That'! O Master who, without marking a distinction between flesh and life-force, joyfully granted a sacred form that is one complete whole! O Sweetness that is impossible to describe as honey or sugarcane, a taste that sweetens the mind, body, inner life-force, and consciousness! O King of Dance, radiant in the common spacewhich is difficult to classify as sky or light, please graciously accept my garland.
commentary: The divine is found in a state of pure awareness, or Gnana (realized wisdom), where the ego's distinction between 'I' and 'other' dissolves. Vallalar gives thanks for being granted a sacred body that is a "one complete whole," a unified existence where the separation between flesh and life-force is gone. This experience is a deep sweetness that permeates the mind, body, and soul.

translit: eṭṭiraṇṭum eṉeṉṟāl mayaṅkiyaeṉ ṟaṉakkē eṭṭāta nilaiellām eṭṭuvitta kuruvē cuṭṭiraṇṭuṅ kāṭṭātē turiyanilai naṭuvē cukamayamāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cuttaparam poruḷē maṭṭitueṉ ṟaṟivataṟku māṭṭātē maṟaikaḷ mavuṉamuṟap paramparattē vayaṅkukiṉṟa oḷiyē taṭṭaṟiyāt tiruppotuvil taṉinaṭañcey aracē tāḻmoḻieṉ ṟikaḻātē tarittumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: O Guru who, to me who was bewildered when asked what 'eight and two' meant, made me attain all unattainable states! O pure supreme Reality, shining as a being of bliss in the midst of the Turiya state, without pointing out dualities! O Light shining in the highest expanse, about which the Vedas fall silent, unable to know and define it as 'this is its limit'! O King who performs the unique dance in the sacred, unobstructed common space, do not scorn these as humble words; graciously wear them and rejoice.
commentary: God is the ultimate Guru who reveals truths that the intellect cannot grasp, like the secret meaning of the phrase 'eight and two'. This supreme Reality is experienced as pure bliss in Turiya, the fourth state of consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. This divine light is so vast that even the sacred scriptures fall silent, unable to describe or limit it.

translit: cātikulam camayamelām tavirtteṉaimēl ēṟṟit taṉittatiru amutaḷitta taṉittalaimaip poruḷē ātinaṭuk kaṭaikāṭṭā taṇṭapaki raṇṭam āruyirkaḷ akampuṟammaṟ ṟaṉaittumniṟai oḷiyē ōtiuṇarn tavarellām eṉaikkēṭka eṉaittāṉ ōtāmal uṇarntuṇarvām uruvuṟaccey uṟavē cōtimaya māyviḷaṅkit taṉippotuvil naṭikkum tūyanaṭat taracēeṉ collumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O unique, supreme Reality who abolished caste, clan, and religion for me, elevated me, and gave me the unique, sacred ambrosia! O Light that fills the cosmos, all its divisions, precious lives, their inner and outer aspects, and everything else, without revealing a beginning, middle, or end! O Kin who made me into a form of awareness, realized without study, causing all who have studied and realized to inquire of me! O pure King of Dance, shining as a being of Jothi and dancing in the unique common space, please graciously wear my words.
commentary: True spirituality transcends all human-made divisions like caste, clan, and religion, elevating the soul to a state of unity. Vallalar testifies that divine grace gave him a direct realization of truth, an awareness that comes from within, not from studying texts. He addresses God as the universal Jothi (divine light) that fills every part of existence, whose dance is for all.

translit: aṭikkaṭieṉ akattiṉilum puṟattiṉilum cōti aruḷuruvāyt tirintutirin taruḷkiṉṟa poruḷē paṭikkaḷaviṉ maṟaimuṭimēl ākamattiṉ muṭimēl patintapatam eṉmuṭimēl patittataṉip patiyē poṭikkaṉakat tirumēṉit tirumaṇaṅkaṟ pūrap poṭimaṇattō ṭakampuṟamum putumaṇañcey amutē aṭikkaṉaka ampalattē tirucciṟṟam palattē āṭalpuri aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Reality that repeatedly wanders within me and without as a form of grace-Jothi, bestowing grace! O singular Master who placed upon my head the sacred feet that are imprinted upon the crest of the extensive Vedas and the crest of the Agamas! O Ambrosia with a sacred body like golden powder, who imparts a new fragrance inside and out with the scent of sacred camphor powder! O King who performs the dance in the foundational golden hall, the Thiru Chithambalam, please graciously wear my garland.
commentary: The divine is described here as a tangible, recurring presence felt both inside and out, a light and a fragrance. To have the Master's feet placed on one's head is a powerful symbol of receiving the highest possible grace, an authority that surpasses even that of the most sacred scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas (texts on ritual and philosophy). This grace is experienced as a dance within the Thiru Chithambalam, the sacred space of one's own consciousness.

translit: aṟaiyāta mikuperuṅkāṟ ṟaṭittālum ciṟitum acaiyātē aviyātē aṇṭapaki raṇṭat tuṟaiyāvum piṇṭavakait tuṟaimuḻutum viḷaṅkat tūṇṭātē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa jōtimaṇi viḷakkē maṟaiyātē kuṟaiyātē kaḷaṅkamum illātē mayakkātē paṉikkātē vayaṅkukiṉṟa matiyē iṟaiyāyev vuyirakattum akappuṟattum puṟattum ilaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O jeweled lamp of Jothi! You shine without being kindled, illuminating all realms of the cosmos and all divisions of the microcosm; you do not flicker or go out in the slightest, even when an unceasing, mighty wind blows. O Moon that shines without hiding, diminishing, or having any blemish, and without causing delusion or coldness! O King of Dance, shining as the Supreme within every soul, in their inner and outer being, and externally, please graciously wear my song.
commentary: God's nature is explained through paradox: God is a lamp of divine light (Jothi) that can never be extinguished and needs no fuel, and a moon that gives perfect light without any of the flaws of the physical moon, such as blemishes, cycles, or coldness. The divine light is steady, perfect, and self-sufficient, illuminating everything without any outside help.

translit: pārttālum niṉaittālum paṭittālum paṭikkap pakkamniṉṟu kēṭṭālum parintuḷuṇarn tālum īrttālum piṭittālum kaṭṭiaṇait tālum ittaṉaikkum tittikkum iṉittacuvaik karumpē vērttāvi mayaṅkātu kaṉintanaṟuṅ kaṉiyē meymmaiaṟi vāṉantam viḷakkumaruḷ amutē tīrttāeṉ ṟaṉparelām toḻappotuvil naṭikkum teyvanaṭat taracēeṉ ciṟumoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O sweet sugarcane, delicious whether I look at you, think of you, read of you, listen as another reads, lovingly feel you within, am drawn to you, hold you, or embrace you. O fragrant fruit that ripened to perfection without struggle or faintness. O nectar of grace that reveals the bliss of true knowledge. O sacred purifier, whom all devotees worship as you dance in the common hall! O divine King of Dance, graciously accept my humble words.
commentary: The experience of God is a pure and effortless sweetness, accessible through any form of devotion: thinking, reading, listening, or feeling. This divine reality is compared to a fruit that ripened perfectly without any struggle, suggesting that this blissful state is a gift of grace, not something earned through difficult effort. As the great purifier (Tīrttā), God cleanses all who come to Him.

translit: paṟṟutalum viṭutalumuḷ aṭaṅkutalum mīṭṭum paṭutaloṭu cuṭutalumpuṇ paṭuttalumil lātē uṟṟoḷikoṇ ṭōṅkieṅkum taṉmayamāy ñāṉa uruvāki uyirkkuyirāy ōṅkukiṉṟa neruppē cuṟṟutalum tōṉṟutalum maṟaitalumvec ceṉṟē cuṭutalumil lāteṉṟum tulaṅkukiṉṟa cuṭarē muṟṟumuṇarn tavaruḷattē tirucciṟṟam palattē muyaṅkumnaṭat taracēeṉ moḻiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O soaring fire, the life of life, the very form of wisdom! You shine and rise high, pervading all space as your own substance, yet without catching and extinguishing, being contained and rekindled, scorching, or causing wounds. O flame that shines forever, without circling about, appearing and disappearing, or burning with searing heat! O King of Dance, who intimately dances in the sacred hall of consciousness, Thiru Chitrambalam, and in the hearts of those who have realized completely, please graciously adorn yourself with my words.
commentary: God is a fire of pure wisdom, but one that acts opposite to earthly fire. This divine fire is the life within all life; it illuminates and pervades everything without burning, consuming, or causing pain. It is a steady, eternal flame of consciousness that dances within the hearts of those who have attained complete realization in the inner space of Thiru Chitrambalam (the sacred hall of consciousness).

translit: aimpūta paraṅkaḷmutal nāṉkumavaṟ ṟuḷḷē aṭuttiṭunan nāṉkumavai akampuṟamēl naṭukkīḻ kampūta pakkamutal ellāntaṉ mayamāyk kāṇumavaṟ ṟappuṟamum kalantataṉik kaṉalē cempūta ulakaṅkaḷ pūtāṇṭa vakaikaḷ ceḻittiṭanaṟ katirparappit tikaḻkiṉṟa cuṭarē vempūtat taṭaitavirntār ēttamaṇi maṉṟil viḷaṅkumnaṭat taracēeṉ viḷampumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O unique fire, blended even beyond all things! You are the very substance of the four transcendent levels of the five elements, their sixteen subdivisions, their inner, outer, upper, middle, and lower aspects, and everything from the foundational elemental planes onward. O flame that shines, spreading your benevolent rays to make the worlds of pure elements and the varieties of elemental universes flourish! O King of Dance, shining in the gem hall, praised by those who have overcome the hindrances of the harsh elements, please graciously adorn yourself with my words.
commentary: The divine is the very substance of the entire physical universe, from its subtlest elemental layers to its vast worlds. While the poem lists complex cosmic structures, the core message is simple: God is in every part of creation and is every part, and also extends beyond it. This divine presence, praised in the radiant "gem hall" (maṇi maṉṟam), is what allows the cosmos to flourish.

translit: vātuṟumin tiyakaraṇa paraṅkaḷmutal nāṉkum vakuttiṭunan nāṉkumakam puṟamēlkīḻ naṭuppāl ōtuṟummaṟ ṟellāntaṉ mayamākak kalantē ōṅkavaṟṟiṉ appuṟamum oḷirkiṉṟa oḷiyē cūtuṟumin tiyakaraṇa lōkāṇṭam aṉaittum cuṭarparappi viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cuyañcōtic cuṭarē pōtuṟuvār palarniṉṟu pōṟṟanaṭam potuvil puriyumnaṭat taracēeṉ pukalumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O light that shines even beyond all things! You rise high, blended as your own substance with the four transcendent levels of the contending senses and inner faculties, their sixteen subdivisions, their inner, outer, upper, lower, and middle aspects, and all else spoken of. O flame of self-emanating light, spreading your radiance and illuminating all the universes of the deluding senses and inner faculties! O King of Dance, performing in the public hall as many who come to you stand and praise, please graciously adorn yourself with my words.
commentary: Just as God is the substance of the outer world, God is also the reality underlying our inner world of senses and mental faculties, which are often a source of confusion. The divine is a Svayaṃjothi (self-emanating light) that shines on its own, illuminating all the realms of our inner experience and extending beyond them. This light brings clarity to the mind and is praised by all who approach it.

translit: pakutipara mutalnāṉkum avaṟṟuṟunan nāṉkum paravielām taṉmayamām paṭiniṟaintu viḷaṅkit takutipeṟum appakutik kappuṟamum ceṉṟē taṉioḷicceṅ kōlnaṭattit taḻaikkiṉṟa oḷiyē mikutipeṟu pakutiula kampakuti aṇṭam viḷaṅkaaruṭ cuṭarparappi viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cuṭarē tokutipeṟu kaṭavuḷarkaḷ ēttamaṉṟil naṭikkum turiyanaṭat taracēeṉ collumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O flourishing light, wielding the scepter of unique light! You go even beyond Prakṛti itself, shining and spreading to fill everything, so that its four transcendent levels and their sixteen subdivisions all become your own substance. O flame that shines, spreading the flame of grace to illuminate the vast worlds and universes of Prakṛti! O King of the Turiya dance, performing in the hall as the hosts of gods praise you, please graciously adorn yourself with my words.
commentary: The divine reality permeates and finally transcends even Prakṛti, the primal source of all matter. God's light is so absolute that it fills and transforms the very foundation of material existence, making it an expression of the divine. The dance here is called the dance of Turiya (the transcendent fourth state), signifying a reality beyond the ordinary states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.

translit: māmāyaip paramāti nāṉkumavaṟ ṟuḷḷē vayaṅkiyanan nāṉkuntaṉ mayattālē viḷakki āmāṟam māmāyaik kappuṟattum niṟaintē aṟivoṉṟē vaṭivāki viḷaṅkukiṉṟa oḷiyē tāmāyā puvaṉaṅkaḷ māmāyai aṇṭam taḻaittuviḷaṅ kiṭakkatircey taṉittaperuñ cuṭarē tēmālum piramaṉumniṉ ṟēttamaṉṟil naṭikkum teyvanaṭat taracēeṉ ciṟumoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O Light that shines with awareness alone as your form, illuminating by your very nature the four states beginning with Parama (the supreme) within Mahāmāyai and the four divisions within each of them, while also pervading everything beyond that Mahāmāyai! O unique great Flame that radiates light for the unfading worlds and the universe of Mahāmāyai to flourish and shine! O King of the divine dance, who performs in the hall as Vishnu and Brahma stand and praise, please graciously accept my humble words.
commentary: God is a light of pure awareness that illuminates and exists beyond Mahāmāyai, the great cosmic power of illusion that makes the world seem separate from its source. Even the great gods like Vishnu (the preserver) and Brahma (the creator) are shown as devotees who praise this ultimate reality. This places the dancing Lord beyond all cosmic functions and hierarchies, as the supreme truth itself.

translit: cuttapara mutalnāṉkum avaṟṟuṟunan nāṉkum tūyaoḷi vaṭivākat tulaṅkumoḷi aḷittē nittaparam paranaṭuvāy mutalāyan tamatāy nīṭiyaōr perunilaimēl āṭiyapē roḷiyē vittamuṟum cuttapara lōkāṇṭam aṉaittum viḷakkamuṟac cuṭarparappi viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cuṭarē cattiyañā ṉāṉantac cittarpukaḻ potuvil taṉittanaṭat taracēeṉ cāṟṟumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great Light who danced upon a vast, great state, being the middle, the beginning, and the end of the eternal Paraṁpara! You grant the light that shines as a form of pure effulgence for the four states beginning with Śuddha Parama and the four divisions within each. O Flame who shines, spreading your radiance to illuminate all the seed-like universes of the pure supreme world! O King of the unique dance in the common space, praised by the Siddhas of truth, awareness, and bliss, please graciously adorn yourself with what I say.
commentary: The divine light is the timeless source, substance, and destination of even the purest and most subtle realms of existence. The verse speaks of the Śuddha Parama (the pure supreme), a level of reality beyond ordinary cosmic structures, and describes the light as the beginning, middle, and end of Paraṁpara (succession or lineage), meaning it is the eternal ground of all being. This reality is directly perceived by Siddhas, perfected beings who have attained the state of truth, awareness, and bliss.

translit: cāṟṟukiṉṟa kalaiaintil paramāti nāṉkum takkaavaṟ ṟūṭirunta nannāṉkum niṟaintē ūṟṟukiṉṟa akampuṟamēl naṭukkīḻmaṟ ṟaṉaittum uṟṟiṭuntaṉ mayamāki oḷirkiṉṟa oḷiyē tōṟṟukiṉṟa kalaiulakam kalaiaṇṭa muḻutum tulaṅkukiṉṟa cuṭarparappic cūḻkiṉṟa cuṭarē pōṟṟukiṉṟa meyaṭiyar kaḷippanaṭit taruḷum potuvilnaṭat taracēeṉ pukalumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Light that shines, becoming one with everything that springs forth: inside, outside, above, in the middle, below, and all else! You pervade the four states beginning with Parama within the five declared Kalais and the four divisions within each. O Flame who surrounds all, spreading your radiance to illuminate the manifest worlds of Kalai and the entire universe of Kalai! O King of the dance in the common space, who graciously dances for the true devotees to rejoice, please graciously adorn yourself with my praise.
commentary: The divine light is the single substance that makes up everything that exists, in every direction and dimension. Vallalar uses the image of the five Kalais (fundamental aspects of divine creative power) to show how this light pervades every mode of manifestation. This cosmic, all-encompassing reality is also deeply personal: it is the same light that dances to bring joy to its true devotees.

translit: nāṭṭiyaōṅ kāramaintil paramutalōr nāṉkum nannāṉku māṟiṭattum nayantuniṟain taruḷi īṭṭiyacem poruḷnilaiyō ṭilakkiyamum viḷaṅka iṉituniṉṟu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa iṉpamaya oḷiyē kūṭṭiyaōṅ kāra:ula kōṅkāra aṇṭam kuṭiviḷaṅkak katirparappik kulavuperuñ cuṭarē pāṭṭiyalkoṇ ṭaṉparelām pōṟṟamaṉṟil naṭikkum paramanaṭat taracēeṉ pāṭṭumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Light of blissful nature that stands sweetly, illuminating the state of the ultimate reality and its defining attributes! You graciously and lovingly pervade the four states beginning with Parama within the five established aspects of Oṃkāra, and in the six places of the four divisions within each. O great Flame who flourishes, spreading your rays so the assembled worlds of Oṃkāra and the universe of Oṃkāra may thrive! O King of the supreme dance, who performs in the hall as all devotees praise you with songs, please graciously adorn yourself with my song.
commentary: The blissful light of God is the ultimate reality expressed through Oṃkāra, the primal sound of creation. In many traditions, Oṃkāra (the sacred sound 'Om') is the vibration from which the universe emerges. Vallalar sees the divine light as the source that illuminates both the cosmos born from this sound and the ultimate truth it represents. The verse then brings this vast principle back to an intimate scale, as the poet asks this supreme dancer to accept his humble song.

translit: maṉṉukiṉṟa aparacattip paramāti avaṟṟuḷ vakuttanilai yātielām vayaṅkavayiṉ ellām paṉṉukiṉṟa paṟpalavām vicittiracit tiraṅkaḷ paraviviḷaṅ kiṭaviḷaṅkip patintaruḷum oḷiyē tuṉapara cattiula kaparacatti aṇṭam cukampeṟavē katirparappit tulaṅkukiṉṟa cuṭarē uṉṉumaṉpar uḷaṅkaḷikkat tirucciṟṟam palattē ōṅkumnaṭat taracēeṉ uraiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Light that graciously imprints yourself, shining so that the many varied and wondrous creations spoken of may spread and shine within the established Apara Śakti, within the states beginning with Parama therein, and in all places where the defined primary states shine forth! O Flame who shines, spreading your rays so that the dense world of Apara Śakti and the universe of Apara Śakti may attain well-being! O King of the dance who reigns in the sacred golden hall, dancing for the hearts of meditating devotees to rejoice, please graciously adorn yourself with my words.
commentary: The divine light is also the source of manifestation in the material world, called Apara Śakti (lower power). It is this light that enables the beautiful diversity of creation to exist. The dance of God in the sacred hall (Thiru Chitrambalam) is what brings joy and well-being to this entire manifested reality.

translit: viḷaṅkupara cattikaḷiṉ paramāti avaṟṟuḷ virintanilai yātielām viḷaṅkioḷi vaḻaṅkik kaḷaṅkamilāp paraveḷiyil antammutal naṭuttāṉ kāṭṭātē niṟainteṅkum kalantiṭumpē roḷiyē uḷaṅkulavu paracatti ulakamaṇṭa muḻutum oḷiviḷaṅkac cuṭarparappi ōṅkutaṉic cuṭarē vaḷaṅkulavu tiruppotuvil mānaṭañcey aracē makiḻnteṉatu coleṉumōr mālaiaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great Light, the supreme origin of the manifest Supreme Powers! You illuminate and bestow light upon all the states and origins that expanded from within them. You fill and pervade everywhere in the flawless supreme space, without showing an end, beginning, or middle. O singular Flame that rises, spreading your radiance to illuminate the entire world-sphere of the mind's indwelling Supreme Power! O King who performs the great dance in the prosperous, sacred Common Space! Please, joyfully accept and wear this garland of my words.
commentary: Having described God's presence in the lower powers, Vallalar now turns to the source. God is the origin of even the highest Supreme Powers (Para Śaktis). This ultimate reality is a boundless light filling the supreme space (paraveḷi), a state of pure consciousness with no beginning or end. It is this singular, transcendent flame that illuminates even the highest reaches of the soul.

translit: terintamakā cuttapara mutalumavaṟ ṟuḷḷē ciṟantanilai yātikaḷum teḷintuviḷaṅ kuṟavē parintaoru civaveḷiyil nīkkamaṟa niṟaintē paramacuka mayamākip paraviyapē roḷiyē virintamakā cuttapara lōkāṇṭa muḻutum meyaṟivā ṉantanilai viḷakkukiṉṟa cuṭarē purintatavap payaṉākum potuvilnaṭat taracē puṉmoḻieṉ ṟikaḻātē puṉaintumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: O great Light, the discerned, great, pure, supreme Origin! You fill the compassionate space of Sivam without any separation, becoming the very form of supreme bliss, so that the excellent states and origins within it are clearly revealed. O Flame that illuminates the state of true knowledge and bliss throughout all the vast, great, pure, supreme world-spheres! O King who dances in the Common Space, you who are the fruit of performed austerities! Do not scorn these as humble words; please adorn yourself with them and be pleased.
commentary: The divine is described as the very essence of supreme bliss, a great light that fills the compassionate space of God (Sivaveḷi). This light is more than a presence; it is an active illumination that reveals the nature of true knowledge and bliss everywhere. Reaching this state is the ultimate goal, the true fruit of all sincere spiritual practice (thavam).

translit: vāyntapara nātamaintil paramutalum avaṟṟuḷ maṉṉunilai yātikaḷum vayaṅkiyiṭa niṟaintē āyntapara civaveḷiyil veḷiuruvāy ellām ākiyataṉ iyalviḷakki alarntiṭumpē roḷiyē tōyntapara nāta:ula kaṇṭamelām viḷaṅkac cuṭarparappi viḷaṅkukiṉṟa tūyataṉic cuṭarē vēyntamaṇi maṉṟiṭattē naṭampuriyum aracē viḷampuṟumeṉ coṉmālai viḷaṅkaaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great Light, the supreme Origin within the five sublime supreme sounds! You fill all, so that the enduring states and origins within them shine forth. You bloom in the scrutinized supreme space of Sivam, taking the form of space itself, becoming all things, and revealing your own nature. O pure, singular Flame that shines, spreading your radiance to illuminate all the world-spheres of the pervasive supreme sound! O King who performs the dance in the gem-adorned hall! Please wear this garland of words I proclaim, so it may shine brightly.
commentary: This verse reaches for the most fundamental level of being: the supreme sound or vibration (Para Nātham) from which all else emerges. God is the source of this sound and the very space in which it vibrates. In a single unity, God becomes all of creation while simultaneously remaining the pure, self-revealing light that illuminates it.

translit: kallārkkum kaṟṟavarkkum kaḷipparuḷum kaḷippē kāṇārkkum kaṇṭavarkkum kaṇṇaḷikkum kaṇṇē vallārkkum māṭṭārkkum varamaḷikkum varamē matiyārkkum matippavarkkum matikoṭukkum matiyē nallārkkum pollārkkum naṭuniṉṟa naṭuvē nararkaḷukkum curarkaḷukkum nalaṅkoṭukkum nalamē ellārkkum potuvilnaṭam iṭukiṉṟa civamē eṉaracē yāṉpukalum icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Joy that grants joy to the unlearned and the learned alike! O Eye that gives sight to those who do not see and to those who do! O Boon that grants boons to the capable and the incapable! O Wisdom that gives wisdom to those who disregard you and to those who revere you! O Justice that stands impartial for the good and the wicked! O Goodness that gives well-being to mortals and to celestials! O Sivam who dances in the Common Space for all! My King, please accept and wear this melody I offer.
commentary: God's grace is available to everyone without exception: the educated and uneducated, the powerful and weak, even the good and the wicked. He is the ultimate source of joy, sight, and wisdom, dancing in a common space accessible to all, from ordinary humans to celestial beings (surar).

translit: kāṭciyuṟak kaṇkaḷukkuk kaḷikkum vaṇṇam uḷatāyk kaiyummeyyum paricikkac cukaparicat tatuvāyc cūḻcciyuṟa nācikkuc cukantañcey kuvatāyt tūyacevik kiṉiyatoru cukanātat tatuvāy māṭciyuṟa vāykkiṉiya peruñcuvaiī kuvatāy maṟaimuṭimēl paḻutteṉakku vāyttaperum paḻamē āṭciyuṟa aruḷoḷiyāl tirucciṟṟam palattē āṭalpuri aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: You exist as a delightful vision for the eyes to behold; you are a blissful touch for the hand and body to feel; you artfully provide a pleasant fragrance for the nose; you are a sweet, pleasant sound for the pure ears; you magnificently give a great, sweet taste to the mouth. O great Fruit that ripened atop the crown of the Vedas and has become available to me! O King who performs the dance in the sacred little hall, ruling through the light of grace! Please accept and wear my garland.
commentary: The divine is a tangible experience available to all five senses: a joyful sight, a blissful touch, a sweet smell, a pleasant sound, and a delicious taste. Vallalar calls God a great fruit that has ripened on the highest branches of the Vedas (sacred scriptures) and has now become available to him in the sacred hall of his heart (Thiru Chitrambalam).

translit: tiraiilatāy aḻivilatāyt tōlilatāyc ciṟitum ciṉaippilatāyp paṉippilatāyc ceṟintiṭukō tilatāy viraiilatāyp puraiilatāy nārilatāy meyyē meyyāki aruḷvaṇṇam viḷaṅkiiṉpa mayamāyp paraiveḷikkap pālviḷaṅku taṉiveḷiyil paḻuttē paṭaittaeṉa tuḷattiṉikkak kiṭaittataṉip paḻamē uraivaḷarmā maṟaikaḷelām pōṟṟamaṇip potuvil ōṅkumnaṭat taracēeṉ uraiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O unique fruit, obtained to sweeten my mind! You ripened in the singular expanse that shines beyond the space of Parai. You are without film, without decay, without skin, without the slightest blemish, without dewiness, without a dense seed, without fragrance, without flaw, and without fiber. You have become truth itself, shining with the quality of grace, suffused with bliss. O King of Dance, exalted in the gem-adorned common hall, praised by all the great, ever-growing Vedas, please graciously wear my words as well.
commentary: This divine fruit, which ripened in the space beyond even Parai (the supreme creative energy), is perfectly pure. It has none of the flaws of a physical fruit: no skin, no seed, no decay, no blemish. It is truth itself, suffused with grace and bliss, a perfect spiritual nourishment meant to sweeten the soul.

translit: kārppilatāyt tuvarppilatāy uvarppilatāyc ciṟitum kacappilatāyp puḷippilatāyk kāyppilatāyp piṟavil cērppilatāy eññāṉṟum tiripilatāy uyirkkē tiṉaittaṉaiyum nōytarumat tīmaioṉṟum ilatāyp pārppaṉaiyēṉ uḷḷakattē viḷaṅkiaṟi viṉpam paṭaittiṭameyt tavappayaṉāl kiṭaittataṉip paḻamē ōrppuṭaiyār pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟiṭattē veḷiyāy ōṅkiyapē raracēeṉ uraiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O unique fruit, obtained through the true reward of my austerities! You are without pungency, astringency, or saltiness; without the slightest bitterness, sourness, or unripeness. You have no other admixtures, are ever unchanging, and are free from even a millet-seed's worth of the evil that brings disease to life. You shine within the inner self of me, who am like a helpless fledgling, creating the bliss of wisdom. O great King, who soars openly in the gem-adorned hall, praised by the discerning, please graciously wear my words as well.
commentary: The spiritual fruit of realization has a perfect sweet nature, free from all the sharp or unpleasant tastes of the world like bitterness or sourness. (In Sanmarkkam, it is eventually required to move to a diet based on sweet foods, avoiding salty, spicy and sour foods. It seems that such tastes except the sweet taste are detrimental to a high spiritual state, hence Vallalar's advice to avoid salt.) It is unchanging and brings no harm to the soul. Vallalar, calling himself as helpless as a fledgling bird, says this fruit, gained through true tapas, shines within him and creates the bliss of knowing.

translit: teṟṟiyilē nāṉpacittup paṭuttiḷaitta taruṇam tiruamutōr tirukkarattē tikaḻvaḷḷat teṭuttē oṟṟiyiṟpōyp pacittaṉaiyō eṉṟeṉaiyaṅ keḻuppi uvantukoṭut taruḷiyaeṉ uyirkkiṉitān tāyē paṟṟiyaeṉ paṟṟaṉaittum taṉaṭippaṟ ṟākap parintaruḷi eṉaiīṉṟa paṇpuṭaien tāyē peṟṟiyuḷār cuṟṟiniṉṟu pōṟṟamaṇip potuvil perunaṭañcey aracēeṉ pitaṟṟumuvan taruḷē.
translation: At the moment I lay exhausted with hunger on a raised platform, you took divine ambrosia in a shining vessel in your sacred hand. You woke me, asking, "Did you go hungry in Otriyur?", and joyfully gave it to me. O mother so sweet to my soul! O my kind mother who gave birth to me, who compassionately transformed all my attachments into an attachment for your feet! O King who performs the great dance in the gem-adorned common hall, praised by the worthy who stand surrounding you, please joyfully accept even my prattling.
commentary: The poem shifts from abstract metaphor to a moving personal story. Vallalar recalls a time he was exhausted with hunger, and God appeared in a tangible form to feed him, speaking with the loving concern of a parent. For him, the Divine is an intimate presence, a mother who tends to his needs and transforms his worldly attachments into love for the divine itself.

translit: tāymutalō roṭuciṟiya paruvamatiltillait talattiṭaiyē tiraitūkkat taricitta pōtu vēyvakaimēl kāṭṭātē eṉṟaṉakkē ellām veḷiyākak kāṭṭiyaeṉ meyuṟavām poruḷē kāyvakaiil lātuḷattē kaṉintanaṟuṅ kaṉiyē kaṉaviṭattum naṉaviṭattum eṉaippiriyāk kaḷippē tūyvakaiyōr pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟilnaṭam puriyum cōtinaṭat taracēeṉ collumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: When, as a small child with my mother and others, I had the vision at the sacred site of Thillai as the curtain was lifted, you did not show me a limited form, but revealed everything openly to me alone. O my true kinsman, the ultimate substance! O fragrant, ripe fruit that has ripened in my heart without any bitterness! O bliss that never leaves me, in dreams or in waking! O King of the Jothi Dance, performing in the gem-adorned hall and praised by the pure, please graciously wear my sayings as well.
commentary: This verse describes a foundational mystical experience from Vallalar's childhood. At the temple in Thillai (modern Chidambaram), a curtain is lifted during a key ritual to reveal an empty space symbolizing the formless divine. While others saw emptiness, the young Vallalar alone was given a vision of the complete reality, establishing a direct, personal connection that has never left him.

translit: ōṅkiyaōr tuṇaiiṉṟip pātiira vatilē uyarntaōṭṭut tiṇṇaiyilē paṭuttakaṭaic ciṟiyēṉ tūṅkimikap puraṇṭuviḻat taraiyilviḻā teṉaiyē tūkkieṭut taṇaittukkīḻk kiṭattiyameyt tuṇaiyē tāṅkiyaeṉ uyirkkiṉpam tantaperun takaiyē caṟkuruvē nāṉceyperun tavappayaṉām poruḷē ēṅkiyaeṉ ēkkamelām tavirttaruḷip potuvil ilaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: In the middle of the night, without any other support, I, the lowly, small one, was lying on a high, tiled platform. As I slept soundly and turned, about to fall, you were my true companion who caught me before I hit the ground, lifted, embraced, and laid me down safely. O great and magnanimous one who supported me and gave bliss to my soul! O Satguru! O substance that is the great reward of the austerities I performed! O King of Dance, shining in the common hall, you graciously ended all my yearnings; please graciously wear my songs as well.
commentary: This is another striking account of God's direct, physical intervention in his life. He describes being miraculously saved from a fall in his sleep, caught and gently laid down by a divine presence. This experience shows his view of God as a true companion and Satguru (true spiritual teacher), a tangible protector who cares for his physical well-being.

translit: taṉicciṟiyēṉ ciṟitiṅkē varuntiyapō tataṉait taṉvaruttam eṉakkoṇṭu tariyātak kaṇattē paṉippuṟumav varuttamelām tavirttaruḷi makaṉē payamuṉakkeṉ eṉṟeṉṉaip parintaṇaitta kuruvē iṉippuṟunaṉ moḻipukaṉṟeṉ muṭimicaiyē malarkkāl iṇaiamartti eṉaiyāṇṭa eṉṉuyirnaṟ ṟuṇaiyē kaṉittanaṟuṅ kaṉiyēeṉ kaṇṇēciṟ capaiyil kalantanaṭat taracēeṉ karuttumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: When I, this solitary little one, suffered even slightly here, you took that suffering as your own. Unable to bear it, in that very instant you removed all that shivering sorrow, lovingly embraced me, and said, "My son, what fear is there for you?" O Guru! You spoke sweet, good words, placed your paired flower-feet upon my head, and took me as your own, O my life's good companion! O ripened, fragrant fruit, my very eye! O King of Dance who merges with the Chit Sabhai! Please adorn yourself with my thoughts as well.
commentary: Divine compassion is presented as so immediate that it cannot tolerate even the slightest suffering in a devotee. Vallalar describes God feeling his sorrow as God's own and instantly removing it, offering the tender reassurance of a parent speaking to a child. This grace is shown through the classic gesture of a Guru (spiritual teacher) placing his feet on the disciple's head, an act signifying total acceptance and initiation into the divine reality of the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness).

translit: orumaṭantai valintaṇaintu kalantakaṉṟa piṉṉar uḷamvarunti eṉceytōm eṉṟayarnta pōtu perumaṭañcēr piḷḷāyeṉ keṭṭatoṉṟum ilainam peruñceyaleṉ ṟeṉaittēṟṟip piṭittaperun takaiyē tirumaṭantai māriruvar eṉetirē naṭikkac ceytaruḷic ciṟumaielām tīrttataṉic civamē karumaṭamtīrn tavarellām pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟil kāṭṭumnaṭat taracēeṉ pāṭṭumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: After a woman forcibly embraced me, united with me, and then left, I grew weary with grief, thinking, "What have I done?" At that moment, you consoled me, saying, "O child of great folly, nothing is lost. This is our great deed," and you took hold of me, O great and noble one! You made two divine women dance before my very eyes, removing all my lowliness, O singular Sivam! O King of Dance who reveals yourself in the bejeweled hall, praised by all who are free from the darkness of ignorance, please adorn yourself with my song as well.
commentary: A woman forcibly embraced him and left, and he was stricken, asking, “What have I done?” God steadied him at once: “O simple child, nothing is spoiled; this is Our great work.” What seemed his fall lay within God's own doing. God then made two divine women dance before him and removed all his smallness.

translit: iruḷiravil orumūlait tiṇṇaiyilnāṉ pacittē iḷaippuṭaṉē paṭuttirukka eṉaittēṭi vantē poruḷuṇavu koṭuttuṇṇac ceyvittē paciyaip pōkkiaruḷ purintaeṉṟaṉ puṇṇiyanaṟ ṟuṇaiyē maruḷiravu nīkkiellā vāḻvumeṉak karuḷi maṇimēṭai naṭuirukka vaittaoru maṇiyē aruḷuṇavum aḷitteṉṉai āṭkoṇṭa civamē ampalatteṉ aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: In the dark of night, as I lay on a corner verandah, hungry and exhausted, you came searching for me. You gave me substantial food, made me eat, appeased my hunger, and bestowed grace, O my virtuous, good companion! You removed the night of delusion, granted me every kind of prosperous life, and seated me in the center of a bejeweled stage, O singular gem! O Sivam who also gave me the food of grace and made me your own! O my King of the Ambalam, please adorn yourself with my garland.
commentary: Grace manifests here in the most fundamental way: as food for the hungry. Vallalar recounts God searching for him in the night to alleviate his physical hunger and then providing the "food of grace" to nourish his soul. This shows a God who cares for the complete well-being of the person, body and spirit alike.

translit: nāṉpacitta pōtellām tāṉpacitta tāki naluṇavu koṭutteṉṉaic celvamuṟa vaḷarttē ūṉpacitta iḷaippeṉṟum tōṟṟāta vakaiyē oḷḷiyateḷ ḷamuteṉakkiṅ kuvantaḷitta oḷiyē vāṉpatikkum neṭumāṟkum nāṉmukaṟkum aritām vāḻveṉakkē ākiyuṟa varamaḷitta patiyē tēṉparitta malarmaṇamē tiruppotuvil ñāṉat tirunaṭañcey aracēeṉ ciṟumoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: Whenever I was hungry, you became hungry as if it were your own hunger. You gave me good food and raised me to be prosperous. You are the Light who lovingly gave me the bright, clear nectar here, so that the weariness of bodily hunger would never appear. O Master, you granted me the boon of a life difficult even for the lord of heaven, the great Vishnu, and four-faced Brahma, making it my own! O fragrance of a honey-laden flower! O King who performs the sacred dance of wisdom in the sacred Pothu, please accept my simple words.
commentary: God's empathy is so deep that He feels Vallalar's hunger as His own. The grace given is a meal and a divine "nectar" that removes the very condition of hunger itself. By granting him a life state sought even by the highest celestial beings like Vishnu and Brahma, Vallalar shows that the path of direct, compassionate grace leads to a goal beyond even what is imagined in traditional worship.

translit: naṭaikkuriya ulakiṭaiōr nallanaṇpaṉ āki nāṉkuṟitta poruḷkaḷelām nāḻikaioṉ ṟatilē kiṭaikkaeṉak kaḷittakattum puṟattumakap puṟattum kiḷarntoḷikoṇ ṭōṅkiyameyk kiḷaieṉumpē roḷiyē paṭaippumutal aintoḻilum koḷkaeṉak kuṟittē payantīrtteṉ uḷḷakattē amarntataṉip patiyē kaṭaippaṭumeṉ karattiloru kaṅkaṇamum taritta kakaṉanaṭat taracēeṉ karuttumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: In this world of practical affairs, you became a good friend and, within a single nāḻikai (a unit of time, about 24 minutes), you granted me all the things I desired. O great Light called the "True Kin", who rose up, took hold of light, and soared within, without, and in the inner-outer space! You declared, "Take up the five cosmic functions, beginning with creation," dispelled my fear, and settled within my heart, O singular Master! You placed a kangaṇam on my lowly hand, O King of the celestial dance! Please adorn yourself with my thoughts as well.
commentary: In this final verse of the poem, God's role evolves from protector and teacher to an empowering master. He first acts as a "good friend" helping with worldly needs, then bestows the ultimate spiritual authority: the "five cosmic functions" of creation, preservation, and dissolution that are normally God's alone. The kangaṇam, a ceremonial wrist-band, symbolizes this commissioning, showing that the perfected soul is deputized to carry out God's own work.

translit: nīniṉaitta naṉmaielām yāmaṟintōm niṉaiyē nērkāṇa vantaṉameṉ ṟeṉmuṭimēlmalarkkāl tāṉnilaikka vaittaruḷip paṭuttiṭanāṉ cerukkit tāḷkaḷeṭut tappuṟattē vaittiṭattāṉ nakaittē ēṉniṉaittāy ivvaḷavu cutantarameṉ makaṉē eṉakkilaiyō eṉṟaruḷi eṉaiyāṇṭa kuruvē tēṉnilaitta tīmpākē carkkaraiyē kaṉiyē teyvanaṭat taracēeṉ ciṟumoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: "We knew all the good you intended. We have come to see you in person," you said, placing your flower-like foot firmly upon my head and making me lie down. But I, in my arrogance, took your feet and set them aside. You laughed and graciously asked, "My son, why did you think you had such freedom? Do I not possess it?" O Guru who made me yours! O sweet syrup where honey settles, O raw sugar, O ripe fruit! O King of the divine dance, please graciously accept my humble words.
commentary: This verse reveals a startlingly familiar and loving relationship with the divine. When God places his feet on Vallalar's head in a gesture of ultimate grace, Vallalar's lingering ego makes him push them away. Instead of anger, God responds with a gentle, fatherly laugh, reminding him of who is really in charge. This is a relationship of playful intimacy, where even human imperfection is met with divine love.

translit: mūrttikaḷum neṭuṅkālam muyaṉṟālum aṟiya muṭiyāta muṭivellām muṉṉiyaōr tiṉattē ārttiyuṭaṉ aṟiyaeṉak kaḷittaruḷi aṭiyēṉ akattiṉaittaṉ iṭamākki amarntaaruṭ kuruvē pārttiparum viṇṇavarum paṇintumakiḻn tēttap paranāta nāṭṭaracu pālitta patiyē ērttikaḻum tiruppotuvil iṉpanaṭat taracē eṉṉuṭaiya coṉmālai ilaṅkaaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O grace-Guru who, in a single day you intended, graciously enabled me to know with great eagerness all the final truths that even the divine forms cannot know, though they strive for ages! You made this devotee's heart your own place and took your seat there. O Master who grants dominion over the kingdom of transcendent sound, whom earthly kings and celestials bow to, praise, and rejoice in! O King of the blissful dance in the beautiful sacred common space! Please wear my garland of words and let it shine.
commentary: The path to ultimate truth is through grace, more than personal effort. Vallalar states that he was given in a single day the wisdom that even gods (mūrtis) fail to attain through ages of striving. God makes the devotee's heart his own home and grants him authority over the highest spiritual states, like the "kingdom of transcendent sound" (paranātha). True knowledge is received as a gift when the heart is made ready.

translit: iccaioṉṟum illātē iruntaeṉak kiṅkē iyaluṟucaṉ mārkkanilaik kiccaiyaiuṇ ṭākkit taccuṟavē piṟamuyaṟci ceyuntōṟum avaṟṟait taṭaiyākki ulakaṟiyat taṭaitīrtta kuruvē eccamaya muṭipukaḷum tirucciṟṟam palattē iruntaeṉa eṉakkaruḷi icaivitta iṟaiyē muccakamum pukaḻamaṇi maṉṟiṭattē naṭikkum mutalaracē eṉṉuṭaiya moḻiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: To me, who was here without a single desire, you created the desire for the state of the true path, Sanmarkkam. Whenever I contrived to make other efforts, you turned them into obstacles, and then, O Guru, you removed those obstacles for all the world to see. O Lord who graciously revealed to me that the conclusions of all faiths reside in the sacred Chit Sabhai! O foremost King, dancing in the jeweled hall praised by the three worlds! Please wear my words as well.
commentary: God actively guides the seeker to the right path. Vallalar explains that he had no spiritual desires until God himself planted the desire for the true path, or Sanmarkkam. When he strayed toward other methods, God caused them to fail, clearing the way by blocking all other exits. The destination of all paths, he learns, is the inner "hall of consciousness" (tirucciṟṟampalam), where God's presence is directly experienced.

translit: kaiyāta tīṅkaṉiyē kayakkāta amutē karaiyāta kaṟkaṇṭē puraiyāta karumpē poyyāta peruvāḻvē pukaiyāta kaṉalē pōkāta puṉalēuḷ vēkāta kālē koyyāta naṟumalarē kōvāta maṇiyē kuḷiyāta perumuttē oḷiyāta veḷiyē ceyyāta pērutavi ceytaperun takaiyē teyvanaṭat taracēeṉ ciṟumoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O sweet fruit that is never bitter! O ambrosia that never causes disgust! O rock candy that never dissolves! O sugarcane without flaws! O great life that is never false! O fire that never smokes! O water that never goes away! O wind that is never hot within! O fragrant flower that is never plucked! O gem that is never strung! O great pearl that is never dived for! O space that is never hidden! O great, noble one who rendered me immense help that had never been rendered before! O King of the divine dance, please graciously accept my humble words.
commentary: God's nature is a perfection that transcends all earthly limitations. Vallalar uses a series of paradoxes to describe this: he is a fruit that is never bitter, a fire that gives light without smoke, a flower that is fragrant without ever being plucked. Each image points to a reality that is complete, pure, and eternal. This is a felt reality, a "great, noble one" who has helped him in a way no one ever had before.

translit: eṇṇāta mantiramē eḻutāta maṟaiyē ēṟāta mēṉilainiṉ ṟiṟaṅkāta niṟaivē paṇṇāta pūcaiyilē paṭiyāta paṭippē pārāta pārvaiyilē patiyāta patippē naṇṇāta maṉattakattē aṇṇāta nalamē nāṭāta nāṭṭakattē naṭavāta naṭappē aṇṇāeṉ appāeṉ aiyāeṉ aracē aṭiiṇaikkeṉ coṉmālai aṇintumakiḻn taruḷē.
translation: O mantra that is not recited! O scripture that is not written! O fullness that, standing in a high state one cannot ascend, never descends! O learning gained in worship that is not performed! O impression made by a sight that is not seen! O goodness approached within a mind that cannot approach! O dance that takes place in a land that is not sought! O Aṇṇā (elder brother, Lord), my Father, my Master, my King! Please wear the garland of my words on your sacred twin feet and graciously rejoice.
commentary: The highest spiritual reality transcends all the usual religious methods we use to find it. It is a truth not contained in written scriptures or chanted mantras, and a state of grace reached without formal worship or pilgrimage. This points to a direct, inner experience of the divine that is beyond the grasp of the rational mind and its familiar tools.

translit: cākāta kalviyilē talaiyāṉa nilaiyē caliyāta kāṟṟiṭainiṉ ṟoliyāta kaṉalē ēkāta puṉaliṭattē iṭiyāta puviyē ēcāta mantirattē pēcāta poruḷē kūkāeṉ ṟeṉaikkūṭi eṭukkātē eṉṟum kulaiyāta vaṭiveṉakkē koṭuttataṉi amutē mākātal uṭaiyārkaḷ vaḻuttamaṇip potuvil mānaṭañcey aracēeṉ mālaiyumēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: You are the supreme state within the deathless education, the soundless fire standing in the unwearying wind, the indestructible earth in the undiminishing water, the unspoken reality in the blameless mantra. O unique nectar who gave me a form that never perishes, so that no one will ever gather round me crying "kū, kā" and carry me away! O King performing the great dance in the jeweled hall, praised by those with immense love, please accept my garland as well.
commentary: The divine is the silent, stable essence at the heart of all experience: the head of the deathless learning, the soundless fire within the wind, the unspoken truth within a mantra. This reality has given Vallalar a form that never perishes, so that no mourners will ever gather round him wailing and carry him off. Deathlessness of the body is stated here as a gift already received.

translit: cuttanilai aṉupavaṅkaḷ tōṉṟuveḷi yākit tōṟṟumveḷi yākiavai tōṟṟuvikkum veḷiyāy nittanilai kaḷiṉnaṭuvē niṟaintaveḷi yāki nīyāki nāṉāki niṉṟataṉipporuḷē cattiyamē cattuvamē tattuvamē navamē camaracacaṉ mārkkanilait talainiṉṟa civamē puttamutē cittielām vallatirup potuvil puṉitanaṭat taracēeṉ pukalumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: You became the space where experiences of the pure state appear, the space that is manifest, and the space that causes them to manifest. You became the space that fills the midst of eternal states, O unique reality that stands as both You and me. O Truth, O Goodness, O Essence, O Newness! O Sivam, standing supreme in the state of Samarasa Sanmarkkam! O fresh nectar in the sacred hall that can grant all siddhis, O King of the sacred dance, please adorn yourself with my speech as well.
commentary: The divine is the very space of consciousness where all experience happens. This ultimate reality is a single existence that appears as both "You" (God) and "me" (the soul). This state of union is the goal of Samarasa Sanmarkkam (the path of true harmony), where one realizes that Sivam (the ultimate auspicious reality) is the source of all siddhis (spiritual powers) and the ground of one's own being.

translit: nāṉaḷakkun tōṟumataṟ kuṟṟatupōl kāṭṭi nāṭṭiyapiṉ oruciṟitum aḷaviluṟā tākit tāṉaḷakkum aḷavatilē muṭiveṉat tōṟṟit taṉaḷavuṅ kaṭantappāl maṉṉukiṉṟa poruḷē vāṉaḷakka muṭiyātē vāṉaṉantaṅ kōṭi vaittaperu vāṉaḷakka vacamōeṉ ṟuraittut tēṉaḷakkum maṟaikaḷelām pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟil tikaḻunaṭat taracēeṉ ciṟumoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: Each time I try to measure you, you seem to fit the measure, but then you reveal you cannot be contained by any measure at all. You appear as the final limit within the very measure that measures itself, O reality that endures, surpassing even your own measure! The honey-like Vedas all praise you in the jeweled hall, saying, "The sky cannot be measured; is it possible then to measure the great space that holds countless billions of skies?" O King of the radiant dance, please accept my humble words.
commentary: God's nature is a paradox: while seeming to fit within our limited attempts to define it, God is finally beyond all measure. Even the most ancient scriptures, the Vedas, declare that if one cannot measure the physical sky, it is impossible to measure the God who created countless skies. This verse is a statement on divine infinity, where every attempt to grasp it only reveals how much further there is to go.

translit: ticaiyaṟiya māṭṭātē tikaittaciṟi yēṉait teḷivittu maṇimāṭat tiruttavicil ēṟṟi nacaiaṟiyā naṟṟavarum maṟṟavaruñ cūḻntu nayappaaruṭ civanilaiyai nāṭṭavaitta patiyē vacaiyaṟiyāp peruvāḻvē mayalaṟiyā aṟivē vāṉnaṭuve iṉpavaṭi vāyirunta poruḷē pacaiaṟiyā maṉattavarkkum pacaiaṟivit taruḷap parintanaṭat taracēeṉ pāṭṭumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: When I, this small one, was bewildered and lost, you gave me clarity and raised me to the sacred throne in the jeweled mansion. O Master, you established me in the state of graceful Sivam, to be surrounded and admired by good, desire-free ascetics and others. O great life that knows no blame, O awareness that knows no delusion! O reality existing as a form of bliss in the center of the sky! O King who dances with compassion to teach affection even to those whose hearts know no attachment, please adorn yourself with my song as well.
commentary: Vallalar describes his own experience of being lost and confused, then being rescued and elevated by God to a state of enlightened consciousness (Sivam). He praises God as a reality free from delusion, a pure bliss at the center of existence. The most powerful image is the last one: God dances with compassion to teach love even to those with hard, detached hearts, showing that divine grace can soften anyone.

translit: eṉuyirum eṉuṭalum eṉporuḷum yāṉē icaintukoṭut tiṭavāṅki iṭṭataṉpiṉ makiḻntē taṉuyirum taṉuṭalum taṉporuḷum eṉakkē tantukalan teṉaippuṇarnta taṉittaperuñ cuṭarē maṉuyiruk kuyirāki iṉpamumāy niṟainta maṇiyēeṉ kaṇṇēeṉ vāḻmutalē maruntē miṉṉiyapoṉ maṇimaṉṟil viḷaṅkunaṭat taracē meyyumaṇin taruḷvōyeṉ poyyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: After I willingly offered my life, my body, and my possessions, you accepted them. Then, delighting, you, O unique great flame, gave your life, your body, and your possessions to me, mingled with and united with me. O Gem, who are the life within all enduring lives and overflowing bliss! O my eye, source of my life, my medicine! O King of dance, brilliant in the glittering, golden, jeweled hall! You who deign to wear truth, please adorn yourself with my falsehood as well.
commentary: The path to union is a complete exchange: Vallalar gave his life, body, and all he had to God, and God in turn gave His own life, body, and being back to him, erasing all separation. This mutual self-giving culminates in a plea of deep intimacy. He asks God, who is truth itself, to accept his truths and his "falsehoods", his imperfections and failings, as an offering.

translit: maṉṉukiṉṟa poṉvaṭivum mantiramām vaṭivum vāṉvaṭivum koṭutteṉakku maṇimuṭiyuñ cūṭṭip paṉṉukiṉṟa toḻilaintuñceytiṭavē paṇittup paṇpuṟaeṉ akampuṟamum viḷaṅkukiṉṟa patiyē uṉṉukiṉṟa tōṟumeṉak kuḷḷamelām iṉittē ūṟukiṉṟa teḷḷamutē orutaṉippē roḷiyē miṉṉukiṉṟa maṇimaṉṟil viḷaṅkunaṭat taracē meyyumaṇin taruḷvōyeṉ poyyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: You gave me an eternal golden form, a form of mantra, and a form of the vast sky. You crowned me with a jeweled crown and commanded me to perform the five great functions. O Lord who beautifully illuminates my inner and outer self! O clear ambrosia that wells up, sweetening my whole heart whenever I think of you! O singular great light! O King of Dance, resplendent in the glittering hall of gems! You who graciously accept my truths, please graciously accept my falsehoods as well.
commentary: God has granted him divine gifts: an eternal golden body, a body made of sacred utterance (mantra), and a body of pure space. He has even been empowered to perform the five cosmic functions (creation, preservation, etc.) that are typically God's alone. Despite this incredible elevation, the experience remains personal and sweet. He ends by repeating his humble plea for God to accept his imperfections along with his truths, showing a grace that is unconditional.

translit: naṉmaielām tīmaieṉak kuraittōṭit tiriyum nāykkulattil kaṭaiyāṉa nāyaṭiyēṉ iyaṟṟum puṉmaielām perumaieṉap poṟuttaruḷip pulaiyēṉ poyuraimey uraiyākap purintumakiḻn taruḷit taṉmaielām uṭaiyaperun tavicēṟṟi muṭiyum tarittaruḷi aintoḻilcey caturaḷitta patiyē iṉmaielām tavirntaṭiyār iṉpamuṟap potuvil ilaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: I am your dog-slave, the lowest of the dog-clan, one who wanders around declaring good things to be evil. You graciously forgive all the vile deeds I perform, treating them as great ones. You joyfully accept the false words of this base one as true. O Lord who seated me on the great throne possessing all divine qualities, placed a crown on my head, and granted me the skill to perform the five functions! O King of Dance, resplendent in the common space so that devotees, all their wants removed, can attain bliss! Please graciously accept my song as well.
commentary: Vallalar uses extreme humility, calling himself worse than a dog, to highlight the sheer scale of God's grace. In a divine reversal, God does forgive his flaws and sees them as virtues, his lies as truth. This grace transforms the most wretched being into a crowned king, empowered to perform God's work in the "common space" (podu), a universal place of worship accessible to all.

translit: viḻukkulattār aruvarukkum puḻukkulattil kaṭaiyēṉ meyyuraiyēṉ poyyuraiyai viyantumakiḻn taruḷi muḻukkulattōr muṭicūṭṭi aintoḻilcey eṉavē moḻintaruḷi eṉaiyāṇṭa mutaṟṟaṉippē roḷiyē eḻukkulattil purintamaṉak kaḻukkulattār tamakkē eṭṭāta nilaiyēnāṉ eṭṭiyapoṉ malaiyē maḻukkulattār pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟilnaṭam puriyum mānaṭatteṉ aracēeṉ mālaiaṇin taruḷē.
translation: I am the lowest of the worm-caste, despised by those of noble birth. I do not speak the truth, yet you marveled at my false words and graciously took delight. O singular, primal great light who ruled me, crowning me as chief of all castes and commanding, “Perform the five functions!” O golden mountain I have reached, a state unattainable to those of the seven castes whose minds are filled with impurity! O my King of the great dance, performing in the hall of gems praised by the clan who wield battle-axes! Please graciously accept my garland as well.
commentary: The contrast between human judgment and divine grace is stark: society despises him as a "worm," but God elevates him to be "chief of all castes." His spiritual state is beyond the reach of conventional religious or social structures. By delighting in his "false words," God reveals that divine grace operates on a logic completely different from the world's, dissolving all hierarchies.

translit: kalaikkoṭikaṇ ṭaṟiyāta pulaikkuṭiyil kaṭaiyēṉ kaitavaṉēṉ poytavamum karuttiluvan taruḷi malaikkuyarmāt tavicēṟṟi maṇimuṭiyuñ cūṭṭi makaṉēnī vāḻkaeṉa vāḻttiyaeṉ kuruvē pulaikkoṭiyār oruciṟitum pulappaṭakkaṇ ṭaṟiyāp poṉṉēnāṉ uṇṇukiṉṟa puttamutat tiraḷē vilaikkaṟiyā māmaṇiyē veṟuppaṟiyā maruntē viḷaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ viḷampumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: I am the lowest of a base clan that has never known the banner of learning. I am a deceiver, yet you graciously delighted in my false penance. O my Guru, you seated me on a great throne higher than a mountain, crowned me with a jeweled crown, and blessed me, saying, “My son, may you live long!” O gold that cruel eaters of flesh have never glimpsed in the slightest! O fresh ambrosial essence that I consume! O priceless great gem! O medicine that knows no aversion! O resplendent King of Dance! Please graciously accept my spoken words as well.
commentary: God acts as the ultimate Guru (spiritual teacher), seeing value where the world sees none. He ignores Vallalar's lack of learning, his "false penance," and his lowly state, instead treating him with the tenderness of a father blessing a son. The divine is a priceless medicine that accepts all who come to it, without aversion.

translit: matameṉṟum camayameṉṟum cāttiraṅkaḷ eṉṟum maṉṉukiṉṟa tēvareṉṟum maṟṟavarkaḷ vāḻum patameṉṟum patamaṭainta pattaraṉu pavikkap paṭṭaaṉu pavaṅkaḷeṉṟum paṟpalavā virinta vitamoṉṟum teriyātē mayaṅkiyaeṉ taṉakkē veṭṭaveḷi yāaṟivit tiṭṭaaruḷ iṟaiyē catamoṉṟum cuttaciva caṉmārkkap potuvil taṉinaṭañcey aracēeṉ cāṟṟumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: Creeds, religions, and scriptures; the established gods and the realms where they reside; the experiences enjoyed by devotees who attain those realms, I was bewildered, knowing nothing of these many branching paths. To me, you, O Lord of grace, revealed everything as open space. O King who performs the unique dance in the eternal common space of Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam! Please graciously accept what I proclaim as well.
commentary: After being lost in the confusing maze of different religions, scriptures, and gods, Vallalar received a profound revelation. God showed him that all these complex systems resolve into one simple truth: the divine is veṭṭaveḷi, a vast, empty, open space of pure consciousness. This is the heart of Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Pure Siva), a universal way beyond all sectarian divisions. Having received this clarity, he asks God to accept his proclamation of this truth.

translit: eṉācai ellāmtaṉ aruḷvaṭivan taṉakkē eytiṭaccey tiṭṭaruḷi eṉaiyumuṭaṉ iruttit taṉācai ellāmeṉ uḷḷakattē vaittut tāṉumuṭaṉ iruntaruḷik kalantaperun takaiyē aṉṉāeṉ āruyirē appāeṉ amutē āvāeṉ ṟeṉaiyāṇṭa tēvāmeyc civamē poṉṉārum potuvilnaṭam purikiṉṟa aracē puṇṇiyaṉē eṉmoḻippūṅ kaṇṇiyumēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O great Magnanimous One, who graciously made all my desires reach your form of grace and seated me with you; who placed all your desires within my heart and, residing with me, merged with me! O Mother, my precious life! O Father, my ambrosia! O Deva, true Sivam, who exclaimed 'Ah!' and took me as your own! O King who performs the dance in the golden common space! O Virtuous One, please graciously accept this garland of my flower-like words.
commentary: This verse describes the experience of total union with the divine, a merging so complete that it is impossible to tell where the self ends and God begins. Vallalar says God took all his human desires and, in return, placed the divine will within his heart.
