Addressing God as Mother, Father, and his own life, he portrays a relationship of two beings melting into one.

translit: taṉaracē celuttiniṉṟa tattuvaṅkaḷ aṉaittum taṉittaṉieṉ vacamākit tāḻntēval iyaṟṟa muṉaracum piṉaracum naṭuaracum pōṟṟa muṉṉumaṇṭa piṇṭaṅkaḷ evaṟṟiṉumep pālum eṉaracē eṉṟuraikka eṉakkumuṭi cūṭṭi iṉpavaṭi vākkieṉṟum ilaṅkavaitta civamē eṉaracē eṉuyirē eṉirukaṇ maṇiyē iṇaiaṭippoṉ malarkaḷukkeṉ icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Sivam, who made all the tattvas, which had been conducting their own rule, individually come under my control, bow down, and perform service; who, praised by kings of past, present, and future, crowned me to declare 'It is my rule' before all, in all cosmic and physical realms, and everywhere; who transformed me into a form of bliss and made me shine forever! O my King, my life, the jewel of my two eyes! Please graciously adorn your pair of golden, flower-like feet with my music.
commentary: When one merges with the divine, the entire universe rearranges itself in response. Vallalar describes how the tattvas, the fundamental principles of reality that govern everything from mind to matter, now come under his command. He is crowned ruler of all worlds, as a sign that he has become one with the central organizing power of the cosmos, Sivam (the ultimate auspicious reality).

translit: paraveḷiyē naṭuveḷiyē upacānta veḷiyē pāḻveḷiyē mutalāka ēḻveḷikkap pālum viraviyamā maṟaikaḷelām taṉittaṉiceṉ ṟaḷantum meyyaḷavu kāṇātē melintiḷaittup pōṟṟa uravilavai tēṭiyaav veḷikaḷukkuḷ veḷiyāy ōṅkiyaav veḷikaḷaittaṉ ṉuḷaṭakkum veḷiyāyk karaiyaṟaniṉ ṟōṅkukiṉṟa cuttaciva veḷiyē kaṉintanaṭat taracēeṉ karuttumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O King of the ripened dance! O Suddha Siva Velithat stands and soars without limit! You are the space within those spaces forcefully sought by the Vedas and the space that contains those lofty spaces within yourself. You are beyond the supreme space, the central space, the space of sublime peace, and the seven spaces beginning with the void space, spaces that all the great, widespread Vedas grew weary trying to measure and, failing to find their true extent, languished and praised. Please graciously adorn yourself with my thoughts.
commentary: The highest spiritual realms are often described as different kinds of space, like the supreme space (paraveḷi) or even the void (pāḻveḷi). Vallalar says that even the ancient Vedas (sacred scriptures) failed to measure their full extent. The ultimate reality, which he calls Suddha Siva Veli (the space of pure Sivam), is something more: it is the limitless space that contains all other spaces and exists beyond them, forever beyond the reach of intellect or scripture.

translit: veyyalilē naṭantiḷaippu mēviyaak kaṇattē mikuniḻalum taṇṇamutum tantaaruḷ viḷaivē maiyalciṟi tuṟṟiṭattē maṭantaiyarkaḷ tāmē valintuvarac ceyvitta māṇpuṭaiya naṭpē kaiyaṟavāl kalaṅkiyapō takkaṇattē pōntu kaiyaṟavu tavirttaruḷik kāttaḷitta turaiyē aiyamuṟēl eṉṟeṉaiyāṇ ṭamutaḷitta patiyē ampalatteṉ aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O fruit of grace who, the moment I grew weary from walking in the harsh sun, gave me abundant shade and cool ambrosia! O magnificent Friend who, when I felt a little infatuation, made the young women themselves come to me insistently! O Lord who, when I was distraught with helplessness, came at that very moment, graciously removed my helplessness, and protected me! O Master who took me as your own, saying, 'Do not doubt,' and gave me ambrosia! O my King of the Ambalam, please graciously adorn yourself with my garland.
commentary: Divine grace is a constant, practical help in daily life. Vallalar recalls moments when God provided shade when he was hot, support when he felt desire, and rescue when he was helpless. This shows a God who is an intimate friend who cares for every need, from the mundane to the deepest, finally dispelling all doubt at the Ambalam, the sacred stage of consciousness.

translit: kolaipurivār taviramaṟṟai ellārum niṉatu kulattārē nīeṉatu kulattumutal makaṉē malaivaṟavē cuttaciva camaracacaṉ mārkkam vaḷaravaḷarn tirukkaeṉa vāḻttiyaeṉ kuruvē nilaiviḻaivār tamaikkākkum nittiyaṉē ellā nilaiyumviḷaṅ kuṟaaruḷil niṟuttiyaciṟ kuṇaṉē pulaiyaṟiyāp peruntavarkaḷ pōṟṟamaṇip potuvil puṉitanaṭat taracēeṉ pukalumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O my Guru, who blessed me saying, "Except for those who commit murder, all others are of your lineage. You are the firstborn son of my lineage. Live and grow so that the Suddha Siva Samarasa Sanmarkkam may flourish without confusion"! O Eternal One who protects those who desire the ultimate state! O one of virtuous consciousness who, in your grace, established me so that all states are illuminated! O King of the sacred dance in the jeweled common space, praised by great ascetics who know no baseness! Please graciously adorn yourself with my words.
commentary: God, acting as Vallalar's own teacher (Guru), gives him his life's mission: to establish the Suddha Siva Samarasa Sanmarkkam (path of pure Siva universal harmony). This path defines a universal family, declaring that all souls are kin, with one critical exception: those who commit murder are excluded. This establishes non-killing and no flesh eating as a foundational requirement for belonging to his spiritual community.

translit: uyirkkolaiyum pulaippocippum uṭaiyavarkaḷ ellām uṟaviṉattār allaravar puṟa:iṉattār avarkkup payirppuṟumōr pacitavirttal māttiramē purika parintumaṟṟaip paṇpuraiyēl naṇputavēl iṅkē nayappuṟucaṉ mārkkamavar aṭaiyaḷavum itutāṉ namāṇai eṉṟeṉakku naviṉṟaaruḷ iṟaiyē mayarppaṟumeyttavarpōṟṟap potuvilnaṭam puriyum mānaṭatteṉ aracēeṉ mālaiaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Lord of Grace, who declared to me, "All those who kill living beings and eat their foul flesh are not our kin; they are an out-group. For them, only relieve their abhorrent hunger. Do not offer them words of good character or befriend them here, until they attain the desirable Sanmarkkam. This is Our command." O my King of the great dance, who performs in the common space praised by true sages free of delusion, graciously wear my garland.
commentary: Here, God gives a precise and strict command regarding those who kill and eat meat. They are to be considered an "out-group," separate from the community of the Sanmarkkam (path of true knowledge). The only duty toward them is to feed them if they are hungry. All other forms of relationship, like friendship or spiritual instruction, are forbidden until they give up the practice of killing and eating flesh. This is presented as a divine law.

translit: vaṉpuṭaiyār kolaikaṇṭu pulaiuṇpār ciṟitum marapiṉaraṉ ṟātaliṉāl vakuttaavar aḷavil aṉpuṭaiya eṉmakaṉē pacitavirttal purika aṉṟiaruṭ ceyaloṉṟum ceyattuṇiyēl eṉṟē iṉpuṟaeṉ taṉakkicaitta eṉkuruvē eṉaittāṉ īṉṟataṉit tantaiyē tāyēeṉ iṟaiyē tuṉpaṟumeyt tavarcūḻntu pōṟṟatirup potuvil tūyanaṭat taracēeṉ collumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O my Guru, who joyfully declared to me, "The hard-hearted who kill and eat foul flesh are not of our tradition in the slightest. My loving son, toward that class of people, just relieve their hunger. Do not dare to perform any other act of grace." O my sole Father who gave me birth, my Mother, my God! O King of the pure dance in the sacred common space, surrounded and praised by true sages free of suffering, graciously wear my words as a garland.
commentary: This verse reinforces the divine command from the previous one. Those who kill and consume flesh are declared to be completely outside the spiritual tradition. The instruction to his "loving son" is clear and limited: relieve their hunger, but do not attempt any other act of grace for them. By addressing God as his Guru, Father, and Mother, Vallalar frames this difficult teaching as a law received from the most trusted and loving source imaginable.

translit: koṭiyavarē kolaipurintu pulainukarvār eṉiṉum kuṟittiṭumōr āpattil varuntukiṉṟa pōtu paṭiyilataip pārttukavēl avarvaruttam tuṉpam payantīrntu viṭukaeṉap parinturaitta kuruvē neṭiyavarē nāṉmukarē nittiyarē piṟarē niṉmalarē eṉkiṉṟōr ellārum kāṇa aṭiyumuyar muṭiyumeṉak kaḷittaperum poruḷē ampalatteṉ aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Guru who compassionately instructed me, "Even if they are cruel people who commit murder and eat flesh, when they suffer in some grave danger in this world, do not look on it and rejoice. Free them from their distress, suffering and fear." O great Reality who gave me Your feet and lofty crown for all, Vishnu, Brahma, the eternal ones, others, and those who call you the Pure One, to see! O my King of the Ambalam, graciously wear my floral garland.
commentary: After establishing a strict rule of separation, this verse gives a compassionate command. If people who commit murder and eat flesh are in grave danger, you must not look on their suffering with satisfaction; you must relieve their distress, pain and fear. Compassion to every living being is absolute and overrides the separation in times of crisis. You do not befriend them, but you do not abandon them to their pain.

translit: tayaiuṭaiyār ellārum camaracacaṉ mārkkam cārntavarē īṅkavarkaḷ tammōṭuṅ kūṭi nayamuṟunal aruḷneṟiyil kaḷittuviḷai yāṭi naṇṇukaeṉ ṟeṉakkicaitta naṇpuṟucaṟ kuruvē uyaluṟumeṉ uyirkkiṉiya uṟavēeṉ aṟivil ōṅkiyapē raṉpēeṉ aṉpiluṟum oḷiyē mayalaṟumeyt tavarcūḻntu pōṟṟummaṇi maṉṟil mānaṭatteṉ aracēeṉ mālaiaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O my beloved true Guru, who told me, "All who possess compassion belong to the Samarasa Sanmarkkam. Here, join with them, and live, joyfully playing in the good and desirable path of grace." O dear kin, sweet to my striving soul! O great love that soars in my mind! O light that dwells in my love! O my King of the great dance in the Hall of Gems, surrounded and praised by true sages free from delusion, graciously wear my garland.
commentary: The only requirement for joining the true spiritual path is having compassion in your heart. Vallalar calls this path Samarasa Sanmarkkam (the way of harmonious true knowledge) and says that all compassionate people already belong to it. This creates a universal community based on a shared inner quality. Spiritual life, he suggests, should be a joyful, playful path shared with others who value kindness.

translit: aruḷuṭaiyār ellārum camaracacaṉ mārkkam aṭaintavarē ātaliṉāl avaruṭaṉē kūṭit teruḷuṭaiya aruḷneṟiyil kaḷittuviḷai yāṭic ceḻittiṭuka vāḻkaeṉac ceppiyacaṟ kuruvē poruḷuṭaiya peruṅkaruṇaip pūraṇameyc civamē pōtānta mutalāṟum niṟaintoḷirum oḷiyē maruḷuṭaiyār tamakkumaruḷ nīkkamaṇip potuvil vayaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ mālaiyumēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O true Guru who declared, "All who possess grace have attained the Samarasa Sanmarkkam; therefore, join with them, prosper and live well, joyfully playing in the clear path of grace." O true and perfect Sivam of meaningful, great compassion! O Light that fills and shines through the six cosmic principles beginning with Bodhaantam! O King of the radiant dance in the jeweled common space, who removes the delusion of the deluded, graciously accept my garland as well.
commentary: Possessing grace is the sign that one has entered the Samarasa Sanmarkkam. Here, grace and compassion are presented as two sides of the same coin; having one means you are on the true path. The path is one that takes you beyond the limits of the ordinary mind, which he alludes to with the term Bodhaantam (the end of intellect), into a state of pure, compassionate being.

translit: vemmālaic ciṟuvaroṭum viḷaiyāṭit tiriyum mikacciṟiya paruvattē viyantuniṉai namatu pemmāṉeṉ ṟaṭikuṟittu pāṭumvakai purinta perumāṉē nāṉceyta peruntavameyp payaṉē cemmānta ciṟiyēṉaic ciṟuneṟiyil ciṟitum celuttāmal peruneṟiyil celuttiyanaṟ ṟuṇaiyē ammāṉē eṉāvik kāṉaperum poruḷē ampalatteṉ aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great one who, even in my tender youth as I wandered and played with troublesome boys, miraculously made me sing songs praising your feet, calling you 'our Lord'! O true fruit of the great penance I performed! O good companion who guided me on the great path, never letting arrogant little me stray even slightly onto the wrong path! O Master, great substance of my very life! O my King in the sacred hall, graciously wear my garland.
commentary: God's grace can be a guiding force from the very beginning of life. Vallalar shares a personal memory of how, as a young boy, he was inspired to sing praises to God even while playing. He sees this as a sign of God acting as a constant, loving companion who kept him from straying and led him onto the great spiritual path, a blessing earned through spiritual efforts in past lives.

translit: āṇavamām iruṭṭaṟaiyil kiṭantaciṟi yēṉai aṇimāyai viḷakkaṟaiyil amarttiaṟi vaḷittu nīṇavamām tattuvappoṉ māṭamicai ēṟṟi niṟaintaaruḷ amutaḷittu nittamuṟa vaḷarttu māṇuṟael lānalamum koṭuttulakam aṟiya maṇimuṭiyum cūṭṭiyaeṉ vāḻmutalām patiyē ēṇuṟuciṟ capaiiṭattum poṟcapaiyiṉ iṭattum ilaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: You took little me, who was lying in the dark room of egoism, seated me in the beautiful lamplit room of illusion, and gave me knowledge. You then raised me to the golden mansion of the enduring principles, gave me the full nectar of grace, and nurtured me to be eternal. O Lord, the source of my life, who bestowed every good thing on me for my excellence and, for the world to see, crowned me with a jeweled crown! O King of Dance, shining in the exalted Hall of Consciousness and in the Golden Hall, graciously wear my music as well.
commentary: This verse uses powerful metaphors to describe the soul's way to God. We begin in the darkness of ego, what Vallalar calls Āṇavam. Grace then moves us into the world of experience, a room lit by the beautiful but confusing lamp of Māyai (illusion), where we gain knowledge. From there, we are raised to understand the fundamental principles of existence (Tattvas) and are finally perfected by grace. It is a path from the deepest ignorance to the highest state of consciousness, symbolized by God's dance in the Hall of Consciousness (Ciṟ-Capai) and the Golden Hall (Poṟ-Capai).

translit: pāṉmaṟuttu viḷaiyāṭum ciṟuparuvat tiṭaiyē pakarumula kiccaioṉṟum patiyāteṉ uḷattē māṉmaṟuttu viḷaṅkutiru ainteḻuttē patiya vaittaperu vāḻvēeṉ vāḻviluṟum cukamē mīṉmaṟuttuc cuṭarmayamāy viḷaṅkiyatōr viṇṇē viṇaṉantam uḷḷaṭaṅka virintaperu veḷiyē ūṉmaṟutta peruntavaruk koḷivaṭivam koṭuttē ōṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ uraiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great life that, in my early youth while I played games spurning even milk, allowed no worldly desire to take root in my mind, but instead impressed upon it the sacred five letters that shine, spurning the deer! O bliss experienced in my life! O a sky that shines as a mass of light, outshining the stars! O vast expanse that expanded to contain infinite skies! O exalted King of Dance, who gives a form of light to the great ascetics who have renounced the flesh, graciously wear my words as well.
commentary: Grace protected him from worldly desires even in childhood, replacing them with a deep love for the Aintelu-ttu, the sacred five-letter mantra of Siva. This inner state was not his own effort; it was a gift, a "great life" placed within him by God. He praises this divine reality as a vast, luminous expanse that dwarfs the physical cosmos, a light given to those who have overcome attachment to the body.

translit: meyccukamum uyirccukamum mikuṅkaraṇac cukamum viḷaṅkupatac cukamumataṉ mēlvīṭṭuc cukamum eccukamum taṉṉiṭattē eḻuntacukam āka eṅkaṇumōr nīkkamaṟa eḻuntaperuñ cukamē accukamum aṭaiyaṟivum aṭaintavarum kāṭṭā tatutāṉāy atuatuvāy appālām poruḷē poyccukattai virumpāta puṉitarmakiḻn tēttum potunaṭatteṉ aracēeṉ pukalumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great bliss that arises everywhere without exception, with the bliss of the body, the bliss of the soul, the abundant bliss of the inner faculties, the shining bliss of spiritual states, and the bliss of liberationall arising from within you! O substance beyond all, which is Itself That, which cannot be shown even by those who have attained that bliss and its defining knowledge! O my King of the universal dance, whom the pure ones who desire no false pleasure praise with joy, graciously wear my praise as well.
commentary: Every kind of happiness, from the physical pleasure of the body to the ultimate bliss of liberation (vīṭu), comes from a single source: God. This divine bliss is more than another state to be achieved; it is the substance of all joy itself, including the joy of the inner faculties (karaṇam) and spiritual states (patam). Vallalar describes it as a reality beyond words, something that cannot be pointed out or explained. The final line praises God's universal dance (potu naṭam), celebrated by those who have turned away from fleeting worldly pleasures.

translit: aṇṭavakai evvaḷavō avvaḷavum avaṟṟil amainta:uyir evvaḷavō avvaḷavum avaikaḷ kaṇṭaporuḷ evvaḷavō avvaḷavum avaṟṟil kalantakalap pevvaḷavō avvaḷavum niṟaintē viṇtakumōr nātaveḷi cuttaveḷi mōṉa veḷiñāṉa veḷimutalām veḷikaḷelām nirampik koṇṭatuvāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cuttaciva mayamē kulavunaṭat taracēeṉ kuṟṟamumkoṇ ṭaruḷē.
translation: You completely fill all the many types of universes, all the many lives established within them, all the many objects they perceive, and all the many ways they intermingle. O pure Sivamayam, shining as that which has filled and encompassed all the expanses, such as the expanse of sound, the pure expanse, the expanse of silence, and the expanse of wisdom! O King of the glorious dance, graciously accept even my faults.
commentary: God is the absolute fullness of existence, pervading every universe, every life-form, and every object within them. This divine presence, which Vallalar calls Sivamayam (being wholly Siva), also fills all the inner worlds of consciousness: the expanse of sound (nāta-veḷi), the expanse of silence (mōṉa-veḷi), and the pure expanse of wisdom (ñāṇa-veḷi). In a humble conclusion, he asks this all-encompassing God to accept his praises and even his faults, folding them into that infinite wholeness.

translit: cattiyanāṉ mukaraṉantar nāraṇarmaṟ ṟuḷavām talaivaravar avarulakil cārntavarkaḷ piṟarkaḷ itticaiat ticaiyāka icaikkumaṇṭap pakuti ettaṉaiyō kōṭikaḷil irukkumuyirt tiraḷkaḷ attaṉaipēr uṇṭālum aṇuvaḷavum kuṟaiyā taruḷveḷiyil oḷivaṭivāy āṉanta mayamāyc cuttaciva aṉupavamāy viḷaṅkiyateḷ ḷamutē tuyanaṭat taracēeṉ collumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O clear ambrosia, you who shine as the experience of pure Siva, a form of light filled with bliss in the space of grace! Even if Satya Brahma, Anantar, Narayana, and other such lords, along with those in their worlds and the multitudes of lives in the many crores of cosmic regions spoken of in every direction, were all to consume you, you would not diminish even by an atom. O King of the pure dance, graciously wear my words as well.
commentary: God's grace is pictured as an infinite and inexhaustible nourishment, a clear ambrosia of pure divine experience. Even if all the gods and every living being in countless universes were to partake of this grace, it would not diminish by a single atom. This powerfully conveys that the divine is endlessly available to everyone, without scarcity or limit.

translit: poṟikaraṇa mutaṟpalavām tattuvamum avaṟṟaip purintiyakki naṭattukiṉṟa pūraṇarum avarkkuc ceṟiyumupa kārikaḷām cattikaḷum avaraic celuttukiṉṟa cattarkaḷum taṉoḷiyāl viḷaṅka aṟivaṟivāy avvaṟivuk kaṟivāyev viṭattum āṉatuvāyt tāṉatuvāy atuatuvāy niṟaintē neṟivaḻaṅkap potuvilaruḷ tirunaṭañcey aracē niṉaṭiyēṉ coṉmālai nilaikkaaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O King who performs the sacred dance of grace in the common space to grant the Path! By your own light, you cause to shine the many tattvas, such as the senses and inner faculties; the perfected beings who understand and direct them; the Saktis who are their close helpers; and the Saktars who impel them. You are the consciousness of consciousness and the consciousness for that consciousness, becoming every place, becoming yourself, and becoming each and every thing, filling them completely. Graciously wear this garland of words from me, your slave, that it may endure.
commentary: God is the fundamental light of consciousness that makes everything in existence knowable and active. This light illuminates all levels of reality: the basic principles of being (tattvas), the divine feminine powers (Saktis), and the perfected beings who wield them (Saktars). Crucially, God is the "consciousness of consciousness," the very source of awareness within our own minds. This dance of consciousness happens in the Podu, a universal common space, making the spiritual path accessible to all.

translit: uṇṇukiṉṟa ūṇveṟuttu vaṟṟiyumpuṟ ṟeḻuntum orukōṭip peruntalaivar āṅkāṅkē varuntip paṇṇukiṉṟa peruntavattum kiṭaipparitāyc ciṟiya payalkaḷiṉum ciṟiyēṟkuk kiṭaittaperum patiyē naṇṇukiṉṟa peruṅkaruṇai amutaḷitteṉ uḷattē nāṉākit tāṉāki amarntaruḷi nāṉtāṉ eṇṇukiṉṟa paṭiellām aruḷkiṉṟa civamē ilaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great Lord, you are so difficult to obtain even through the immense penance performed with much suffering by a crore of great masters, who abhor food, become emaciated, and have anthills grow on them. Yet, you were obtained by me, who is smaller than even a small boy. O Sivam, you gave me the ambrosia of great compassion, graciously settled in my heart as both myself and yourself, and now grant all that I think of! O King of the brilliant dance, graciously wear my song as well.
commentary: Attainment of God comes through pure grace. Vallalar contrasts the great masters who suffer for ages in severe penance, yet fail to reach God, with his own experience. As someone who considers himself utterly small and unworthy, he found God easily, by receiving the "ambrosia of great compassion" as a gift. The verse suggests that God's presence is given out of love and settles in the heart, rather than being won through heroic struggle.

translit: koḷḷaiviṉaik kūṭṭuṟavāl kūṭṭiyapal camayak kūṭṭamumak kūṭṭattē kūvukiṉṟa kalaiyum kaḷḷamuṟum akkalaikaḷ kāṭṭiyapal katiyum kāṭcikaḷum kāṭcitaru kaṭavuḷarum ellām piḷḷaiviḷai yāṭṭeṉanaṉ kaṟivittiṅ keṉaiyē piḷḷaieṉak koṇṭupiḷḷaip peyariṭṭa patiyē taḷḷariya meyyaṭiyār pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟil taṉinaṭañcey aracēeṉ cāṟṟumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Lord, you made me clearly understand that it is all child's play: the various religious groups brought together by the association of immense karma; the doctrines proclaimed in those groups; the various destinies shown by those deceitful doctrines; the visions, and the gods who grant those visions. You took me here as your child and gave me a child's name. O King who performs the unique dance in the Hall of Gems, praised by true devotees who can never be turned away, graciously wear my utterances as well.
commentary: God made Vallalar know clearly that all of it is child's play: the many religious groups gathered by the bonds of karma, the doctrines cried out in them, the destinies those deceitful doctrines promise, their visions, and the gods who grant those visions. In their place God took him as His own child and gave him a child's name. The dance goes on in the Hall of Gems, praised by true devotees.

translit: nālvaruṇam āciramam ācāram mutalā naviṉṟakalaic caritamelām piḷḷaiviḷai yāṭṭē mēlvaruṇam tōlvaruṇam kaṇṭaṟivār ilainī viḻittitupār eṉṟeṉakku viḷampiyacaṟ kuruvē kālvaruṇaṅ kalaiyātē vīṇilalai yātē kāṇpaṉael lāmeṉakkuk kāṭṭiyameyp poruḷē mālvaruṇaṅ kaṭantavarai mēlvaruṇat tēṟṟa vayaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ mālaiaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Satguru, you explained to me, saying: “All the scriptural accounts of the four varnas, the asramas, codes of conduct, and so on, are child's play. No one has ever seen and known a ‘higher varna’ or a ‘skin varna.’ Open your eyes and see this!” O True Substance, you showed me all that can be seen, without my foundation being shaken and without my wandering in vain. O King of the radiant dance, who elevates those who have transcended the varna of delusion to the highest varna, graciously wear my garland.
commentary: Social and religious hierarchies, like the caste system, are man-made illusions. The true teacher (Satguru) revealed to Vallalar that the traditional four social orders (varnas) and stages of life (asramas) are meaningless distractions. No one, the teacher insists, has ever actually seen a "higher caste" or a "lower caste" as a spiritual reality; these are just ideas. True spiritual elevation comes from transcending delusion, not from one's birth or social position.

translit: evviṭattum evvuyirkkum ilaṅkucivam oṉṟē eṉṉāṇai eṉmakaṉē iraṇṭillai āṅkē cevviṭattē aruḷoṭucērt tiraṇṭeṉakkaṇ ṭaṟinī tikaippaṭaiyēl eṉṟeṉakkuc ceppiyacaṟ kuruvē avviṭattē uvviṭattē amarntatupōl kāṭṭi aṅkumiṅkum appuṟamum eṅkuniṟai poruḷē ovviṭacciṟ capaiiṭattum poṟcapaiyiṉ iṭattum ōṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ uraiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Satguru who told me, "In every place and for every life, the radiant Sivam is one. By my command, my son, there is no second. There, in that perfect place, see and know for yourself that it appears as two when joined with Grace. Do not be bewildered." O Essence, you show yourself as if seated in that place and this, while filling here, there, beyond, and everywhere! O King of the exalted dance in the fitting Chit Sabhai and the Potsabai, please graciously accept and wear my words as well.
commentary: The Satguru tells Vallalar that the Sivam shining in every place and in every life is one alone, and swears there is no second. Yet in its proper place, joined with its Grace (aruḷ), it is to be seen as two: Sivam and Grace. He is told not to be bewildered. God seems to be seated here or there, yet fills here, there, beyond and everywhere, and dances in the Chit Sabhai and the Porsabai.

translit: iyalvētā kamaṅkaḷpurā ṇaṅkaḷiti kācam ivaimutalā intiracā laṅkaṭaiyā uraippār mayalorunūl māttirantāṉ cālameṉa aṟintār makaṉēnī nūlaṉaittum cālameṉa aṟika ceyalaṉaittum aruḷoḷiyāl kāṇkaeṉa eṉakkē tiruvuḷampaṟ ṟiyañāṉa tēcikamā maṇiyē ayalaṟiyā aṟivuṭaiyār ellārum pōṟṟa āṭukiṉṟa aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O great gem of a Jnana Desika, who grasped my very heart and said to me, "Those who list the books from the Vedas, Agamas, Puranas and Itihasas down to the Indrajalam, in their delusion take only that one book to be jalam, mere conjuring. My son, know that all these books are jalam. See every action by the light of Grace." O King who dances, praised by all those with a wisdom unknown to outsiders, please graciously accept and wear my garland of words.
commentary: All scriptures are an illusion compared to the direct light of Grace. In a startling statement, Vallalar's teacher (Jnana Desika, or wisdom-teacher) dismisses all sacred texts, the Vedas, Agamas, and Puranas (foundational Hindu scriptures), as a kind of spiritual magic show. The deluded take only the book of conjuring to be jalam; the teacher says to see them all as jalam. The only reliable guide is the inner light of Grace, which allows one to perceive truth directly, without any textual filter.

translit: tōṉṟiyavē tākamattaic cālameṉa uraittēm coṟporuḷum ilakkiyamum poyeṉakkaṇ ṭaṟiyēl ūṉṟiyavē tākamattiṉ uṇmainiṉak kākum ulakaṟivē tākamattaip poyeṉakkaṇ ṭuṇarvāy āṉṟatiru varuṭceṅkōl niṉakkaḷittōm nīyē āḷkaaruḷ oḷiyāleṉ ṟaḷittataṉic civamē ēṉṟatiru vamuteṉakkum īntaperum poruḷē ilaṅkunaṭat taracēeṉ icaiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O unique Sivam who bestowed this upon me, saying, "We have declared the manifest Vedas and Agamas to be an illusion. But do not perceive their words, meanings, and literary forms to be false. The truth within those profound scriptures will become yours. You will see and realize that the Vedas and Agamas, as the world knows them, are false. We have given you the noble scepter of divine Grace. You yourself shall rule by the light of Grace." O great Essence who also gave me the fitting divine amrita! O King of the radiant dance, please graciously accept and wear my song as well.
commentary: While scriptures are false as worldly knowledge, their inner truth is revealed through Grace. God clarifies the previous verse's bold claim: the way the world reads and understands the scriptures is an illusion. However, the deep, essential truth hidden within those same texts will be revealed directly to one who has received Grace (arul). Vallalar has been given the "scepter of Grace," empowering him to govern his life by this inner light, independent of any external religious authority or text.

translit: nāṉmukarnal uruttirarkaḷ nāraṇarin tirarkaḷ navilarukar puttarmutal matattalaivar ellām vāṉmukattil tōṉṟiaruḷ oḷiciṟitē aṭaintu vāṉakattum vaiyakattum maṉampōṉa paṭiyē tēṉmukantuṇ ṭavareṉavē viḷaiyāṭā niṉṟa ciṟupiḷḷaik kūṭṭameṉa aruṭperuñcō tiyiṉāl tāṉmikakkaṇ ṭaṟikaeṉac cāṟṟiyacaṟ kuruvē capaiyilnaṭat taracēeṉ cāṟṟumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Satguru who declared, "Brahma, the good Rudras, Narayana, Indra, the professed Arhats, Buddhas, and all other founders of religions appeared in the celestial expanse, attained just a little of the light of Grace, and then played about in heaven and on earth as they pleased, like people who have scooped up and drunk honey. Know this clearly for yourself through ArutPerunJothi: they are a crowd of small children." O King of the dance in the Sabai, please graciously accept and wear my pronouncements as well.
commentary: The Satguru (true teacher) tells Vallalar to see for himself, by the light of ArutPerunJothi, what the founders of religions are. Brahma, Rudra, Narayana, Indra, the Arhats, the Buddhas and every other founder received only a little of the light of Grace, then played in heaven and on earth as they pleased, like those who have scooped up honey. They are a crowd of small children. A little Grace is not the Vast Grace-Light.

translit: tavaṟāta vētānta cittānta mutalāc cāṟṟukiṉṟa antamelām taṉitturaikkum poruḷai ivaṟāta cuttaciva caṉmārkka nilaiyil iruntaruḷām peruñcōti koṇṭaṟital kūṭum evarālum piṟitoṉṟāl kaṇṭaṟital kūṭā teṉāṇai eṉmakaṉē aruṭperuñcō tiyaittāṉ tavaṟātu peṟṟaṉainī vāḻkaeṉṟa patiyē capaiyilnaṭat taracēeṉ cāṟṟumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Lord who said, "The Essence that all the conclusive philosophies, beginning with the unfailing Vedanta and Siddhanta, speak of individually can be known by taking hold of the great Jothi of Grace while remaining in the state of the generous Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam. By my command, my son, it is impossible for anyone to see and know it by any other means. You have unfailingly received ArutPerunJothi. May you prosper!" O King of the dance in the Sabai, please graciously accept and wear my pronouncements as well.
commentary: The ultimate truth that different philosophies like Vedanta and Siddhanta try to describe can only be truly known in one way. It is realized through the great Jothi (light) of Grace, which is found on the path of Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the path of pure good). God makes it clear this is not a philosophical debate: no other method can lead to this direct knowledge. Vallalar has received this supreme Grace and is blessed to prosper in it.

translit: aiyamuṟēl eṉmakaṉē ippiṟappiṟ ṟāṉē aṭaivatelām aṭaintaṉainī añcalaieṉ ṟaruḷi vaiyamicait taṉiirutti maṇimuṭiyum cūṭṭi vāḻkaeṉa vāḻttiyaeṉ vāḻkkaimutaṟ poruḷē tuyyaaruṭ peruñcōti cuttaciva veḷiyē cukamayamē ellāñcey vallataṉip patiyē uyyuneṟi kāṭṭimaṇi maṉṟiṭattē naṭikkum orumainaṭat taracēeṉ uraiyumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: You graciously said, "Do not doubt, my son. In this very birth, you have attained everything there is to attain. Do not fear." You seated me alone upon the earth, placed a jeweled crown on me, and blessed me to live long. You are the primal substance of my life. O pure, great radiance of grace, O pure expanse of Civa, O embodiment of bliss, O singular Lord who has the power to do everything! O King of the singular dance, who performs in the jeweled hall showing the path to salvation, graciously wear my utterance as well.
commentary: God gives Vallalar the ultimate reassurance: he has already attained everything possible in this very lifetime. He is told not to doubt or fear, for he has been granted spiritual sovereignty over his own being. This is the promise of complete fulfillment, right here and now, through the power of pure Grace.

translit: kālaiyilē eṉṟaṉakkē kiṭaittaperum poruḷē kaḷippēeṉ karuttakattē kaṉintanaṟuṅ kaṉiyē mēlaiyilē immaiyilē orumaiyilē tavattāl mēvukiṉṟa perumpayaṉām viḷaivaielām tarumac cālaiyilē orupakalil tantataṉip patiyē camaracacaṉ mārkkacaṅkat talaiamarnta nitiyē mālaiyilē ciṟantamoḻi mālaiaṇin tāṭum mānaṭatteṉ aracēeṉ mālaiyumēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: O great substance that came to me this morning! O my delight! O fragrant fruit ripened within my thoughts! O singular Lord who, in a single day at the hall of charity, gave all the great resulting benefits attained through austerity in the hereafter, in this life, and in oneness! O treasure seated at the head of the Samarasa Sanmarkkam Sangam! O my King of the great dance, who dances in the evening wearing a garland of choice words, graciously accept my garland as well.
commentary: The spiritual benefits that might take lifetimes of austerity to achieve were given to Vallalar in a single day. This happened at his tarumac cālai (hall of charity), linking his ultimate spiritual realization directly to his compassionate act of feeding the hungry. The verse marvels at the overwhelming speed and generosity of Grace, which bestows the highest rewards for service.

translit: ciṟpatamum taṟpatamum poṟpatattē kāṭṭum civapatamē āṉantat tēmpākiṉ patamē coṟpataṅkaḷ kaṭantataṉṟi muppatamum kaṭantē turiyapata muṅkaṭanta periyataṉip poruḷē naṟpatameṉ muṭicūṭṭik kaṟpatelāṅ kaṇattē nāṉaṟintu tāṉāka nalkiyaeṉ kuruvē paṟpatattut talaivarelām pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟil payilumnaṭat taracēeṉ pāṭalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O state of Civathat reveals the state of pure consciousnessand the state of selfin your golden feet! O state of sweet, ambrosial bliss! O great, singular substance that has transcended the states of words and the three states and even the fourth state! O my Guru who, crowning my head with your good feet, graciously enabled me to instantly know all there is to learn and to become That myself! O King of the dance who performs in the jeweled hall, praised by lords of many realms, please graciously wear my song as an adornment.
commentary: The ultimate reality, which he calls the "state of Civa" (civapatam), is the source from which we understand both pure consciousness (ciṟpatam) and our own true self (taṟpatam). This reality is beyond all words and even beyond the highest mystical states known to yogis, such as turīyam (the ‘fourth’ state beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep). In a moment of grace, God acted as his Guru, placing his feet on Vallalar's head and granting him knowledge and the direct experience of becoming that ultimate reality himself.

translit: ātiyilē eṉaiyāṇṭeṉ aṟivakattē amarnta appāeṉ aṉpēeṉ āruyirē amutē vītiyilē viḷaiyāṭit tirintapiḷḷaip paruvam mikapperiya paruvameṉa viyantaruḷi aruḷām cōtiyilē viḻaivuṟaccey tiṉiyamoḻi mālai toṭuttiṭaccey taṇintukoṇṭa turaiyēciṟ potuvām nītiyilē niṟaintanaṭat taracēiṉ ṟaṭiyēṉ nikaḻttiyacoṉ mālaiyumnī tikaḻttiaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Father, my Love, my precious life, my ambrosia, who ruled me from the beginning and settled within my consciousness! You graciously marveled at my childhood days of playing and wandering in the streets, calling it a "very great phase." You made me yearn for the radiance of grace and compose a garland of sweet words, which you then wore, O Master! O King of the dance, filled with the justice that is the common expanse of consciousness! Today, please make radiant and graciously wear this garland of words uttered by your servant.
commentary: God's grace is a constant presence that has guided him since his earliest days. In a beautiful, intimate touch, Vallalar recalls how the Lord looked upon his carefree childhood play as a "very great phase," validating his entire life. It was this ever-present divine love that stirred the longing in him and inspired him to compose these poems. The divine dance occurs in the cit-potu, the universal expanse of consciousness available to all.

translit: kaṇakkuvaḻak katukaṭanta peruveḷikku naṭuvē katirparappi viḷaṅkukiṉṟa kaṇniṟainta cuṭarē iṇakkamuṟum aṉparkaḷtam itayaveḷi muḻutum iṉituviḷaṅ kuṟanaṭuvē ilaṅkumoḷi viḷakkē maṇakkunaṟu maṇamēciṉ mayamāyeṉ uḷattē vayaṅkutaṉip poruḷēeṉ vāḻvēeṉ maruntē piṇakkaṟiyāp peruntavarkaḷ cūḻamaṇi maṉṟil perunaṭañcey aracēeṉ pitaṟṟumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O eye-filling effulgence, shining and spreading your rays in the midst of the great expanse that is beyond all measure and account! O lamp of light that shines in the middle of the entire heart-expanse of loving devotees, illuminating it sweetly! O fragrant aroma! O singular substance that shines in my mind as pure consciousness! O my life! O my medicine! O King who performs the great dance in the jeweled hall, surrounded by great ascetics who know no conflict, please graciously wear even my prattle.
commentary: The divine is described here as a vast, immeasurable light, yet it is also an intimate inner lamp that illuminates the hearts of those who love it. This presence is more than abstract light; it is a tangible experience, a fragrant aroma, the very substance of life, a healing medicine, and the pure consciousness (cinmayam) within one's own mind. In a touching display of humility, Vallalar refers to his sublime verses as mere "prattle," asking the Lord to accept even this humble offering.

translit: aṭicciṟiyēṉ accamelām orukaṇattē nīkki aruḷamutam mikaaḷittōr aṇiyumeṉak kaṇintu kaṭikkamalat tayaṉmutalōr kaṇṭumika viyappak katirmuṭiyum cūṭṭieṉaik kaḷittāṇṭa patiyē vaṭittamaṟai muṭivayaṅku māmaṇippoṟ cuṭarē maṉamvākkuk kaṭantaperu vāṉnaṭuvām oḷiyē paṭittalattār vāṉtalattār paraviyiṭap potuvil parintanaṭat taracēeṉ pāṭṭumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: O Master, in a single instant you removed all the fears of this lowly servant, gave me abundant grace-nectar, and adorned me as one of your own. You crowned me with a radiant crown and joyfully took me as your subject, to the great astonishment of Brahma on his fragrant lotus and all the others. O brilliant, gem-like golden flame shining at the pinnacle of the refined Vedas! O light in the center of the vast expanse, beyond mind and speech! O King of the compassionate dance, whom the people of earth and heaven praise in the universal space, please graciously accept and wear my song as well.
commentary: The transformation by grace is instantaneous and total. In a single moment, God removed all fear, gave him the "nectar of grace" (aruḷamutam), and crowned him, elevating him to a status that astonished even the celestial beings. This shows that the Lord's compassion can accomplish in an instant what might otherwise seem impossible. This ultimate reality is beyond scriptures and thought, a compassionate dance taking place in the universal space (podu) for all to witness.

translit: ettuṇaiyum ciṟiyēṉai nāṉmukaṉmāl mutalōr ēṟaritām perunilaimēl ēṟṟiuṭaṉ iruntē meyttuṇaiyām tiruvaruṭpē ramutammika aḷittu vēṇṭiyavā ṟaṭināyēṉ viḷaiyāṭap purintu cuttaciva caṉmārkka neṟioṉṟē eṅkum tulaṅkaaruḷ ceytaperuñ cōtiyaṉē potuvil citturuvāy naṭampuriyum uttamacaṟ kuruvē ciṟcapaieṉ aracēeṉ ciṟumoḻiēṟ ṟaruḷē.
translation: You raised me, who am utterly small, to a great state difficult for even Brahma, Vishnu, and the others to attain. Staying with me, you gave me the abundant, great nectar of holy grace, my true companion, and let me, your servant-dog, play as I wished. O great Jothi, who decreed with grace that the path of Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam alone should shine everywhere! O supreme Satguru, who performs the dance as the very form of consciousness in the universal space! O my King of the Chit Sabhai, please graciously accept my humble words.
commentary: The highest spiritual state is a gift of grace for the humble. Through this grace, Vallalar was taught that the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (path of pure divine truth) is the single, universal way. He identifies God as the Satguru (perfect true teacher) who reveals this truth by dancing as pure consciousness in the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness).

translit: irunta:iṭan teriyātē iruntaciṟi yēṉai evvulakil uḷḷavarum ēttiṭamēl ēṟṟi aruntavarum ayaṉmutalām talaivarkaḷum uḷattē aticayikkat tiruvamutum aḷittaperum patiyē tiruntumaṟai muṭipporuḷē poruḷmuṭipil uṇarntōr tikaḻamuṭin tuṭkoṇṭa civapōkap poruḷē peruntavarkaḷ pōṟṟamaṇi maṉṟilnaṭam puriyum perunaṭatteṉ aracēeṉ pitaṟṟumaṇin taruḷē.
translation: I was so lowly, my very whereabouts were unknown, yet you raised me up so that people of all worlds praise me. O great Master, you gave me the sacred nectar, making rare ascetics and the chief gods like Brahma marvel in their hearts. O essence at the pinnacle of the perfected Vedas! O substance of Siva-Bliss, which those who have realized the ultimate truth grasp and embody in their glorious culmination! O my King of the great dance, performing in the Mani Mandram as great ascetics praise you, please graciously accept and wear even my babblings.
commentary: Grace can lift a person from complete obscurity to a position of honor recognized by all worlds. This is the miracle Vallalar celebrates. God is both the ultimate truth described in scripture and the direct, lived experience of civapōkam (Siva-Bliss) enjoyed by the fully realized. The divine dance in the Mani Mandram (hall of gems) is a metaphor for this luminous, blissful realization.

translit: kuṇamaṟiyēṉ ceytaperuṅ kuṟṟamelāṅ kuṇamāk koṇṭaruḷi eṉṉuṭaiya kuṟippellām muṭittu maṇamuṟupē raruḷiṉpa amutameṉak kaḷittu maṇimuṭiyum cūṭṭieṉai vāḻkaeṉa vāḻttit taṇavililā teṉṉuḷattē tāṉkalantu nāṉum tāṉumoru vaṭivākit taḻaittōṅkap purintē aṇavuṟupēr aruṭcōti aracukoṭut taruḷi āṭukiṉṟa aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: Though I am ignorant of virtue, You graciously considered all my great faults to be virtues and fulfilled all my desires. You gave me the delightful, fragrant, great nectar of grace-bliss, crowned me with a jeweled crown, and blessed me, saying, ‘May you prosper.’ Without any separation, you mingled within my heart and made it so that you and I flourished as a single form. You graciously bestowed on me the kingdom of the great, ever-present Grace-Jothi. O King who dances, please graciously accept and wear my garland of words.
commentary: God's grace is so powerful that it sees virtue in our faults and merges with the soul until the two become one. Vallalar describes this union as a shared flourishing, where he is given the "kingdom of the great Grace-Jothi" (light of grace) to rule with God. It is a state of complete, inseparable oneness.

translit: talaikāliṅ kaṟiyātē tirintaciṟi yēṉait tāṉvalintāṭ koṇṭaruḷit taṭaimuḻutun tavirttē malaivaṟumey aṟivaḷittē aruḷamutam arutti vallapacat tikaḷellām maruviyiṭap purintu nilaiyuṟavē tāṉumaṭi yēṉumoru vaṭivāy niṟaiyaniṟai vittuyarnta nilaiyataṉmēl amartti alartalaippēr aruṭcōti aracukoṭut taruḷi āṭukiṉṟa aracēeṉ alaṅkalaṇin taruḷē.
translation: I was a lowly one wandering here, not knowing my head from my feet, but you forcefully took me as your subject and removed all obstacles. You gave me unwavering true knowledge, fed me grace-nectar, and made it so that all the mighty Shaktis came to me. Making your servant and yourself a single, stable form, you filled me to overflowing and seated me in that high state. You graciously bestowed on me the kingdom of the great, blossoming Grace-Jothi. O King who dances, please graciously accept and wear my garland of words.
commentary: Even a person who is completely lost can be saved by God's powerful and unsolicited intervention. Vallalar recalls being directionless before God forcefully removed all his obstacles, gave him true knowledge, and granted him Shaktis (divine powers). This grace culminates in a stable, permanent union where the soul and God become a single form, sharing the kingdom of light.

translit: mayarppu - cōrvu. mutaṟpatippu.
translation: mayarppu — 'weariness'. First edition.

translit: poṉpuṉai puyaṉum ayaṉummaṟ ṟavarum pukalarum periyaōr nilaiyil iṉpuru vāki aruḷoṭum viḷaṅki iyaṟṟalē ātiain toḻilum taṉpotuc camukat taivarkaḷ iyaṟṟat taṉiara ciyaṟṟumōr talaivaṉ aṉpeṉum kuṭicai nuḻaintaṉa ṉāṉāl avaṉtaṉai maṟuppavar yārē.
translation: He is the one leader who rules his unique kingdom, shining as the form of bliss with grace in a great state that Vishnu, Brahma, and others cannot describe. He has the deities in his universal assembly perform the five primary functions and all that follows. When he has entered the hut called love, who is there to refuse him?
commentary: The Lord who rules a unique kingdom, beyond the description of Vishnu, Brahma and the gods, has the deities carry out the five cosmic functions on His behalf. Yet this same sovereign enters the small hut called love. Vallalar's wonder lies in the contrast: the greatest power in existence comes to the humblest dwelling. Once He has entered, no one can turn Him away.

translit: maṉpatai vakukkum piramarnā raṇarkaḷ maṉṉurut tirarkaḷē mutalā oṉpatu kōṭit talaivarkaḷ āṅkāṅ kuṟuperun toḻilpala iyaṟṟi iṉpuṟac ciṟitē kaṭaikkaṇit taruḷi ilaṅkumōr iṟaivaṉiṉ ṟaṭiyēṉ aṉpeṉum kuṭicai nuḻaintaṉaṉ antō avaṉtaṉai maṟuppavar yārē.
translation: A shining Lord bestows grace with a mere side-glance, delighting the ninety million leaders, beginning with the Brahmas and Vishnus who form the living worlds and the enduring Rudras, as they perform their many great tasks in their respective places. Today, alas, he has entered this servant's hut called love. Who is there to refuse him?
commentary: God is so vast that even the great cosmic deities like Brahma and Vishnu receive only a passing glance of grace. Yet, Vallalar says, this same immense God has chosen to enter fully into the simple "hut" of a loving human heart, showing that love makes the infinite personal and accessible.

translit: taṉṉika rillāt talaivaeṉ ṟaraṟṟit taṉittaṉi maṟaikaḷā kamaṅkaḷ uṉṉiniṉ ṟōṭi uṇarntuṇarn tuṇarā orutaṉip perumpati uvantē puṉṉika rillāp pulaiyaṉēṉ piḻaikaḷ poṟuttaruṭ pūraṇa vaṭivāy eṉṉuḷam pukuntē niṟaintaṉaṉ antō entaiyait taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: The one, unique, great Master, whom the Vedas and Agamas separately seek, crying "O matchless leader!", contemplating, searching, and striving to realize, yet never fully realizing him, has willingly appeared as the form of perfect grace. He has forgiven the faults of this wretch, unequalled even by a blade of grass. Alas, he has entered and filled my heart! Who is there to stop my Father?
commentary: The ultimate reality, which even the most sacred scriptures like the Vedas (ancient sacred texts) and Agamas (texts on ritual) cannot fully describe, has come directly to a humble person. This encounter is a free gift of grace that forgives all faults and fills the heart completely.

translit: pālvakai āṇō peṇkolō irumaip pālatō pāluṟā atuvō ēlvakai oṉṟō iraṇṭatō aṉāti iyaṟkaiyō ātiyiṉ iyalpō mēlvakai yātō eṉamaṟai muṭikaḷ viḷampiṭa viḷaṅkumōr talaivaṉ mālvakai maṉattēṉ uḷakkuṭil pukuntāṉ vaḷḷalait taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: He is the one leader who shines, as the crests of the Vedas proclaim their search, asking: "Is it male, female, both, or without gender? Is it one or two? Is it beginningless nature or the nature of the Primal Being? What is its supreme state?" He has entered the heart-hut of me, one with a deluded mind. Who is there to stop the great Benefactor?
commentary: God is beyond all human categories and philosophical questions, such as whether the divine is male, female, one, or two. While the great scriptures (Upanishads) can only pose these questions, Vallalar says this undefinable reality has entered the heart of someone who admits their own confusion, showing that direct experience of God transcends intellectual understanding.

translit: varampeṟum āṉma uṇarcciyum cellā varupara uṇarcciyum māṭṭāp parampara uṇarcci tāṉumniṉ ṟaṟiyāp parāpara uṇarcciyum paṟṟā urampeṟa uṇarvār yāreṉap periyar uraittiṭa ōṅkumōr talaivaṉ karampeṟu kaṉipōl eṉṉuḷam pukuntāṉ kaṭavuḷait taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: He is the one exalted leader, of whom the great ones say: "He cannot be reached by the blessed experience of the soul, nor grasped by the experience of the transcendent. The experience of the beyond-transcendent cannot stand and know him, and the experience of the transcendent-immanent cannot hold him. Who, then, can realize him with certainty?" Like a fruit placed in my palm, he has entered my heart. Who is there to stop God?
commentary: Even the highest states of mystical awareness cannot grasp God. Yet, this same unreachable being can reveal himself with startling simplicity. The experience is a direct gift, as concrete and undeniable as being handed a fruit.

translit: paṭaittiṭal mutalain toḻilpurin tilaṅkum parampara oḷielām aṇuvil kiṭaittiṭak kīḻmēl naṭueṉak kāṭṭāk kiḷaroḷi yāyoḷik kellām aṭaittakā raṇamāyk kāraṇaṅ kaṭanta aruṭperuñ jōtiyām oruvaṉ kaṭaittaṉic ciṟiyēṉ uḷampukun tamarntāṉ kaṭavuḷait taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: The One who is the Vast Grace-Light, who performs the five functions beginning with creation, whose transcendent light is fully contained within an atom, a radiant light that reveals no top, bottom, or middle, who is the ultimate cause of all lights and yet transcends cause, has entered and settled in the heart of me, this final, solitary, small one. Who can stop this God?
commentary: The ArutPerunJothi, or Vast Grace-Light, is the formless power that runs the cosmos and is the source of all existence. Vallalar declares that this same infinite light, which contains everything, has come to reside personally in the heart of a single, small individual, revealing the paradox of God being both cosmic and intimate.

translit: aḷavelāṅ kaṭanta peruntalai aṇṭa aṭukkelām ammaōr aṇuviṉ piḷavilōr kōṭik kūṟṟiloṉ ṟākap pēcaniṉ ṟōṅkiya periyōṉ kaḷavelān tavirtteṉ karuttelām nirappik karuṇaiyā ramutaḷit tuḷamām vaḷavilē pukuntu vaḷarkiṉṟāṉ antō vaḷḷalait taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: The Great One, the supreme Head who transcends all measure, stands exalted, spoken of as making all the stacked universes fit within one part in ten million of a fissure in an atom. Oh! He has ended all my deceit, filled my every thought, given me the full nectar of compassion, entered the mansion of my heart, and is growing there. Alas, who can stop this Patron?
commentary: God's presence in the heart is an active, ongoing transformation. This being, so vast that all universes could fit in a crack within an atom, enters the "mansion" of the heart to purify it, fill every thought with grace, and then continues to grow there, making the divine an ever-expanding inner reality.

translit: uḷḷavām aṇṭa kōṭi kōṭikaḷil uḷavuyir muḻuvatum oruṅkē koḷḷaikoṇ ṭiṭiṉum aṇuttuṇai eṉiṉum kuṟaipaṭāp peruṅkoṭait talaivaṉ kaḷḷaneñ cakattēṉ piḻaielām poṟuttuk karuttelām iṉitutan taruḷit taḷḷarum tiṟatteṉ uḷḷakam pukuntāṉ tantaiyait taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: The great, generous Leader, whose bounty would not diminish by even the measure of an atom if all lives in tens of millions of universes plundered it at once, has forgiven all the faults of my deceitful heart, has graciously and sweetly granted all my heart's desires, and has entered my inner self with irresistible power. Who can stop this Father?
commentary: God's generosity has no limit. If every life in countless universes plundered it at once, it would not lessen by an atom. This boundless Giver forgave all the faults of Vallalar's deceitful heart, sweetly granted every wish of his heart, and entered him with a power that cannot be resisted. Who, he asks, can stop such a Father?

translit: aṟintaṉa aṟintāṅ kaṟintaṟin taṟiyā taiyakō aiyakō aṟiviṉ maṟintaṉa mayarntēm eṉamaṟai aṉantam vāykuḻain turaitturait turaiyum muṟintiṭa vāḷā iruntaeṉ ṟaṟiñar moḻiyumōr taṉipperun talaivaṉ ceṟinteṉa tuḷattil cērntaṉaṉ avaṉṟaṉ tiruvuḷam taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: The unique great Leader of whom the wise say that the infinite Vedas, stammering again and again, "We knew what we knew, and knowing and knowing we did not know; alas, alas, we are overturned in our knowing and bewildered," at last broke off their speech and fell silent: He has settled densely within my heart. Who can stop His sacred will?
commentary: The scriptures, endless as they are, finally confess defeat: they knew and knew, and in knowing more they came to not know, until their speech broke off and they fell silent. So say the wise. This Lord, beyond the reach of every scripture, has settled within Vallalar's heart. What the books could not reach has come to him by grace, and no one can stop God's will.

translit: karumutaṟ karuvāyk karuviṉuṭ karuvāyk karuelāṅ kāṭṭumōr karuvāyk kurumutaṟ kuruvāyk kuruelāṅ kiṭaitta koḷkaiyāyk koḷkaiyō ṭaḷavā arumutal aruvāy allavāy appāl aruṭperuñ jōtiyān talaivaṉ maruvieṉ uḷattil pukuntaṉaṉ avaṉtaṉ vaṇmaiyait taṭuppavar yārē.
translation: The Leader, who is the Vast Grace-Light, who is the origin of the first origin, the origin within the origin, the one origin that reveals all origins, the guru of the first guru, the principle by which all gurus are attained, who is immeasurable by any principle, the formless source of the formless, who is also the void, and who is beyond even that, has mingled with and entered my heart. Who can stop His generosity?
commentary: God, the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), is the ultimate source of everything, even the source of origin itself, and the principle behind all spiritual masters. Vallalar marvels that this incomprehensible Being has personally entered his heart. This act of grace is a generous, unstoppable force.

translit: vāṉirukkum piramarkaḷum nāraṇarum piṟarum mātavampaṉ ṉāṭpurintu maṇimāṭa naṭuvē tēṉirukkum malaraṇaimēl paḷikkaṟaiyi ṉūṭē tiruvaṭicērt taruḷkaeṉac ceppivarun tiṭavum nāṉirukkum kuṭicaiyilē valintunuḻain teṉakkē nallatiru aruḷamutam nalkiyataṉ ṟiyumeṉ ūṉirukkum kuṭicaiyilum uvantunuḻain taṭiyēṉ uḷḷameṉum ciṟukuṭicai yuḷḷumnuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: While Brahmas, Narayanas, and others in the heavens perform great penance for many days, pleading and pining from within a crystal chamber upon a honeyed flower-bed in a bejeweled hall, saying, "Grant us union with your sacred feet!", you willfully entered the hut where I live and gave me the blessed, divine ambrosia of grace. Beyond that, you gladly entered the hut of my flesh, and even entered into the little hut of your devotee’s heart.
commentary: This verse highlights a central theme: the shocking intimacy of grace. While the great gods of the heavens perform immense penance just to plead for God's attention, God has ignored them and come directly and willfully to Vallalar. The grace is progressively deeper, moving from his simple home to his physical body and finally into the core of his being, his heart.

translit: paṭiceypira maṉmutalōr paṟpalanāḷ varuntip paṉmaṇikaḷ oḷiviḷaṅkap patittaciṅkā taṉattē aṭiceyteḻun taruḷiemai āṇṭaruḷal vēṇṭum aracēeṉ ṟavaravarum āṅkāṅkē varunta vaṭiceymaṟai muṭinaṭuvē maṉṟakattē naṭikkum malaraṭikaḷ civappaoru vaḷamumilā acuttak kuṭicainuḻain taṉaiyēeṉ ṟēcuvarē aṉpar kūcāmal eṉṉuḷamām kuṭicainuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: While Brahma the creator and others suffer for many days, pining in their respective places and pleading, "O King, you must place your feet upon the lion-throne, inlaid with many shining gems, and rule over us!", your devotees will surely scold, saying, "You have entered an impure hut devoid of any merit, causing your flower-like feet, which dance in the Hall at the crown of the well-formed Vedas, to redden!" Yet, you entered the hut of my heart without any shame.
commentary: God ignores the pleas of celestial beings to occupy a grand throne, choosing instead to enter Vallalar's humble, "impure" existence. Vallalar imagines that other devotees would be shocked by this act, scolding God for lowering himself by entering such an unworthy place. This shows that divine grace operates beyond all human notions of status, purity, and propriety.

translit: uḷḷapaṭi uḷḷatuvāy ulakamelām pukiṉum oruciṟitum taṭaiyilatāy oḷiyatuvē mayamāy veḷḷaveḷi naṭuvuḷatāy iyaṟkaiyilē viḷaṅkum vētamuṭi ilakkiyamā mēṭaiyilē amarnta vaḷḷaṉmalar aṭicivappa vanteṉatu karuttiṉ vaṇṇamelām uvantaḷittu vayaṅkiyapē riṉpam koḷḷaikoḷak koṭuttatutāṉ pōtātō aracē koṭumpulaiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: You are the Benefactor, seated on the dais that is the ultimate aim of the Vedas' crown. It exists as it truly is, it enters all worlds without the slightest obstruction, it is the very essence of light, and it shines naturally in the midst of the vast expanse. You came, causing your flower-like feet to redden, gladly bestowed all that my mind could conceive, and gave me brilliant, great bliss to plunder in abundance. Is that not enough, O King? Yet you also joyfully entered the hut of me, a wretched, lowly one.
commentary: God is the ultimate truth, the light that fills all existence and the highest goal of scripture (Vedas). Having already bestowed incomprehensible bliss upon Vallalar, the poet asks with astonishment, "Is that not enough?" Yet God's grace goes even further, choosing to personally enter the life of one who sees himself as a "wretched, lowly one," demonstrating a generosity that exceeds all expectation.

translit: taṭaiyaṟiyāt takaiyiṉatāyt taṉṉikaril latuvāyt tattuvaṅkaḷ aṉaittiṉukkum tārakamāy avaikku viṭaiyaṟiyāt taṉimutalāy viḷaṅkuveḷi naṭuvē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cattiyamā mēṭaiyilē amarnta naṭaiyaṟiyāt tiruvaṭikaḷ civantiṭavan teṉatu nalivaṉaittun tavirttaruḷi ñāṉaamu taḷittāy koṭaiyitutāṉ pōtātō eṉṉaracē aṭiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kōṇātē kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: You are seated on the dais of Truth, which shines in the midst of the radiant Expanse. This dais is of a nature that knows no obstacle, it is without equal, it is the foundation for all tattvas, and it is the singular Origin, the answer to which they do not know. You came, causing your sacred feet which know no worldly gait to redden, you graced me by removing all my afflictions, and you gave me the ambrosia of gnanam. Is this generosity not enough, my King? Yet you also entered the hut of your devotee, straightforwardly and with delight.
commentary: God is described as the absolute foundation of reality, a singular origin beyond the grasp of all cosmic principles (tattvas). This ultimate Being has already removed all of Vallalar's afflictions and granted him gnanam (supreme knowledge). Posing the question again, "Is this generosity not enough?", Vallalar expresses his awe that God would then choose to personally and joyfully enter his humble existence.

translit: iṟaiyaḷavum turicilatāyt tūymaiyatāy niṟaivāy iyaṟkaiyatāy aṉupavaṅkaḷ evaikkummuta liṭamāy maṟaimuṭiyō ṭākamattiṉ maṇimuṭimēl muṭiyāy maṉṉukiṉṟa meyññāṉa maṇimēṭai amarnta niṟaiyaruṭcī raṭimalarkaḷ civantiṭavan taṭiyēṉ niṉaittaelām koṭuttaruḷi nilaipeṟaccey taṉaiyē kuṟaivilatip peruvarantāṉ pōtātō aracē koṭumpulaiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: You are seated on the bejeweled dais of true supreme knowledge, which is the very crown upon the jeweled crest of the Vedas and Agamas. It is without the slightest impurity, it is pure and complete, it is natural, and it is the primary ground for all experiences. You came, causing your glorious, graceful flower-feet to redden, you graced me by giving me everything I could imagine, and you made me attain a permanent state. Is this flawless, great boon not enough, O King? Yet you also joyfully entered the hut of me, a wretched, lowly one.
commentary: Seated at the very pinnacle of spiritual truth, beyond the highest scriptures (Vedas and Agamas), God has already given Vallalar everything he could possibly desire and secured him in a permanent state of grace. For the final time, Vallalar asks if this perfect gift is not enough, expressing his unending astonishment that God's love is a continuous, intimate presence that joyfully enters the life of one who feels completely unworthy.

translit: uruviṉatāy aruviṉatāy uruaruvāy uṇarvāy uḷḷatuvāy orutaṉmai uṭaiyaperum patiyāy maruviyavē tāntamutal vakuttiṭuṅka lānta varaiataṉmēl aruḷveḷiyil vayaṅkiyamē ṭaiyilē tiruvuṟavē amarntaruḷum tiruvaṭikaḷ peyarttē ciṟiyēṉkaṇ aṭaintaruḷit tiruvaṉaittum koṭuttāy kuruvēeṉ aracēī tamaiyātō aṭiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kōṇātē kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: As form, as formless, as both form and formless, as consciousness, as that which exists, as the great Lord of a singular nature, You are seated in splendor on a shining dais in the expanse of grace, beyond the very endpoint of all decreed philosophies like Vedānta. Lifting Your sacred feet, You came to me, this lowly one, and gave me all sacred wealth. O Guru! My King! Is this not enough? You have joyfully entered even this devotee's hut without hesitation.
commentary: God cannot be boxed in by any philosophical system, such as Vedānta. He is form and formless, being and consciousness, transcending all categories we might invent. When this boundless reality arrives as a personal Guru (spiritual teacher), the greatest gift is not the "sacred wealth" He brings, but His simple, direct presence in the devotee's life.

translit: maṇamuḷatāy oḷiyiṉatāy mantiraā taramāy vallatuvāy nallatuvāy mataṅkaṭanta varaippāy vaṇamuḷatāy vaḷamuḷatāy vayaṅkumōru veḷiyil maṇimēṭai amarntatiru aṭimalarkaḷ peyarttē eṇamuḷaeṉ pālaṭainteṉ eṇṇamelām aḷittāy iṅkitutāṉ pōtātō eṉṉaracē ñāṉak kuṇamalaiyē aruḷamutē kuruvēeṉ patiyē koṭumpulaiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: As fragrant, as luminous, as the foundation for mantras, as omnipotent, as benevolent, as the boundary beyond all religions, You are seated on a jeweled dais in a beautiful, abundant, and shining space. Lifting Your sacred lotus-feet, You came to me, who is full of intentions, and fulfilled all my thoughts. O my King, O mountain of wise virtue, O ambrosia of grace, O Guru, O my Lord, is this not enough? You have joyfully entered even the hut of this vile, base one.
commentary: The divine presence is beyond all religions, yet it is also the very foundation of sacred mantras (powerful spiritual sounds). While God grants every one of the devotee's wishes, Vallalar insists that the true miracle is more personal: the intimate arrival of the Lord into his own being, which he again calls a humble "hut."

translit: cirampeṟuvē tākamattiṉ aṭinaṭuvum muṭiyum cellāta nilaiatuvāy ellāmval latuvāy paramparamāyp paramparamēṟ paravucitam paramāyp pativeḷiyil viḷaṅkukiṉṟa maticivamē ṭaiyilē taraṅkulava amarntatiru vaṭikaḷpeyart teṉatu cārpaṭainteṉ eṇṇamelām tantaṉaieṉ aracē kuraṅkumaṉac ciṟiyēṉuk kiṅkitupō tātō koṭumpulaiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: As the state unreachable by the beginning, middle, or end of the revered Vedas and Agamas; as the all-powerful; as the supreme transcendental reality, and as the Chidambaram spreading over it; You are seated in excellence on the dais of wisdom-Siva shining in the Lord's own expanse. Lifting Your sacred feet, You came to my side and granted all I desired, my King. Is this not enough for me, a lowly one with a monkey mind? You have joyfully entered even the hut of this vile, base one.
commentary: The Supreme Being, called Siva, exists in a state that even the holy scriptures cannot fully describe. This is Chidambaram, the infinite space of consciousness. Vallalar marvels that this divine consciousness would choose to enter and quiet his "monkey mind," a classic term for a restless and distracted state, making the act of grace all the more personal.

translit: paṟṟiyapaṟ ṟaṉaittiṉaiyum paṟṟaṟaviṭ ṭaṟivām pāṉmaioṉṟē vaṭivākip paḻuttaperi yavarum uṟṟaṟitaṟkariyaoru peruveḷimēl veḷiyil ōṅkumaṇi mēṭaiamarn tōṅkiyacē vaṭikaḷ peṟṟaṟiyap peyarttuvanteṉ karuttaṉaittuṅ koṭuttē piṟavāmal iṟavāmal piṟaṅkavaittāyaracē koṟṟamuḷēṉ taṉakkitutāṉ pōtātō koṭiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kōṇātē kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: Your exalted feet are seated on a high jeweled dais in a space above a great space, a place difficult even for the great ones to reach and know, those who have completely renounced all attachments and matured into the very form of knowledge. Lifting those feet, You came so that I could receive and know them. You granted all my heart's desires and made me shine, free from birth and death, O King! Is this not enough for me, now victorious? You joyfully entered the hut of me, a cruel one, without hesitation.
commentary: The ultimate reality is a state that even the most accomplished sages, who have renounced everything, find difficult to reach. Yet, God comes directly to the devotee, granting the ultimate gift: freedom from the cycle of birth and death. But even this is surpassed by the final, most intimate act of grace, God's choice to reside within the devotee's imperfect self. This presence is what makes the devotee truly "victorious."

translit: karuviyoṭu karaṇamelām kaṭantukaṭan tataṉmēl kāṭciyelām kaṭantataṉmēl kāṇātu kaṭantu orunilaiyiṉ aṉupavamē uruvākip paḻutta uṇarcciyiṉum kāṇāmal ōṅkumoru veḷiyil maruviyatōr mēṭaiyilē vayaṅkiyacē vaṭikaḷ malarttivanteṉ karuttaṉaittum vaḻaṅkiṉaiiṉ puṟavē kurumaṇiyē eṉṉaracē eṉakkitupō tātō koṭumpulaiyēṉ kuṭicaiyilum kulavinuḻain taṉaiyē.
translation: Transcending and again transcending all instruments and inner faculties; beyond that, transcending all perceptions; and beyond that, passing unseen; You are in a soaring space, invisible even to the matured awareness that has become the very form of singular experience. Graciously extending Your radiant sacred feet from a dais there, You came and joyfully granted all my heart's desires. O gem of a Guru, my King, is this not enough for me? You have joyfully entered even the hut of this vile, base one.
commentary: God's existence is beyond all our tools of knowing: the senses, the inner mind (karaṇam), perception, and even the deepest, formless mystical states. From this unknowable state, God revealed Himself to Vallalar, joyfully granting all his desires. The overwhelming feeling is gratitude that this ultimate reality, a true gem of a Guru (spiritual teacher), would personally enter the "hut" of his flawed human existence.
