sections.title: A Sight the Eyes Cannot Contain

translit: aṭuttāṉai aṭiyēṉai añcēl eṉṟiṅ kāṇṭāṉaic ciṟuneṟikaḷ aṭaiyā teṉṉait taṭuttāṉaip peruneṟikkut taṭaitīrt tāṉait taṉṉaruḷum taṉporuḷum tāṉē eṉpāl koṭuttāṉaik kuṟṟamelām kuṇamāk koḷḷum kuṇattāṉaic camayamatak kuḻiniṉ ṟeṉṉai eṭuttāṉai ellāñcey valla cittē īntāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I remain in bliss, having seen the One who drew near to me, His slave, said, “Do not fear,” and ruled me here; who stopped me from taking lesser paths and cleared the obstacles on the great path; who Himself gave His grace and His own substance to me; who possesses the character to take all my faults as virtues; who lifted me from the pit of religions and creeds; and who bestowed the all-powerful Siddhi.
commentary: Vallalar finds his bliss in the direct experience of God, who he sees as a personal savior. God has guided him away from lesser spiritual paths, lifted him beyond the confines of organized religions, and accepted all his faults as if they were virtues. This divine being gave grace and Its very self, bestowing the ultimate Siddhi (power), which is this state of joyful union.

translit: virittāṉaik karuvielām viriya vētam vitittāṉai meynneṟiyai meyyē eṟkut terittāṉai naṭampotuvil ceykiṉ ṟāṉaic ciṟiyēṉuk karuḷoḷiyāl ciṟanta paṭṭam tarittāṉait tāṉēnā ṉāki eṉṟum taḻaittāṉai eṉaittaṭutta taṭaikaḷ ellām erittāṉai eṉuyiruk kiṉpā ṉāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I remain in bliss, having seen my Lord: the One who expanded all the instruments of being and ordained the Vedas; who truly revealed the true path to me; who performs the dance in the Common Space; who, by His light of grace, conferred a glorious title upon me, the lowly one; who flourishes forever, having Himself become me; who burned away all the obstacles that blocked me; and who became the sweetness of my very life.
commentary: God is both the cosmic creator who established the scriptures and the intimate reality who performs the divine dance in the Common Space. Vallalar rejoices in this Lord who personally revealed the true path to him, burned away all his inner obstacles, and conferred a spiritual title upon him. The ultimate miracle is that God has become one with him, flourishing as his very self and filling his life with sweetness.

translit: naṭṭāṉai naṭṭaeṉai nayantu koṇṭē nammakaṉnī añcaleṉa naviṉṟeṉ ceṉṉi toṭṭāṉai eṭṭiraṇṭum colli ṉāṉait tuṉpamelām tolaittāṉaic cōrntu tūṅka oṭṭāṉai meyaṟivē uruvāy eṉṉuḷ uṟṟāṉai uṇarntārkkum uṇarntu koḷḷa eṭṭāṉai eṉṉaḷavil eṭṭi ṉāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I remain in bliss, having seen my Lord: the One who befriended me and, desiring me who sought His friendship, touched my head, saying, “You are our son, do not fear”; who taught me the “eight and two”; who destroyed all my sorrows and does not let me falter or sleep; who entered within me, taking the very form of true knowledge; and who, though beyond the grasp of even those who have realized, came within my own reach.
commentary: God is experienced here as an intimate friend and master. He gives personal comfort, touches the seeker's head, and whispers a secret teaching, the "eight and two." This divine friend destroys all sorrow and awakens the soul, making Himself accessible even though He is beyond the reach of ordinary understanding.

translit: cōṟṟāṉaiccōṟṟiluṟum cukatti ṉāṉait tuḷakkamilāp pārāṉai nīrā ṉāṉaik kāṟṟāṉai veḷiyāṉaik kaṉalā ṉāṉaik karuṇaineṭuṅ kaṭalāṉaik kaḷaṅkar kāṇat tōṟṟāṉai nāṉkāṇat tōṟṟi ṉāṉaic collaṟiyēṉ colliyapuṉ collai yellām ēṟṟāṉai eṉṉuḷattil eyti ṉāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I remain in bliss, having seen my Lord: the One who is the food and the pleasure that comes from food; who is the unshakable earth, the water, the wind, the space, and the fire; who is a vast ocean of compassion; who does not appear for the flawed to see, but appeared for me to see; who accepted all the base words I spoke, I who am ignorant of speech; and who has arrived within my heart.
commentary: The divine is present in the most basic realities of life. He is the food we eat, the pleasure of eating, and the very elements of earth, water, fire, wind, and space. While those with flawed perception cannot see Him, He reveals Himself directly to the devoted heart, accepting even clumsy, imperfect words of praise.

translit: cērttāṉai eṉṟaṉaittaṉ aṉpa rōṭu ceṟiyāta maṉañceṟiyac cempoṟ ṟāḷil ārttāṉai ampalattil āṭā niṉṟa āṉanta naṭattāṉai aruṭkaṇ nōkkam pārttāṉaip pārāraip pārā tāṉaip pārppaṟavē pārttirukkap paṇṇi eṉṉai īrttāṉai aintoḻilnī iyaṟṟeṉ ṟāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I remain in bliss, having seen my Lord: the One who joined me with His devotees; who bound my wandering mind to His fine golden feet; who is of the blissful dance performed in the Ambalam; who looked upon me with His gaze of grace; who does not regard those who do not regard Him; who drew me to Himself, making me see without the act of seeing; and who said, “You shall perform the five functions.”
commentary: The path of grace first connects you to a community of fellow devotees and stills the restless mind at God's feet. The divine gaze then draws you into a state of pure awareness, a "seeing without seeing." In the culmination of this union, God entrusts the seeker with His own cosmic work: the five great functions of creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, and grace.

translit: muḷaiyāṉaic cuttaciva veḷiyil tāṉē muḷaittāṉai mūvāta mutalā ṉāṉaik kaḷaiyāṉaik kaḷaṅkamelām kaḷaivit teṉṉaik kāttāṉai eṉpiḻaiyaik karutik kōpam viḷaiyāṉaic civapōkam viḷaivit tāṉai vēṇṭāmai vēṇṭalivai mēvi eṉṟum iḷaiyāṉai mūttāṉai mūppi lāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I see my Lord and remain in bliss: the one who is the sprout, who sprouted by Himself in the expanse of pure Civa-ness; the unaging origin; the one who weeded out all my flaws and protected me; the one who does not grow angry considering my errors; the one who cultivates the bliss of Civa; the one who, embodying both desire and desirelessness, is ever young, the eldest, and without old age.
commentary: God is the source of all, a self-generating life that sprouts in the pure space of consciousness (Civa). This timeless being is beyond all contradictions: both the youngest and the eldest, embodying desire and its absence. He is a loving protector who weeds out the soul's flaws and, instead of growing angry at mistakes, cultivates the ultimate bliss of divine union.

translit: puyalāṉai maḻaiyāṉai atirppi ṉāṉaip pōṟṟiyamiṉ oḷiyāṉaip puṉita ñāṉac ceyalāṉaic ceyalellān tikaḻvit tāṉait tirucciṟṟam palattāṉait teḷiyār uḷḷē ayalāṉai uṟavāṉai aṉpu ḷāṉai aṟintārai aṟintāṉai aṟivāl aṉṟi iyalāṉai eḻilāṉaip poḻilā ṉāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I see my Lord and remain in bliss: the one who is the storm cloud, the rain, the thunder, and the lauded light of lightning; the one who is the act of sacred wisdom, who makes all actions manifest; the one of the sacred small-expanse; a stranger in the hearts of the unenlightened, yet a kinsman and full of love for the devout; the one who knows those who know Him; the one who cannot be attained except through true knowledge; the one who is beauty itself, who is a flourishing grove.
commentary: God is revealed in the power of nature and is the hidden force that makes all actions possible. To those who are spiritually unaware, God feels like a stranger, but to those who are devoted, God is the closest of kin. He knows those who know Him, and He is reached by nothing other than true knowledge (arivu).

translit: tāyāṉait tantaieṉak kāyi ṉāṉaic caṟkuruvu māṉāṉait tamiyēṉ uḷḷē mēyāṉaik kaṇkāṇa viḷaṅki ṉāṉai meymmaieṉak kaḷittāṉai vētañ coṉṉa vāyāṉai vañcamilā maṉatti ṉāṉai varaṅkoṭukka vallāṉai maṇimaṉ ṟaṉṟi ēyāṉait turiyanaṭu virukkiṉ ṟāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I see my Lord and remain in bliss: the one who became my mother, my father, and my true guru; the one who dwells within me, the solitary one; the one who shines so my eyes can see; the one who bestowed Truth upon me; the mouth that spoke the Vedas; the one with a mind free of deceit; the one powerful enough to grant boons; the one who abides nowhere but the Hall of Gems; the one who dwells at the center of the Turiya state.
commentary: For the devotee, God takes on the most intimate roles: mother, father, and true teacher (sarguru). He abides nowhere but in the Hall of Gems, the Manimanram, and dwells at the center of Turiya, the high state of consciousness found within.

translit: taḻaittāṉait taṉṉaioppār illā tāṉait tāṉētā ṉāṉāṉait tamiya ṉēṉaik kuḻaittāṉai eṉkaiyilōr koṭaitan tāṉaik kuṟaikoṇṭu niṉṟēṉaik kuṟittu nōkki aḻaittāṉai aruḷamutam aḷikkiṉ ṟāṉai accamelām tavirttāṉai aṉpē eṉpāl iḻaittāṉai eṉṉitayat tirukkiṉ ṟāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I see my Lord and remain in bliss: the one who flourishes, who has no equal, who is self-created; the one who softened me, the solitary one; the one who placed a gift in my hand; the one who, seeing me standing with my shortcomings, singled me out and called to me; the one who gives the ambrosia of grace; the one who dispelled all my fears; the one who wove love itself into my being; the one who is in my heart.
commentary: Divine grace is a deeply personal and tender act. God actively seeks out the lonely and imperfect soul, softens the heart, dispels fear, and fills the devotee with love, demonstrating that our shortcomings do not bar grace.

translit: uṭaiyāṉai aruṭjōti uruvi ṉāṉai ōvāṉai mūvāṉai ulavā iṉpak koṭaiyāṉai eṉkuṟaitīrt teṉṉai āṇṭu koṇṭāṉaik kollāmai kuṟitti ṭārai aṭaiyāṉait tiruciṟṟam palatti ṉāṉai aṭiyēṉuk karuḷamutam aḷikka vēpiṉ iṭaiyāṉai eṉṉācai ellān tanta emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I see my Lord and remain in bliss: the ultimate sovereign, in the form of Grace-Light; the one who never ceases and never ages, a gift of inexhaustible bliss; the one who ended my shortcomings and took me as His own; the one who does not go near those who disregard the principle of non-killing; the one of the sacred small-expanse; the one who became the means to give this devotee the ambrosia of grace; the one who granted all my desires.
commentary: God is the form of Grace-Light (ArutJothi) and the source of endless bliss, but there is a condition for receiving it. The Lord does not go near those who disregard the practice of non-killing (kollāmai), making compassion for all life a necessary prerequisite for divine union.
NOTES
Note 270

tamil: சோறு - முத்தி. முதற்பதிப்பு. ஈண்டு சோறு என்பது உண்ணும் சோறே.
translit: cōṟu - mutti. mutaṟpatippu. īṇṭu cōṟu eṉpatu uṇṇum cōṟē.
translation: cōṟu — mutti, reading of the first edition. Here cōṟu means the cōṟu that is eaten.

translit: aṟintāṉai aṟivaṟivuk kaṟivā ṉāṉai aruṭperuñcō tiyiṉāṉai aṭiyēṉ aṉpil ceṟintāṉai ellāñcey valla cittāyc ciṟantāṉaic ciṟuneṟiyil ceṉṟār tammaip piṟintāṉai eṉṉuḷattil kalantu koṇṭa piriyamuḷa perumāṉaip piṟavi taṉṉai eṟintāṉai eṉaieṟiyā teṭuttāṇ ṭāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I am filled with joy, having seen my Lord: He who knows all, who is the knowledge within the consciousness of knowledge, who is the Great Vast Grace-Light, who is densely present in this devotee's love, who is supreme as the Siddha capable of doing everything, who separates Himself from those who follow petty paths, the beloved Great Lord who has mingled with my heart, who has cast away birth itself, and who, without casting me away, took me up and made me His own.
commentary: God is both the ultimate reality, the consciousness behind all knowing, and a personal presence found within the devotee's love. This divine being, the Great Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), actively separates from those following narrow, selfish paths and mingles with the heart of the sincere seeker. The ultimate gift of this union is liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

translit: pālāṉait tēṉāṉaip paḻatti ṉāṉaip palaṉuṟuceṅ karumpāṉaip pāyntu vēkāk kālāṉaik kalaicākāt talaiyi ṉāṉaik kāleṉṟum talaiyeṉṟum karutaṟ keytā mēlāṉai mēlnilaimēl amutā ṉāṉai mēṉmēlum eṉatuḷattē viḷaṅkal aṉṟi ēlāṉai eṉpāṭal ēṟṟuk koṇṭa emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I am filled with joy, having seen my Lord: He who is milk, who is honey, who is fruit, who is the sweet red sugarcane, who is the unburning vital air and the head where wisdom never dies, who is supreme beyond being conceived as 'foot' or 'head', who is the ambrosia in the highest state, who is incapable of anything other than shining ever brighter in my heart, and who accepted my song.
commentary: God is the essence of all that is sweet and nourishing: milk, honey, fruit, and sugarcane. While he can be described with yogic terms like the vital air (kāl) or the seat of wisdom (talai), he transcends any such concepts. His nature is to be an ever-present, ever-brightening light within the heart.

translit: uḷḷāṉaik katavutiṟan tuḷḷē kāṇa uḷaveṉakkē uraittāṉai uṇarār pāṭṭaik koḷḷāṉai eṉpāṭṭaik kuṟikkoṇ ṭāṉaik kollāmai viratameṉak koṇṭār tammait taḷḷāṉaik kolaipulaiyait taḷḷā tārait taḻuvāṉai yāṉpurinta tavaṟu nōkki eḷḷāṉai iṭartavirt tiṅkeṉṉai āṇṭa emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I am filled with joy, having seen my Lord: He who is within; who told me alone that He is there to be seen inside, once the door is opened; who does not accept the songs of those who lack true understanding, but took my song as His aim; who does not push away those who have taken the vow of not killing, but does not embrace those who fail to reject killing and meat-eating; who does not look at the wrongs I have done and scorn me, and who removed my afflictions and rules me here.
commentary: The path to God is inward; a door must be opened within the self to see the one who resides there. This verse states plainly who is accepted and who is rejected. God embraces those who take the vow of non-killing (kollāmai) and shuns those who kill and eat meat. This principle is a fundamental condition for a relationship with the divine.

translit: uṟavāṉai eṉṉuyirkkuḷ uyirā ṉāṉai uṟupiḻaikaḷ ceyiṉumavai uṉṉi eṉṉai maṟavāṉai aṟavāḻi vaḻaṅki ṉāṉai vañcakarkkut tirukkōyil vaḻikka pāṭan tiṟavāṉai eṉṉaḷavil tiṟantu kāṭṭic ciṟcapaiyum poṟcapaiyum cērvit tāṉai iṟavāṉaip piṟavāṉai iyaṟkai yāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I am filled with joy, having seen my Lord: He who is my true relation, who is the life within my life, who, even if I commit grave wrongs, does not dwell on them and forget me, who granted me the ocean of righteousness, who does not open the temple door to the deceitful, but who, for me, opened and revealed, and made me join the Hall of Consciousness and the Golden Hall, He who neither dies nor is born, who is existence itself.
commentary: The divine is our truest relation, the very life within our life, and is so merciful that even grave mistakes are forgiven. Vallalar makes it clear that access to the holiest inner spaces, the Hall of Consciousness (Chit Sabhai) and the Golden Hall (Por Sabhai), is not for the deceitful. It is granted only to the sincere seeker, for whom God opens the way personally.

translit: akattāṉaip puṟattāṉai aṇuvā ṉāṉai aṇuviṉukkuḷ aṇuvāṉai ataṉuḷ ḷāṉai makattāṉai makattiṉumōr makattā ṉāṉai māmakattāy iruntāṉai vayaṅkā niṉṟa cakattāṉai aṇṭamelām tāṉā ṉāṉait taṉiaruḷām peruṅkaruṇait tāyā ṉāṉai ikattāṉaip parattāṉaip potuvil āṭum emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: I am filled with joy, having seen my Lord: He who is within, who is without, who is the atom, who is the atom within the atom, and who is inside that; who is vast, who is vaster than the vast, who exists as supremely vast; who is this radiant world, who became all the universes, who is the mother of great compassion, which is peerless grace, who is of this world and the world beyond, and who dances in the Universal Hall.
commentary: God's presence is total, existing at every scale of reality from the sub-atomic to the cosmic. He is inside us, outside us, and is the very substance of the universe itself. Despite this unimaginable vastness, Vallalar experiences this ultimate reality as something intimate and personal: the boundless compassion of a mother, dancing for all in the Universal Hall (Podhu).

translit: ceyyāṉaik kariyāṉaip pacumai yāṉait tikaḻntiṭupoṉ maiyiṉāṉai veṇmai yāṉai meyyāṉaip poyyāṉai meypoy illā veḷiyāṉai oḷiyāṉai viḷampu vārkkuk kaiyāṉai eṉṉaiyeṭut taṇaittuk koṇṭa kaiyāṉai eṉṉaieṉṟum kaiyā tāṉai eyyāṉai evvulakum ētta eṉṉai īṉṟāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: The one who is red, black, and green, the one who is radiant gold and white; the one who is truth and untruth, the one who is the space devoid of truth and untruth; the one who is light, a helping hand to those who speak of him; the one whose hands lifted and embraced me, the one who never abandons me; the unwearying one praised by all worlds, the one who gave birth to me, I have seen him and remain in bliss.
commentary: God encompasses all opposites, transcending categories like color, truth, and falsehood. After describing this abstract, all-containing nature, Vallalar shifts to a moment of deep intimacy. This incomprehensible being is also the one who physically lifted and embraced him, a tangible, parental love that never abandons him.

translit: maruntāṉai maṇiyāṉai vaḻuttā niṉṟa mantiraṅka ḷāṉāṉai vāṉa nāṭṭu viruntāṉai uṟavāṉai naṇpi ṉāṉai mēlāṉaik kīḻāṉai mēlkīḻ eṉṉap poruntāṉai eṉṉuyiril porunti ṉāṉaip poṉṉāṉaip poruḷāṉaip potuvāy eṅkum iruntāṉai iruppāṉai irukkiṉ ṟāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: The one who is the medicine and the gem; the one who has become the very mantras that are praised; the one who is a feast for the celestial realm, who is kin and friend; the one who is above and below, yet does not fit into such categories; the one who has merged with my very life; the one who is gold and substance; the one who was, is, and will be present everywhere as the common reality, I have seen my Lord and remain in bliss.
commentary: God is the solution to suffering (the medicine), the ultimate value (the gem), and the very power within sacred chants (mantras). He is simultaneously the highest reality beyond all conception and the most intimate relation: a friend who has merged with Vallalar's own life, present in every moment of past, present, and future.

translit: āṉṟāṉai aṟivāṉai aḻivi lāṉai aruṭperuñjō tiyiṉāṉai alarnta jōti mūṉṟāṉai iraṇṭāṉai oṉṟāṉāṉai muṉṉāṉaip piṉṉāṉai mūṭa neñcil tōṉṟāṉait tūyaruḷē tōṉṟi ṉāṉaic cuttaciva caṉmārkkan tulaṅka eṉṉai īṉṟāṉai ellāmāy allā tāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: The perfected one, the one who is knowledge, the indestructible one; the one who is the Vast Grace-Light; the one who, as the blossomed Jothi, is three, two, and one; the one who is before and after; the one who does not appear in the hearts of the foolish, but who appears as pure grace; the one who gave birth to me to make the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam flourish; the one who is everything and also not-everything, I have seen my Lord and remain in bliss.
commentary: The ultimate reality is ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light. This divine Jothi (light) can appear as many things but is finally one. It cannot be perceived by the foolish or unprepared, revealing itself only as pure grace to the sincere. Vallalar sees his own life's purpose as a divine commission: to make the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, the universal path of truth and compassion, known to the world.

translit: tōyntāṉai eṉṉuḷattē eṉpāl aṉpāl cūḻntāṉai yāṉtoṭutta coṟpū mālai vēyntāṉai eṉṉuṭaiya viṉaitīrt tāṉai vētānta muṭimuṭimēl viḷaṅki ṉāṉai vāyntāṉai eyppiṭattē vaippā ṉāṉai maṇimaṉṟil naṭippāṉai varaṅkaḷ ellām īyntāṉaiāyntavartam itayat tāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: The one who has mingled within my heart; the one who, out of love, has surrounded me; the one who wore the flower-garland of words I fashioned; the one who resolved my karma; the one who shines on the very crown of Vedanta's conclusion; the one who is my treasure in times of weariness; the one who dances in the Hall of Gems; the one who grants all boons; the one who dwells in the hearts of those who have deeply inquired, I have seen my Lord and remain in bliss.
commentary: The divine is an intimate beloved who responds to acts of devotion. Vallalar describes God wearing the "flower-garland of his words," a beautiful image of the divine treasuring his poetic offerings. This relationship is deeply practical, resolving karma (the consequences of past actions) and providing comfort, while also being the ultimate truth shining beyond even the highest philosophy of Vedanta.

translit: naṉṟāṉai maṉṟakattē naṭikkiṉ ṟāṉai nāṭāmai nāṭalivai naṭuvē ōṅki niṉṟāṉaip poṉṟāta nilaiyi ṉāṉai nilaiaṟintu nillātār neñci lēcam oṉṟāṉai evvuyirkkum oṉṟā ṉāṉai oruciṟiyēṉ taṉainōkki uḷamnī añcēl eṉṟāṉai eṉṟumuḷa iyaṟkai yāṉai emmāṉaik kaṇṭukaḷit tirukkiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: The one who is goodness, dancing within the Hall; the one who stands towering between seeking and not-seeking; the one of the undying state; the one who does not unite even by a trace with the hearts of those who know the true state yet do not abide in it, yet who is one with all lives; the one who looked upon me, a simple person, and said, "Heart, do not fear"; the one who is eternal nature itself, I have seen my Lord and remain in bliss.
commentary: God is one with every life, yet He does not unite even by a trace with the hearts of those who know the true state and still do not abide in it. To Vallalar, who received grace, He came close and said directly, "Do not fear in your heart."
NOTES
Note 268

tamil: ஈந்தானை - முதற் பதிப்பு, பொ. சு., பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: īntāṉai - mutaṟ patippu, po. cu., pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: īntāṉai — reading of the first edition and of the Po. Su., P. Irā. and S. Mu. Ka. editions.

sections.title: Declaring: I Saw, I Ripened, I Merged

translit: aruḷaracai aruṭkuruvai aruṭperuñ cōtiyaieṉ ammaiyaieṉ appaṉaieṉ āṇṭavaṉai amutait teruḷuṟumeṉ uyiraieṉṟaṉ uyirkkuyirai ellām ceyyavalla taṉittalaimaic cittacikā maṇiyai maruvuperu vāḻvaiellā vāḻvumeṉak kaḷitta vāḻmutalai maruntiṉaimā maṇiyaieṉkaṇ maṇiyaik karuṇainaṭam purikiṉṟa kaṉakacapā patiyaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: The King of grace, the Guru of grace, the Vast Grace-Light, my Mother, my Father, my Master, the ambrosia, my soul that has gained clarity, the life of my life, the singular, sovereign Crest-Jewel of Siddhas who can do all things, the great life one attains, the Source of life who gave me all lives, the Medicine, the great Gem, the apple of my eye, the Kanakasabhapati (Lord of the Golden Hall) who performs the dance of compassion, with joy, I have seen, I have ripened, and I have merged.
commentary: This verse announces the three core stages of spiritual union: seeing, ripening, and merging. First comes the vision ("I have seen"), an encounter with the divine in all its forms: as parent, teacher (Guru), master, and as the ultimate reality of ArutPerunJothi. This vision leads to a deep inner transformation, a softening or ripening ("I have ripened"). The final step is the joyful dissolution of the self into the divine ("I have merged"), becoming one with the source of all life.

translit: tiruttakuvē tāntamoṭu cittānta mutalāt tikaḻkiṉṟa antamelām tēṭiyuṅkaṇ ṭaṟiyā oruttaṉaiuḷ ḷoḷiyaioḷir uḷḷoḷikkuḷ oḷiyai uḷḷapaṭi uḷḷavaṉai uṭaiyaperun takaiyai niruttaṉaimeyp poruḷāṉa niṉmalaṉaic civaṉai nittiyaṉaic cattiyaṉai niṟkuṇaṉai eṉatu karuttaṉaicciṟ capaiyōṅku kaṭavuḷaieṉ kaṇṇāl kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: The One who cannot be found or known even when sought through all the final conclusions, beginning with the worthy Vedanta and Siddhanta; the inner light, the light within that shining inner light; the great Being who exists just as he is, the Possessor of all; the Dancer, the immaculate one who is the true substance, Sivam, the eternal one, the true one, the one without attributes; my Lord, the God preeminent in the hall of consciousness, with my own eyes, with joy, I have seen, I have ripened, and I have merged.
commentary: The God that Vallalar experienced cannot be captured by any scripture or philosophy. He states that even the highest traditional paths, Vedanta (philosophy based on the Vedas) and Siddhanta (the philosophy of Saivism), cannot grasp this reality. God is a living light within our own consciousness, an unblemished, eternal substance (Sivam) that must be experienced directly.

translit: pāṭṭuvantu paricaḷitta patiyaiaruṭ patiyaip pacupatiyaik kaṉakacapā patiyaiumā patiyait tēṭṭamikum perumpatiyaic civapatiyai ellām ceyyavalla taṉippatiyait tikaḻteyvap patiyai āṭṭiyalcey taruḷparama patiyainava patiyai āṉanta nāṭṭiṉukkōr atipatiyai ācai kāṭṭieṉai maṇampurinteṉ kaipiṭitta patiyaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: The Lord who delighted in my song and gave me a reward, the Lord of grace, Pasupati (Lord of all souls), Kanakasabhapati, Umapati (Lord of Uma), the great Lord who is the ultimate quest, the Lord Sivam, the unique Lord who can do all things, the radiant, divine Lord, the supreme Lord who graciously performs his dance, the new Lord, the sovereign of the land of bliss, the Lord who awakened desire in me, married me, and took my hand, with joy, I have seen, I have ripened, and I have merged.
commentary: This verse describes the divine union using the intimate language of a mystical marriage. God is the supreme Lord (Pati) who awakens spiritual desire in the soul, seeks it out, and lovingly takes its hand. This tradition, known as bridal mysticism, frames the relationship with God as a deeply personal and loving bond between the soul and its divine beloved.

translit: matittiṭutal ariyaoru māṇikka maṇiyai vayaṅkiyapē roḷiyuṭaiya vacciramā maṇiyait tutittiṭuvē tākamattiṉ muṭimuṭitta maṇiyaic cuyañcōtit tirumaṇiyaic cuttaciva maṇiyai vitittalmutal toḻiliyaṟṟu vittakuru maṇiyai viṇmaṇiyai ammaṇikkuḷ viḷaṅkiyameym maṇiyaik katittacuka mayamaṇiyaic cittacikā maṇiyaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: A ruby gem, impossible to value; a great diamond gem of brilliant, vast light; the gem that crowns the summit of the praised Vedas and Agamas; the sacred gem of self-existent light; the pure gem of Sivam; the guru-gem who causes the cosmic functions, beginning with creation, to be performed; the gem of the heavens; the true gem shining within that gem; the gem that is the embodiment of emergent bliss; the Crest-Jewel of Siddhas, with joy, I have seen, I have ripened, and I have merged.
commentary: God is portrayed here as the ultimate, priceless gem from which all value and light originate. This divine jewel is more precious than any ruby or diamond, and it is the crowning truth of all sacred texts, like the Vedas (ancient holy books) and Agamas (traditional scriptures). More than just a static object of beauty, this gem is also the "guru-gem" that intelligently directs the entire cosmos, the source of all universal law and order.

translit: māṟṟaiaḷan taṟintilameṉ ṟarumaṟaiā kamaṅkaḷ vaḻuttamaṇi maṉṟōṅki vayaṅkumaruṭ poṉṉai āṟṟalmiku perumpoṉṉai aintoḻilum puriyum arumpoṉṉai eṉtaṉṉai āṇṭaceḻum poṉṉait tēṟṟamiku pacumpoṉṉaic cempoṉṉai ñāṉa citamparattē viḷaṅkivaḷar civamayamām poṉṉaik kāṟṟaṉalā kāyamelām kalantavaṇṇap poṉṉaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: The Gold of Grace, praised by the rare Vedas and Agamas which declare, "We could not measure its fineness," that shines preeminent in the jeweled hall; the great Gold of immense power; the rare Gold that performs the five cosmic functions; the fine Gold that took me as its own; the pure Gold of great clarity; the refined, red Gold; the Gold that is the embodiment of Sivam, shining and growing in the Chidambaram of wisdom; the Gold whose nature is to be mingled in wind, fire, ether, and all else, with joy, I have seen, I have ripened, and I have merged.
commentary: The divine is like pure, immeasurable gold. Vallalar notes that even the sacred scriptures admit they cannot fully grasp its value. This "Gold of Grace" is both the supreme power running the cosmos and the intimate reality that claims the soul personally. It is mingled with the very elements of existence: wind, fire, and space.

translit: āytaruvē tākamattiṉ aṭimuṭiniṉ ṟilaṅkum ariyaperum poruḷaiavaik kaṉupavamām poruḷai vēytarutat tuvapporuḷait tattuvaṅkaḷ viḷaṅka viḷaṅkukiṉṟa paramporuḷait tattuvaṅkaḷ aṉaittum tōytaralil lātataṉic cuyañcōtip poruḷaic cuttaciva mayamāṉa cukātītap poruḷaik kāytaralil lāteṉṉaik kāttaaruṭ poruḷaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: The rare, great Substance that stands as the root and crown of the researched Vedas and Agamas; the Substance that is their direct experience; the Substance of the Tattvas that pervades all; the Supreme Substance that illuminates, making the Tattvas themselves luminous; the unique, self-luminous Jothi Substance, untouched by any of the Tattvas; the Substance of blissful transcendence that is pure Sivam; the Substance of Grace that protected me without harshness, I saw it, I ripened into it, I merged with it, rejoicing.
commentary: The ultimate reality is the fundamental "Substance" from which everything arises. It is the source of the scriptures and also the direct experience they point toward. Vallalar presents a paradox: this substance forms all the Tattvas (the constituent principles of the universe), yet it remains utterly untouched by them. It is a self-luminous Jothi (light) that is both the fabric of existence and completely beyond it.

translit: tiruttamiku muṉivarkaḷum tēvarkaḷum aḻiyāc cittarkaḷum ciruṭṭiceyum tiṟattarkaḷum kākkum aruttamiku talaivarkaḷum aṭakkiṭalval lavarum alaipurikiṉ ṟavarkaḷumuḷ aṉukkirakip pavarum poruttumaṟṟaic cattikaḷum cattarkaḷum ellām poruḷetuvō eṉattēṭip pōkaavar avartam karuttiloḷit tirukkiṉṟa kaḷvaṉaieṉ kaṇṇāl kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: Sages of great purity, Devas, immortal Siddhas, those with the power to create, the great leaders who sustain, those skilled in dissolution, those who cause delusion, and those who bestow grace from within, along with all the other corresponding Saktis and Saktars (possessors of power), when they all go searching for the true Substance, he hides in each of their minds. I saw that Thief with my own eyes, I ripened into him, I merged with him, rejoicing.
commentary: Even the most powerful beings, from celestial Devas to perfected Siddhas, are searching for the ultimate reality. Vallalar playfully calls God a "Thief" who hides from them, right inside their own minds. This suggests that the divine cannot be grasped through power, status, or external questing. It is found only through an inward turn, by seeing the one who was hiding in plain sight within your own consciousness.

translit: kōṇāta nilaiyiṉarāyk kuṟikuṇaṅkaṇ ṭiṭavum kūṭāta vaṇṇammalaik kukaimutalām iṭattil ūṇāti viṭuttuyirppai aṭakkimaṉam aṭakki uṟupoṟikaḷ aṭakkivarum ukaṅkaḷpala kōṭit tūṇāka acaitaliṉṟit tūṅkātu viḻitta tūyacatā niṭṭarkaḷum turiyanilai iṭattum kāṇāta vakaioḷitta kaḷvaṉaieṉ kaṇṇāl kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: In places like mountain caves, the pure ones in constant meditative absorption remain unmoving like pillars for many billions of Yugas. Forsaking food, controlling their breath, mind, and senses, they stay awake without sleeping. Even for them, in the state of Turiya, he hides in a way they cannot see him. I saw that Thief with my own eyes, I ripened into him, I merged with him, rejoicing.
commentary: This verse makes a powerful point about the limits of spiritual technique. Even yogis who perform extreme austerities for billions of ages (Yugas), perfectly controlling mind and body to reach the highest state of consciousness (Turiya), cannot force God to appear. The divine "Thief" remains hidden even from them. The final vision, Vallalar suggests, is a gift of grace received with joy.

translit: nīṭṭāya cittānta nilaiyiṉiṭat tamarntum nikaḻkiṉṟa vētānta neṟiyiṉiṭat tiruntum āṭṭāya pōtāntam alaivaṟunā tāntam ātimaṟṟai antaṅkaḷ aṉaittiṉumuṟ ṟaṟintum vēṭṭācaip paṟṟaṉaittum viṭṭulakam pōṟṟa vittakarāy viḷaṅkukiṉṟa muttarkaṭkum taṉṉaik kāṭṭāmal oḷittirukkuṅ kaḷvaṉaieṉ kaṇṇāl kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: Even to those established in the extensive state of Siddhanta or on the path of Vedanta; even to those who have reached and known Bodhantam, the unwavering Nadhantam, and all other such ultimate states; even to the Muktas who shine as sages praised by the world, having abandoned all clinging desires, he hides without revealing himself. I saw that Thief with my own eyes, I ripened into him, I merged with him, rejoicing.
commentary: Even the most advanced spiritual practitioners, who have mastered entire schools of philosophy like Siddhanta and Vedanta and attained liberation, still cannot see God by their own merit. By calling God a "Thief" who hides even from these liberated sages, Vallalar emphasizes that this ultimate vision is a deeply personal revelation that transcends all known categories of attainment.

translit: maruḷneṟicēr mala:uṭampai aḻiyāta vimala vaṭivākki ellāñcey vallacittām poruḷait taruṇamatu terinteṉakkut tāṉēvan taḷitta tayānitiyai eṉaiīṉṟa tantaiyaieṉ tāyaip poruḷniṟaiciṟ ṟampalattē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa patiyaip pukalaritām cuttaciva pūraṇameyc cukattaik karuṇaiaruṭ peruñcōtik kaṭavuḷaieṉ kaṇṇāl kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kaṉintukoṇṭēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ kaḷittē.
translation: The Substance that is the all-performing supreme Siddhi, which transforms this impurity-filled body on its path of delusion into an immortal, immaculate form; the Treasure of Compassion who, knowing the right moment, came and gave himself to me; my father who birthed me, my mother; the Master who shines in the substance-filled Chitrambalam; the Perfect, True Bliss of Pure Sivam, which is difficult to describe; the God who is the Great Jothi of compassionate Grace, I saw him with my own eyes, I ripened into him, I merged with him, rejoicing.
commentary: After explaining how God remains hidden from the powerful, the ascetic, and the wise, Vallalar reveals how he finally saw the "Thief." It was not through his own effort. Instead, God, as a "Treasure of Compassion," came to him directly, choosing the right moment to grant this vision. This grace transformed his very being, turning his mortal body immortal and filling his consciousness with the blissful light of the divine.

sections.title: The Holy Vision of the Lord

translit: aruḷelām aḷitta ampalat tamutai aruṭperuñ jōtiyai aracē maruḷelām tavirttu vāḻvitta maruntai vaḷḷalai māṇikka maṇiyaip poruḷelām koṭutteṉ puntiyil kalanta puṇṇiya nitiyaimeyp poruḷait teruḷelām valla cittaimeyñ ñāṉa tīpattaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have beheld the ambrosia of the Ambalam that bestows all grace, the Grace-Vast-Jothi, the King, the medicine that banished all delusion and made me live, the benefactor, the ruby gem, the treasure of merit who gave me all things and mingled in my intellect, the true substance, the Cit that commands all clarity, the lamp of true wisdom.
commentary: This verse overflows with metaphors to describe the direct experience of God. God is a tangible reality: nourishing like ambrosia, healing like medicine, precious like a gem, and illuminating like a lamp. Vallalar celebrates that this divine substance has been seen and has mingled with his own intellect, bringing total clarity and banishing all delusion.

translit: tuṉpelām tavirtta tuṇaiyaieṉ uḷḷat turicelān tolaittameyc cukattai eṉpolā maṇiyai eṉcikā maṇiyai eṉṉiru kaṇṇuḷmā maṇiyai aṉpelām aḷitta ampalat tamutai aruṭperuñ jōtiyai aṭiyēṉ eṉpelām urukki iṉpelām aḷitta entaiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have beheld the companion who averted all suffering, the true bliss that destroyed all impurities in my heart, my flawless gem, my crest-gem, the great gem within my two eyes, the ambrosia of the Ambalam that gives all love, the Grace-Vast-Jothi, my Father, who melted all my bones and gave me all bliss.
commentary: The vision of God is described here as an intensely personal and loving encounter. God is a companion who ends all suffering and a father whose presence gives overwhelming bliss. The powerful image of having his "bones melted" conveys a complete surrender of his old identity, his very structure dissolving in the ecstatic experience of divine grace.

translit: citattilēūṟit teḷintateḷ ḷamutaic cittelām vallameyc civattaip patattilē paḻutta taṉipperum paḻattaip parampara vāḻvaiem patiyai matattilē mayaṅkā matiyilē viḷainta maruntaimā mantiran taṉṉai itattilē eṉṉai iruttiāṭ koṇṭa iṟaivaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have beheld the clear ambrosia that steeped in my cittam and became clarified, the true Sivam who masters all siddhi, the unique, great fruit ripened in the supreme spiritual state, the transcendent life, our Master, the medicine that grew in an intellect not deluded by dogma, the great mantra itself, the Lord who established me in well-being and graciously took me as His own.
commentary: Divine realization is an internal process that clarifies the mind and purifies it of rigid dogma. The divine presence soaks into the cittam (the stuff of mind and feeling) like a clarifying ambrosia. Vallalar points out that this inner medicine grows in an intellect free from fixed religious doctrines, suggesting that true spirituality is found by looking within, not through adherence to external systems. Union with this true Sivam (the auspicious, divine reality) is what grants mastery over all spiritual capacities (siddhi).

translit: uṇarntavar uḷampōṉ ṟeṉṉuḷat tamarnta oruperum patiyaieṉ uvappaip puṇarnteṉaik kalanta pōkattai eṉatu poruḷaieṉ puṇṇiyap payaṉaik koṇarntoru poruḷeṉ karattilē koṭutta kuruvaieṇ kuṇapperuṅ kuṉṟai maṇantaceṅ kuvaḷai malareṉak kaḷitta vaḷḷalaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have beheld the one great Master who abides in my heart just as in the hearts of the realized, my own joy, the ecstasy that joined and mingled with me, my own substance, the fruit of my merit, the Guru who brought a substance and placed it in my hand, the great mountain of eight qualities, the benefactor who gave me bliss like a fragrant red water lily flower.
commentary: God is both the inner guide and one's own true self. This divine Master is present in the hearts of great saints and is equally present in Vallalar's own heart as his deepest joy and substance. The experience is made tangible when he says the Guru (the spiritual teacher, who is God) "brought a substance and placed it in my hand," signifying a direct, undeniable gift of grace that is as real as any physical object.

translit: pulliya neṟinīt teṉaieṭut tāṇṭa poṟcapai appaṉai vētam colliya paṭieṉ colelām koṇṭa jōtiyaic cōtiyā teṉṉai mallikai mālai aṇintuḷē kalantu maṉṉiya patiyaieṉ vāḻvai elliyum iravum eṉṉaiviṭ ṭakalā iṟaivaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have beheld the Father of the Golden Hall who lifted me from the base path and took me as His own, the Jothi who accepted all my words as if they were the Vedas, the eternal Master who, without testing me, adorned me with a jasmine garland and mingled within me, my very life, the Lord who does not leave me day or night.
commentary: Divine grace is unconditional and astonishingly intimate. God accepts him "without testing," lifting him from a lesser state out of pure compassion. Most remarkably, the divine light (Jothi) accepts his own heartfelt words as if they were the Vedas (the most sacred scriptures). This values personal, sincere devotion as highly as ancient holy texts, affirming that God is a constant companion who never leaves.

translit: paṇṇiya tavamum palamummeyp palañcey patiyumām orupacu patiyai naṇṇieṉ uḷattait taṉṉuḷam ākki nalkiya karuṇainā yakaṉai eṇṇiya paṭiyē eṉakkaruḷ purinta iṟaivaṉai maṟaimuṭi ilaṅkum taṇṇiya viḷakkait taṉṉika rillāt tantaiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have found and seen the one Lord of the soul, who is the penance I performed, its fruit, and the Master who bestows the true fruit. He is the gracious Lord who approached me, made my mind his own, and granted me grace exactly as I had envisioned. He is the cool lamp shining at the crest of the Vedas, the father without peer.
commentary: The spiritual path, the effort, and the goal are all revealed to be one and the same divine reality. God is not a distant reward for spiritual practice; He is the practice itself, the fruit that comes from it, and the master who gives it. This union is so complete that God "made my mind his own," dissolving the distinction between the seeker and the sought, and fulfilling the deepest desires of the heart.

translit: peṇmaiyai vayaṅkum āṇmaiyai aṉaittum piṟaṅkiya potumaiyaip periya taṇmaiyai ellām vallaōr citta cāmiyait tayāniti taṉṉai vaṇmaiyai aḻiyā varattiṉai ñāṉa vāḻvaieṉ matiyilē viḷaṅkum uṇmaiyai eṉṟaṉ uyiraieṉ uyiruḷ oruvaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have found and seen him who is femininity, shining masculinity, and the neutrality in which all things manifest. He is great coolness, the one all-powerful Siddha Master, a treasure of compassion, generosity, the undying boon, the life of wisdom, the truth shining in my intellect, my very soul, and the one within my soul.
commentary: God holds all seeming opposites within a single, unified reality. He is the essence of femininity, masculinity, and the neutral ground from which both arise. This all-powerful Siddha (perfected being) is also the embodiment of pure compassion, generosity, and the living truth that shines as wisdom within one's own mind.

translit: ātiyai āti antamī teṉa:uḷ aṟivitta aṟivaieṉ aṉpaic cōtiyai eṉatu tuṇaiyaieṉ cukattaic cuttacaṉ mārkkattiṉ tuṇipai nītiyai ellā nilaikaḷum kaṭanta nilaiyilē niṟaintamā nitiyai ōtiyai ōtā tuṇarttiya veḷiyai oḷitaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have found and seen the beginning, the awareness that made me understand from within, "This is the beginning and this is the end." He is my love, the Jothi, my companion, my happiness, the core principle of Suddha Sanmarkkam, and justice itself. He is the great treasure filling the state that transcends all other states, the expanse that imparts understanding without being formally taught, the light itself.
commentary: True spiritual knowledge is a direct, inner awakening, not something learned from outside sources. God is the very awareness that reveals reality from within, the foundational truth of Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path). This understanding is felt as a vast, open space that teaches without words, a treasure found in a state beyond all other levels of consciousness.

translit: eṉceyal aṉaittum taṉceyal ākki eṉṉaivāḻ vikkiṉṟa patiyaip poṉceyal vakaiyai uṇarttieṉ uḷattē poruntiya maruntaiyeṉ poruḷai vaṉceyal akaṟṟi ulakelām viḷaṅka vaittacaṉ mārkkacaṟ kuruvaik koṉceyal oḻitta cattiya ñāṉak kōyilil kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: The master who makes me live, having made all my actions his own actions. The one who taught me the nature of the golden art, the medicine that has settled in my heart, my very own substance. The true guru of Sanmarkkam who removed cruel actions and established the path to illuminate the entire world. I have found and seen him, who abolished all useless deeds, within the temple of true wisdom.
commentary: When the divine takes over, your actions are no longer your own; they become expressions of God's will. This inner presence is a true teacher, or guru, who purifies the heart of cruelty and reveals the principles of Sanmarkkam (the True Path). This transformation happens within the "temple of true wisdom," which is one's own consciousness.

translit: puṉṉika rillēṉ poruṭṭiruṭ ṭiravil pōntaruḷ aḷittacaṟ kuruvaik kaṉṉikar maṉattaik karaitteṉuṭ kalanta karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭavuḷait taṉatu coṉṉikar eṉaeṉ colelāṅ koṇṭē tōḷuṟap puṉaintameyt tuṇaiyait taṉṉika rillāt talaivaṉai eṉatu tantaiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have found and seen the true guru who came in the dark of night and bestowed grace for the sake of me, who am less than grass; the God of compassion who melted my stone-like heart and mingled within me; the true companion who, accepting all my words as equal to His own, wore them as a garland upon His shoulders; the leader without peer, my father.
commentary: Divine grace is given freely, even to one who feels as worthless as grass. God is the compassionate one who can melt a heart as hard as stone and merge with it completely. In this intimate relationship, the devotee's simple words are received and cherished as if they were divine utterances, and the soul is embraced by its true, unequaled parent.

translit: ēṅkalai makaṉē tūṅkalai eṉavan teṭutteṉai aṇaittaeṉ tāyai ōṅkiya eṉatu tantaiyai ellām uṭaiyaeṉ oruperum patiyaip pāṅkaṉil eṉṉaip parintukoṇ ṭellāp paricumiṅ kaḷittataṟ parattait tāṅkumōr nītit taṉipperuṅ karuṇait talaivaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen my mother who came to me, saying, "Do not grieve, my son, do not languish," and lifted and embraced me. I have seen my exalted father, my one great Lord who possesses everything, the Supreme One who lovingly took me in and gave me every gift right here, the Leader of singular, great compassion who is a supporting justice.
commentary: God is experienced here as both a tender mother and a supreme father. The motherly presence offers intimate comfort, telling him not to worry. The fatherly presence represents the all-powerful Lord (pati) who owns everything and provides every form of support. This shows that the ultimate reality is a source of complete, personal care.

translit: tuṉpuṟēl makaṉē tūṅkalai eṉaeṉ cōrvelān tavirttanaṟ ṟāyai aṉpuḷē kalanta tantaiyai eṉṟaṉ āviyaip pāviyēṉ uḷattai iṉpilē niṟaivit taruḷuru vākki iṉitamarn taruḷiya iṟaiyai vaṉpilāk karuṇai māniti eṉumeṉ vaḷḷalaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen my good mother who dispelled all my weariness, saying, "Do not suffer, my son, do not languish." I have seen my father who mingled with my love, the God who filled the heart of this sinner with bliss, made me a form of grace, and blissfully took his seat within. I have seen my generous benefactor, who is the great treasure of compassion without harshness.
commentary: Divine compassion is an active, healing force. God, as a loving mother, erases his exhaustion and, as a father, fills him with love. Vallalar, acknowledging his own past flaws, describes being completely filled with bliss and remade into a "form of grace." The transformation is total, turning a person into a vessel of divine light.

translit: naṉavilum eṉatu kaṉavilum eṉakkē naṇṇiya taṇṇiya amutai maṉaṉuṟu mayakkam tavirttaruṭ cōti vaḻaṅkiya peruntayā nitiyaic ciṉamutal āṟun tīrttuḷē amarnta civakuru patiyaieṉ ciṟappai uṉalarum periya turiyamēl veḷiyil oḷitaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the cool ambrosia that came to me in my waking state and in my dreams. I have seen the great treasure of compassion who dispelled my mind's confusion and granted me the Grace-Light. I have seen the Siva-Guru Lord who, eradicating the six flaws beginning with anger, took his seat within. I have seen the Light in the great space beyond Turiyam, which is difficult to comprehend and is my own splendor.
commentary: The divine encounter is a continuous presence, felt in waking life and in dreams. This presence grants the Grace-Light, which dispels confusion and removes inner flaws like anger. Vallalar locates this experience in a sublime inner space "beyond Turiyam," a known state of superconsciousness, showing that this union with the Light is the pinnacle of spiritual attainment.

translit: karumpiliṉ cāṟṟaik kaṉintamuk kaṉiyaik karutukōṟ ṟēṉnaṟuñ cuvaiyai arumpeṟal amutai aṟivaieṉ aṉpai āviyai āviyuṭ kalanta peruntaṉip patiyaip peruñcukak kaḷippaip pēcutaṟ karumperum pēṟṟai virumpieṉ uḷattai iṭaṅkoṇṭu viḷaṅkum viḷakkiṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the juice of sugarcane, the three ripened fruits, and the fragrant taste of pure honey from the comb. I have seen the rare ambrosia, consciousness, my love, my life-breath, and the one who mingled with my life-breath. I have seen the great, unique Lord, the ecstasy of great bliss, the great boon that is difficult to speak of, the Lamp that, desiring me, took my heart as its place and now shines there.
commentary: Words fail to capture the divine, so Vallalar uses metaphors of ultimate sweetness: sugarcane, ripe fruits, pure honey. God is experienced as rare ambrosia, as consciousness itself, and as the very love and life within him. This supreme being is an intimate presence, a "Lamp" that has chosen to take his heart as its dwelling place and shine from within.

translit: kaḷaṅkoḷuṅ kaṭaiyēṉ kaḷaṅkelāṅ tavirttuk kaḷippelām aḷittacark karaiyai uḷaṅkoḷun tēṉai uṇavuṇat teviṭṭā tuḷḷakat tūṟumiṉ ṉamutai vaḷaṅkoḷum periya vāḻvaieṉ kaṇṇuḷ maṇiyaieṉ vāḻkkaimā nitiyaik kuḷaṅkoḷum oḷiyai oḷikkuḷē viḷaṅkum kuruvaiyāṉ kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the sugar that removed all the faults of this lowly, faulty one and gave me every bliss. I have seen the honey that captivates the heart, the sweet ambrosia that wells up within, never cloying. I have seen the great, prosperous life, the pupil of my eye, the great treasure of my life, the cool and pervasive Light, and the Guru who shines from within that Light.
commentary: The divine presence is an inner sweetness that both purifies a person of their faults and provides unending bliss. This sweetness is an ambrosia that constantly wells up from within, always satisfying and never cloying. This inner source is also a guiding Light, and from within that Light shines the Guru, or inner teacher, who is as precious as the pupil of one's eye.

translit: citampara oḷiyaic citampara veḷiyaic citampara naṭampuri civattaip patantaru patattaip parampara patattaip paticiva patattaittaṟ patattai itantarum uṇmaip peruntaṉi nilaiyai yāvumāy allavām poruḷaic catantaruñ cacci tāṉanta niṟaivaic cāmiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the Light of Chidambaram and the Space of Chidambaram; Sivam who performs the dance in Chidambaram; the state that bestows the supreme state, the transcendent state, the state of Lord Sivam, and the state of the Self; the great, unique state of truth that brings goodness; the substance that is everything yet is not them; the fullness of eternal Satchitānanda; I have seen the Master.
commentary: The ultimate reality is experienced as a union of paradoxes. It is centered in Chidambaram, which is both a physical place and the inner "space of consciousness". In this space, God (Sivam) is seen as both pure Light and the dynamic cosmic Dancer. This single reality, the source of all states of being, is the fullness of Satchitānanda (being, consciousness, and bliss).

translit: āraṇa muṭimēl amarpira mattai ākama muṭiamar parattaik kāraṇa varattaik kāriya tarattaik kāriya kāraṇak karuvait tāraṇa nilaiyait tattuva patiyaic cattiya nittiya talattaip pūraṇa cukattaip pūraṇa civamām poruḷiṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the Brahman that sits atop the crown of the Vedas; the Supreme that sits atop the crown of the Agamas; the boon of the Cause and the foundation of the effect; the very essence of cause and effect; the state that is the foundation of all; the Lord of all tattvas; the ground of eternal truth; the perfect bliss, and the substance that is perfect Sivam.
commentary: The divine reality Vallalar has seen is the single, ultimate source pointed to by all scriptures and philosophies. It is the Brahman of the Vedas and the Supreme Being of the Agamas (the two main branches of Hindu sacred texts). It is the origin of causality, the lord of all the tattvas (fundamental principles of reality), and the ground of all truth, experienced directly as perfect Sivam.

translit: cuttavēta tānta piramarā ciyattaic cuttacit tāntarā ciyattait tattuvā tītat taṉipperum poruḷaic camaraca cattiyap poruḷaic cittelām valla cittaieṉ aṟivil teḷintapē rāṉantat teḷivai vittamā veḷiyaic cuttaciṟ capaiyiṉ meymaiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the kingdom of Brahman of pure Vedānta; the kingdom of pure Siddhānta; the great, unique substance beyond all tattvas; the substance of harmonious truth; the all-powerful Chit; the clear essence of great bliss that dawned in my awareness; the vast causal space, and the very reality of the pure hall of consciousness.
commentary: The highest spiritual truth unites different paths, revealing a single reality. Vallalar sees the "kingdom" promised by both pure Vedānta and pure Siddhānta (two major Indian philosophical traditions) as one and the same. This ultimate substance is beyond all tattvas (principles of reality) and is experienced directly as pure, all-powerful Chit (consciousness), a clear bliss arising within his own awareness.

translit: camayamum matamum kaṭantatōr ñāṉa capainaṭam purikiṉṟa taṉiyait tamaiaṟin tavaruṭ cārntameyc cārvaic cattuva nittacaṟ kuruvai amaiyaeṉ maṉattait tiruttinal laruḷā ramutaḷit tamarntaaṟ putattai nimalaniṟ kuṇattaic ciṟkuṇā kāra nitiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the unique One who dances in the hall of wisdom beyond all religions and creeds; the true refuge who dwells within those who have realized themselves; the eternal Sat-Guru of pure being; the wonder who perfectly reformed my mind, gave me the sweet nectar of good grace, and established himself there; the flawless one without attributes, and the treasure who is the very form of conscious qualities.
commentary: God's presence is not limited by religion or creed; it is a universal wisdom available to all. This divine reality is the ultimate refuge found within those who know themselves, acting as the Sat-Guru (the true, eternal teacher). This inner teacher personally reforms the mind with grace, revealing a wonder that is both without attributes and yet full of perfect, conscious qualities.

translit: aḷavaikaḷ aṉaittum kaṭantuniṉ ṟōṅkum aruṭperuñ cōtiyai ulakak kaḷavaiviṭ ṭavartaṅ karuttuḷē viḷaṅkum kāṭciyaik karuṇaiyaṅ kaṭalai uḷavaieṉ ṟaṉakkē uraittelām valla oḷiyaiyum utaviya oḷiyaik kuḷavayiṉ niṟainta kuruciva patiyaik kōyilil kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: In the temple, I have seen the ArutPerunJothi that soars beyond all measures; the vision that shines in the minds of those who have abandoned worldly deceit; the beautiful ocean of compassion; the Light who told the inner secret to me alone and also gave me the all-powerful Light; and the Guru-Siva-Pati who fills the sacred inner center.
commentary: The divine is an ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) that cannot be measured or contained by the mind. This light, an ocean of pure compassion, becomes visible only to those who have let go of worldly illusions. Vallalar experiences this light as an intimate presence that spoke truth directly to him and now fills his innermost being as the divine master, the Guru-Siva-Pati.

translit: cārkalān tātic caṭāntamuṅ kalanta camaraca cattiya veḷiyaic cōrvelān tavirtteṉ aṟiviṉuk kaṟivāyt tulaṅkiya jōtiyaic cōtip pārpeṟāp patattaip patamelāṅ kaṭanta paramacaṉ mārkkameyp patiyaic cērkuṇān tattiṟ ciṟantatōr talaimait teyvattaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the true expanse of harmonious oneness that pervades the six antas beginning with Kalānta; the Jothi that dispelled all my weariness and shone as the knowledge within my knowledge; the state that those who test and examine cannot attain; the true Master of the supreme Sanmarkkam that transcends all states; and the one foremost divinity who excels beyond the end of qualities.
commentary: God is a harmonious, true expanse that pervades all six antas, the six "ends" of spiritual systems beginning with Kalānta. This divine Jothi (Light) is the knowledge shining within one's own knowledge. It is the Lord of the supreme Sanmarkkam, a state that those who merely test and examine can never attain.

translit: aṭinaṭu muṭiyōr aṇuttuṇai yēṉum aṟintiṭap paṭātamey aṟivaip paṭimutal aṇṭap parappelāṅ kaṭanta patiyilē viḷaṅkumeyp patiyaik kaṭiyaeṉ maṉaṉāṅ kallaiyum kaṉiyiṟ kaṭaikkaṇit taruḷiya karuṇaik koṭivaḷar iṭattup peruntayā nitiyaik kōyilil kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: In the temple, I have seen the true awareness whose beginning, middle, and end cannot be known by even an atom's measure; the true Master who shines within the Master who transcends the entire expanse of the universe from this world outward; the Grace that, with a side-glance, graciously ripened my hard, stone-like mind into a fruit; the great treasure of compassion on whose side the creeper-like goddess flourishes.
commentary: A single glance of divine grace can utterly transform a person. Vallalar describes his mind as a hard, unripe stone, which God's compassion instantly softened and ripened into a sweet fruit. This shows that spiritual awakening is a gift of grace from a divine reality that is itself beyond all knowing, a "great treasure of compassion."

translit: payamumvaṉ kavalai iṭarmutal aṉaittum paṟṟaṟat tavirttaruṭ paricum nayamumnaṟ ṟiruvum uruvumīṅ keṉakku nalkiya naṇpainaṉ ṉāta iyamuṟa veṉatu kuḷanaṭu naṭañcey entaiyai eṉṉuyirk kuyiraip puyaṉaṭu viḷaṅkum puṇṇiya oḷiyaip poṟpuṟak kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have splendidly seen Him: the One who banished fear, harsh anxiety, suffering, and all such things without a trace and granted me here the gift of His grace, goodness, sacred wealth, and a true form; my friend; the good Lord, my Father, who fittingly dances in the center of my inner lake; the very life of my life; the blessed light shining amidst the clouds.
commentary: Seeing God removes all fear and suffering, replacing them with grace and a true sense of self. Vallalar describes this relationship in deeply intimate terms: God is a friend, a father, and the very life-force within his own soul. The image of the Lord dancing in his "inner lake" beautifully captures the joyous, living presence of the divine discovered within a calm and clear mind.

translit: kalainiṟai matiyaik kaṉalaicceṅ katiraik kakaṉattaik kāṟṟiṉai amutai nilainiṟai aṭiyai aṭimuṭi tōṟṟā niṉmala niṟkuṇa niṟaivai malaivaṟum uḷattē vayaṅkumey vāḻvai varavupōk kaṟṟaciṉ mayattai alaiyaṟu karuṇait taṉipperuṅ kaṭalai aṉpiṉiṟ kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: In love, I have seen the full-orbed moon, the fire, the red-rayed sun, the sky, the wind, the ambrosia; the state of the feet of fullness; the immaculate, quality-less plenitude whose beginning and end are not perceived; the true life that shines in an unwavering mind; the pure consciousnessthat is without coming or going; the unique, great ocean of waveless compassion.
commentary: Through love, one can perceive the divine in everything, from the elements of nature to the highest spiritual states. This experience reveals God as cinmayam (pure consciousness), an unchanging reality that is the source of all life. Vallalar describes this ultimate state as a vast, silent ocean of compassion, a deep peace that can only be known through a heart filled with love.

translit: mummaiyai ellām uṭaiyapē raracai muḻutoruṅ kuṇarttiya uṇarvai vemmaiyait tavirttiṅ keṉakkaru ḷamutam viyappuṟa aḷittamey viḷaivaic cemmaiyai ellāc cittiyum eṉpāl cērntiṭap puriaruṭ ṭiṟattai ammaiyaik karuṇai appaṉai eṉpē raṉpaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen the great King who possesses all the triads, the awareness that made me realize the whole all at once; the true fruition who banished my inner heat and, to my wonder, gave me the ambrosia of grace here; the perfection, the power of grace that made all siddhis come to me; the Mother, the compassionate Father, my great Lover.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual experience is a sudden, all-encompassing realization of unity with God. This union quenches the "inner heat" of suffering and brings extraordinary abilities, or siddhis (supernatural powers), as a natural side effect. Most importantly, this experience reveals God as a loving Mother, a compassionate Father, and a great Lover to the soul.

translit: karuttaṉai eṉatu kaṇaṉai yavaṉaik karuṇaiyā ramuteṉak kaḷitta oruttaṉai eṉṉai uṭaiyanā yakaṉai uṇmaivē tākama muṭiyiṉ aruttaṉai varaṉai apayaṉait tirucciṟ ṟampalat taruḷnaṭam puriyum niruttaṉai eṉatu nēyaṉai ñāṉa nilaiyaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen and realized the Creator, the one who is like my own eye, the unique one who gave me the nectar of compassion, the Lord who possesses me, the one who is the meaning at the pinnacle of the true Vedas and Agamas, the supreme bestower of boons, the giver of refuge, the Dancer who performs the dance of grace in the sacred golden hall, my beloved, the one who is the state of wisdom.
commentary: The God of direct, personal experience is the same ultimate reality pointed to by the highest scriptures. Vallalar connects his own realization of God as his "Lord" and "beloved" to the deep meaning of the Vedas and Agamas (sacred Hindu texts). He also identifies this presence with the divine dancer in the "sacred golden hall," a traditional image of God's blissful activity at the heart of the cosmos.

translit: vittelām aḷitta vimalaṉai ellā viḷaivaiyum viḷaikkaval lavaṉai attelāṅkāṭṭum arumpeṟal maṇiyai āṉantak kūttaṉai aracaic cattelām āṉa cayampuvai ñāṉa capaittaṉit talaivaṉait tavaṉaic cittelām valla cittaṉai oṉṟān teyvattaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen and realized the immaculate one who provided all seeds, the one able to bring about all effects, the rare gem that reveals all that is, the Dancer of bliss, the King, the self-manifested one who has become all existence, the sole Head of the hall of wisdom, the embodiment of spiritual discipline, the Siddha who is all-powerful in consciousness, the one God.
commentary: God is the single source, substance, and power behind all of existence. He is the "seed" for all things, the "Dancer of bliss," and the very fabric of being (sat). At the same time, God is the perfected consciousness (cit) of a Siddha (a perfected being), who has mastered all knowledge and power. This vision unifies the material world and spiritual realization into one divine reality.

translit: uttara ñāṉa cittimā purattiṉ ōṅkiya oruperum patiyai uttara ñāṉa citampara oḷiyai uṇmaiyai orutaṉi uṇarvai uttara ñāṉa naṭampuri kiṉṟa oruvaṉai ulakelām vaḻuttum uttara ñāṉa cuttacaṉ mārkkam ōtiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen and realized the one great Lord exalted in the great city of the perfection of supreme wisdom, the light of the supreme wisdom-space, the Truth, the singular consciousness, the one who performs the dance of supreme wisdom, the one who taught the path of Suddha Sanmarkkam of supreme wisdom, which all the worlds praise.
commentary: The highest spiritual attainment is a state of pure wisdom, and God himself has taught the way to reach it. Vallalar names this way the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path), a universal teaching praised by all worlds. The "dance of supreme wisdom" is a cosmic event and an inner realization available to all who follow this path.

translit: pulaikolai tavirtta neṟiyilē eṉṉaip puṇarttiya puṉitaṉai ellā nilaikaḷum kāṭṭi aruṭperu nilaiyil niṟuttiya nimalaṉai eṉakku malaivaṟat teḷinta amutaḷit taḻiyā vāḻkkaiyil vāḻavait tavaṉait talaivaṉai īṉṟa tāyaieṉ urimait tantaiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen and realized the holy one who united me with the path that shuns meat-eating and killing; the immaculate one who showed me all states and established me in the state of vast grace; the one who gave me clear nectar that ends confusion and made me live an imperishable life; the Lord, the mother who gave birth to me, my very own father.
commentary: The entire spiritual path, leading to an imperishable life of grace, begins with a simple ethical commitment: to stop killing and eating meat. Vallalar states plainly that it was God who united him with this path of non-harm. This practice is the foundation that allows one to receive divine clarity and be established in a state of grace, cared for by God as a loving parent.

translit: paṉiiṭar payantīrt teṉakkamu taḷitta paramaṉai eṉṉuḷē paḻutta kaṉiaṉai yavaṉai aruṭperuñ cōtik kaṭavuḷaik kaṇṇiṉuḷ maṇiyaip puṉitaṉai ellām vallaōr ñāṉap poruḷeṉak kaḷittameyp poruḷait taṉiyaṉai īṉṟa tāyaieṉ urimait tantaiyaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉē.
translation: I have seen and realized the supreme one who ended my trembling suffering and fear and gave me nectar; the one who is like a fruit ripened within me; the God of Vast Grace-Light; the pupil within the eye; the holy one; the True Substance who granted Himself to me as the one, all-powerful substance of wisdom; the solitary one; the mother who gave birth to me, my very own father.
commentary: The divine presence is experienced in many ways at once: as comfort that ends fear, as an essence ripening within you, as the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), as the very awareness in your eyes, and as the ultimate wisdom that is both all-powerful and your own. This reality, though solitary and supreme, feels as close as your own parents.
